Cardinals-Chiefs Reveal Star-Studded Week 11 Injury Report
full_text:
The Arizona Cardinals and Kansas City Chiefs have revealed their first injury reports of Week 11 ahead of their clash at Arrowhead.
It's a fairly lengthy report with 25 total names between the two sides, with stars such as Patrick Mahomes and Budda Baker headlining their respective squads.
Wednesday's practice report:
With new rookie quarterback Carson Beck in the mix, the Cardinals' offense is hoping to take the next step — and a big part of that could be with starting center Hjalte Froholdt progressing through concussion protocol.
Froholdt wasn't spotted wearing a yellow non-contact jersey during practice — a good sign for his availability moving forward.
"I texted 'Fro' (Hjalte Froholdt) Sunday night after the game because he wasn't there just being in the protocol and all that. I said, 'You're going to have a lot of fun playing with this guy.' So that'll be good," Cardinals head coach Mike LaFleur told reporters.
"This was basically the first walkthrough that they've had where Carson's running the huddle so I'm curious to see what he felt like in that 35, 40 minutes. What he'll provide with practice if he's able to go tomorrow and then into Sunday if he's able to go, is just a guy that's done it for a really long time. He's played in hostile environments. Up until the injury, I thought he was just getting better and better each week handling his job. I'm excited if he's able to clear this thing and be out there."
Top NFL MVP candidate Kenneth Walker III is likely to miss another week, reading between the words of Chiefs head coach Andy Reid today.
"He had a sore groin (last week). It's getting better. We just don't want to do something stupid. ... He's feeling better," he said today ( h/t Nate Taylor ).
It sounds like the Chiefs are being cautious with a game next Thursday (Thanksgiving) around the corner.
Though Kelce and Mahomes are listed on the report, it'd be a surprise if either missed Sunday's game against Arizona.

title: James Conner Update Keeps Cardinals' Biggest Mystery Alive
full_text:
TEMPE — The mystery of Arizona Cardinals running back James Conner only grows with each passing week.
In Week 3 of last year, Conner suffered a season-ending foot injury that required surgery. Though no official timetable was set in place for the veteran back, the Cardinals restructuring his contract to keep him with Arizona gave fans hope that the team would have not only a tough bruising back available, but also a key leader in the locker room for first-year head coach Mike LaFleur.
We're now over halfway done with the 2026 season, the last of Conner's contract before he'll be a free agent, and the Cardinals have yet to see him removed from injured reserve. Despite taking part in individual drills during training camp, we haven't seen Conner suit up for the organization — and it's a massive question mark if that will change.
LaFleur, at numerous points, has been asked about Conner with little wiggle room or budging on his stance: Conner's a well respected guy who has earned the right to decide when he comes back.
It was the same song and dance with LaFleur this week.
"But James, again, it's what I said a couple weeks ago: he's working his butt off to get himself in a position to return to perform, not just be out there," he said.
Before sprinkling in a different two-step in calling Conner's injury "not good":
"I don't know if it did go awry. And honestly, I'd rather have — I mean, obviously, he's not available to you guys in that facet — but I'd rather have him answer that," LaFleur said when asked where Conner's injury went wrong.
"It was not a good injury. And so again, James has earned the right to know how he's feeling and you go about his process, I guess, if you will. We're all rooting for him, and if he could, and if he felt like he could help this team win football games, he'd be out there. But right now, it kind of is what it is."
There was some thought that Conner could be traded at the deadline or released near the end of the season to help a contending team with their playoff run. Arizona's running back stable, when fully healthy, is stocked with Jeremiyah Love, Tyler Allgeier and Bam Knight leading the charge.
There's seven games remaining in the Cardinals' schedule — we'll see what comes of Conner's role.

title: Cardinals Explain Big Bet on Elijah Higgins
full_text:
ARIZONA — The Arizona Cardinals ' future is anything but known at this point in time, though we do know tight end Elijah Higgins will be part of their plans moving forward.
Higgins inked a three-year extension with the Cardinals over the weekend. While details are still emerging, the deal is reportedly worth up to $26.8 million.
It's not often you see a backup tight end awarded that much money, though with the Cardinals ranking second in 13 (three tight end) personnel under new head coach Mike LaFleur , the investments in a valuable position group are deemed worthy.
LaFleur, meeting with reporters, says Higgins is made of all the right stuff.
"Well, one he's made of all the right stuff. Two, he is super strong, and he is not even, in my opinion like I've told him, has come close to what I think he's going to be," LaFleur said.
"He can do a lot of things without the football, and he's excited about doing those things without the football. I've talked to people in the building about how important Juice (Kyle Juszczyk) is up in San Francisco. He touches the ball here and there, but man, does he impact the game in so many other ways. Elijah impacts the game in so many other ways.
"And with that being said, I think he's only going to get better with the football as well in ways that we can get him. So I'm glad that we have him wrapped up long term. He's exactly what you want in a guy in the locker room. He's tough. He's heavy on contact. He can play in-line. He can move linebackers. If he has edges on even some of the big d-ends, he can move those guys. He's smart. I'm excited to watch him continue to grow. Not just this week, but really kind of moving forward."
Higgins initially entered the league as a receiver before moving to tight end, starting his career with the Miami Dolphins (2023) before being picked up by the Cardinals the day after he was waived ahead of final roster cuts.
The rest has been history — even if it's unconventional.
"I can't answer your question in terms of giving you other names that's like that. I'm sure there has been, but for our situation, that's what makes it really unique is because when you have those guys, you're thinking, 'Man, are they a tight end? Are we labeling them a tight end even though everyone knows they can't block?' It's like the opposite of that," LaFleur said.
"He's just continuing to get better at that. And again, I'm really excited. I'm kind of actually telling you the conversation I'm going to have with him probably sometime today, but really excited to watch him really take this next step over these next seven weeks, starting this week."

title: Breaking Down Cardinals' Injuries Heading Into Week 11 (Who's Hurt & Who Could Return vs Chiefs)
full_text:
The Carson Beck era is officially underway in the desert, though the Arizona Cardinals are hoping to finish their 2026 season on a high note after a disaster 3-7 start. The red-hot Kansas City Chiefs waiting at Arrowhead won't be any easier of a challenge for Beck and co. moving into Week 11.
So who is expected to return, and who still might miss some time?
Digging into the full slate of Cardinals injuries as a new week begins:
Wingard wasn't initially mentioned by head coach Mike LaFleur in his post-game list of injuries, though the Cardinals' coach mentioned on Monday that the starting safety would miss extensive time.
“We have 'Dewey' (S Andrew Wingard) (who) ended up having a wrist (or) hand (injury) — something like that, so he'll be out for an extended period of time," LaFleur said.
He was placed on injured reserve Tuesday after the Cardinals initially believed he wasn't a candidate to land on the list.
Burch went down to the grass of State Farm Stadium on Sunday with what appeared to be a serious knee injury, which was later confirmed by LaFleur as a season-ending MCL injury.
“Not shocked at anything," LaFleur said of all the injuries piling up. "Again, I'll just always go back to it really sucks for the player. Yes, it sucks for our club and all those kinds of things, but (when) injuries happen, it sucks for the player. The list just continues to grow, but that's who I'm feeling for more."
Gaines, who has missed time due to an ankle injury, is trending well according to LaFleur.
“I'll have a better update for you on Wednesday, but I think it's trending well," he said. When asked if Gaines could potentially slot back into the starting right guard spot, he added, "There's a chance, yes.”
He was ruled out on Friday ahead of the weekend.
Froholdt was in concussion protocol last week and was marked as a DNP all three days before being ruled out. There's hope the Cardinals will have their starting center back in the mix this week, though it all depends on where he's at in the league's return to play program.
The seventh-round rookie was questionable entering Sunday before being ruled out with a knee injury. He did practice all three days last week before not playing, which could be encouraging for his status this week.

title: Grading Carson Beck's NFL Debut: Cardinals Rookie Delivered
full_text:
Carson Beck made his NFL debut on Sunday, officially beginning a new era of football for the Arizona Cardinals .
Exactly how long it lasts remains to be seen.
The hope is for Beck to develop into a quarterback the Cardinals are confident enough to roll out in 2027 and perhaps beyond. While the rookie third-round pick wasn't going to slay any dragons on Sunday, all eyes were fixated on State Farm Stadium to see what the first step of Beck's evaluation looked like.
So far, so good. The Cardinals loved what Beck accomplished on Sunday, and after reviewing the film , so did we. His box score (11-18, 108 yards, 0 TD, 2 INT) would lead you to believe Beck looked terrible.
That wasn't close to the case.
Grading Beck on six different categories after his first NFL start:
That's the cumulative grade of the six different categories above, and that feels correct.
Beck was by no means perfect. There were a handful of throws that were just off or out of reach for players — but that's life in the NFL, especially as a rookie playing with a ragtag crew of offensive players against the preseason Super Bowl favorites.
Beck's numbers would lead the average person to believe his debut was a massive disappointment. Though given context and the distinct poor play around him, Beck's individual performance was among the best out of any Cardinals player who suited up on Sunday.
There's seven more weeks of evaluation left before the Cardinals can feel comfortable on a decision regarding Beck, though his NFL debut was about as good as it could have been considering the circumstances around the rookie passer.

title: Don't Sweat The Stats — Cardinals Loved Carson Beck's Debut
full_text:
ARIZONA — By nearly all accounts, the debut for Arizona Cardinals rookie quarterback Carson Beck was a letdown.
Beck's first start — coming against preseason Super Bowl favorites in the Los Angeles Rams — was practically over by the beginning stages of the third quarter in their ultimate 34-6 blowout loss. Beck threw for two interceptions on the day with just 11 completions on 18 attempts and 108 yards with no touchdowns.
To those who didn't watch, surely that's not an ideal outing. But as we broke down in our film room , Beck's performance was, at an individual level, encouraging.
That's what the Cardinals believe, too.
"Was he doing his job? Was he getting in and out of the huddle? I thought he used the cadence really well," Cardinals head coach Mike LaFleur told reporters on Monday.
"(He) got that first free play on that third and seven. Actually, I chickened out a little bit because we talked about using cadence all week when we were kind of in those disadvantaged situations. The first drive, I kind of wanted to chill out and make sure that we weren't going from third-and-seven to third-and-12, and he stuck with it.
"He stuck with the cadence there, got the free play, and I thought (he) delivered an excellent ball to our receiver. I know our receiver can make that play. When you just look at his element and what he had to do, like I said yesterday, he did everything we asked him to do, and I am really encouraged by it.”
Beck was on the receiving end of poor play from practically everyone around him. He was sacked five times while Arizona's running backs found no success on the ground. Pass catchers missed numerous opportunities to extend drives due to drops while Arizona's defense failed in their own respective game plan.
In total, Beck ran just 34 plays for the Cardinals' offense, which was mostly aided by a 12-minute Rams possession to end the game in the fourth quarter.
“That's the harder part because there's just a smaller sample size," LaFleur said when asked what the rookie could improve.
"It would have been nice to get out there in kind of a semi two-minute mode there in the fourth quarter. Obviously, we couldn't get back out there. That would've been just good for that whole group. Some guys are still kind of learning the two-minute menu a little bit and guys are kind of mixing and matching around. There are things to improve, but again, it was a sharp debut for him.”
Beck shined in many aspects, perhaps the best coming purely in his composure. Oftentimes, rookie passers are doomed thanks to inexperience and the moment being too bright for them.
That wasn't the case for Beck — who looked calm, cool and collected throughout the game despite various factors working against him.
“I think we all probably could notice that, right? I mean, you guys could see with your eyes. As I was talking to you guys right after the game, you guys saw it and then you confirmed it probably with some tape today or whatever you guys were watching. That wasn't shocking at all," LaFleur continued on Beck's composure.
"It's just like I've kind of said with him, you can meet all you want and you can watch all the film (but) he keeps it very simple. At least that's what it comes across as. It's just going to be getting as many reps as he can. That's what stinks about yesterday (was) only having 34 reps and trying to get a little bit of a run game going, which we obviously didn't. Not a huge sample size as of yesterday, but hey, have another one this week and we'll take it from there.”

title: Film Room: Carson Beck's NFL Debut Was Better Than You Think
full_text:
ARIZONA — Arizona Cardinals quarterback Carson Beck is the talk of the town.
Beck's box score didn't quite impress those who weren't able to catch action at State Farm Stadium. In a 34-6 loss to the Los Angeles Rams, Beck threaded 11 of 18 passes for 108 yards and two interceptions with no touchdowns.
Ideal? Probably not, but the film tells a much different story.

Beck, quite frankly, was held back by a lack of supporting cast. Whether it be his offensive line not blocking to the tune of five sacks or pass catchers dropping multiple passes, Beck's statistical outing felt more like a victim of those around him as opposed to his own doing.
“Well, you could still evaluate. Was he doing his job? Was he getting in and out of the huddle? I thought he used the cadence really well," Cardinals head coach Mike LaFleur said of Beck's debut with a banged-up offense.
"(He) got that first free play on that third and seven. Actually, I chickened out a little bit because we talked about using cadence all week when we were kind of in those disadvantaged situations. The first drive, I kind of wanted to chill out and make sure that we weren't going from third-and-seven to third-and-12, and he stuck with it. He stuck with the cadence there, got the free play, and I thought (he) delivered an excellent ball to our receiver. I know our receiver can make that play. When you just look at his element and what he had to do, like I said yesterday, he did everything we asked him to do, and I am really encouraged by it.”
It also didn't help the Cardinals ran just 34 offensive plays in Week 10, a shockingly low number.
“That's the harder part because there's just a smaller sample size," LaFleur contined. "It would have been nice to get out there in kind of a semi two-minute mode there in the fourth quarter. Obviously, we couldn't get back out there. That would've been just good for that whole group. Some guys are still kind of learning the two-minute menu a little bit and guys are kind of mixing and matching around.
"There are things to improve, but again, it was a sharp debut for him.”
The Cardinals loved what Beck did in his first taste of action. Don't let the box score fool you.

title: Did the Cardinals Get It Right? Revisiting 5 Big Moves This Year
full_text:
In honor of Jacoby Brissett getting his first start for the Baltimore Ravens, it is fitting to see how former Arizona Cardinals players and coaches are doing well this season.
The Cardinals had a major overhaul this offseason, both in the coaching staff and roster.
The question is, did they make the right call in moving on?
When Arizona drafted Murray number one overall in 2019, there was hope that he would be the franchise quarterback for years to come. While Murray did have some great plays and moments, he could never string them together in Arizona.
After Arizona cut him this spring, some thought he could rebound with the Vikings. Especially since Minnesota's head coach, Kevin O'Connell, is offensive-minded. However, Murray didn't have a redemption arc with the Vikings. Murray's best games with Minnesota were against the New Orleans Saints and the Miami Dolphins, two of the worst teams in the NFL.
Murray's worst game for the Vikings was against a poor Indianapolis Colts defense in Week 7. In that game, he missed several throws and struggled to connect with superstar wideout Justin Jefferson. Minnesota won, but it was due to their spectacular special teams and defense.
While the Cardinals' quarterbacks haven't been lighting up the scoreboard, it’s safe to say that Murray wouldn't make Arizona drastically better.
Sticking in the NFC North, this might be a coach the Cardinals want back. In 2023 and 2024, the Lions offense put up elite numbers, largely thanks to the offensive coordinator at the time, Ben Johnson. However, after 2024, Johnson was hired as the head coach of the Chicago Bears. Detroit hired John Morton as the new offensive coordinator in 2025, but it didn't go well, and he was let go after one season.
This is where Petzing comes in, having gotten the Lions offense back on track this year. After Week 10, the Lions rank sixth in points per game in the NFL. Quarterback Jared Goff looks comfortable, and running back Jahmyr Gibbs is breaking records and ankles left and right.
Instead of hiring Nathaniel Hackett as offensive coordinator, Arizona could have kept Petzing as the offensive coordinator. Petzing does, after all, run the play-action outside-run scheme that Cardinals head coach Mike LaFleur runs.
While Gannon has done a great job with Green Bay's defense, it was the right move for Arizona to move on from him. The Cardinals were not a great team under Gannon. Some people are just better as coordinators than coaches, and that seems to be the case with Gannon.
Despite moving states and divisions, Harrison's inconsistencies persist. So far with the Texans, Harrison has caught four passes on eight targets. While the quarterbacks who threw Harrison Jr. the ball in Arizona weren't great, that is not the case for the Texans. Quarterback CJ Stroud has been playing at a high level this year. Overall, this was a great trade for the Cardinals' front office.
In Brisset’s lone game with the Ravens, he showed why Baltimore traded for him and why the Cardinals traded him away. He made some great tight-window throws, and Brissett helped the Ravens' passing offense look stable. However, Brissett still has inefficiencies, such as trouble extending the play, and he threw a poor interception. So, it made sense for Arizona to trade him away.
Most of the time, the Cardinals made the right choice in who to move on from. Despite Arizona's front office not making the right move all the time, this is a good sign. Knowing the timeline of players and coaches is a big part of the front office.

title: Cardinals Hit Rock Bottom With Stunning Chiefs Betting Spread
full_text:
ARIZONA — The Arizona Cardinals are currently 16.5-point underdogs to the Kansas City Chiefs ahead of Week 11.
That ties the Miami Dolphins (against the Buffalo Bills this week) for the largest betting spread of the 2026 season.
"Kansas City has jumped out as a 16.5-point favorite after this line first opened at -14 when they host the Cardinals," CBS Sports' Tyler Sullivan wrote .
"The Chiefs are coming off a dominant win over the Falcons, in which Patrick Mahomes threw five touchdowns. They head back to Arrowhead Stadium where they are 3-1 ATS and have an average margin of victory of 15.8 (second-best in the NFL). Arizona is 4-2 ATS on the road."
Kansas City is one of the hottest teams in the league at the moment, having out-scored opponents 70-25 within the last two weeks. Patrick Mahomes looks healthy after avoiding a major elbow injury while Andy Reid and co. typically handle business at Arrowhead.
The last time the Chiefs saw the Cardinals, Kansas City easily handled Arizona in 44-21 fashion to begin the 2022 season.
This will be Carson Beck's first road start of his career. The third-round rookie made his NFL debut last week and managed to play somewhat well despite several injuries impacting the offensive side of the ball.
Sledding won't get any easier against the Chiefs, who are allowing a third-best 17.3 points per game.
Reality has hit the 3-7 Cardinals hard over the last few weeks, which has prompted head coach Mike LaFleur to begin the evaluation process for the future over the remaining seven games on Arizona's schedule.
“I believe in the guys in that room. I love this locker room," LaFleur told reporters on Monday after their blowout loss to the Los Angeles Rams in Week 10.
"They want to do right, trust me. They want to do right and they play hard. That fourth quarter got a little out of whack. It wasn't an effort thing — guys were trying to do a little too much and that's when those things can happen. It ends up being leaky yards in 15 straight carries or whatever it was. These guys will step up, they will. We need to step up and not just continue to fight, but we have to go execute and we have to make some plays.”
The spread could certainly shift over the coming days, though the Cardinals will undoubtedly be eye-opening underdogs when action begins in Kansas City.

title: Cardinals' Injury Crisis Deepens With 2 More Players Sidelined
full_text:
ARIZONA — The Arizona Cardinals have struggled with health since the first day of training camp.
As we enter Week 11 of the regular season, the hits keep coming.
Cardinals head coach Mike LaFleur told reporters that outside linebacker Jordan Burch would be out for the rest of the season with an MCL injury while starting safety Andrew Wingard suffered a wrist injury and will miss extended time. Wingard won't be placed on injured reserve at this point in time.
"Not shocked at anything. Again, I'll just always go back to really it sucks for the player," LaFleur added in his Monday press conference.
"Yeah, it sucks for our club and and all those kind of things but injuries happen. It sucks for the player, and the list just continues to grow. But that's who I'm feeling for more. He [Wingard] hated missing a few games, whatever it was, three games, four games, and he wanted to be out there with his boys. He got back out there, and here we are.
"So we'll see how long it's going to be, but it's most likely not going to be the year or anything like that. But he'll be out for some time."
Prior to this week, the Cardinals had 15 players on some sort of injury designation list, spanning from PUP to IR. Health has simply not been on Arizona's side this season, as the Cardinals are now thin on both sides of the ball.
LaFleur, fresh off the Week 10 loss to the Los Angeles Rams where the Cardinals practically had a practice squad offense on the field, wasn't looking for excuses.
"We got what we've got right now," LaFleur told reporters after Sunday.
"It is what it is, and I told the guys there's no magic wand. There's no magic savior. We have seven more weeks of a massive evaluation to see how this roster's going to look. I put it on front street for the guys. It's shared accountability. It's collective. There's absolutely no doubt, but we can play better than that. We can make plays better than that. We can block better than that. We can stop the run better than that with what we have. There's no doubt in my mind and credit to them. They're a dang good football team. We know that. These next seven weeks are going to be awesome, starting with this week."
Arizona faces the Kansas City Chiefs in Week 11.

title: Atlanta Falcons Move On from Michael Penix Jr. in ESPN's Latest Mock Draft
full_text:
The Atlanta Falcons came into the season with their biggest question being at quarterback. Could Michael Penix Jr. or Tua Tagovailoa show enough this season to solidify himself as the quarterback of the future for this team?
We have a definitive answer on the Tagovailoa part of that question, but after 10 weeks of the 2026 season and a 3-7 record, the jury is still out on Penix. Maybe it shouldn't be all that surprising that a quarterback with 12 career starts, coming off a season-ending knee injury, would have ups and downs this season.
But three years is a lifetime in the NFL, and Penix is running out of time to lock down the Falcons starting quarterback job in 2027.
ESPN's Jordan Reid has already seen enough, and has the Falcons taking Notre Dame quarterback CJ Carr with the No. 8 overall pick, a spot in the draft order made popular by former head coach Arthur Smith.
Reid's reasoning for selecting Carr almost sounds like he's course-correcting for the Falcons and choosing the anti-Penix option.
"Carr is an instinctive passer who consistently has answers and has already been given considerable autonomy in Notre Dame's offense," Reid wrote on ESPN . "He doesn't have the high-end traits of some passers in the class (picture a more mobile Kirk Cousins), but he is polished in many of the skills that are essential to playing the position."
Reid may have hurt his case with Falcons fans by mentioning Cousins, but I've also heard Carr described as a more toolsy Brock Purdy. Purdy didn't have the traits to get drafted in the first round (or almost drafted at all), but he's loaded with all of the "skills essential to playing the position."
At 3-7 with the Minnesota Vikings and Detroit Lions on deck, the Falcons are facing 3-9 in the face and could end up with a higher selection than No. 8. Drew Mestemaker is the only quarterback Reid has taken higher than Carr, going to the Jets at No. 2 overall after a trade with the Chargers.
The Dolphins (No. 3), Eagles (No. 5), and Cardinals (No. 7) will also be threats to take a quarterback, and the Chargers (No. 4) could be a trade-down candidate for a team behind the Falcons looking for a quarterback.
If the Falcons stay put, but don't like the quarterback options available when they're on the clock, offensive tackle, wide receiver, and cornerback are glaring needs. Indiana wide receiver Charlie Becker goes No. 4 to the Chargers. Notre Dame cornerback Leonard Moore is selected by the Jets (ironically, with a pick they got from the Colts for Sauce Gardner) at No. 6. Offensive tackle Jordan Seaton of LSU is taken by the Cardinals at No. 7.
Utah offensive tackle Zereoue Williams is an intriguing prospect still on the board when the Falcons pick and goes to the Texans at No. 9.
General manager Ian Cunningham took the job in January when the Falcons were light on draft picks and low on available salary cap. That won't be a problem this offseason.
However, he's got a lot of holes to fill on a team that is headed towards its ninth consecutive losing season.

title: Falcons Have a ‘Streetball’ Solution to Their Offensive Struggles
full_text:
Jahan Dotson had a simple solution for the Atlanta Falcons (3-7) to overcome their recent offensive slump.
“We need to get an edge as an offense,” the wide receiver told reporters Monday. “And come out with a demeanor like we can’t be stopped and get things going.”
Atlanta has been mercurial with the football this season.
It’s experienced the highest of the highs with quarterback Michael Penix Jr. and the Bijan Robinson-led run game complementing each other. And it’s been at rock bottom, such as when the now-division rival Cooper Rush started the first two games while Penix recovered from a torn ACL.
But the offensive struggles continue despite Atlanta having a relatively healthy unit, with Brian Robinson Jr. among its notable absences .
“I told some of the guys it’s like streetball out there,” Robinson said last Sunday, Nov. 15, after the Falcons turned in a poor output in a 35-13 Week 10 loss to the Kansas City Chiefs .
“Free-flowing, you know your assignment, and just make it happen. That needs to be our mentality.”
Atlanta ranks 17th in total offense, 22nd in passing offense, and third in rushing offense, though not as explosive early in the season.
It also had a midseason surge, scoring a league-leading combined 80 points in Week 3 and Week 4 wins. In their active three-game losing streak, Atlanta averages 10 points.
As offensive coordinator Tommy Rees faces scrutiny over predictable play-calling, slow starts and low-scoring performances, the Falcons are searching for their own version of the NFL Street video game.
Head coach Kevin Stefanski reaffirmed Monday that Rees would retain play-calling duties. But if the offensive struggles persist, that decision could face renewed questions.
“Just trying to dominate,” Dotson said. “That’s really what you do in streetball – to get what we want to do on offense.”
For Atlanta, establishing an edge goes beyond simply playing with more aggression. It’s about developing habits that allow the offense to execute consistently, regardless of the opponent or situation.
The Falcons have proved they can put points on the scoreboard in bunches. The challenge is sustaining that production week to week, especially during a losing streak when scoring opportunities have become increasingly difficult to capitalize on.
Building the right mentality during the week and carrying those habits into games could help Atlanta recapture some of the offensive confidence from earlier in the season.
“It’s definitely a mentality; it’s habits,” Dotson said. “It’s what you do every day in practice. It doesn’t just happen on game day. If you’re going to say you want to be that, you’ve got to be about it every day.”

title: 3 Reasons Why Bijan Robinson Is Underused by Atlanta Falcons
full_text:
The Atlanta Falcons have come under heavy criticism for their use, or lack thereof, of All-Pro running back Bijan Robinson. Much was made of Sunday's anemic effort against the Kansas City Chiefs when the Falcons went three-and-out on their first possession without Robinson touching the ball.
There are several reasons contributing to the perceived misuse of their star player, but let's dig into three big ones.
Defenses have figured out that the way to stop the Falcons' offense is to stop  Robinson and put pressure on Michael Penix Jr. Unfortunately for the Falcons, this can be accomplished by the same method: stack the box and blitz the gaps.
On the Falcons' first play from scrimmage, the Chiefs had seven players on the line of scrimmage, and they had nine in the box. They sent six on a blitz. That's an awfully tough front to run against.
They sent six on the snap; Penix made the right read, throwing the ball to Drake London, whose cornerback came on a blitz, but he airmailed the throw. Now it's second and 10, and you're behind the sticks. The Chiefs blitzed on second down, and the Chiefs blitzed on third down.
Whether you blame offensive coordinator Tommy Rees, the offensive line, Penix, or some combination of all three, Penix's passing numbers against the blitz and against pressure are atrocious.
Of 34 quarterbacks who have faced at least 35 blitzes, Penix ranks 27th in EPA per play, according to Sumer Sports .  His EPA when pressured is 31st of 33 quarterbacks who have faced at least 50 pressures, and his 36.5% completion percentage is dead last.
Robinson leads the NFL in yards after contact, and that's not necessarily a stat I'd be bragging about as an offensive coordinator. The better metric? Yards before contact. Robinson is 12th in the NFL at 2.7 yards per rush, according to Pro Football Reference . It was 1.5 yards before contact against the Buccaneers.
If I'm a defensive coordinator, I know I can flood the Falcons' offensive backfield and stop Robinson, and Penix isn't going to beat me by throwing the ball. That makes playing defense awfully easy.
Robinson had nine touches in the first half. That's not an eye-popping low number of touches, but the Falcons only ran 24 plays, nine of them coming on the only drive on which they converted a first down. They had six drives, and five of them were three-and-out.
No one is getting a lot of touches when you have five three-and-outs and are 5-of-16 on third down in the game. The Falcons have fallen to 27th in the NFL in third-down conversions at 32.4%.
The inability to convert on third down and turn drives into points helps contribute to the team falling behind early. Call this reason 2b, but the Falcons have played more snaps down two scores than any team in the NFL.
Rate of offensive snaps trailing by double-digits... Falcons 35.9% Cardinals 33.5% Titans 31.9% Dolphins 31.6% Chargers 29.1% Steelers 27.5% Raiders 27.3% Patriots 26.9% Panthers 25.3% Browns 24.6% Cowboys 21.9% Commanders 21.9% Jets 19.9% Bucs 18.2% Packers 17.6% Giants 15.9%…
It's hard to establish a running game when you can't extend drives and you're behind in games.
How many people critical of Robinson's lack of use would be surprised to learn he has the second most touches (220) in the NFL behind Detroit Lions running back Jahmyr Gibbs (240)?
The Falcons haven't had a bye yet, but his touches per game are still No. 4 in the NFL at 22.0, trailing only James Cook of the Bills, Kenneth Walker III of the Lions, and Gibbs.
Robinson is getting the ball. Other than the blowout loss to the Bears, he has had at least 19 touches in every game this season.
Maybe. But I don't know that I want Bijan Robinson slamming his head into nine-man fronts, down two scores, on a 3-6 (now 3-7) team who were sellers at the trade deadline.
Until the Falcons figure out how to back defenders off the line of scrimmage, Robinson is going to continue to be limited in his effectiveness, or as some might call it: Misused.

title: Falcons DT Gervon Dexter: 'We’re Not Worried About What’s Going On Offense'
full_text:
The Atlanta Falcons ’ defensive struggles have become increasingly difficult to overcome as the team’s offense continues to search for consistency.
Atlanta suffered its fourth consecutive loss on Sunday, falling 35-13 to the Kansas City Chiefs and dropping to 3-7 on the season. While the defense managed to produce several important stops early in the game, the Falcons ultimately struggled to contain Patrick Mahomes, who finished with 348 passing yards and five touchdown passes.
Following the loss, Falcons defensive lineman Gervon Dexter discussed the importance of complementary football and explained why the defense cannot afford to focus on the struggles happening on the other side of the ball.
“I don’t think none of the guys on defense is worried about what’s going on offense,” Dexter said. “I think we’re more so focused on if we do have to go back out there, get another stop, taking the ball away, getting turnovers and putting points on the board ourselves.”
The numbers illustrate the challenges Atlanta faced against Kansas City. The Chiefs finished with 461 total yards of offense, compared to 370 for the Falcons. Kansas City also scored five touchdowns through the air, consistently finding ways to capitalize on opportunities.
Still, it was a 7-3 game with 3:49 left in the first half when the Falcons had 1st and 10 at their own 19. Three plays later, the Falcons punted, their fifth three-and-out on six possessions in the first half. Kansas City got a quick score before half and took control of the game 14-3.
Dexter acknowledged that Atlanta’s defense had opportunities to keep Kansas City from taking control but emphasized that containing a quarterback like Mahomes requires consistent execution throughout all four quarters.
“Obviously he’s a good quarterback, so you can’t just do it for 30 minutes. You got to do it for the whole game,” Dexter explained.
The defensive lineman pointed to keeping Mahomes off the field and forcing longer down-and-distance situations as areas where Atlanta could have performed better.
Kansas City converted four of its 13 third down attempts, while the Falcons’ defense recorded seven punts. However, the Chiefs were particularly effective when reaching scoring territory, converting all three of their red zone opportunities into touchdowns.
That challenge becomes even more difficult when an offense struggles to sustain drives.
Atlanta converted just five of 16 third-down opportunities and finished with nine penalties for 65 yards. The Falcons also committed two turnovers, including an interception and a lost fumble, further limiting their opportunities to establish offensive momentum.
Another Falcons defender, Cameron Thomas, echoed Dexter’s comments about maintaining accountability rather than pointing fingers at another unit.
“If the offense is going three-and-out, then we got to make them go three-and-out,” Thomas said. “It just comes down to everybody staying together, and let’s keep fighting.”
Thomas’ comments reflect the mentality coming from Atlanta’s locker room entering the bye week. Players understand that neither side of the football can consistently carry the team without receiving support from the other.
The Falcons have seven games remaining to turn their season around, but their margin for error continues to shrink.
With the bye week providing an opportunity to evaluate their performance, Atlanta must find a way to establish more consistency offensively while allowing its defense to play with the support it needs.
The defense cannot control what happens on the offensive side of the ball. However, as Dexter made clear, Atlanta’s defenders must continue to find ways to make plays regardless of the circumstances.
For the Falcons to have any chance of salvaging their season, complementary football must become more than just a talking point.

title: Falcons Have Nobody to Blame but Themselves for Disappointing Season
full_text:
FLOWERY BRANCH – The Atlanta Falcons are 3-7 at the bye, and their biggest problems are largely self-inflicted. Turnovers, penalties, and slow starts have repeatedly put this team in difficult positions, turning winnable games into double-digit losses.
Despite their record, the Falcons still have a chance to get back into the playoff race. They have to stop beating themselves first .
Unbelievably, the Falcons are still within striking distance in the NFC South. The division-leading Panthers have only a one-game advantage (and the tiebreaker), but recent results have done little to inspire confidence that this team has what it takes to get over the hump and reach the postseason for the first time since 2017.
They have lost three straight games by double digits, with all of them feeling out of reach by the fourth quarter. In each one, the Falcons have hurt themselves.
In the 16-point loss to the Buccaneers, Michael Penix Jr. threw four interceptions. In a 17-point loss to the Bengals, they committed 12 penalties. In a 22-point loss to the Chiefs, they had a historically slow start, entering the fourth quarter with 186 yards of offense, plus two turnovers and nine penalties by the final whistle.
“You watch the tape, and it's frustrating and disappointing, but ultimately, as a football team, we're going to own it, and then we're going to move on from this one,” head coach Kevin Stefanski said Monday about the most recent loss. “Learn some lessons, some hard lessons as they are, but then use this bye week to our advantage.”
Stefanski has taken responsibility for how his team has played. He has made several assurances that the mistakes will be corrected, but so far, the lessons haven't taken hold.
After those 12 infractions in Madrid that Stefanski called “inexcusable,” they hurt themselves with game-altering mistakes. They turned Chiefs field goals into touchdowns and ended their own possessions with false starts and holding penalties. Analyst JJ Watt openly called out right tackle Jawaan Taylor on the CBS broadcast.
A struggling Penix didn’t settle in until the game was out of reach (155 of his 286 passing yards came in the fourth quarter), and he kept struggling under pressure. He missed open receivers and was rushed, even when no one was in his face.
Since winning NFC Offensive Player of the Week in the win over the 49ers, the Falcons’ quarterback has completed only 51 of 98 passes for 573 yards, one touchdown, and six interceptions.
Penix's struggles have been compounded by the Falcons' inability to consistently lean on their most reliable offensive weapon: Bijan Robinson.
The running back carried the ball only seven times in the first half of Sunday’s loss to the Chiefs, and the Falcons already trailed by double digits by the time they started using him more.
The Falcons identified their rushing attack as a defining trait of their offensive identity, but their star back has had more than 20 carries just once during the last five games – and he hit that mark in their only win during that span.
Robinson took his role in stride.
“I do whatever I can for the team, no matter what the situation is,” the star running back said after the game. “I know that they have a plan, and I gotta follow that plan as best as possible. Yeah, I’ll just leave it from there.”
But the Falcons have kept their biggest weapon in the holster, and the results speak for themselves.
The playoffs are in sight, but there is not a lot of confidence that this team can get there – at least until they get out of their own way.
“You can’t win football games in this league without not beating yourself first, and we did that [Sunday against the Chiefs],” wide receiver Jahan Dotson said. “Penalties, pre- and post-snap, and just little things like not lining up correctly and just simple things that don’t take effort. That’s what it comes down to.
“We gotta look ourselves in the mirror and fix the internal things.”
Those mistakes have doomed them, and their upcoming slate of games could, too. Following this week off, the Falcons will face three straight opponents with six or more wins, including the team that fired Stefanski in January.
“We can make this run because the division is still wide open,” cornerback A.J. Terrell said. “We still control our destiny and things like that.”
The odds are certainly stacked against them. According to Statehead, only two teams in history have made the playoffs after starting 3-7, and the Falcons have the added benefit of playing in a winnable division. This team will need to start winning games for any of that to matter.
The next several weeks will be difficult, but the Falcons still see a chance to save the season .
“I think the way our team is wired, and the way we were brought on this year – it's not pretty, but we're gonna keep fighting,” guard Matthew Bergeron said. “You just gotta turn that frustration into motivation. And listen, we have a week to fix the bumps and bruises and get back to work.”
The Falcons still have an opportunity to save their season, but the margin for error has all but disappeared. The bye week gives them time to address their mistakes. Now they have to prove they can actually correct them.

title: J.J. Watt Exposes Embarrassing Falcons Problem During Chiefs Loss
full_text:
The Atlanta Falcons may have been giving away more information than they realized before the snap, and NFL legend J.J. Watt made sure everyone watching Sunday’s game against the Kansas City Chiefs knew about it.
During CBS’ broadcast of Atlanta’s 35-13 loss to Kansas City, Watt identified a potential pre-snap tell involving Falcons offensive tackle Jawaan Taylor that could allow opposing defenses to anticipate whether the offense is preparing to run or pass.
Watt broke down Taylor’s positioning, using several graphics to show how his foot placement changes when lining up in a three-point stance. He also highlighted differences in Taylor’s hand placement when operating out of a two-point stance.
Look closely... 👀 @JJWatt accurately predicts a pass vs. a run based on Falcons OT Jawaan Taylor's stance. CBS | Paramount+ pic.twitter.com/naMymtucuX
The former NFL defensive star explained that Taylor’s positioning could provide defensive linemen with valuable information before the ball is even snapped.
“As a defensive lineman, you watch every single guy. This isn’t something that anybody in the league doesn’t already know,” Watt explained during the broadcast.
Watt also pointed out that this was exactly the type of information the Chiefs would be studying throughout the week.
“This is the type of stuff the Chiefs are studying this week,” Watt said.
There was another reason why Kansas City could have been particularly familiar with Taylor’s tendencies. The offensive tackle spent the previous three seasons with the Chiefs before joining Atlanta in free agency.
CBS even showed an example of Michael Penix Jr. changing a play at the line of scrimmage, apparently switching from a pass to a run. Taylor immediately adjusted his hand placement, giving Watt another opportunity to demonstrate the potential tell.
Watt also identified a specific foot positioning that indicated a pass was coming.
“You’ll see, when he’s in that deep stagger, that’s when it’s gonna be a pass,” Watt explained.
The concerning part for Atlanta is that this wasn't identified internally, or at least fixed internally.  NFL defensive coordinators and defensive linemen spend countless hours studying film, making it reasonable to question whether opposing teams had already recognized similar patterns before being exposed by Watt.
Following Sunday’s loss, Falcons head coach Kevin Stefanski was asked about Watt’s observations and whether Atlanta was aware of Taylor potentially tipping plays.
“Every team has tendencies; we’re aware of ours,” Stefanski said.
That response suggests the coaching staff understands that opposing defenses are constantly searching for small advantages when studying Atlanta’s offense.
However, the Falcons will need to make sure those tendencies are not giving opponents an unnecessary advantage.
Taylor also had a difficult afternoon against his former team, committing two false-start penalties as Atlanta struggled to establish consistency offensively.
The Falcons managed just three points and 186 total yards through the first three quarters before Kansas City eventually pulled away.
Atlanta is now 3-7 after suffering another disappointing defeat , with plenty of questions surrounding the team’s offensive execution.
Taylor’s stance might seem like a relatively minor detail, but at the NFL level, small advantages can make a significant difference. If opposing defenses can consistently identify whether Atlanta is running or passing before the snap, it becomes considerably more difficult for the offense to find success.
The Falcons now have their bye week to evaluate what went wrong and make necessary adjustments before returning to action against the Minnesota Vikings on November 29.
If Watt can identify Atlanta’s tendencies from the broadcast booth, the Falcons need to make sure opposing defenses cannot continue to take advantage of them.

title: Are Falcons Checking Out? Three-Game Skid Puts Atlanta at a Crossroads
full_text:
The Atlanta Falcons’ losing streak has reached three .
And from what’s been on display, there’s not much reason to believe they’re capable of a turnaround.
As the season spirals, running back Bijan Robinson posed a question after Sunday’s 35-13 home loss to the Kansas City Chiefs : “Is this how we want to go about the rest of the season with this product, or are we going to change? Are we going to strain for each other, go out there and play for each other no matter the situation?”
The Falcons (3-7) may verbally answer with what sounds good to the ear of fans, who showered them with boo birds in Mercedes-Benz Stadium on Sunday.
But the on-field play tells another story.
Especially with a cloud hanging over the franchise’s future as tanking talks get louder after the Falcons became trade deadline sellers in exchange for draft picks last week.
“I don’t think you have to worry about the fight of this football team,” head coach Kevin Stefanski told reporters in Sunday’s postgame press conference when asked how to keep his team from checking out.
“Our guys understand what’s in front of us.”
Atlanta moved its star free safety and team captain Jessie Bates III to the Jacksonville Jaguars and starting center Ryan Neuzil to the Baltimore Ravens .
Entering the week, Tankathon has Atlanta slated for the No. 8 overall pick in the 2027 NFL Draft.
The pick may hold up or even rise with Minnesota and Detroit as the next two games. More than half of the season is gone, and Atlanta is looking like one of the worst teams in the NFL through Week 10.
“Nobody feels bad or cares about how the Atlanta Falcons feel except for us. And we can make a change to the narrative,” said Falcons cornerback A.J. Terrell Jr. “We still got the season in front of us, and we can either take advantage of that or plummet.”
Through the struggles, Atlanta has a saving grace: NFC South bedlam.
The Falcons are currently in the division’s fourth and final spot, with the Carolina Panthers leading the way with a 4-5 record.
Again, welcome to the NFC South, where you can compete for the division crown and a draft pick simultaneously.
“You’re always going to have a chance as long as there are games left on the schedule in the NFC South,” said Corey Levin, the newly appointed starting center for the Falcons .
American football will get a break from the uninspiring product the Falcons have put on the field in recent weeks. They’re on a bye for Week 11.
Then the gauntlet continues at the Minnesota Vikings and former Falcons quarterback Kirk Cousins on Nov. 29, kicking off Atlanta’s final seven regular season games.
“The biggest thing for us is to stay together,” Robinson said. “I think the teams that start to lose a lot later in the season are the teams that drift apart and go amongst themselves.”
Can the Falcons reverse course in the next month and a half and ultimately land a playoff spot?
But Stefanski’s and the players’ optimism has yet to translate into results, leaving the Falcons with seven games to prove their words carry weight.

title: Falcons Winners and Losers: Atlanta's Offense Disappears in Loss to Chiefs
full_text:
The Atlanta Falcons suffered another frustrating loss, falling 35-13 to the Kansas City Chiefs on Sunday. The offense struggled to find any consistency; the passing game never developed a rhythm, and the defense gave Patrick Mahomes too many opportunities to make explosive plays.
There were a few individual bright spots, particularly among Atlanta's young defensive players, but this was another performance that gave a clear indication the team was thinking more about the 2027 NFL Draft than they are about winning the NFC South.
Here are the winners and losers from Sunday's loss.
Hellams deserves credit for stepping into a much larger role following the trade of Jessie Bates . Replacing a veteran safety and team leader is not an easy assignment, but Hellams showed he was capable of handling the opportunity.
He finished with 10 total tackles, including six solo tackles and four assists, leading the way in the secondary. He was active around the football and helped make several stops against the Chiefs.
There will naturally be growing pains with Bates no longer in Atlanta, but Hellams provided some encouraging signs in his expanded role.
A bright spot for Atlanta's future
The rookie linebacker duo continued to show why Falcons fans should be excited about their development.
Perkins finished with five tackles, including four solo tackles and one assist. Daniels contributed seven tackles, with two solo tackles and five assists.
Both players were flying around the football and showed good energy throughout the afternoon.
With Divine Deablo missing another week, this was valuable experience for two young linebackers who could have significant roles moving forward. Their development is one of the few positives Atlanta can take away from this game.
Moody provided some stability after recently taking over for Nick Folk .
He finished the afternoon perfect on all three kicking attempts, converting two field goals from 28 and 38 yards and making his lone extra point.
He accounted for seven of Atlanta's 13 points and didn't leave any points on the field.
Moody also executed a picture-perfect onside kick; the first successful onside kick this season.
you won’t see an onside kick prettier than this. pic.twitter.com/1oSTxR1Hq0
While the Falcons have much bigger problems to address, Moody did exactly what was expected of him. After making a midseason change at kicker, getting a reliable performance is encouraging.
There are legitimate questions about Tommy Rees' offensive approach following Sunday's performance.
Atlanta struggled to establish any consistency, and the play sequencing was questionable at times. One of the biggest concerns continues to be the lack of involvement for Bijan Robinson.
Robinson finished with 71 rushing yards on 16 carries and added six receiving yards on four catches. He averaged 4.4 yards per carry, yet Atlanta struggled to consistently build its offense around him.
Another concerning trend is the Falcons' approach on third down.
There seems to be a lack of trust in the traditional dropback passing game, particularly when Atlanta knows opposing defenses are going to bring pressure. The Chiefs were able to create problems with their blitz packages, and the Falcons didn't consistently have answers.
Rees needs to find ways to get the football out quicker, create easier opportunities for Penix and put his playmakers in better positions.
The talent is there. The offensive execution and playcalling need to improve.
This was a particularly rough afternoon for the veteran left tackle.
Matthews was flagged three times, although the official play by play identifies two holding penalties and one false start. Those mistakes repeatedly put Atlanta behind the chains.
The holding penalties were particularly damaging because they erased positive plays and forced the offense into difficult situations.
For a veteran who has been one of Atlanta's most dependable offensive linemen for years, this was a performance he'd like to forget.
Another frustrating afternoon
Penix finished with 23 completions on 43 attempts for 286 yards, with the majority of those yards in garbage time, zero touchdowns, and an interception. He also rushed four times for 29 yards.
Atlanta finished with 370 yards, but most of them came once the game was well out of reach. They converted only five of 16 third downs. Their first four drives were three-and-outs.
Penix never seemed to find a consistent rhythm. There were flashes, including some productive connections with Drake London and Jahan Dotson, but they weren't enough to sustain drives.
He doesn't deserve all the blame. The offensive line, playcalling and overall offensive execution all contributed to the struggles.
However, Atlanta needs more from its quarterback if it wants to compete consistently.
The continued lack of involvement for Pitts is becoming increasingly difficult to understand.
He finished Sunday's game with four catches for 50 yards on four targets, without a touchdown. He had two catches for nine yards in the first half, and his third catch came with the Falcons down 35-13, and he promptly fumbled.
Those numbers are particularly disappointing considering how much the coaching staff has emphasized getting him involved in the offense.
Offensive coordinator Tommy Rees has previously acknowledged that the Falcons are better when Pitts is involved. However, that philosophy hasn't translated into consistent production this season.
Pitts has the athletic ability to create mismatches against linebackers and safeties. Yet Atlanta continues to struggle to make him a meaningful part of the passing attack.
At some point, the coaching staff has to figure out how to get one of its most talented offensive weapons involved.
This deserves its own category because the Falcons' secondary had a difficult afternoon against Patrick Mahomes.
Mahomes finished with 22 completions on 35 attempts for 348 yards, five touchdowns and zero interceptions, posting a 135.5 passer rating.
Kansas City consistently found opportunities downfield, finishing with 453 total yards and five passing touchdowns.
Terrell recorded five tackles, while Henderson finished with two. However, the tackle totals don't tell the entire story.
There were multiple explosive plays that exposed Atlanta's coverage, including a 50-yard completion to Rashee Rice with Henderson involved in the coverage and a 39-yard touchdown to Cyrus Allen.
The Chiefs also connected on a 43-yard touchdown to Ashton Armstrong late in the fourth quarter.
For Terrell, who is the 11th highest-paid cornerback in the NFL, these are the types of performances that raise questions about the return on investment.
For Henderson, the timing is notable. He recently received a significant two-year contract extension after stepping into a starting role and showing improvement. Atlanta needs that version of Henderson consistently, not performances where opposing quarterbacks can repeatedly attack the secondary.
Losing Jessie Bates certainly doesn't make things easier, but the remaining defensive backs have to do a better job limiting explosive plays.
Mahomes was far too comfortable against this defense, and the coverage issues were a major reason why Kansas City was able to pull away.
There weren't many positives from Sunday's loss. Hellams, Perkins, and Daniels showed encouraging signs, and Moody delivered a perfect performance. However, the offensive struggles, questionable playcalling, and secondary issues continue to raise serious concerns about where this Falcons team is headed.
The Falcons have the week off before they face Kirk Cousins and the Minnesota Vikings (7-2) on Sunday, November 29th in Minnesota.

title: 5 Brutal Takeaways From Atlanta Falcons Loss to Kansas City Chiefs
full_text:
ATLANTA – The Atlanta Falcons lost their third straight game, and the fifth of their last six, on Sunday. They fell to the Chiefs 35-13, marking the third double-digit loss.
The Falcons had a start to forget on offense, surrendering four consecutive three-and-outs to begin the game, marking their worst start in 26 years. Michael Penix Jr. faced pressure on several dropbacks and had a few misfires that put the Falcons behind the chains early. The offense faced third-down distances of 10, 10, 17, and 4 yards.
But the biggest issue was that Bijan Robinson only touched the ball three times over those four possessions. Unsurprisingly, the star running back snapped the drought on the fifth drive with a 17-yard rush that set up the Falcons’ first points of the game.
The Falcons seemed to find some rhythm on that possession, but they quickly went back to another three-and-out, their fifth of the first half. Robinson finished the half with only eight touches and fewer than 20 carries for the fifth time in the last six games (all ended in a loss).
The second half didn’t go much differently, and the Falcons’ drives ended in a punt, turnover on downs, punt, and punt before finally finding the end zone down 28-3 with 8:15 left.
Penix never got comfortable, and he and offensive coordinator Tommy Rees are struggling to find success. Since his outstanding performance against the 49ers, the offense has averaged a dreadful 10.0 points per game.
Fans voiced their displeasure with the team, showering the offense with boos.
"They put in their hard-earned work every single week to try to make it to these games, and it's our job to make it count for them," running back Bijan Robinson said of the fans. "So yeah, when they boo us, we deserve it."
Atlanta was 5-of-16 on third down and only scored one touchdown on five red zone trips.
With the Falcons’ offense struggling to find any semblance of rhythm, the defense was forced into some unfortunate possessions. They started slowly, too, allowing an easy touchdown drive to begin the game, but locked the Chiefs up for much of the game.
The defense just didn’t get any help, and eventually Patrick Mahomes broke through again. After that opening drive score, both of his subsequent touchdown throws came after shortcomings from another unit: the first on an offside negated a field goal and the second after a failed fourth-down conversion at midfield.
Mahomes’ fourth touchdown came in the fourth quarter, with the game firmly in hand and the Falcons’ defense reeling. The fifth came on a scramble drill.
The Falcons held the Chiefs' rushing attack (without Kenneth Walker III) to 122 yards, but Mahomes would finish with 348 yards and five touchdowns – the first time he hit that scoring mark since 2022.
The rookie linebacker was making plays all over the field on Sunday. He finished with five tackles and a tackle for loss, but he was effective in both coverage and as a pass rusher. Perkins delivered big hits and was constantly finding himself around the football.
He has taken full advantage of Divine Deablo’s absence and is pushing for the staff to find ways to keep him on the field once the veteran is back healthy.
Michael Penix Jr. continued to struggle when the defense applied pressure. He was sacked three times and kept accelerating his progressions to check down and avoid getting hit. Even without a blitz, the Chiefs sent simulated pressure that still got Penix off his spot and sped him up. He struggled for most of the game, completing 23-of-43 passes for 286 yards (most of which came with the game out of reach) and an interception.
Until he can find his way under pressure, the Falcons’ offense will keep struggling.
A week after 12 penalties crushed the Falcons in Madrid, some ill-timed infractions came back to bite them in Atlanta. They committed nine penalties for 65 yards, but seven came on offense, and both defensive penalties extended drives that ended in touchdowns.
The worst of which was an offsides penalty that turned a field goal try into a touchdown at the end of the first half. Kansas City took a 14-3 lead into the locker room instead of 10-3, and received the ball to start the second half.
Jawaan Taylor and Jake Matthews were both flagged several times for false starts or holds that snuffed out offensive possessions.
"When you're playing good football teams, you have to be at your best," Kevin Stefanski said. "And we were not at our best."
But beyond the penalties, the Falcons turned the ball over twice in the fourth quarter. For the second week in a row, the Falcons could not get out of their own way.
Corey Levin took over for Ryan Neuzil at center and had one bad snap exchange that ended in a fumble (Penix jumped on it), but it snuffed out a potential touchdown opportunity. The offensive line did not have its best day, allowing three sacks and rushing for 100 yards.
New kicker Jake Moody connected on both field-goal attempts from 28 and 38 yards, but he nailed an onside kick in the fourth quarter to give the Falcons new life. He put the football right in the outstretched arms of Chris Blair, who toe-tapped on the sideline to steal a possession. That play capped a strong afternoon for the Falcons’ special teams.
Tommy Rees also made his first appearance on the sideline instead of in the booth this season. He was seen sitting with Penix during defensive possessions, but the offensive issues persisted, and his unit finished with five three-and-outs.
DeMarcco Hellams stepped in for recently traded Jessie Bates III at safety and was a big winner in this game. His first start since 2023 was outstanding, and he finished with a game-high 11 tackles.
The Falcons lost the fifth of their last six games heading into their bye week, and the schedule gets no easier after next Sunday. Atlanta will face the Vikings, Lions, and Browns before it finally eases up a bit, with winnable games against the Commanders and NFC South opponents to end the season.
At 3-7, any hope of their first winning season since 2017 feels bleak, but they are still alive in the woeful NFC South. They trail the first-place Panthers by one win, don’t hold the tiebreaker, but are still unbelievably alive in that race.
Both the players and Stefanski were confident after the game that they won't lose the locker room amid this skid, but the bye week will be a welcome sight for this team.
Garrett Chapman is a sports broadcaster, writer, and content creator based in Atlanta. He has several years of experience covering the Atlanta sports scene, college football, Georgia high school football, recruiting for 24/7 Sports, and the NFL. You can also hear him on Sports Radio 92.9 The Game.

title: FalconsSI Staff Unanimous in Falcons vs. Chiefs Predictions
full_text:
The Atlanta Falcons are looking to get back on track in Week 10, but they face a difficult challenge with Patrick Mahomes and the Kansas City Chiefs coming to Mercedes-Benz Stadium.
Atlanta has lost four of its last five games and is coming off a disappointing performance against the Cincinnati Bengals in Madrid. Now, the Falcons will have to find a way to slow down another talented quarterback while dealing with significant changes to their own roster.
Kansas City will enter the matchup without running back Kenneth Walker III , which could make things more manageable for Atlanta’s struggling defense. However, Mahomes and Travis Kelce remain major threats, and the Chiefs have plenty of weapons to exploit the Falcons’ defensive weaknesses and deficiencies.
How will the game play out? The FalconsSI staff delivers its weekly predictions.
The Falcons have had some frustrating games this year, suffering through two weeks of Cooper Rush and a monsoon in Tampa, for example. But last week in Madrid was different. The Cincinnati Bengals simply showed the Falcons aren't good enough this year.
Their defense has been patched together with duct tape and one-year contracts, and it simply couldn't hold up against Joe Burrow, Ja'Marr Chase, and Tee Higgins. General manager Ian Cunningham saw the same thing we did, and rather than deluding himself into thinking 3-6 in a weak NFC South was good enough, he sold at the trade deadline.
Now Patrick Mahomes and Travis Kelce come to Mercedes-Benz Stadium, and the Falcons are without All-Pro safety Jessie Bates III after trading him to the Jaguars. Mahomes and the Chiefs aren't as explosive as the Bengals, but, well, they're still Mahomes and the Chiefs... and they're better on defense.
We'll see if Michael Penix Jr. and the offense can play well enough to take another step towards feeling good about Penix in 2027, but the Falcons are staring 3-7 in the face.
Prediction: Chiefs 31, Falcons 17
The notion of the Falcons playing up to the competition is fading away.
Plus, there’s a belief that Atlanta is now playing for draft positioning instead of ending its playoff drought.
The Chiefs present too many issues for the Falcons. We all know what Patrick Mahomes can do in the passing attack. And we all watched the Atlanta secondary struggle with Bengals playmakers in Madrid. With Kenneth Walker III out, that may soften the blow against the Falcons’ dwindling run defense .
Offensively, Atlanta is looking pretty “eh.” Michael Penix Jr. has gotten off of his heater and must prove himself as the franchise quarterback against one of the top pass defenses in the league. Additionally, Kansas City is top-10 at stopping the run and will likely stack boxes to stonewall Bijan Robinson as the Falcons deal with the key loss of powerback Brian Robinson Jr.
Atlanta is looking at a third consecutive loss on the road to the 2027 NFL Draft.
Prediction: Chiefs 34, Falcons 21
The Falcons have lost four of their last five, and the road to snapping that skid will run through the Kansas City Chiefs. The perennial contenders will be without Kenneth Walker, but Patrick Mahomes and Travis Kelce are still willing and able to run wild on a reeling Falcons defense that just moved Jessie Bates.
On offense, Corey Levin will be taking over at center , and he'll have a pretty difficult challenge opposite him.
This should be a tight game, but I'm not sure the Falcons can overcome this team opposite them right now.
Prediction: Chiefs 20, Falcons 17
Expects a closer game with Walker sidelined, but Mahomes will ultimately make the difference.
Atlanta’s defense has continued to struggle, and the departure of Bates doesn’t provide much confidence that things will improve against Kansas City’s passing attack.
The Falcons also face questions offensively with a new starting center stepping into the lineup midway through the season. That transition could create additional problems against a talented Chiefs defense.
Atlanta remains competitive, but Kansas City will pull away late to secure the victory.
Prediction: Chiefs 23, Falcons 16
Despite being only a half game back from first place in the division, it really seems like the clock is ticking on the Falcons’ season. The performances in recent weeks and the trades the Falcons made at the deadline make this game feel like a “crap or get off the pot” moment for this team.
There is hope, though. The Chiefs are good, but the Falcons have beaten better teams this year (which sounds crazy given they’ve only won three games). The blueprint for beating the Chiefs is pretty straightforward: stop the run.
The issue is, the Falcons have struggled to do that, especially against inside runs, and the Chiefs are an inside-running team. If they can pull it off, the Falcons’ pass defense matches up well against the Chiefs’ passing offense on paper (even without Jessie Bates).
On the other side of the ball, the Chiefs’ defense has been solid, but I think they have a real weakness in the secondary with the injury to their rookie Mansoor Delane. To exploit it, though, the Falcons will need to get the run game going. Their passing offense has been pretty ineffective when the ground game stalls.
This is a game the Falcons can win... but whether they will is a different story.
Prediction: Chiefs 24, Falcons 16
Despite differences in the projected final scores, all five contributors are picking Kansas City to win in Week 10.
The absence of Kenneth Walker could give Atlanta an opportunity to make this a more competitive matchup, but Mahomes remains the biggest difference-maker heading into Sunday.
For the Falcons, the challenge will be finding a way to slow down Kansas City’s passing attack while getting enough production from Penix and the offense.
Atlanta needs a win to stop its recent slide, but the consensus among our staff is that the Chiefs will leave Mercedes-Benz Stadium with another victory.
Kickoff is set for 1:00 p.m. EST at Mercedes-Benz Stadium and will be shown on CBS.
