title: Bills' GTA Rewind: What was Buffalo's Record for Every GTA Release?
full_text:
For the first time in 13 years, video gamers worldwide will have a new "Grand Theft Auto" title to play when "Grand Theft Auto VI" drops on Nov. 19.
While all of this is going on, the Buffalo Bills are in the midst of an impressive season , which has no doubt been a rarity for almost every GTA release.
With the most anticipated video game release in history set to take place, we're looking back at how the Bills were doing when each GTA dropped since 1997, and how they finished those seasons.
Release date: Nov. 28, 1997 Bills' record at release: 5-7 Bills' final record: 6-10
After their four failed Super Bowl trips, the Bills missed the playoffs in two of the next six seasons, with 1997 being one of those years.
That was also the first season of the post-Jim Kelly era , as the legendary Bills quarterback retired in January of that year, and Marv Levy called it a career after the 1997 campaign was over.
Buffalo started the season with a 4-3 mark and had a 5-7 record when the first GTA released, but the Bills went on to lose three of their last four games after that.
Todd Collins and Alex Van Pelt started games under center for the Bills, and Billy Joe Hobert got into two games, also. Talk about a significant drop-off at quarterback.
Release date: Oct. 22, 1999 Bills' record at release: 4-2 Bills' final record: 11-5
The Bills ripped off seven wins in 11 games after GTA 2 came out and managed to make the postseason before losing to the Tennessee Titans via the Music City Miracle.
This would be the Bills' last trip to the postseason for a long, long time, as Buffalo didn't make it to the playoffs again until 2017. This was also Bruce Smith's last season in Buffalo before finishing his career in Washington.
Release date: Oct. 22, 2001 Bills' record on release: 1-3 Bills' final record: 3-13
Over the course of the 17-year playoff drought, this was the worst record the Bills put up. Buffalo posted just one win over its first 11 games before winning two of the last five.
Bills fans had to withstand half a season apiece of Alex Van Pelt and Rob Johnson under center. Talk about a season to forget.
Release date: Oct. 29, 2002 Bills' record on release: 5-3 Bills' final record: 8-8
The Bills looked to be heading to the playoffs with a 5-3 mark before Vice City dropped, but it was all downhill from there.
Buffalo went just 3-5 over the final eight contests despite big years from its offensive stars, including Drew Bledsoe, Travis Henry, Peerless Price and Eric Moulds.
The biggest problem for Buffalo? A defense that ranked 27th in points allowed and 29th in rushing yards permitted.
Release date: Oct. 26, 2004 Bills' record on release: 1-5 Bills' final record: 9-7
The release of San Andreas was actually a good omen for the Bills, who managed to rip off eight wins in their last 10 games before just falling short of the playoffs.
If only the newest GTA that year had dropped earlier, the Bills might have made the postseason and ended their drought. The 9-7 mark was tied for the best record Buffalo posted during its dreadful streak.
Release date: April 29, 2008 Bills' record on release: 0-0 Bills' final record: 7-9
This marked the first and only year that a mainline GTA game didn't come out during the NFL season, so the Bills hadn't gotten started yet.
But, as is the case with the seasons before this one, there was nothing to get excited about, as the Bills went just 7-9.
Marshawn Lynch and Lee Evans both topped 1,000 yards, but the quarterback play was not good, with Trent Edwards starting 14 games and J.P. Losman starting in the other two.
Release date: Sept. 17, 2013 Bills' record on release: 1-1 Bills' final record: 6-10
The first season of EJ Manuel did not go well, as the Bills finished with a 6-10 mark to extend their streak of years without a postseason berth.
Buffalo saw C.J. Spiller and Fred Jackson combine for over 1,800 yards on the ground, but that wasn't enough to overcome a struggling passing attack and OK but not great defense.
Release date: Nov. 19, 2026 Bills' record on release: 8-1 Bills' final record: TBD
It has been a whole 13 years since the release of the last GTA game and a lot has changed in Buffalo since then.
The Bills not only broke their playoff drought in 2017, but they've also been in the postseason every year since 2019, which was the second year of the Josh Allen era.
In 2026, the Bills once again look like true Super Bowl contenders with their 8-1 mark that has them sitting in the No. 1 seed in the AFC.
Since 2020, four teams have taken the No. 1 seed with 14 wins, so if they Bills can win six of their last eight games , they should secure it.
And it's not crazy to think they can do that with four divisional matchups left on the schedule.

title: Charting Buffalo Bills' Path to No. 1 Seed in AFC Playoff Race
full_text:
Sitting at 8-1 through nine games, the Buffalo Bills are tied for the best record in the NFL and own the best mark in the AFC, which means they are currently sitting in the No. 1 seed .
Of course, the No. 1 seed would be huge for Buffalo, as not only will they get a first-round bye, but home-field advantage throughout the playoffs.
But there is plenty of competition for Buffalo, so nothing is close to set in stone yet. Behind the Bills are four 7-2 teams, including the Kansas City Chiefs, Jacksonville Jaguars, Denver Broncos and Cincinnati Bengals.
One thing the Bills have working in their favor is they have one of the easiest slates in the NFL, with Buffalo's strength of its rest-of-season schedule being the ninth-easiest, per Tankathon . Only Denver and the Jags have easier slates of the 7-2 AFC teams.
Here's a look at the Bills' remaining schedule and what they need to do over the last eight games to secure the No. 1 seed.
The Bills' remaining schedule is as follows:
Week 11: vs. Miami Dolphins Week 12: vs. Kansas City Chiefs Week 13: at New England Patriots Week 14: at Green Bay Packers Week 15: vs. Chicago Bears Week 16: at Denver Broncos Week 17: at Miami Dolphins Week 18: vs. New York Jets
Five of the Bills' remaining eight games are against teams with a record of .500 or better, although we know the Patriots have been significantly downgraded because of the injury to Drake Maye , so they might be closer to the Dolphins and Jets at this point than they are their fellow .500-or-better teams.
But Kansas City, Green Bay, Chicago and Denver are four of the better teams in the NFL, so the road to the No. 1 seed won't be easy. Here's how the Bills can get there.
Since 2020, the No. 1 seed in the AFC has won 14 or more games four times, so we'll peg that as the number of wins Buffalo will need. Knowing that, Buffalo needs six more wins.
The best way to get four of those wins is the four divisional games the Bills have left against the Dolphins (two), Jets and Patriots. All four of those contests are games the Bills should win considering the current states of those teams.
The Jets were fairly competitive earlier in the season, but they are getting worse and worse by the week.
Miami has been a lot more competitive than we expected them to be this season, but the Dolphins are still lacking talent in a lot of areas and they are missing Malik Willis for at least three more games due to injury .
The Patriots have accounted for the Bills' only loss this season but may have lost Maye for this season with his ankle injury. Even if he does make it back, it won't be by the time Buffalo sees the Pats in Week 13, so that's a huge lift for the Bills.
With everything we know, the Bills should be able to go a perfect 4-0 in the division the rest of the way, which means they need two more wins to hit that targeted number of 14.
There are no gimmes in the games against the Chiefs, Packers, Bears and Broncos. All four are very formidable foes and will challenge the Bills to the fullest extent possible.
But the Bills don't need a clean sweep of those games, or to even go above .500. A simple 2-2 mark against those squads is a very realistic outcome and would get the Bills to 14-3.
If the Bills can accomplish that task, along with sweeping the rest of their divisional games, Buffalo should get the bye and home-field advantage throughout the playoffs.

title: Tre'Davious White's Inevitable Return to Bills' Lineup May Be Closer Than You Think
full_text:
Tre Day is on the horizon this holiday season.
Although the actual date is not yet known, the Buffalo Bills appear close to deploying veteran cornerback Tre'Davious White for game action.
"I think he's really close to being able to help us. We had some injuries here this last game, if need be, I think he's ready to step up and play for us," said Bills' defensive coordinator Jim Leonhard on Monday following the Week 10 win over the New York Jets.
White, a 2017 first-round draft pick who has been with the Bills for nine of his 10 seasons, last appeared during the team's divisional round road loss to the Denver Broncos last January.
Garnering limited interest on the free-agent market, the 31-year-old White eventually took the opportunity to return to Orchard Park for one more crack at winning a Lombardi. He officially signed on October 19 as the Bills embarked on their Week 7 bye.
Although seemingly content with starting off as a practice squad player, one has to think White didn't come off the couch to sit back and watch others play the position he has mastered.
White's first practice was on October 28 as the Bills began preparations for a November 1 home game against the Baltimore Ravens.
Having not had the benefit of a training camp, the grizzled veteran recognizes he may need a little extra practice time to ramp up.
"This was a different kind of offseason for me. I've been sitting on the couch, drinking ginger ale and eating popcorn for a while," said White while appearing on Eric Wood's Centered On Buffalo podcastlast month. "I got so much respect for the position, I'd disrespect the position just thinking I can just come off the couch and come out there and be Tre White."
A reasonable four-week ramp up puts a potential debut around the November 26 game against the Kansas City Chiefs on Thanksgiving night.
“Anytime you kind of onboard some veteran players as the season goes on, that's part of the process is how many plays do you think you could play right now? I like where he's at," said Leonhard.
Physically speaking, White appeared to have enough tread left on his tires when he unexpectedly made 16 regular season starts for the Bills in 2025 as first-round draft pick Max Hairston began his rookie year on Injured Reserve.
"I thought he played really good football at the end of last season," said head coach Joe Brady on Wednesday. "Genetically, he's kind of a freak. A guy that can kinda roll out of bed, and maybe not do it as much for a long time, and still look like a guy that was a first-round pick for a reason."
Furthermore, White, who built a reputation for being a true student of the game early on in his Bills' tenure, has reached an experience level that makes Buffalo comfortable with deploying him when needed .
"I got the confidence that whenever that time does come, and Tre White has to be up, there's gonna be no holding the breath, because I know he's so calm, cool collected, he's ready to go," said Brady.
With Buffalo somewhat banged up in the defensive secondary following the November 15 road win, the time may come as early as this Sunday against the Miami Dolphins.
Starting boundary cornerback Christian Benford and slot cornerback Dee Alford both left the Week 10 road game due to injuries and never returned.
Benford is dealing with a groin injury , which is usually more than a day-to-day issue. Alford was ruled out against the Jets after being evaluated for a concussion .
After second-round rookie starter Davison Igbinosun and the aforementioned Hairston, the Bills have no other true outside cornerbacks on their 53-man roster. Meanwhile, nickel cornerback Jordan Hancock is the next man up behind Alford.
Simply put, Buffalo will most likely need at least one more cornerback on the Week 11 game day roster, and an obvious option in the elevate White.

title: New Bills 2027 Mock Draft Upgrades Buffalo's Offensive Line
full_text:
Buffalo Bills ' general manager Brandon Beane deserves credit for the work he's done this year. While he did completely whiff on CJ Gardner-Johnson, he made up for that by adding Amani Hooker at the NFL trade deadline.
This was after adding DJ Moore in a trade with the Chicago Bears during the offseason. While Moore hasn't put up elite numbers, he's been a difference-maker when healthy and has helped the offense with several big plays.
Both those players are under contract in 2027 as well, which means Beane won't need to fill two positions that have been considered needs for several years. Instead, he can look for upgrades elsewhere, which is what NFL Draft On SI's Justin Melo has him doing in his latest 2027 NFL mock draft.
With their top pick, which Melo has at No. 32 overall, the Bills take Notre Dame guard Anthoine Knapp . Melo praises Knapp's hand usage and anchor, while saying he could be an upgrade over current left guard, Alec Anderson.
"The Buffalo Bills acquired safety Amani Hooker at the trade deadline. Hooker is under contract for several more seasons, crossing 'safety' off Brandon Beane's offseason to-do list,"  Melo wrote. "We turn our attention to left guard, where starter Alec Anderson can be upgraded on. Notre Dame's Anthonie Knapp protects the interior with a strong anchor and well-developed hand usage."
The 6-foot-5, 305-pound actually played left tackle for the first two seasons of his career. He played well in that role, surrendering four sacks as a freshman and just one during his sophomore campaign. This year, he moved inside to left guard and his play has vastly improved.
Knapp has given up six pressures and no sacks in 322 pass protection snaps. He's also been a weapon in the run game, earning a 74.4 in run blocking through his first 10 games of the season.
As for Anderson, he hasn't been bad by any means this season. He enters Week 11 with a PFF rating of 62.3 overall , which is 37th out of 77 qualified guards. He has, however, had issues in the pass game. Anderson has a pass-protection grade of 50.5 while allowing 14 pressures and two sacks.
Anderson has been a decent starter and the Bills would be more than comfortable turning to him again in 2027. Of course, with Anderson set for free agency, Buffalo could decide to go with a more affordable rookie and Knapp could be a major upgrade.

title: Three Rookies Giving Bills Much Needed Midseason Boost
full_text:
After slow starts to their rookie campaigns, several of the Buffalo Bills ' 2026 draft picks are beginning to make a consistent impact for the team.
As the defense continues to improve , build chemistry and gain time on task against inferior QBs, three defensive rookies have emerged as impactful players that Joe Brady and Jim Leonhard will be able to count on.
Sunday's win over the Jets solidified three defensive rookies as important starters or role players for Buffalo's defense moving forward.
Igbinosun has asserted himself as an aggressive, playmaking cornerback opposite Christian Benford. After playing a combined 57 defensive snaps through the first three weeks of the season, the second round pick has been above 80% of snaps in five of the last six games.
The uptick in playing time is for good reason, too. The Ohio State product currently leads all rookies with 11 pass breakups (including two on Sunday against the Jets), which also happens to be the third most among all players this season.
Prior to Sunday's game against the Jets, Igbinosun ranked eighth in lockdown coverage rate , right behind players like Trent McDuffie, Denzel Ward and Derek Stingley. His 84.4 impact score from Pro Football Network led all rookie DBs at the halfway point of the season.
After the pass defense suffered a rough start to the season, Igbinosun is firmly locked in place as a cornerstone of the secondary that continues to improve each week.
Echoing what I wrote about in my rookie report card at the end of October, the plan with Parker was never for him to play a majority of snaps in Year 1. The investments in Bradley Chubb and Michael Hoecht  to pair with Greg Rousseau left an uphill climb for Buffalo's first pick in 2026.
Well, Parker may be on an accelerated course. He's tallied three sacks over the last three weeks, while hovering around the 50% mark for defensive snaps played in that stretch. His eight QB pressures in that three-game span double the amount he had in the first six games of the season.
Parker is slowly emerging as a reliable edge rusher faster than anticipated. While his sack numbers should regress to the mean in the coming weeks, his consistent pressure numbers would be a welcome sign for an edge rush room desperate for more contribution opposite Rousseau.
Buffalo's fourth-round pick quietly saw his highest snap share of the season last week, 35.2% against the Jets. On 25 defensive snaps, he recorded two tackles, a fumble recovery, and allowed zero catches in coverage. He also continued his streak of not been charged with a missed tackle yet this year, a rare feat for a rookie linebacker.
The path for Elarms-Orr to start is murky. Dorian Williams continues to make impact plays, recording a sack, INT, or fumble recovery in each of the last four games. However, the coaching staff is beginning to put more on the rookie's plate, playing over a quarter of defensive snaps in four straight games.
Whether it's three linebacker sets in short yardage and goal line packages, one of Williams or Terrel Bernard needing a breather, or more of a consistent rotation between the off-ball linebackers, expect Elarms-Orr to continue finding himself around the football and making plays in the middle of the field.

title: Why Derrick Henry Doesn’t Pose a Major Threat to New-Look Panthers D
full_text:
The Baltimore Ravens are coming to town , and they're bringing Derrick Henry with them. Ordinarily, that might pose a huge threat to the Carolina Panthers this week.
The Panthers give up the 10th-most rushing yards per game, and they're prone to letting people run all over them. They have two games surrendering 250 rushing yards or more. The Chicago Bears nearly had 300 in Week 1.
That doesn't inspire confidence for the Panthers, but there are a few reasons no one should be overly concerned about this week's matchup.
Are the Panthers worried about Jacoby Brissett? That is highly unlikely, which means that they can stack the box against Derrick Henry more often than not. The Panthers have a strategic advantage there.
The winless Los Angeles Chargers just held the Henry-led rushing attack to 16 yards. It is the third-fewest in a game in NFL history, and the Panthers are a much better team than the Chargers.
CBS Sports' John Breech pointed out that without Lamar Jackson, Henry has 81 touches for 246 yards. His 3.0 average per touch in five games is the lowest for any player in a five-game span. Ever.
Without Jackson, Henry looks very human. And the Panthers likely aren't worried about human running backs. Despite getting Trevor Etienne back and having Alvin Kamara, the New Orleans Saints ran for 49 yards.
Under Todd Wash , the Panthers have a much stronger run defense. In the two games since Ejiro Evero's firing, the Panthers have allowed 136 yards combined on the ground. Opponents are averaging 2.72 yards per attempt against this new-look defense.
Jaelan Phillips is back, too. That would normally be bad news for Jacoby Brissett, and it is. But it's also bad news for Derrick Henry. Phillips was the second-highest graded run defender in the NFL in Week 10.
He sets the edge better than most Panthers OLBs, and he forces running backs to either get past him (which they're not) or cut back inside to Derrick Brown, Lee Hunter, and others. It's a winning formula. So far, it's worked out impossibly well.
If you look at fantasy, Henry has a strong projection, and the Panthers are marked as a green matchup. That is skewed, and it's misleading. The Panthers probably have the advantage here, and Henry shouldn't strike fear into their hearts like he once did.

title: NFL Week 11 Expert Picks Paint Picture of Panthers' Chances vs. Ravens
full_text:
The Carolina Panthers would love to do two things: get on a winning streak and get back to .500. In doing so, they'd also remain at the top of the NFC South. After beating the New Orleans Saints, that is all on the table.
The Baltimore Ravens are coming to town without Lamar Jackson and fresh off a crushing defeat to the previously winless Los Angeles Chargers. The Panthers have a good opportunity here, but only if they aren't looking ahead to the Tampa Bay Buccaneers the week after.
CBS Sports' Pete Prisco rarely picks the Panthers. He picked them to beat the Buccaneers, and he was badly wrong. Other than that, last week vs. the Saints was the only other time he's gone their way. He's doing it again, picking them to get a 23-22 win at home.
"Both of these teams are in desperation mode when it comes to needing victories for the postseason. The Ravens lost at home Monday night to the previously winless Chargers and now have to head out on the road on a short week. That's tough. The Panthers played better defense last week against the Saints, which will help them here. Carolina wins it late, but it's close," he wrote.
His CBS colleague, John Breech , disagrees, taking the Ravens by a field goal. SI's Iain MacMillan is taking the Panthers not only to win, but to cover the 2.5-point spread.
"The Panthers aren't elite in any area, but they aren't bad in any area either, ranking 12th in EPA per play and 17th in opponent EPA per play. The Ravens come in at slightly worse in most metrics, and now they have to hit the road on a short week," he wrote. "That's enough for me to take Carolina as a 2.5-point home favorite."
Here's how the rest of SI is picking:
Covers' C Jackson Cowart is taking the Panthers, 27-21. ""Carolina allowed just 131 rushing yards on 50 carries across its last two games. The Ravens, meanwhile, managed only 16 rushing yards in Monday's 23–20 loss to the Chargers. A short week leaves little time to repair that imbalance before another road test," he wrote.
NFL Spin Zone's Lou Scataglia incomprehensibly said there's little difference between Bryce Young and Jacoby Brissett, but he's ultimately picking the Panthers to win by three thanks to a "more solidified" team.
The Athletic's Nick Kostos is taking the Panthers to cover. "Ultimately, I trust the Panthers more than I do the Ravens. I expect Bryce Young to make some plays in the fourth quarter to secure a close home victory," he wrote.
Obviously, people like the Panthers in this one. But the margins are almost always slim. Most people believe this will be decided by a field goal, potentially the inconsistent leg of Ryan Fitzgerald. So while these two teams are seemingly heading in opposite directions, the Panthers must bring their A game .

title: Fantasy Football Advice: To Keep or Trade Panthers WR Jalen Coker
full_text:
It's been an up-and-down season for the Carolina Panthers , both in real life and in fantasy football as well. Bryce Young started the year as a top-10 QB; Tetairoa McMillan had the best Week 4 performance of any receiver, and Jalen Coker was the WR1 after Week 1.
The highs have come in short spurts; the rest of the season has been mediocre or just bad from a fantasy perspective. Focusing on Coker, he's avaeraging 10.8 points in PPR, and is a top 40 fantasy receiver entering Week 11.
Coker is coming off his worst game of the season, posting just 0.3 fantasy points against the New Orleans Saints. The only Panther who was actually productive against the Saints was Chuba Hubbard, posting 34.2 points.
Coker hasn't scored over 10 fantasy points since Week 6 against the Philadelphia Eagles. Since then, his highest point total was against the Packers, posting 9.6 points.
On a good team, just under 10 points is passable at flex spot, assuming the receiving core is good around Coker. The question around Coker and the Panthers as a whole, when it comes to fantasy, is if there's any reliability for the rest of the season.
Coker has been far from reliable, which means his trade value isn't high.
If Coker was going to be traded off a roster, it should've been done after Week 1, or after Week 6. The only scenarios where trading Coker makes sense are if a team needs a running back more than receivers, or if someone in a league has multiple players on bye, and is willing to give up a solid player in return who isn't playing this week.
There's no real value on Coker right now, realistically, he's not starting in a 10-man league this week, and would be a flex in a 12-man league. Now four weeks removed from his last double-digit performance, the best thing to do with Coker is to keep him on the bench, especially this week against a good Ravens defense.
Potential trade targets if a team needs a running back include Broncos RB Jonah Coleman, Washington RB Rachaad White, 49ers receiver Keenan Allen, or Vikings RB Aaron Jones Sr.
Trading Coker would require specific circumstances, but entering Week 11 , it's smarter to wait and see if he can string together a few good games or even one great performance, making him a sell-high candidate.

title: Jaelan Phillips’ Panthers Return Means More to Defense Than Anyone Realized
full_text:
The Carolina Panthers and everyone else all knew that they were missing Jaelan Phillips. The pass rush wasn't exactly lighting it up before he went down, but missing his career 13.7% pressure rate didn't help.
Everyone knew that his healthy return would help the defense. He's a good player, even if that $120 million contract hasn't aged terribly well so far. But on Sunday, he looked worth it . He had, according to PFF , the second-most pressures in Week 10.
He was essentially unguardable on Sunday, and the pass rush finally got home. But his impact went beyond that, and it totally transforms this team's outlook moving forward.
Jaelan Phillips was seemingly in the backfield on every play against the New Orleans Saints. He had eight pressures and recorded a sack, as well as another QB hit. He also had a sack reversed by a very questionable horse-collar flag .
Put simply, the Saints could not protect Tyler Shough from him. That's what the Panthers paid for. What they might not have expected was his tremendous impact on the run defense.
According to PFF, Phillips wasn't just the second-best pass rusher on Sunday. He was also the second-best run defender. His 90.6 grade ranked only behind Quinnen Williams in terms of defending the run.
Not many could've predicted that Phillips would help turn the Panthers into an elite run defense. That unit has been much-maligned this year, and for good reasons. But when Phillips is on the field, things are much better in that area.
For the year, they have the 10th-worst run defense at 124 yards per game. When Phillips plays, though, they give up 118.3, and that's including the anomalous opening-week drubbing by the Chicago Bears game. If we exclude that, the average with Phillips on the field is 83.8 yards per game.
Plus, Todd Wash seems to be a better coordinator for Phillips. He never looked that dominant in the pass rush under Ejiro Evero. And while Evero's run defense was generally awful, Wash has it working a whole lot better.
This defense has rightfully been maligned for poor play all year, but they've got good players. Now, they might have the right coordinator, and Phillips is apparently the key to both the pass rush and the run defense.
And if this continues, the Panthers will be a very fearsome opponent down the stretch.

title: Bryce Young’s Stats Have Dipped, But NFL Analyst Rightfully Points Finger Elsewhere
full_text:
The Carolina Panthers have seen a decline in quarterback Bryce Young's statistics as of late, resulting in criticism from some analysts. However, according to NFL analyst Brent Sobleski, there is another aspect of the offense that is currently being overlooked.
Bleacher Report's Brent Sobleski is taking a look at some of the key takeaways from Week 10 of NFL play. He takes a look at the struggles of Carolina Panthers quarterback Bryce Young. While his numbers have been on the decline as of late, the offensive line and the pass protection they are providing the quarterback also deserve attention.
Young started the season strong with 11 touchdowns through the first six games of the season and just two interceptions. In those games, Young seemed to be getting better as the season progressed and looked to be the Panthers' answer at quarterback that they were hoping for when they drafted him with the No. 1 overall pick in the 2023 draft.
This season has been somewhat of a regression for the fourth-year quarterback. He had a three-touchdown game against the Broncos in Week 9, but outside of that, he has struggled. He has been under 57% completion in four of the last five games.
In the win over the New Orleans Saints on Sunday, Young threw for 200 yards on 17-of-30 passing. He threw no touchdowns and no interceptions, but helped lead the Panthers to a game-winning field goal by Ryan Fitzgerald. The passing game, however, still has a lot of room for improvement.
While the quarterback has some responsibility for getting the ball out sooner, the offensive line has to be able to protect him on passing plays. Through nine games this season, Young has been sacked 29 times, more than the 27 sacks he suffered during the entire 2025 season.
For the most part, the offensive line has been a mess with injuries and inconsistency all season. Many of Young's problems can be blamed on him holding onto the ball too long at times, but he cannot be expected to play well on passing plays when he is constantly being harassed by opposing defenses.
This has been an issue for the Panthers as of late as well. In the game against the Buccaneers, Young was sacked five times. In the game against the Packers, he was sacked six times. In those games, it was clear that the Panthers were not giving the quarterback enough protection to make things happen on the field.
As Sobleski explained in his Week 10 breakdown of the Panthers , Young's sack total is a major part of the conversation when evaluating his recent passing numbers. The same issue was highlighted in an earlier On SI breakdown of the numbers behind Young's sack problems.
Carolina can improve Young's passing game, but in addition to improving the passing game, the Panthers need to address the problems with the offensive line. Young is having a hard time developing a passing game when he is constantly under pressure from the defense.
Carolina can help Young by finding ways to make things easier for its young quarterback. This can be done by providing better protection, having Young get the ball out quicker or using the running game to help take pressure off him.
The Panthers are coming off a big division win over New Orleans, but there is still plenty of room for improvement on offense. Young has shown that he can play at a much higher level, but the Panthers must find a way to help protect their quarterback.
While Young has had plenty of mistakes to account for in the last few games, it would be unfair to put all of the blame on his shoulders. The offensive line has been just as concerning, and Carolina has several issues to fix before the team can reach its full potential.

He previously wrote for Greenville Sports Media, where he covered various sports and teams across the Carolinas. His experience includes game coverage, feature stories and interviews.

title: The Panthers Managed a Win, But More Is Needed Moving Forward
full_text:
The Carolina Panthers ' first win since October 18th wasn't pretty; the offense managed just 20 points and just 200 passing yards from Bryce Young. That doesn't mean Young had a bad performance against the Saints; it just wasn't spectacular.
Panthers OnSI's Mark Livingston gave Young a C+ for his performance against New Orleans, doing just enough to secure a win. Chuba Hubbard carried the Panthers on Sunday, having the best game of his career. Hubbard posted 172 scrimmage yards, and both of Carolina's touchdowns

Bleacher Report dropped its Week 11 NFL power rankings on Monday, and those rankings featured the Panthers rising to No. 16, a two-spot improvement from last week's No. 18 slot.
In explaining Carolina's ranking, the win itself matters most, but Bleacher Report's Moe Moton remains aware that the Panthers have a low ceiling. His argument focuses on Bryce Young's dip in production; since Week 6, Young has dropped from top-two in passing yards per game to now being No. 6.
Another point that Moton pointed to, the offensive line has crumbled, and that's a major reason that the Carolina passing game isn't thriving like it was for the first month of the season.
Carolina has surrendered at least 3 sacks per game in the last four weeks. Expanding on that point, Rasheed Walker is among the league leaders in pressures allowed at left tackle, with 45 surrendered so far.
The Panthers have to find more consistency in the pass blocking, the first four weeks of the season, Carolina posted over 30 points three out of four games, and Young was sacked 10 times in those four weeks.
Carolina hasn't scored more than 30 points since Week 4 against Detroit. Since Week 7, another four-game stretch, Young has been sacked 17 times, including back-to-back games where he was sacked 5+ times.
It may sound repetitive, it may be beating a broken drum, but the offensive inconsistency truly begins and ends up front.

title: Panthers' Bryce Young Earns C+ Grade After Win Over Saints
full_text:
Bleacher Report's Brent Sobleski has been tracking the play of Panthers quarterback Bryce Young throughout the season. Following Carolina's 20-17 victory over the New Orleans Saints on Sunday, Sobleski gave Young a C+ grade for his performance against the Saints. Young threw for 200 yards on 17-of-30 passing with no touchdowns and no interceptions in the win.
A huge part of why the Panthers were able to win was the offense's final two possessions, according to Sobleski. Carolina was able to go 98 yards and score 10 points on the final two possessions. On the first of those two drives, Young threw a pair of passes to Chuba Hubbard for 29 and 34 yards, setting up the running back for a 1-yard touchdown run to give Carolina a 17-14 lead with 1:49 left in the game.
After the Saints had tied the game up with a field goal on their next drive, the Panthers' offense got the ball back with a chance to win the game. After moving down the field for a potential long field goal, a pass interference penalty was called on Kool-Aid McKinstry. Fitzgerald made the 54-yard field goal as time expired to give the Panthers the win.
Despite his subpar numbers against the Saints, the Panthers' passing attack still needs to improve. Young threw no touchdowns on the day, but did not turn the ball over in the win. His connection with Hubbard on the late touchdown drive was key in the Panthers' win.
While Young received a C+ grade against the Saints, the grade does not completely reflect his play throughout the season. He has had some ugly games, but has also shown the ability to be a very competent passer on numerous occasions. He needs to continue to build on those better performances and display his ability to play at that level on a more consistent basis.
Carolina is still in the thick of things in the NFC South, but the Panthers need more from quarterback Bryce Young. Even when things aren't going well, the offense needs to keep moving, and Young is a big part of that. There is still plenty of room for Young to grow as a passer, and Carolina needs to see more consistency from him as the season continues.
There have been some great moments this season, but the Panthers need to see that talent more consistently.
On SI previously took a look at Bryce Young's recent statistical regression, but that doesn't mean that the Panthers' quarterback has completely stopped growing as a player this season. There are plenty of games left for Young to prove that he can be a more consistent quarterback for the Carolina Panthers.

title: Panthers Could Save Millions and Upgrade Offensive Line With First-Round Draft Pick
full_text:
The Carolina Panthers will have a lot of decisions to make this offseason with regards to their offensive line. Even though they have spent a great deal of money to protect quarterback Bryce Young, the unit has had trouble keeping pressure away from him throughout the 2026 season.
This may result in some changes when the offseason comes around. CBS Sports' Josh Edwards has the Carolina Panthers picking Minnesota interior offensive lineman Greg Johnson with the 19th pick in the 2027 NFL Mock Draft. This would provide the Panthers with another option up front and create the possibility for the team to part ways with one of its highest-paid players.
Edwards feels that the Panthers may look into parting ways with right guard Robert Hunt this offseason, which could save the team $14 million in regards to the salary cap. Hunt signed a five-year, $100 million deal with the Panthers in 2024 and was named to the 2025 Pro Bowl Games following that season.
However, his play in 2026 has brought up many questions regarding the future of the position. The Panthers have had numerous issues throughout their offensive line, and Edwards stated that the unit had the second-highest pressure rate allowed in the NFL this season, according to TruMedia.
Young has demonstrated that he can make plays when things are going well offensively; however, consistent protection remains crucial if the Panthers hope to continue to take steps forward.
The Panthers have already made substantial investments into their offensive line. As On SI pointed out previously in its article on the expensive offensive line for the Panthers, the Panthers have invested heavily into providing a strong group around Young. Improving the interior of the line without increasing the investment significantly may be a key component of the offseason plans.
Johnson is listed as a 6-foot-6, 325-pound senior interior offensive lineman from Minnesota. He is ranked by Edwards as the No. 14 overall prospect and the second-ranked player at his position in this mock draft.
Edwards thinks Johnson can help stabilize the Panthers' offensive line. If Carolina opts to move on from Hunt, selecting a first-round guard would provide the team with a potential replacement while creating further salary-cap flexibility.
It is uncertain what direction Carolina will decide to go in terms of moving on from Hunt or if Johnson will be available when Carolina picks. The mock draft is simply an initial projection, and many things can occur between now and the 2027 NFL Draft. Regardless, using a first-round pick to address the interior is something to consider considering the issues Carolina has faced up front.
The Panthers also need to assess other needs prior to determining how they should proceed. Their offensive line has been a prominent subject of conversation throughout the season, and questions regarding potential changes to the starting group have already begun to emerge. On SI recently reported that the Panthers could consider changes to their offensive line.
Carolina must determine if their current offensive line can provide Young with enough protection moving forward. While they have invested heavily into their group, the results have not always met that level of commitment.
Parting ways with Hunt would be a big decision, especially since Carolina signed him to a large contract in 2024. However, the potential salary-cap savings could allow general manager Dan Morgan more room to operate on other parts of the roster.
While selecting Johnson in the first round won't solve all of the problems up front, it provides Carolina with another young player to develop. If Carolina believes that they need a reset on the interior, then Johnson may be an option worth keeping an eye on as the 2027 NFL Draft approaches.

title: Regression Has Come for Bryce Young, But Here's What That Really Means
full_text:
Bryce Young had Panthers fans feeling pretty confident during the opening weeks of the 2026 season. He was completing throws that didn't always seem to be there in his first two NFL seasons. His numbers were starting to look like what Carolina hoped to see from the first overall pick in the 2023 NFL Draft. For a short time, Young was in the conversation for NFL MVP.
Now, though, the Panthers' quarterback's numbers have taken a turn for the worse. So which version of Young should Carolina's fans believe in? The one who was playing like one of the best quarterbacks in the NFL early in the season? Or the one who hasn't been able to put up the same numbers as of late? Carolina still has questions about how well it has supported Young .
The first four games of the season saw Young put up some of the best numbers of his NFL career. He threw for 361 yards and three touchdowns in a loss to the Chicago Bears, 287 yards and three touchdowns in a win over the Atlanta Falcons, 291 yards and one touchdown in a loss to the Cleveland Browns, and 329 yards and two touchdowns in a win over the Detroit Lions.
In his first four games of the season, Young had over 300 passing yards in three games and multiple touchdown passes in three games as well. He looked like he was in complete control of the offense, making tough throws and leading the Panthers down the field for long drives. It was everything that Panthers fans had hoped for from the first overall pick in the 2023 NFL Draft. But even the best quarterbacks have off days, and it would be unreasonable to expect Young to be able to sustain that level of play for an entire season.
The first few games of the season were special for Young and the Panthers, but that doesn't mean that the last few games have been bad. He is still growing as a quarterback and having some struggles along the way.
After the Detroit game, Young's passing yards began to drop. He had 281 passing yards in a loss to the Philadelphia Eagles, 163 passing yards in a loss to the Tampa Bay Buccaneers, 209 passing yards in a loss to the Green Bay Packers, 276 passing yards and three touchdowns in a loss to the Denver Broncos, and 200 passing yards in a win over the New Orleans Saints.
It is worth noting that Young has been hit a lot in recent weeks. The Buccaneers sacked him five times, while the Packers brought him down six times. The numbers behind Young's sack problems point to bigger issues with Carolina's protection . The Panthers' offensive line has had its struggles with injuries this season, and when healthy, it has been up and down as a unit. This can be challenging for any quarterback, let alone one who is trying to develop as a passer and make the most of the time he has in the pocket.
As much as Young needs to do a better job of dealing with pressure, it is also important to note that Carolina can do a lot to help the quarterback. First, getting the offensive line healthy and giving Young more time to read defenses would be a huge help.
As mentioned earlier, Carolina has a higher floor at quarterback this season than it did last year. Yes, there have been some bad games from the young quarterback, but there have also been some very good games from him. He has kept the Panthers in games that they could have easily lost.
Last Sunday's game against the Saints was not his best, but the Panthers pulled out a win, and that's what matters most. Young was 17-for-30 for 200 yards with no interceptions. He also helped set up the game-winning field goal with time running out, as Carolina improved to 6-4 on the season. Young did enough to help the Panthers secure the win over New Orleans.
We are still trying to figure out what kind of quarterback Young is. There will be games like the ones against Tampa Bay and Green Bay, but also games like the ones against Chicago, Atlanta and Detroit.
We may not be seeing MVP numbers from Young right now, but that is probably for the best. He is growing as a quarterback and has shown that he can be a good quarterback for the Panthers. His start to the season was as good as it gets, but these last few games have shown that he still has a lot of work to do to reach that level on a regular basis.

title: Todd Wash Giving Panthers Rookies More Opportunities to Make an Impact
full_text:
Todd Wash, interim defensive coordinator for the Carolina Panthers, continued to make adjustments on defense in Sunday’s 20-17 victory over the New Orleans Saints. As the Panthers look to get more out of their young players, several saw more time on defense, including rookie defensive tackle Lee Hunter, who played 15 defensive snaps on Sunday after seeing 13 in the Panthers’ game against the Denver Broncos last week. Hunter made a huge play in the second quarter when he stopped Saints running back Travis Etienne for a loss on a fourth-and-inches play from the Panthers’ 25-yard line.
The Panthers have been hoping to get more out of the rookie, but his snaps have been somewhat limited so far this season. The Panthers have a number of defensive linemen and utilize a variety of defensive fronts, so it’s been difficult to find a consistent role for the rookie.
During the week leading up to the Saints game, Wash spoke about getting the rookie more playing time on the field. Hunter had 15 defensive snaps in Sunday’s game after seeing 13 in the previous game against the Denver Broncos.
“It is a major, major point of emphasis to make sure he gets more. I’ll take that. He has to play more. He’s a good football player, and it is as simple as getting him in the game, and he will be in the game more,” Wash said.
Hunter had three tackles on the day, including one for a loss. He made a big play on a fourth-and-inches from the Panthers’ 25-yard line when he burst through the Saints’ offensive line to bring down Etienne for a loss.
The Panthers continued to make changes on defense in Sunday’s game, as rookie safety Zakee Wheatley played 63 defensive snaps while veteran Nick Scott played 28 defensive snaps, or 44% of the defensive total.
Wheatley took over the every-down role at safety alongside Tre’von Moehrig, as Scott moved to a role as the third safety in the Panthers’ secondary. Wheatley was inactive for the season opener against the Broncos but has played in every game since then, making his first start on Sunday.
Prior to the game, Dave Canales spoke with Scott about the change in role. Canales said that Wheatley’s development, along with his communication with his teammates, played a part in the decision to give the rookie safety more responsibility in the Panthers’ secondary.
Wheatley finished with three tackles, including one for a loss of 3 yards, and was targeted twice in coverage. He allowed one reception for 18 yards. Canales highlighted Wheatley’s communication with teammates, tackling and his ability to get the secondary on the same page.
It is clear that interim defensive coordinator Todd Wash is doing everything possible to help the Panthers be successful on defense. In addition to making changes to the defensive strategy, Wash is also making adjustments to give Panthers players opportunities to produce on the field.
These are positive moves by Wash and the rest of the coaching staff as the Panthers look to determine what a number of their younger players can provide on the defensive side of the ball. There is still a lot of work to be done on defense, but hopefully some of the younger players can continue to produce when given the opportunity.
The Panthers are continuing to look for ways to use the players on the roster in different roles throughout the season. Hopefully, Hunter and Wheatley can continue to produce when given the opportunity, giving the Panthers more reliable options on defense.

title: Why Bears Must Exercise Caution with Jeffery Simmons and Kyler Gordon
full_text:
Wednesday's Bears injury report could have been expected to be among the best they've had all year in terms of participation, considering they're coming off a week away.
With only two active not fully participating, it really should be a reason for optimism. This isn't really even an injury report as much as a guesstimate as to what would have happened had they practiced -- they were off Wednesday after holding a full practice on Tuesday instead.
However, this is quite possibly the worst news Bears defensive coordinator Dennis Allen and coach Ben Johnson could get at this point.
With Jeffery Simmons listed on the injury report as limited due to a knee issue, and Kyler Gordon not practicing at all and day to day with a shoulder injury, the Bears are without full participation from their two most impactful defensive players.
WELCOME BACK, KYLER GORDON 📺: FOX pic.twitter.com/mLaoOqQgPt
The Bears are going for their fifth straight win, trying to match their longest winning streak under Johnson. Their current four-game winning streak coincides with the returns of Caleb Williams and Gordon from injuries.
Gordon's pass rush and run support, as well as his coverage in nickel defense, have been keys in the streak. When Simmons arrived, the consistency of their interior pass rush increased dramatically. The end result of both has been the best third-down defense in the NFL.
Before Gordon's return, the Bears were allowing an outstanding 26% third-down conversion rate. Since his return it has plummeted and was 19% over the last four weeks with 60% overall completions allowed. Since Simmons was acquired by trade, they have allowed 13% on 3 of 23 on third downs, with 35-of-66 total completions and three interceptions.
Head coach Ben Johnson with injury updates on WR Luther Burden Ill and DB Kyler Gordon. In his latest press conference. 🐻⬇️ 🎥: @ForeverBearDown (TikTok) pic.twitter.com/2NUIgg8Jub
Obviously not having either or not having both would make a colossal difference in their defense.
The trouble is, they may want to think about resting both depending on the severity of the injury. The reason for this is they play again already on Thursday and the game in Detroit is not only going to be tougher on a player with a knee injury because it's on Ford Field's artificial turf, but it's only four days after the previous game.
In 55 years, there has never been an NFL Defensive Player of the Year to win after being traded midseason #Bears DT Jeffery Simmons could be the first in NFL history His 100.0 PFN Impact grade is tied for the best among all NFL defenders this year pic.twitter.com/3YRBd9W65Z
If they start one or both, it's possible they might not be ready yet for the next game on Thanksgiving, a key division battle against Johnson's former team.
Brad Biggs of the Tribune correctly pointed out in his regular spot on WSCR-AM 670 the Score that Lions QB Jared Goff is relatively immobile and it leaves him susceptible to the interior pass rush. The Bears will need Simmons in that Thursday game more than they need him against New Orleans, if there is a risk.
Also, having Gordon available then to cover Amon-Ra St. Brown would be preferable to rookie Malik Muhammad.
It makes little sense to jeopardize injured players in a game the Bears might be able to control anyway. They beat New Orleans without Simmons last year. They were able to go 3-2 before Gordon returned and were missing their quarterback for three of those five games, as well.
If both Gordon and Simmons play or one of them plays, it needs to be done with an eye toward Thanksgiving, when they need to win a divisional game and stake a claim for repeating their NFC North title.
Limited reps Sunday for the slightly injured or none at all needs to be the order of the day because divisional games must be the priority. They are 0-2 in their division and since Johnson became coach they are 2-6 in regular season within the division, but16-2 outside of it.  The divisional game on the holiday is the critical one and Sunday is something they can get through if they need to rest two key players.
The Bears acquired Jeffery Simmons because he's a fantastic player who can dominate against anyone. But specifically, Simmons may really give the Lions trouble because Jared Goff makes his living stepping up in the pocket and dissecting opponents, as @BradBiggs said. pic.twitter.com/JVbMOLYkms

title: Bears Have Two Problems Ben Johnson Wants Fixed Before They Cost Them Against the Saints
full_text:
Bears coach Ben Johnson found two real sources of irritation when he looked back at the way the team played in the season's first half.
To be sure, there are other issues like the running game consistency, the big plays allowed in the passing game and the inability to keep opponents from gaining consistent rushing yards.
Each of those seems more isolated to the week's opponent than a general and consistent plague upon the team.
The two problems Johnson had were their fumbling and penalties. One is a total disaster. The other adds up.
The penalties should really irritate Johnson because of the ones the Bears seem to keep getting. What was almost humorous was Johnson picked a comment about special teams to bring up penalties as an issue.
Bailed out by defensive penalties? 👀 Which QBs benefit the most on plays that otherwise wouldn't have gained any yards? Excl. pre-snap penalties | Min. 5 EPA Not shown: Caleb Williams (3.1), Trevor Lawrence (2.5) pic.twitter.com/ZED9NgtY2f
"We've got to clean up the penalties," he said. "I think that's the most glaring thing in that phase right now, and it's certainly been brought to their attention, and we'll work towards that.”
Penalties have been painful on kick return, that's for sure. However, they didn't commit that penalty the officials thought they saw. It was clearly an official's mistake when D'Marco Jackson got called for holding on Zavion Thomas' 92-yard kickoff return for a touchdown.
The really comical aspect of the comment by Johnson is special teams actually is the one area of the game where the Bears are committing the fewest penalties in relation to the rest of the league. The Bears have eight special teams penalties according to NFLpenalties.com . Only the Rams, Texans, 49ers and Cardinals have fewer than eight.
THIS IS AN AWFUL CALL BY THE REFS: The #Bears returned a kickoff 92 yards for a TOUCHDOWN, but the refs wiped it away with a bogus holding penalty on Chicago. The player barely made any contact, and the flag completely changed the game. BRUTAL CALL 😳😳 pic.twitter.com/DbAzTGcluc
If Johnson wants to take a shot at someone for penalties, he needs to look no further than his own offense and not for their total penalties, but for the type.
The Bears have 23 pre-snap penalties on offense. Only four teams committed more than they have. Pre-snap penalties keep the offense spinning its wheels in longer down and distance, and Johnson has constantly talked about this as a past detriment. For some reason now he doesn't seem as keen on punching that button even though it's in a terrible state.
The defense is also tied for ninth in penalties against. Some of those have been very painful. For instance, Montez Sweat has had a pair of sacks wiped out by defensive penalties.
189 flags for 1,699 penalty yds in 13 games Sunday (SNF + chart) 🔸 Avg 14.5 flags/gm & 130.7 penalty yds/gm 🔸 8 of 15 games had 15+ flags 🔸 10 of 13 games > 100+ penalty yds NFL is becoming unwatchable. Especially when 1/4 of flags feel VERY borderline LET PLAYERS PLAY https://t.co/MAfNYa8Xbu pic.twitter.com/o9AFngcaJh
The turnover issue is a critical problem, and it's not especially Caleb Williams' interceptions even after he threw a career-high four the last game. Two were fluky, as he said, while the other two were carelessness on his part. However, that was only the second game this year when he threw an interception and he still has the fewest interceptions (18) per his career pass total (1,325) in the history of the NFL.
Fumbles are the real Bears problem, even greater than pre-snap penalties.
"The one thing that really stood out is just where we are in the turnover margin right now," Johnson said. "We're minus-four, and prior to this week's games, that put us at 29th in the league, and that's just not winning football. I think we're doing a solid job defensively and on special teams taking the ball away. It's really more offensively, we've got to do a better job making sure we have good ball security."
It's anyone's guess why this has happened, but last year they fumbled 13 times total and lost four of them. This year they've already fumbled 12 times with eight games to go and have lost twice as many as they lost all last year. Only one team has lost more fumbles than the Bears this year, and that's this Sunday's opponent, New Orleans. They have lost 10.
D'ANDRE SWIFT FUMBLES AT THE GOAL LINE 😳 #NFL pic.twitter.com/bqkiMsUt7l
D'Andre Swift and Luther Burden each lost two fumbles, one by Burden when he was knocked unconscious. Colston Loveland, Roschon Johnson, Case Keenum, and Rome Odunze each lost one. Caleb Williams fumbled twice but recovered them and Kalif Raymond recovered one he fumbled. Keenum also recovered one of his own two fumbles.
One reason they could have more running back fumbles than in the past is the absence of running backs coach Eric Bieniemy, who went to Kansas City after last season as offensive coordinator. He was always on the backs about retaining possession with drills in practice but new backs coach Eric Studesville is no less vigilant, although he isn't as vocal at practice.
What they haven't had is continuity at running back after Week 4. Kyle Monangai hasn't been there to carry the ball. It's meant carries for backs who either don't carry as often or at all. Also, when Monangai carries there is the sense they won't fumble. He has never lost one in college or in the pros.
FUMBLE!! Roschon Johnson suelta el balón y Atlanta toma la posesión. Los Falcons tienen el balón cerca de la mitad del campo, perdiendo por 16 puntos y con 8:07 por jugar. #VamosOsos pic.twitter.com/38jHeYSI8C
In the offseason critics of how the Bears succeeded last year insisted they couldn't finish on top in takeaways again like last year. It's difficult, but they're tied for 10th in takeaways with 13 and tied for 11th in interceptions with seven. They've also kept their total up with six fumbles recovered.
However, the differential is so poor at 27th overall with minus-4 mostly because they're losing fumbles when they didn't last year.
It all makes their dominance at No. 1 in time of possession (34:31) all the more remarkable and makes it easy to wonder what they could do if they start holding onto the football. All lost fumbles are costly but they'd probably have one fewer loss if Swift hadn't fumbled at the 1-yard line against Minnesota.
🚨BREAKING: THE REFS JUST MISSED A CLEAR HELMET-TO-HELMET PENALTY ON #BUCS REUBEN BAIN JR. Bain’s hit on #Bears WR Luther Burden forced a fumble and Burden is now down on the field injured. TB now has a chance to WIN THE GAME because of this missed call. pic.twitter.com/tbSVUg5Df0

title: Monangai, Burden, Simmons Injury Updates & More From Bears' Wednesday Practice Report
full_text:
The Chicago Bears have put out their first official injury report of the week ahead of the Week 11 game against the New Orleans Saints.
The Bears switched things up this week after emerging from the bye, with the team holding practices on Monday and Tuesday before having the day off on Wednesday.
As a result, the Bears' Wednesday injury report is an estimation, but it still gives us some insight into how players are doing with their respective injuries.
This week's injury report includes five players: Kyle Monangai, Kyler Gordon, Jeffery Simmons, Luther Burden and Malik Muhammad. Here's the latest on each.
Simmons, Gordon and Burden are all new additions to the injury report coming out of the bye, but we knew Burden and Gordon would be included, so no surprises there.
The good news is, Burden is good to go for this week after head coach Ben Johnson revealed he has cleared the concussion protocol .
As for Gordon, he is dealing with a shoulder injury that Johnson said has him labeled as day-to-day. He did not take part in the practices on Monday and Tuesday, so no surprise he's a non-participant in the estimated injury report.
It looks like we'll be monitoring Simmons' status for the rest of the week after he was added to the injury report with a knee issue.
That said, the fact that Simmons was able to put in a limited practice to start the week suggests he should be fine. We'll know more over the next two days, though.
Muhammad's full practice is an upgrade from his participation over the last few weeks, when he was only able to log limited practices before sitting out the last two contests . This puts Muhammad on track to return against the Saints.
As is the case with Muhammad, Monangai's full practice is a step forward after he logged a limited session on the Friday before Week 9, when he was ruled out again.
Monangai told reporters on Monday that he expects to play and the full participation backs that. The concern, however, is that Monangai will be managing the injury the rest of the season .
"The time off definitely helped but I mean (the injury is) going to be there," Monangai said. "Offseason I'll heal it. That will be for then."
Monangai's return will be a huge boost for the Bears' offense, as he was the team's best running back before his injury. His return will take some of the pressure off D'Andre Swift, also.

title: Has Theo Benedet Done Enough to Cement His Status as Bears' Answer at LT?
full_text:
We expected Theo Benedet to be the placeholder at left tackle until Ozzy Trapilo was back in football shape .
The Bears coaching staff probably had similar expectations, as Trapilo fortified the position (after taking the job from Benedet) down the stretch last season. They also didn't place the 2025 second-round selection on IR to begin the year, seemingly hoping he would return to the field relatively early .
However, he's been active over the past four contests and has only played 36 snaps. 18 of them came in his debut against Atlanta, and he's played sparingly since then. He wasn't a noticeable liability over any of those snaps (although he did commit a holding penalty that negated a 24-yard Rome Odunze catch-and-run).
Instead, Benedet has played too well to leave the field since taking over the job for an injured Braxton Jones in Week 4. The job will presumably be his to lose, and he hasn't done anything to warrant a switch up until this point.
Benedet started eight games for Chicago last season, and he played better than Braxton Jones in virtually every area. However, he was a much better run blocker than pass protector, as he was a liability in that regard.
However, the 2024 undrafted free agent seemingly made huge strides in that department this season. According to Pro Football Focus , he has allowed one sack across 267 pass-blocking snaps this season. His 71.3 PFF grade also ranks 28th among tackles, while his pass-blocking grade of 68.4 ranks 43rd.
Meanwhile, he's also picked up right where he left off in the running game. He plays with tenacity in that department, and his 73.3 run-blocking grade (which ranks 21st) doesn't even do him justice.
PFF grades can be tricky. They're no longer the end-all, be-all for grading offensive line play. Still, when those metrics match the eye test, that reinforces a player's standing. Benedet has passed the eye test with flying colors.
Would the Bears have hoped Trapilo would've cemented his status as the answer at left tackle? Probably. They used a second-round pick on him, after all. Benedet went undrafted in 2024.
With that said, they're both 25. Benedet is only five days older than Trapilo. The playing field is even, and they'll be thrilled if either becomes the long-term answer at the position. Benedet is playing out a one-year deal, so Chicago will have to re-sign him if he proves to be the guy.
Nevertheless, they'd probably be able to do so relatively cheaply considering his limited sample size. That would put the Bears in a great position to address their weaknesses on defense. They'll desperately need to address cornerback, with Tyrique Stevenson set to hit free agency and Jaylon Johnson playing replacement-level football . They'd also benefit from adding another edge rusher.
Without a first-round pick ( which they shipped off for Jeffery Simmons ), addressing those needs would be tough if they also needed to fortify the left tackle position. The task becomes much more manageable if Benedet proves to be the answer, though.
Benedet has defied the odds every step of the way throughout his short NFL career. He played college football at the University of British Columbia and held his own across eight starts last season.
At this point, it'd be wise not to bet against him. He just might be the answer the team has been looking for at the most important position along the offensive line.
Jerry Markarian has been an avid Chicago Bears fan since 2010 and has been writing about the team since  2022.  He has survived the 2010 NFC Championship Game, a career-ending injury to his favorite player (Johnny Knox), the Bears' 2013 season finale, a Double Doink, Mitchell Trubisky, Justin Fields, and Weeks 8-17 of the 2024 NFL season. Nevertheless, he still Bears Down!

title: Bears Say They're Convinced Tyler Shough and Saints Pose Threat This Time
full_text:
After all of the self-scout and self-aggrandizing of the past few days, the Bears do need to get back to the business of the day.  You can't talk about baseball MVP videos and what you did on your week off forever.
The Bears have an actual game to play Sunday against a New Orleans team with some dangerous talent, an ability to play opponents tough, but ultimately one committing so many stupid mistakes that they can lose a game when their opponent commits 17 penalties for 152 yards. The Saints did this last week against Carolina.
"I see a team with a lot of playmakers, especially on the outside, a different group of running backs that can all do a little bit of different things," Bears defensive tackle Grady Jarrett said. "Obviously they've had to do some shuffling up front (on offense) but all of those guys can play at a really high level.
Fellow Saints fans, I want to hold yall hands when I tell yall this, but Tyler Shough might not be the franchise savior QB we thought he was
"The record isn't always indicative of what a team is and if you really look at it it's a lot of one-score games. Obviously I've played this organization a lot, a super prideful organization, so they're always going to be ready to show up and play so we need to make sure we are ready too."
The Saints actually don't look a lot different on the surface than last year when the Bears played them, except for the fact their quarterback is Tyler Shough, a bigger and stronger multipurpose threat than Spencer Rattler was in the game the Bears won 26-14 last October.
When the Bears won that game, the Saints were having problems running and stopping the run, would have occasional outbursts in the passing game and their defensive front was keeping them in many games. The Bears ran for 222 yards in that win. Later in the year, they began to put it all together and won five of their last eight, but they have reverted now to doing what they did early last year.
“We gotta beat those guys. That wasn’t a win by them, they obviously are a good team, but we feel like we lost that game as the Saints. […] I feel like we shot ourselves in the foot there, and that stings even more.” #Saints QB Tyler Shough on the disappointment of the missed… pic.twitter.com/q3SG7VmBHC
They can't run. Their defensive front rushes the passer well but they give up too many passing yards, too many rushing yards and Shough can't get it downfield enough to outstanding receivers like Chris Olave, Devaughn Vele, and tight end Juwan Johnson.
Rushing is at the root of most of their trouble since Kellen Moore became head coach, as they've gained 107 yards rushing or less in 19 games out of 27 he has coached. However, there have been signs of their ground game coming to life, as they ran for 175 yards against the first-place Giants in a win and beat Cleveland, another team with a winning record, by running for 160 yards. They reverted back to form with 18 rushing yards against Pittsburgh and 49 against the Panthers.
Some Saints fans have forgotten the QB hell we’ve endured since Brees retired Shough has hit a “skid”, but look at what he’s working with - No veteran QB to mentor him - An incompetent coaching staff - A terrible O-line - Absolutely no run game The biggest problem is Kellen… pic.twitter.com/KkFCZRRCrn
It's been a case of their strong defensive line trying to hold it together until the other promising aspects come together, and it all never seems to entirely materialize.
“They’ve had two games I think that they lost by more than one score," Bears quarterback Caleb Williams said. "Everything else has been one score, it's been really close. So the record may not show what type of team they are, but when we go out there, we have to put our best foot forward and go out there and execute. Coach (Ben Johnson) is going to deliver us a good plan. We've got to go out there and execute with the right mentality.”
While the Saints haven't exactly found ways to put it all together, what the Bears need to remember is they have risen to the occasion against the better teams on their schedule.
“This version of the passing game and this version of Tyler Shough…I hate it.” @robertmays , @davehelman_ and Derrik Klassen weigh in on the struggling New Orleans Saints offense. pic.twitter.com/XxcBWy7r3q
They nearly beat Detroit in Ford Field opening day, losing on a missed two-point conversion gamble in overtime. They lost to Baltimore by a touchdown, kept within a touchdown against the Vikings until a Minnesota fourth-quarter field goal, lost by six to Pittsburgh, lost by a TD and two-point conversion to the Raiders and then by a 54-yard game-ending field goal last week despite benefiting from the 17 Panthers penalties.
Johnson didn't need a self-scout last week to tell him the Bears were minus-4 in turnover differential heading into last week's games.
"That put us at 29th in the league and that's just not winning football," he said.
The Saints, though, are even worse at minus-8 and better in this regard than only the Falcons, Patriots and Colts. The pathetic state of their division makes them a potential playoff team, though.
Dennis Allen gets another shot at his former team. He has a point to prove when the Bears face the Saints. Presented by @pjscoffee pic.twitter.com/zLZ4ZA1fsM
"I don't care what their record says right now, they're in every single game and there's a bunch of one-score games throughout this," Johnson said. "I know they're fighting for the (NFC South) division this back half of the season. So there’s a lot at stake."
The Bears' last game looked like a walk-through after they took a 14-0 lead against one of the underachieving NFC South contenders, Tampa Bay. It didn't turn out that way.
They can't afford to repeat the same mistake they made two weeks earlier while involved in an NFC North race so tough that one slip-up last week for Green Bay meant dropping down into last, two games behind everyone else.
“It really doesn't matter right now," Johnson said. "Once again, it's all about winning this week. We'll worry about everything else when it's time. It's not time for that. There's still eight games to be played, and this is the most important one because it's the next one.”
They said this last game and even appeared ready, but things change rapidly in the NFL on a week-to-week basis. Last week's team capable of squandering a 17-penalty advantage can be this week's beneficiary of gifts if the Bears play like they did against Tampa Bay for three quarters.

title: Bears Fans Shouldn't Worry About Ben Johnson's 3-2 Record After Bye Weeks Before Saints
full_text:
The first half of the 2026 NFL season could not have gone much better for the Chicago Bears. They went 7-2 through nine games and climbed to the top of the NFC North, but they took a bye-week tumble down the standings after Detroit and Minnesota secured big wins in Week 10. Nevertheless, the Bears are big favorites in their Week 11 game against the 3-6 New Orleans Saints and appear primed to extend their winning streak to five.
However, there is one reason for Bears fans to feel some trepidation ahead of what looks like a tune-up game, and that has to do with head coach Ben Johnson. Since becoming a play-caller in 2022, Johnson's teams are just 3-2 after bye weeks, including a playoff bye. Taken at face value, that's a concerning record for a head coach as obsessed with details and fundamentals as Johnson, but there may be more to this than meets the eye.
With that in mind, let's pop open the hood of Johnson's post-bye record and take a deeper look, starting with last season.
After a shaky 2-2 start to the Ben Johnson era, the Bears entered an early Week 5 bye, which seemingly came at just the right time. They ended up beating the Washington Commanders on the road in rainy conditions, with backup kicker Jake Moody sealing a 25-24 victory with a walk-off field goal.
This wasn't the prettiest game from Chicago's offense, especially in regard to the passing game, but the run game finally got going for the first time all year, racking up 150 rushing yards. This post-bye victory showed that Ben Johnson understood what wasn't working for his offense and that he could make the necessary adjustments.
Johnson's final game as a Detroit Lion was probably not what he'd hoped it would be: a stunning playoff loss . The Lions got rolled by the Commanders in the Divisional Round of the playoffs after securing a Wild Card bye, but it's hard to blame this one on Johnson, try as some Lions fans might.
His offense put up 521 total yards and 30 first downs, besting the Commanders in each category. They put up 31 points. The problem was that a heavily injured defense gave up 45 points and Jared Goff threw three mind-numbing interceptions. Johnson can call the plays, but he can't throw the ball for his quarterback.
Ben Johnson just seems to have the Cowboys' number over the last two years. He got his first win as a head coach in a dominant 31-14 Week 3 win against Dallas last year, and less than a year before that he led a 47-9 shellacking of the Cowboys as the Lions' offensive coordinator after an early bye week.
The Lions scored on every single drive of that game except two, with one being a one-play kneel-down to end the first half and a turnover on downs at the end of the game, after the starters had already been pulled. The game was effectively over by halftime as Johnson's offense raced out to a 27-6 lead and never looked back.
This post-bye victory was another statement win for Ben Johnson, which came right around the time when he became the hottest head coaching candidate in the NFL. Back when the Chargers were actually a well-coached, tough team, Johnson's offense dropped 533 yards on them while going 8-for-18 on third and fourth downs en route to a 41-38 win.
In this game, Detroit's defense once again came up short, allowing the Chargers to hang around the entire game. But a walk-off field goal from Riley Patterson secured the win and boosted Johnson's national profile.
Johnson's first post-bye game as a play-caller didn't go quite as well as subsequent performances. In fact, it was mostly a disaster. They lost to the Cowboys 24-6 in a game where they only ran 56 plays for 312 yards.
However, there's not much from this game that can inform Bears fans on Johnson's post-bye tendencies. The Lions were still in the middle of a rebuild, and Johnson was still learning the ropes as a play-caller. At that that point they were still taking their lumps and trying to find a groove.
As aforementioned, Johnson's 3-2 post-bye record doesn't look great on its face. But after looking through the details of each game, it's plain to see that very little blame can be laid at Johnson's feet for those two losses. One was in the middle of what looked like another dismal season for the Lions as their rebuild continued, and the other was a playoff game in which the defense gave up 45 points.
Returning to the present, I see no reason for Bears fans to fear that Johnson has the post-bye yips. There are reasons to fear the Saints in Week 11 , and there's a non-zero chance that they pull off the upset, but it won't be because the head coach wasn't up to the task at hand.

title: Who is Chicago Bears' Midseason Non-QB Most Valuable Player?
full_text:
As the Chicago Bears prepare to return from their bye in Week 11 to face the New Orleans Saints , we are also officially halfway through the 2026 season.
The Bears have played in nine of their 17 contests and sport a 7-2 record. The biggest reason for that is quarterback Caleb Williams, who is easily the team's Most Valuable Player as he continues to cement himself as an elite signal-caller .
But, if we had to name another player as the team's midseason MVP, who would it be?
Well, in my mind, it comes down to two players.
Burden has cemented himself as the Bears' No. 1 wide receiver in 2026 after playing better and more consistent football than his fellow wideout, Rome Odunze.
Burden leads the Bears with 49 receptions, 644 yards and four touchdowns. That puts him on pace to finish with 92 catches, 1,216 yards and seven touchdowns.
But it isn't only about the numbers with him, as Burden is easily the Bears' most consistent pass-catcher while both Odunze and Colston Loveland have struggled with drops.
During a season in which Williams has taken the next step in his career, Burden has been one of the biggest reasons why.
As for Muhammad, the rookie has been far better than expected after being a fourth-round pick back in April. The Texans product is giving up a completion rate of 54.8% and a passer rating of 79.9 when targeted.
What makes his season more impressive is the fact that the rookie has played great football at multiple spots, which is not something you see from rookies often.
First, he started off in the slot with the injury to Kyler Gordon , and Muhammad played well there despite having very little slot experience from his days in college.
Muhammad then moved to the boundary in place of the struggling Tyrique Stevenson upon Gordon's return and his play has not dropped off at all.
As we mentioned, Stevenson has struggled this season, but so has Jaylon Johnson, who is having the worst campaign of his career.
Muhammad's play has been a much-needed boost for Chicago and one has to wonder just where the Bears' defense would've been had the rookie not stepped up.
We're giving it to Burden over Muhammad, and for one very specific reason.
There was nothing more important for the Bears than Williams taking that next step in his career, which he obviously has done.
Because Burden has been Williams' top and most consistent target, that means he has played a huge role in the Bears quarterback's ascension
It's tough to find more value than what Burden has provided for the Bears this season, but we will say Muhammad is very close.
