title: Everything Chicago Bears Have to Fear About New Orleans Saints in Week 11
full_text:
The Chicago Bears and New Orleans Saints will do battle at Soldier Field in Week 11 in a matchup that features two teams going in opposite directions.
At 3-6, the Saints are headed toward another disappointing season after entering the 2026 campaign with some hype after showing promise late in 2025. The saving grace for New Orleans comes from the fact that the team is in one of the worst divisions in football, so its playoff hopes aren't dead yet.
At 7-2, the Bears have looked like a true Super Bowl contender in the third year of the Caleb Williams era. The Bears quarterback is ascending to elite status , if he isn't there already, and Chicago's defense has been a great complement.
Despite how poorly the Saints have played this season, they are still a dangerous team and the Bears cannot take them lightly. Here's three things in particular the Bears need to be ready for.
The Saints already had a solid one-two punch at wide receiver in Chris Olave and the ascending Devaugh Vele, but New Orleans added rookie Jordyn Tyson into the mix a few weeks ago.
Tyson was on the shelf for the first seven games because of a hamstring injury. After a quiet game in his NFL debut, Tyson emerged in Week 10 with 11 catches for 80 yards.
Tyson has played the majority of his snaps in the slot, where the Bears have an injury concern this week with Kyler Gordon, who is dealing with a shoulder injury that has him labeled as day-to-day.
But, as we noted, Tyson isn't the only one the Bears need to be worried about. Both Vele and Olave are in the midst of career-best seasons and can cause major head aches for a Bears secondary that has seen struggles, and namely with Jaylon Johnson and Tyrique Stevenson.
Luckily for Chicago, rookie Malik Muhammad has been better than expected in his first season and has provided some stability on the outside. That said, he has missed the last two games with an injury, so he's someone to keep an eye on during the week.
The Saints might actually have one of the best edge rusher duos in the entire NFL right now.
On one side, New Orleans has Carl Granderson, who has already matched his career-high with 8.5 sacks that are tied for the second-most in the NFL this season.
On the other side, former No. 2 overall pick Chase Young is also on pace to have his best season with eight sacks in nine games, which is just two shy of his personal best.
While it doesn't guarantee the Saints' edge rushers won't have any success, the Bears are well-equipped to handle Granderson and Young with a strong tackle duo of Theo Benedet and Darnell Wright, who have combined for two sacks and 30 pressures allowed this season, per Pro Football Focus .
One way the Bears can neutralize the Saints' talented receiver trio is to get home on Shough and prevent him from throwing the football, or at least bother him when he tries to.
That might be tough, though, as the Shough presents plus mobility that allows him to escape pressure to extend plays — which forces defensive backs to cover for longer — and pick up yards with his legs.
The Bears need to make sure they are securing the edge and not allowing Shough to roll out and have extra time to find his pass-catchers, which could lead to chunk gains.
Chicago also needs to maintain gap integrity so Shough can't find holes up the middle to run through.

title: Kyler Gordon on Injury Watch as Bears Return From Bye to Face Saints
full_text:
The Chicago Bears have had some good injury news to start the week, but not everything has been positive on that front.
On Monday, we found out that both running back Kyle Monangai and wide receiver Luther Burden were practicing , and then it was revealed by head coach Ben Johnson on Tuesday that Burden cleared the concussion protocol .
However, on the flip side, Johnson not only noted that edge rusher Dayo Odeyingbo isn't likely to be back from injured reserve , he also noted that cornerback Kyler Gordon is dealing with an injury.
Here's what we know about that.
The Bears decided to hold a pair of practices on Monday and Tuesday this week before taking off on Wednesday.
In both of those sessions, Gordon did not take part, which puts his status up in the air for Week 11 against the New Orleans Saints.
Johnson told reporters that Gordon is dealing with a shoulder injury and is viewed as day-to-day, ESPN's Courtney Cronin relayed.
"Bears practice just wrapped. Second consecutive practice this week for Kyle Monangai (toe/thumb)," Cronin wrote. "No Kyler Gordon (shoulder). Ben Johnson called it a 'day to day' injury. Gordon missed Monday’s session as well."
According to Brad Biggs of The Chicago Tribune , it appears Gordon came down with the injury in the second quarter of the Tampa Bay Buccaneers game in Week 9. Gordon exited the game to get checked out in the locker room but managed to return and finish out the game. He also played a season-high 52 snaps.
The Bears have not put out an injury report so far this week since they are not required to until Wednesday. However, that practice report will be an estimation. Still, it'll give us a better idea of how Gordon is coming along.
For now, we would expect Gordon to be listed an estimated non-participant based on his lack of participation over the first two days of the week.
That said, the day-to-day label is a good sign for his chances of suiting up.
Replacing Gordon on defense will not be easy because of both his blitzing and coverage skills.
We've seen Gordon's impact in the pass-rush with four sacks, and the veteran defensive back is permitting a completion rate of 57.1% and a passer rating of 86.6.
What could also complicate things is if Malik Muhammad doesn't play again. The rookie has missed the last two games with a toe injury, although it appears he was practicing on Monday and Tuesday, so he might be good to go.
Tyrique Stevenson got hurt in Week 9 , but as is the case with Muhammad, it appears he has been practicing, so his odds of suiting up are looking good.
Because less is more with Stevenson, we'd prefer the Bears move Cam Lewis from safety to the slot and have Elijah Hicks take that starting spot if Gordon is ruled out. Lewis has played 76 snaps in the slot this season because of injuries, and he has played well.
The other approach would be to move Muhammad to the slot, where he played well while Gordon was out earlier in the season, and have Stevenson play on the boundary, but we know how Stevenson has struggled this season.
Hopefully for the Bears, none of this will be necessary and Gordon ends up playing.

title: Punishing the Copy Cats a Goal for Caleb Williams and Bears Offense
full_text:
Caleb Williams and Ben Johnson have addressed the copy cat effect and think the Bears are ready to attack it.
This would be the possibility defenses try to do what Tampa Bay's defense did to get back into their Week 9 game, when they nearly knocked off the Bears by taking away the ball five times. It's not an extraordinary tactic. It's the old A-gap or B-gap blitz.
“Like you said, it's a copycat league," Williams said Tuesday at Halas Hall. "So it's going to show up at some point here soon. Who knows, it could be this week, it could be next week, it could be the week after, it could be postseason, when we get there, whenever that is. It's going to show up at some point.
"Like I said, we've gone back and looked at it already. We'll fix it. For myself in that situation, if it does happen; I mean, there's times when people get through, and it's happened throughout my career. It's going to happen for the rest of my career. Just get the ball out of bounds or anything like that. Then on the other ones, just don't make bad decisions.”
"That's also one of the coolest things about being here in Chicago and what we're building here. It's not just Chicago Bears, it's us as Chicago athletes." Caleb Williams talked about being part of PCA's MVP celebration video shared by the Cubs, and what their friend group is… pic.twitter.com/XbsGasyUfy
The Saints might not seem like the ideal candidates to use this tactic because they have plenty of pass rush from defensive ends Chase Young (8 sacks) and Carl Granderson (8 1/2), and they also have edge Cameron Jordan, who has yet to record a sack in his eight games. Maybe the Bears dodged a bullet by not signing him, if indeed they were interested as many rumors suggested during free agency. However, Jordan remains an imposing physical threat on the line.
However, Johnson thinks they could be bringing the heat.
“These edge players, between the two of them, or really I should say three of them, but the guys that are playing the most right now, Chase Young and Carl Granderson, they're leading the team in sacks, I think they have eight apiece and they're good not only in the pass game, they're great edge setters in the run game as well," Johnson said. "Big challenge there on both sides.
LUTHER BURDEN TOUCHDOWN! Caleb Williams beats the blitz and Burden does the rest! Chicago is HUMMING on Sunday Night Football! pic.twitter.com/CwgObQTkEW
"And then I think this (linebacker Kaden) Elliss that they got back at linebacker, I think he's one of the better pressuring linebackers in the NFL. And so, they're not afraid to plug him in A- or B-gap and make it tough on your protection scheme. That combination, I think, from the interior with him with those two edge rushers is what makes their pressure package so dangerous.”
Elliss is the most likely to be blitzing because of his success. The 6-foot-2, 238-pound 2019 Saints seventh-round pick left New Orleans for Atlanta and then returned. He has two sacks this year, 22 1/2 for his career.
How they actually stop these blitzes better is the mystery Johnson won't reveal, but guards Jonah Jackson and Joe Thuney, and especially center Garrett Bradbury, have the greatest responsibility.
4 turnovers. Bad throws all night. And with the game on the line? Caleb was still Caleb. 🐻 @_JeffWillis on the dime to Loveland that set up the game-winner 🎯 #Bears #DaBears #CalebWilliams pic.twitter.com/qhmXs8ixBr
"There are some things protection-wise that we certainly have to clean up," Johnson said. "We care about the integrity of the A- and B-gaps, and there are too many times on tape right now where we're allowing free runners through those gaps. So we've got to tighten the screws a little bit there, feel good about our rules, feel good about the guys that are up front and getting the calls made.
"We've just got to make sure we're all on the same page, we have our eyes in the right spot. Anytime you see a little something on tape, we're going to get more of it. Until we have proven that we've taken care of that problem, there's more to come.”
For Williams, it wasn't just the blitz that he needs to be concerned with but the mistakes he made. He had to stew on four bad interceptions, two when he tried throwing it away and it was caught just off the ground by defenders.
Todd Bowles refused to let Caleb Williams sit back and pick apart his secondary. When the Bears lined up in 11 personnel on early downs, the Buccaneers changed the math with one pressure type in particular: "Hot" Blitzes. Against Chicago, Bowles used a whole menu of Hot… pic.twitter.com/55PYySdqAm
“Two of them were funky," he said. "One was a bad decision and the other one, the ball popped up in the air. The ball just didn't hit the ground in those situations, which it has in the past. But obviously it's frustrating.
"You don't want to go out there and throw four picks. That's never what you want to do. That's never what the plan is, obviously."
In other words, Williams' way of combatting the A-gap and B-gap blitzes is play smarter.
"The biggest thing in the frustration comes from the feeling of, for me personally, I don't want to let my teammates down," Williams said. "That's always big for me. In those situations, I feel like I did. So that's the frustrating part that lingers. I think that's what lingers.
Highest blitzes faced per dropback rate this season Bears              45.8% Bills                  37.9% Falcons           37.5% Colts                36.1% Browns           35.8% pic.twitter.com/JIWrGQaD8o
"But the other half of it is, like I said, I've thrown three picks before in big games. I've thrown picks before, picks that seal the game and things like that. So I'll move on from it, I've moved on from it. It's more of a how can I get better, what can I be better at; just finding ways to be more consistent.In those other situations where I'm not making a dumb decision like the first one, I'm trying to either get it out of bounds, to just juice it out of bounds."
Williams should know how to handle the pressure from such blitzes by now. Per Pro Football Reference, he faced more blitzes last year than anyone in the league at 174. This year it's come at about the same rate or slightly even higher, but he's not at the top of the league with 100 blitzes faced. Jordan Love has faced 132.  The 100 blitzes if fourth most.
After what happened against Tampa Bay, he can expect the number to start going up unless it's nipped in the bud soon.
“Under pressure Caleb Williams is very pedestrian.” Gerald McCoy doesn’t think Caleb Williams can handle Todd Bowles Blitz package and doesn’t think the WRs can consistently get open vs the Bucs. 👀 #DaBears #Bears pic.twitter.com/jzo5Zm9Z1S

title: 'One Call Going To Cincinnati, Another Staying Here' - Arnold Ebiketie Reacts to Failed Bengals Trade
full_text:
Arnold Ebiketie doesn't hold any ill will toward the Bengals after his botched trade last week. The Eagles defensive end spoke to the media at his locker on Wednesday and gave his take on the odd saga.
Cincinnati was going to trade Philadelphia a sixth-round pick to bring him in for the rest of the 2026 season, but cancelled the trade after discovering it would also cost them a third-round compensatory pick in 2027.
A whirlwind day for the veteran pass rusher.
"One call I was going to Cincinnati, another call I was staying here," Ebiketie said. "So, well, I wasn't mad at the fact that I was staying. So, I got back to my bye week. That was the best part about it ... probably two hours. I would say so because I was out getting breakfast. I had to drive back home. By the time I was about to start packing, I got the news I wasn't going anymore.
"Thinking, trying to figure out how I'm gonna ship my car. I gotta pack. I got a flight that's booked. I got to spend time with my kids for a little bit, so that was alright."
The Bengals didn't lack defensive impact on Sunday night, but it still would've been nice to add a depth piece like Ebekitie while Cashius Howell misses extended time on injured reserve.
Cincinnati did not end up making any trades to add talent at the deadline as they rely on the strength of their 2026 roster build entering the season to attack a Super Bowl run.
It's all water under the bridge for Ebiketie, who could be a Bengal next year. He is winding down a one-year, $4 million deal with a Philadelphia team that's basically just playing out the string of games in a lost season.
"A lot of people ask me, but I wouldn't say it makes me feel awkward. I mean it's just football," the veteran noted. "I'm back at work. I mean, gotta get ready to go and play Pittsburgh this weekend. So, me, I'm just normal."

title: Amarius Mims Earns High Praise For Stellar Start To 2026 Campaign
full_text:
The Cincinnati Bengals recently embarked on what was one of the league’s most highly anticipated fixtures of the season last Sunday, as they took on AFC North rival, the Pittsburgh Steelers in what turned into a dominant 38-18 Cincinnati win.
Following the big win, Zac Taylor's side propped to 7-2, including a new divisional lead as Sunday's win pipped them over the Steelers. A reversal from when the two sides met in the tail end of September, a 30-27 thriller saw the Bengals blink late, leading to a Pittsburgh win.
While the traveling support emptied out of Acrisure Stadium with their heads drooped in late September, there was one immense positive that went under the radar. Amarius Mims’ elite performance.
That Sunday, Mims was pitted against one of the NFL’s best linebackers, T.J. Watt, and Mims snuffed out every attack from Watt, showcasing the development forecasted by several Bengals linemen during the offseason. Of all the things that makes Mims one of the most exciting prospects is that the 2024 NFL Draft pick is just 24 years old.
Ahead of the two's second meeting,  Pittsburgh defensive coordinator Patrick Graham spoke on the development of Mims.
Bengals RT Amarius Mims has been one of the best OT in football this year. Steelers DC Patrick Graham says there's a lot that he does well, and there's still more he can be even better at: "Well, you got to thank his parents first and foremost. 36 inch arms, 6'8. They trust him…
The former Georgia Bulldog has officially become a standout pass-blocker, as Mims has compiled a 79.9 Pro Football Focus pass-blocking grade, which ranks him No. 13 of a qualifying 71 tackles in the league. Mims’ overall grade is watered down thanks to a 59.3 run-block grade that puts him at 570th against the run.
Overall, Mims currently sits at a 72.8, which slots him in at No. 23.
For an offense that is predicated on an elite passing attack, that averages 38 attempts per game through the air against roughly 22 on the ground, Mims’ liabilities on the ground can be slightly forgiven.
In the Bengals' Week 10 win, Mims finished with a 74.9 overall grade, on 63 snaps, and like he did earlier in the season, Mims kept Watt quiet, playing a pivotal part in the relaxing Sunday night victory.
One of the most common coach-speak sayings is that the game is won in the trenches, and while the Bengals are still miles away from a successful season, performers like Mims will account for many more wins than losses.

title: Bengals Veteran Jonathan Allen Reveals What Impresses Him Most About Joe Burrow
full_text:
Joe Burrow locked himself in as the MVP frontrunner after he and the Bengals offense obliterated the Steelers defense at every level. Veteran defensive tackle and teammate Jonathan Allen appeared on the Up & Adams show and pointed out Burrow's ability to handle pressure in the pocket. Allen labeled this as a trait that places him on the level of all-time greats, Tom Brady and Drew Brees.
"When I look at Joe, the thing that is so impressive for me is how he handles pressure in the pocket," Allen said . "His ability to move around the pocket, avoid sacks, and then make perfect throws on the run that only his receivers can catch."
Allen praised his other teammates, Ja'Marr Chase, Tee Higgins, and Dohnte Meyers, saying they, along with Burrow, make the offense fun to watch for him and the rest of the defense on the sideline. He also emphasized how hungry the team is to keep winning, saying they don't feel comfortable or satisfied.
"When you're throwing to guys like Ja'Marr (Chase), Tee (Higgins), and Donnie (Dohnte Meyers), it's so fun to watch. We're on the same team but half the time I'm out there just observing as a fan," Allen said. "This team is just so hungry. We're not comfortable, we're not satisfied with what we've done so far. We realize it's only November."
Burrow has preached a similar message to Allen. He clarified after Sunday night's win over the Steelers that seven wins are still not enough and that there is still a long season ahead.
"Seven wins certainly isn't going to do anything for you, and nobody's winning championships in Week 10 so it's a big win but we got a long way to go," Burrow said.
There is clear urgency that continues to overflow within the Bengals locker room, and they should continue to carry that into a Monday Night Football matchup against the Commanders this week.
Cincinnati is in firm control of the AFC North, but they could put themselves in position for one of the AFC's top playoff seeds if they can continue to win. Burrow and the Bengals will try to win their sixth-straight game on Monday night. The Commanders are hoping to keep pace in the NFC East race.

title: Former Bengals Star Drops Key Reason Why Joe Burrow is NFL's Best Quarterback
full_text:
Former Bengals wide receiver and current NFL analyst Andrew Hawkins dropped some big praise for Cincinnati star Joe Burrow this week.
He appeared on the Dan Le Batard Show and broke down why Burrow is the best quarterback in the NFL this season, along with a secret superpower that helps him stay around the top year in and year out.
Statistically, no passer in the league has touched Burrow this season, ranking first in the following categories so far: Yards Per Game, Completions, Completion%, Adjusted Comp %, Passing TD, Total Touchdowns, NFL Passer Rating, PFF Overall Grade, PFF Passing grade, ESPN QBR.
"I think for Joe Burrow, he is the best quarterback when healthy in the NFL," Hawkins said on the show. "I think what this year is showing us is it's always been the case. Does that mean he's perfect every time? No, but he just plays the position better than anybody. And I'm not excluding anybody from that conversation. That is the Mahomeses. That is Josh Allen. The Lamars. When Joe Burrow is healthy and protected, he is just a savant when he is in the pocket."
Hawkins got solid quarterback play lining up with Andy Dalton from 2011-13, but he's never played with a passer close to the caliber of Burrow.
Burrow's unwavering, fearless mentality helps him make all the great throws and can get him in hot water too.
"Joe Burrow doesn't have that, and so it's a weird thing. It's why he gets injured as much as he does," Hawkins said about his fearlessness. "Because he doesn't have a certain regard for his body and very dangerous proximity to defenders, which allows him to wait to the very last possible second to throw passes and to just again be laser-like and evaluating the defense and not worry about his own livelihood, and that's why he's special because there are quarterbacks that are scared to death, and you can see it the moment they take the snap; they can't wait to get the football out.
"For Joe Burrow, he has that very weird thing that he's born with that you can't teach; you can't learn it in college, high school, or the pros. No guru can give it to you. He has it mixed with the other qualities. That's why he's better than everybody else."

title: Joe Burrow Wins Cincinnati Bengals' 5th AFC Player of the Week Award of the Season
full_text:
For the fourth time in four games, a member of the Cincinnati Bengals has been named AFC Player of the Week.
And for the second time in that span, it’s quarterback Joe Burrow.
The league named Burrow the AFC Offensive Player of the Week following his performance against the Pittsburgh Steelers in which he completed 35 of 44 passes for 409 yards and four touchdowns.
“He’s just on it,” Bengals head coach Zac Taylor said of Burrow after the win. “I thought the protection was really good. There are times that they are going to create some movement, but its blocked movement. I think Joe did an excellent job keeping his eyes down the field and finding guys for some big plays. Those guys made big plays and tremendous catches — all of those guys really. Everyone stepped up and made some plays for us.
“Obviously, he (Burrow) set the tone.”
It’s the 10th career Player of the Week honor for Burrow, who also won in Week 7 for his performance against the Baltimore Ravens. He surpasses Boomer Esiason for the most in franchise history.
That same week punter Ryan Rehkow earned the AFC Special Teams Player of the Week, and the following Sunday, wide receiver Tee Higgins took home the Offensive Player of the Week for his big game against the Tennessee Titans.
It was the first career weekly honor for both Higgins and Rehkow.
Back in Week 1, Bengals kicker Evan McPherson was named the Special Teams Player of the Week.
With five player of the week awards already, the Bengals are closing in on the franchise record of seven, which was set in 2021 season. Second most is six, which occurred in 2022.
The NFL record for most career player of the week awards belongs to Tom Brady with 32.
The active leader is Josh Allen with 19.
Given Burrow’s performance in each of the last games since the calendar flipped to November, he has to be the front runner to win AFC Player of the Month, an award he’s already captured twice (November 2024 and December 2024).
“This is just how he is,” Taylor said when asked how Burrow is in such a good rhythm. “I feel like I’ve seen him in this rhythm quite a bit. He has a lot of confidence. Like I’ve said before, the offensive line is blocking so well, it allows us to play confident. At one point we had 24 passes and six runs. It is what it is. As long as these guys are doing that and we are making our way, that’s how it’s going to be.”

title: Former Super Bowl Champion Details Why Bengal CAN'T Win Super Bowl During 2026 Season
full_text:
Former Super Bowl champion Jeff Saturday isn't buying the Bengals' chances to win it all this year. He appeared on ESPN's Get Up this week and highlighted how Cincinnati's lack of a heavy rushing attack will be their downfall in the playoffs.
Cincinnati is tied with the Packers for the fewest carries per game (21.9) because they have the best passer on Earth in Joe Burrow. Still, they rank in the top half of rushing efficiency metrics despite the low volume.
"I don't think so," Saturday said about them winning the Super Bowl. "I think you play into the other team's hands too much. You depend on weather. You depend on the ball bouncing your way; you depend on offensive line help, all of those things. It's high risk and high reward the way they're throwing it around. Where it's lower risk, high reward when you can run it and be efficient that way.
"I can think back to Peyton Manning, all the different records he was setting, when we finally won the Super Bowl, it was through the run game, right? We rushed the ball for almost 200 yards. All of those things are important. I know Steve (Smith) thinks that receivers win it all. That's just not how it works. I wish it did work that way."
There isn't much evidence this decade that you have to run the ball at a high-volume, elite level to win a title.
SB Champs by rushing success rate this decade: Tampa Bay (22nd during the 2020 season), Los Angeles Rams (20th), Kansas City (sixth), Kansas City (26th), Philadelphia (ninth), Seattle (23rd).
Cincinnati is right in the middle of the pack this season, at 13th in rushing success rate and 14th in rushing EPA. That's perfectly good enough to win a Super Bowl while adding the second-best passing EPA/success rate mark in the NFL.
The Bengals should not be running the ball more; they just need to maintain this efficiency at the current rushing volume level. The days of only winning titles by pounding the football and shortening games to win with defense are long gone.
You have to be able to dial up explosive passes consistently to win titles in the NFL, and the Bengals clearly can do that. Since Week 5, Cincinnati's offense ranks first in EPA/play with a 0.263 mark. That's double the next closest offense in the 49ers, and shows just how nuclear this team has been to opposing defenses since Burrow got into the rhythm of the season.

full_text:
For the second year in a row, the Cincinnati Bengals are getting Bill Vinovich as the referee in Week 11.
Last year it was a road game at Pittsburgh in Week 11, with the Steelers prevailing 34-12 following the Bengals’ bye week.
This will be Vinovich’s 20th Bengals game as a head referee, putting him ahead of Clete Blakeman for the most among active white hats.
Blakeman originally was scheduled to work his 18th Bengals’ game on Sunday Night against the Steelers last week, but the FAA’s ground stoppage of flights Friday forced the NFL to shuffle the assignments.
That resulted in Don Willard working his first and second career games as a head referee – and on the same day Willard did the Dolphins-Colts game in Indianapolis then drove with three other officials, including Cincinnati resident Terry Killens, to Paycor for the Sunday night game.
The Bengals are 8-11 with Vinovich on the call.
The Commanders are 6-13 with him.
One of the longest tenured officials in the league, Vinovich became a head referee in 2004, although he took a five-season hiatus from 2007-11.
He’s earned playoff assignments every year since he returned, including three Super Bowls.
Among Vinovich’s 19 Bengals game is the 2021 AFC Championship Game victory against the Kansas City Chiefs.
Including that game, three of the last five Cincinnati contests Vinovich has worked have gone to overtime.
Vinovich ranks 16th among the 17 regular referees with just 12.5 accepted penalties per game.
He worked the Raiders-Seahawks game Sunday, which featured just two accepted penalties. That’s the fewest in the league this year. The next lowest number is six (49ers-Rams in Week 1 and Seahawks-Chiefs in Week 7).
Last year Vinovich and his crew had the fourth most accepted penalties at 13.53.
Vinovich’s crew has called just 27 offensive holding penalties this year, the fewest in the league.
Their 24 pass interference penalties are second most.

title: Bengals QB Joe Burrow's 2026 Season is Reaching a Historic Level
full_text:
The Cincinnati Bengals' 38-18 win over the Pittsburgh Steelers on Sunday night is a game that this fan base will be talking about for years to come.
It was the kind of performance that put the rest of the league on notice. The Bengals played a nearly perfect game against their longtime rival and made it clear that they are a threat to the AFC crown.
One of the biggest reasons behind the dominant Bengals win was the performance of quarterback Joe Burrow. While the national media begins drooling over Burrow again, his performance Sunday night was something Cincinnati is just accustomed to now.
In the win over the Steelers, Burrow went 35 for 44 on pass attempts, throwing for 409 yards and four touchdowns. Burrow finished the game with a passer rating of 135.7.
Having just nine incompletions on 44 pass attempts sounds like video game numbers, but that's just who Burrow has been this season.
NFL on CBS shared on their X account that Burrow's accuracy this season is reaching historic levels.
As things currently stand, Burrow is second all-time in most touchdowns per game at 3.33. Peyton Manning is the current owner of that record, which he earned during his 2013 NFL MVP season with 3.50 touchdowns per game.
If the season ended today, Burrow would hold the highest completion percentage in an NFL season, as the Bengals star currently has a completion percentage of 74.7, putting him just ahead of New Orleans Saints legend Drew Brees.
Burrow is also throwing for an average of 310 yards a game while having such a ridiculous completion percentage. To put that in perspective, Brees threw for 266 yards per game during the 2018 season, which saw him claim the completion percentage crown.
If you're chronically online like most sports fans, then you have seen posts where people talk about how, a generation ago, "We watched gods play quarterback." Those people might want to take off their nostalgia goggles and realize there is some elite quarterback play happening right now.
The MVP discussion now starts with Burrow. Heading into Week 11, Burrow leads the league in touchdown passes (27) and passing yards per game (310). If the game is on the line and you need a quarterback to go out and win you a game, nobody is looking past number nine in Cincinnati.

title: Checking In On The Bengals 2026 Offseason Departures
full_text:
In the 2025 offseason, eight notable Bengals players found new homes for the 2026 season. Let’s see how they are doing with their new teams.
After a frustrating two seasons with the Bengals, Geno Stone signed a one-year, $1.4 million deal with the Buffalo Bills in the Offseason. The Bills cut him before the regular season began, but he rejoined the Bills' practice squad and has played just 44 snaps this year across two games after being elevated.
Taylor-Britt signed a one-year, 1.4-million-dollar contract to play for the Colts and reunite with former Bengals defensive coordinator Lou Anarumo. Taylor-Britt is currently on the injured list with a groin injury,  but appeared in six games for the Colts and logged 91 snaps across those games, allowing four catches on seven targets for 41 receiving yards.
Ossai was a big signing for the Jets this past offseason, signing a 3-year, $34.5 million contract. He has been plagued by injuries as he began his new chapter in New York, getting injured twice already this season. He started the year with a plantar fascia injury in his foot and, after recovering, appeared in only three games before injuring his ankle; he has been out since. In the three games he has played, he has gotten zero sacks, three pressures, and nine tackles on 107 snaps.
The biggest villain of the offseason, Trey, signed a massive 4-year, $112 million contract. The 31-year-old has amassed a solid 33 pressures in eight games. He also has two sacks and 11 tackles on 301 total snaps and is receiving a PFF grade of 66.1, which ranks him 51st out of 111 eligible edge rushers.
The former Bengals fourth-round pick, who started 48 games, including the 2022 AFC Championship Game, signed a one-year, $3.2 million deal with the Tennessee Titans. He was cut by the Titans before the start of the regular season and has bounced around on the Packers' and Seahawks' practice Squads.
After appearing in only six games, with one start for the Bengals, and losing his starting job to Dalton Risner, Patrick signed a one-year, $1.48 million deal with the New York Giants and was released ahead of the regular season. He quickly found a home with the Washington Commanders and became their starting center. He has logged 345 snaps across seven games (six starts) with a 57.8 PFF grade while allowing zero sacks and five pressures.
After a one-year stint with Cincinnati, where he recorded 34 receptions for 288 yards and 3 touchdowns across 15 games, Fant signed a two-year, $8.75 million contract with the New Orleans Saints. He has appeared in eight games for New Orleans this season, logging 12 receptions on 19 targets for 96 receiving yards and 3 touchdowns while playing roughly 50% of the Saints' offensive snaps.
After serving as Cincinnati’s primary backup quarterback over the past few seasons, Browning signed a one-year, $1.33 million contract with the Tampa Bay Buccaneers in the offseason. After being released ahead of the regular season, he has since signed with the Los Angeles Chargers' practice squad.

title: 2 Browns Players Who Need To Be Better Coming Out of Bye Week
full_text:
The Cleveland Browns are heading into their bye week with a 6-4 overall record.
Over the past few weeks, the talk of the town is whether or not the Browns can win the division, along with making the playoffs.
If Cleveland wants the chance to do either, here are two guys who need to step up their play after the week off.
Jared Verse Was Really Talking To The Texans Offensive Lineman Who Just Jumped Offsides. Letting Him Hear It After The Flag. By The Way, He Hasn't Sniffed A Quarterback Yet This Year. pic.twitter.com/qkQRW8unJO
This one pretty much goes without saying.
So far this season, Jared Verse has yet to record a sack. On top of that lack of production, the 2024 defensive rookie of the year has a combined total of 20 tackles.
For reference, Verse had a total of 58 tackles and 7.5 sacks a year ago.
Obviously, when you get traded for the best player in football along with multiple high draft picks, the expectation will be higher. However, having zero sacks and really being outplayed by backups is unacceptable.
Some may blame it on the schemes or defensive formations, but at a certain point, you have to go out and perform no matter what cards you're dealt. Especially if you are going to trash-talk at any given moment.
While Tytus Howard is coming off of his best game with the Browns, he needs to perform at that level in every game from here on out.
This past offseason, the Browns went out and traded for Howard before signing him to a new three-year deal. In return, they have gotten a mid-tier starting tackle. According to PFF, Howard ranks 42nd out of all 72 tackles in the league.
While we are on the topic of statistics, Howard has done a good job in the pass-blocking game as he ranks 16th in that category.
On the other hand, Howard has been one of the reasons why the run game hasn't been working this year, as he ranks near the bottom of the league at 52nd in run blocking.
To sum it all up, the Browns need to see more from the guys they traded for this offseason.
If Verse can produce on the field half as much as he talks about it, he will be a great player for this Browns defense. As for Howard, if he can work on blocking for the run game, the Browns offense can gain another dimension and become even more consistent.
There's still work to be done, but this is the bye week after all.
After the time off, these guys will have the biggest stage in football to prove it.

title: The Cleveland Browns Need To Get This Running Back More Involved As Year Concludes
full_text:
With the No. 126 pick in the 2025 NFL Draft, the Cleveland Browns selected running back Dylan Sampson.
And within just a few days, it looked like the Browns had completely revitalized their offense.
During that draft, not only did the Browns end up selecting Sampson, but they also added multiple other pieces to the offense, including his counterpart, Quinshon Judkins . Throughout their rookie season, that draft class stood out as excellent additions. Much of that established momentum carried into this year as well.
But Sampson, who had to fill a large role at the end of the 2025 season due to injury, hasn't followed in his draft class's footsteps. Instead of continuing to play a key role in game-day plans, he has practically disappeared.
Across five games, the 22-year-old has 19 carries for 79 yards and zero scores. He has also picked up just one first down this season. In the receiving game, he has been targeted 22 times for 16 receptions and 152 yards. That isn't as much of an issue as his lack of involvement in the backfield, though.
With how dynamic Sampson is in both the rushing and passing attack, he needs more carries and the same pace of targets he is currently on, especially as the Browns' offense looks to finish the season strong.
Judkins has dominated the shares out of the Browns' backfield, taking 126 carries for 423 yards and four scores. He is averaging a team-low 3.4 yards per game , less than quarterback Deshaun Watson, Sampson, Jaleel McLaughlin, Rahiem Sanders and even wideout KC Concepcion.
Not only is he unable to break past that first wall of the defense and pick up chunk yardage, but even with a high volume, his average yards per game sits below 50.
If, through nine games, those numbers haven't grown (which they unfortunately haven't), the Browns need to make changes. It isn't that Judkins deserves a major dip in opportunities, but rather just a counterpart, such as Sampson, to balance the running game out.
Just a few weeks back, head coach Todd Monken said that the rushing game is one of the team's most troublesome areas.
"It's not a negative; it's a fact," Monken told reporters when asked about the Browns' struggles in that area of the offense. "We have got to scheme better, we have got to coach it better, we have got to call it better, and we certainly can block it better."
Since he is aware of the issues, making changes such as getting Sampson more involved could be one of the easiest ways to start making adjustments. If it works, it works. If it doesn't, at least the Browns can cross that off the list and move on to the next.
Because almost like the quarterback situation, the more you kick the can down the road, the longer you prolong the questions.
But as he has shown in the receiving game, all he needs is some open space, and he can make a defense pay.
In his college days, Sampson was elite in both the rushing and passing attacks, being able to spread the field and create chunk plays out of thin air. His speed and athleticism allowed him to weave through traffic as he averaged a whopping 5.9 yards per rush and 8.6 yards per reception.
Cleveland needs to find a way to unlock that form again.
The Browns and Sampson return to the gridiron on Sunday, Nov. 29, giving them a much-needed bye week to reset before the last few weeks of the season. They will take on the Las Vegas Raiders from Huntington Bank Field at 8:20 p.m. EST.

title: Deshaun Watson Finally Sheds Light Into Future in Cleveland Beyond 2026
full_text:
The Cleveland Browns have a nice break from playing on Sundays.
But in the meantime, that leaves plenty of opportunities for the media to poke and pry.
On Wednesday, Nov. 18, Browns quarterback Deshaun Watson was asked by media on whether he would return to the Browns or not following the 2026 campaign. The 31-year-old is in the final year of his $230 million contract.
"That’s up to my agent. That’s all David Mulugheta," Watson said with a laugh. "I don't even worry about that...my future, no matter what that holds, is all in God's hands...
“...Ultimately, it’s up to the front office. It’s up to Jimmy and Dee. It’s up to AB. It’s up to Coach Monken and the city. All I can do is continue to play good football, win games, and then let them kind of figure out what they want to do for the future.”
Browns QB Deshaun Watson was asked when he thinks is the appropriate time to discuss his future in Cleveland. Watson: “That’s up to my agent. That’s all David Mulugheta.” pic.twitter.com/iKDpjNJ3T9
This offseason, he is expected to command a deal anywhere from $ 18 to $ 25 million across two to three years , based on where the quarterback market is currently at, according to Spotrac. The Browns, who have already given Watson quite a bit of money over the last few years, are likely going to mull over the decision into the offseason.
But he has played well this season, and if he leads the Browns to the playoffs, it is going to be hard to deny a return to Cleveland in 2027.
After all, it finally seems like he is coming around as well.
Across nine starts this season, he has 2,118 yards, seven touchdowns and four interceptions through the air, with three straight 300-yard passing games, all while flashing more capabilities in the rushing attack. He has tucked the ball 59 times this year, rushing for 266 yards and two touchdowns.
Earlier in the season, head coach Todd Monken stressed that the coaching staff was working to make Watson more comfortable with his legs this season. Well, it seems that whatever they did behind the scenes worked, as many times he has finished as the Browns' leading rusher in a game.
Watson went on to credit Monken for his ability to grow and find success this season, which also makes his exit from Cleveland less likely, at least on his end, if he has a say.
"I think the big thing is he took the time to get to know me," Watson said. "He took time to really understand the situation, instead of just writing stories and taking what the media is saying about me when they don't really know. I think, being able to sit down and talk and see the bigger picture... he understands, of course, I am not broken.
"I had a lot of personal things going on; I had a lot of injuries going on... and I think anybody that has dealt with what I have had to deal with is going to struggle and have some ups and downs, too... you learn from it. You grow from it... he believed in me."
During camp and the preseason it didn’t look good for Deshaun Watson, but he credits head coach Todd Monken’s people skills for helping him get on track #Browns pic.twitter.com/CBnBR1E02o
It will be intriguing to see the type of contract he demands, especially if he finishes the year at the pace he is currently holding. The Browns have second-year quarterback Shedeur Sanders chomping at the bit, and if Watson leaves, it would become his show on a much cheaper deal.
But winning does matter, and Watson is leading the Browns to many.
The Browns and Watson return to the gridiron on Sunday, Nov. 29, at 8:20 p.m. EST for a primetime game against the Las Vegas Raiders.
Cade Cracas is a sports media professional with experience in play-by-play, broadcasting and digital storytelling. He is a recent graduate of Ashland University with degrees in digital media production and journalism.

title: Browns Have One Major Problem to Fix During Their Much-Needed Bye Week
full_text:
The Cleveland Browns can't run the football.
Let's just say it how it is.
To begin the 2026 NFL regular season, the Browns entered as one of the league's most unexpected sides. Not because they made a bunch of high-level additions, but because they made a few small, team-fitting moves.
Offensively, they added a whole new chunk of youngsters through the NFL Draft, all while bringing in some veterans through free agency and trades.
But unfortunately, the changes made to the offensive line haven't quite panned out the way the front office had hoped they would.
Through the first half of the year, the Browns are 6-4, yet the offensive line has hurt them countless times. The pass protection has led to starting quarterbacks Deshaun Watson and Shedeur Sanders being sacked a whopping 42 times, while the rushing game has barely been able to get out of the backfield, averaging a measly 3.8 yards per attempt.
That's not going to cut it long-term, especially if the Browns want to legitimately compete in the playoffs.
During the bye week, the Browns must focus on finding more success for the offensive line. According to Pro Football Focus, the unit ranks 19th overall out of 32 teams.
Watson and company will be okay in the passing game, but if that rushing attack can't get going, the Browns are going to be limited.
Through nine games, Judkins has rushed for 423 yards and four scores on 126 attempts, all while picking up 22 first downs along the way. He is only averaging 3.4 yards per attempt , though, and 47 yards per game.
That just isn't enough, especially when the Browns' offense is trying to expand the passing game more.
But it isn't all Judkins' fault.
Rookies Austin Barber and Spencer Fano, who have stolen much of the offensive line's spotlight this season, have done a good job at protecting the pass, but even they both have struggled in the rushing game. Fano's ranking sits at 26th out of 72 in the league , while Barber's is 25th out of 77.
The rest of the group, Elgton Jenkins (29th/35), Zion Johnson (26th/77) and Tytus Howard (52nd/72), all need to make better strides in their ability to free up lanes for both Judkins and counterpart Dylan Sampson.
While Judkins' numbers are down , Sampson's usage is practically nothing.
He was injured in the early parts of the season, but has still not been in the equation much when healthy. Averaging more yards than Judkins, though, he has 19 carries for 79 yards and zero scores. Jaleel McLaughlin, who got a lot of work when both backs were injured, also has been pretty effective in limited opportunities . He has 11 carries for 72 yards and one touchdown.
The offensive line may not be all to blame for the rushing attack's struggles this season, but the protection and ability to free up lanes start with them.
From there, the coaching staff needs to find better usage of Judkins, Sampson and McLaughlin, giving each a chance to establish themselves in a running back room that is averaging well below 100 yards per game.
After all, somehow, Watson ends up carrying the total rushing yards in a game at times.
The Browns are a really well-rounded side, but it is obvious that the running game is lackluster. If they can make ample improvements during the bye week and come back out on the other side stronger, they will be better positioned to not just make a push for the playoffs, but for the top spot in the AFC North as well.
Cade Cracas is a sports media professional with experience in play-by-play, broadcasting and digital storytelling. He is a recent graduate of Ashland University with degrees in digital media production and journalism.

title: Cleveland’s 6-4 Start Has Put This Unexpected Browns Storyline in the Spotlight
full_text:
The Cleveland Browns enter their bye week with a surprising 6-4 record and sit in the last wild card spot. They were projected to have five wins, which they have already exceeded. Each of their six wins has been of the fourth-quarter comeback variety.
No one is more emblematic of their success than Deshaun Watson.
Coming off the lack of success, baggage, and a host of injuries since an all-time failure of a trade , Watson’s career was considered over. However, in his fifth season in a Browns uniform, his resurgence was not an expected storyline going into the bye week.
Todd Monken pitted Watson against Shedeur Sanders in training camp to find a starting quarterback. Reports out of training camp were not good for either quarterback, and videos came out of practice of the football hitting the ground. Then the final nail in Watson’s career was just about hammered in during the preseason.
Sanders got the start in the second preseason game , and Watson relieved him in the second half. After an optimistic first half from Sanders, Watson came in and missed a lot of throws. The fans sensed that this could be their last time having to watch Watson, and the boos were heard through the television.
After the game, Watson spoke to the media and called out the fans for their actions. Monken still believed in Watson and named him the starting quarterback. Fans and pundits alike were shocked and it was only a matter of time before the offense got handed over to Sanders. Then the Browns got walloped against Jacksonville in their first game, and the offense looked lost.
Reports were that if they lost their second game in Tampa Bay, then Sanders would start for their first home game. After the first half in Tampa Bay, the Watson experience’s light nearly died out, but then came the second half that changed his career.
They came back and won against their former first-overall pick, Baker Mayfield, and Watson kept his job. He did not relinquish it as he continued to provide incredible play in the fourth quarter on their way to five more wins.
The performance has not always been pretty, but Watson has made play after play when it counted the most. He has looked more comfortable in the offense each week, evidenced by him throwing for 300 yards in each of his last three games. The offense was at its best down 17-0 last week against the Houston Texans when Watson started to show off his arm.
Watson threw the ball downfield more than ever as a Cleveland Brown on Sunday, which led to big plays. He is not only affecting the offense with his arm, but he has been just as important on the ground. Watson is second on the team in rushing yards and has been able to escape collapsed pockets to gain crucial first downs.
Last week, Monken opened up the offense by running read options with Watson. He led the team in rushing for the game and used his read-option ability for the first touchdown of the game.
He is getting more comfortable with his receivers and is more in tune with the flow of the game. After all the time that he missed, Watson is relearning what it takes to be an NFL quarterback. There was never a belief that Watson would play past this season for the Browns, but now they may have to seriously look at a new short-term contract.
The Browns are in the playoff hunt and have been the surprise team of the year in the league. Nothing is more surprising than Watson leading the team to six wins while improving with each start .
Watson has risen to the occasion every time his back was against the wall, which was a storyline ranked lower than the Browns' playoff hopes at the beginning of the season.

title: 5 Browns Players Who Could Benefit Most From the Team’s Bye Week
full_text:
The Cleveland Browns will have a chance to unwind during their bye in Week 11 before gearing up again for the home stretch of the season, one that could still deliver a postseason berth .
Usually, the time off is great for players coming back from injury, but it also affords a chance to refocus for a number of guys who might be losing some steam as the campaign progresses.
Here are five Cleveland Browns who could end up benefiting the most from the team’s bye week :
Bond was supposed to be a big factor for the Browns’ offense in multiple receiver sets, but his role seems to be shrinking.
Bond hasn’t seen a target in the team’s last five games, with his contributions coming only on special teams, where he’s taken over kick-returning duties. For the year, he’s caught five balls for 86 yards, and if he keeps his current pace, he’ll end the season with nine receptions for 146 yards, way below the 18 catches for 338 yards he compiled last year as a rookie.
Maybe the week off will allow Bond to figure out how to get back into the lineup and recover some of the lost targets that he saw at the start of a very promising year.
The first-round rookie has been struggling off the edge lately, particularly since the ugly loss at Pittsburgh.
Expecting a rookie to slump during the year while playing a high-pressure position is totally normal, so there’s no need to sound the alarm . But Fano might benefit from using this week to take a step back, catch his breath, and then roll up his sleeves again for what’s coming up next.
Graham started out 2026 with a bang, collecting four tackles through the first three games. He has had none since.
After an MCL sprain and an ankle sprain forced him to miss two games, Graham returned to the lineup. But he’s struggled at times, along with the rest of the defensive line.
Graham went two full games without a single stat, although he did record three tackles for a loss on the road against the Steelers and a quarterback hit against the Saints. And while Graham’s sacks are missed, the Browns’ run defense needs solid improvement, fast.
The fourth-year defensive back missed last weekend’s matchup against the Texans due to a concussion, so he needs all the rest he can get at this point.
If all goes as expected, Hickman will retake his starting spot alongside Grant Delpit in no time.
The mental block was supposed to be gone. The first sack in a Browns uniform has yet to arrive.
Perhaps no one in Cleveland’s organization needs the week off more than Verse, who's working with a psychiatrist to shake off the criticism after 10 sackless games and re-center his focus on just playing the game the way he knows how.
Verse’s snap percentage on defense has dipped a little over the past two weeks, so having the bye at Week 11 could do wonders for his body, too.
Rafael brings more than two decades worth of experience writing all things football.

title: Browns' 17-Point Comeback Win Revealed Something Important About Todd Monken's Team
full_text:
The Browns are finding ways to secure unexpected victories, as shown again on Sunday. Cleveland found itself trailing 17-0 at the start of the second quarter against the Houston Texans, but rallied to win 27-24.
Much of this success can be attributed to the Browns' head coach, Todd Monken.
Monken has boosted players' confidence and created a new culture that empowers them to win in any situation. In many ways, the Browns mirror Monken, who has an inspiring underdog story of his own.
The 60-year-old head coach has spent 37 years working toward his dream of walking the sidelines as an NFL head coach. Monken began his coaching career as a graduate assistant at Division II Grand Valley State and worked his way up through various coaching roles over the years. However, he never had a chance to be an NFL head coach until the Browns hired him at 59, just a few weeks before his 60th birthday.
Monken took on difficult jobs in both college and NFL ranks to become an NFL head coach, and he never stopped fighting for that dream. It sounds like what the Browns do every Sunday: never stop fighting until the final whistle blows.
Defensive tackle Maliek Collins even thinks the Browns take on Monken's personality.
"We're a reflection of our head man. You know what I'm saying? He's a gritty, gritty [expletive] old, you know what I'm saying? And we do our best to show that," Collins said on Sunday, via Chris Easterling.
In four of their six wins this season, the Browns overcame double-digit deficits, trailing by 10 points against the Buccaneers (Week 2), Ravens (Week 6), 14 points against the Titans (Week 7) and 17 points against the Texans (Week 10).
All six wins came on a fourth-quarter game-winning drive led by quarterback Deshaun Watson.
The Browns might not have the talent advantage in most of these games, but they've shown they have the fight and heart to pull out these wins. There is no reason why the Texans should have lost a 17-point lead to the Browns, especially given all the talent Houston has. But the Browns just wanted it more, which reflects on Monken.
Cleveland will head into its bye week and then return to play the Las Vegas Raiders on "Sunday Night Football" in Week 12.
A win would improve the Browns' record to 7-4, putting them in a good position for a wild-card playoff spot.
Daniel is a sports writer from Northeast Ohio. He has followed the Browns, Cavs, Guardians, and Buckeyes for years and loves sharing his thoughts on the team.

title: Highly Anticipated Browns Matchup Against 2026 No. 1 Pick Flexed to Primetime
full_text:
On Tuesday, the NFL announced that the Cleveland Browns vs. Las Vegas Raiders matchup in week 12 will be moved from 1:00 p.m. to Sunday Night Football.
The game takes over the spot of Chargers vs. Patriots. The change comes after the poor 1-8 start for Los Angeles and the recent injury to Patriots quarterback Drake Maye.
This game will be the second primetime game of the season for the Browns, who may have some big advantages in the game.
Flex: The Week 12  Raiders at  Browns game will move to Sunday Night Football while the Patriots at Chargers game will move to 4:05 p.m. ET and the Titans at Jaguars game will move to 1 p.m. ET.
Heading into this AFC matchup, the Browns get some much-needed time off with a bye in week 11. Meanwhile, for Las Vegas, they will be coming off a game in Denver against the Broncos.
This should play a big factor for Cleveland. Not only has the team played 10 straight games, six of them have been on the road.
The other thing to note is the upcoming schedule after this game.
The Browns were gifted with five straight weeks at home in the heart of the season, and still have three to go.
Being able to get rest, spend time with family, and not have to worry about traveling for nearly another month should give a morale boost to the locker room.
In recent memory, any time you think about the Browns at home in a prime time game, you think of a memorable win.
Not only is this another winnable game for Cleveland, history also shows that their odds to win were boosted the very second the flex was made.
The last time the Browns lost a primetime game at home was week 14 of the 2020 season, when the Baltimore Ravens came to town and provided us with a fantastic 47-42 game.
Regardless, its been over half a century since the Browns have lost one of these big games, and after a look at the game itself shows why the Browns should be in a great position to win.
Not only should this be a fun game to watch, but the playoff implications make it even more important.
Taking a look at the AFC side of the playoffs, here are the current standings:
For the Browns, they are currently in the playoffs as the last wild card spot. Looking at Las Vegas, they barely sit out at the ninth seed.
Looking at the standings as a whole,  the Patriots and Ravens are now without their quarterbacks , while the Browns just beat the Texans.
In other words, a win here for Cleveland puts them in a really good spot to at least sneak into the postseason.

title: Weighing the Pros and Cons of Browns Signing Deshaun Watson to Contract Extension
full_text:
The Cleveland Browns face many major decisions going into the 2027 offseason. At 6-4 entering the bye, the Browns have seven games left to evaluate their roster and decide what comes next at quarterback.
Prior to the 2026 season, it seemed like a foregone conclusion that the Browns would move on from who they once thought was their franchise quarterback, Deshaun Watson. Cleveland acquired Watson and a 2024 sixth-round pick from Houston in 2022 for three first-round picks, a third-round pick, and two fourth-round picks.
Despite high expectations, Watson struggled to deliver in his first four seasons with Cleveland. An 11-game suspension and injuries limited him to 19 games, during which he threw for 3,365 yards, 19 touchdowns, and 12 interceptions.
Watson and new head coach Todd Monken, however, had other plans.
Despite major pushback, Watson was named the Browns' starter for the 2026 season. Cleveland opened with a loss to Jacksonville, but Watson has since led the game-winning drive in all six of the Browns’ victories.
strollin' into the end zone! #HOUvsCLE on Fox pic.twitter.com/wwrB6r3qBi
Watson has thrown for 2,118 yards, seven touchdowns and four interceptions. He’s topped 300 yards in each of his last three starts, but he hasn’t thrown a touchdown pass in his last four. His play late in games is what makes the case for bringing him back for another year.
In March 2025, Browns co-owner Jimmy Haslam said the team  “took a big swing and miss” with Watson. Now Cleveland has to consider whether he could serve as a bridge while the team develops a younger quarterback.
The Browns Owner Jimmy Haslam said "the team is still recovering from a big swing and a miss on Deshaun Watson." He adds, "hold me and Dee accountable". pic.twitter.com/okFloN5tOE
Watson could command a large amount of money, more than Browns fans may expect, to return to Cleveland as that bridge. Looking at the recent quarterback market, names like Aaron Rodgers and Jacoby Brissett come to mind when trying to compare what a contract may look like.
Pittsburgh guaranteed Aaron Rodgers $22 million for 2026, while Arizona guaranteed Jacoby Brissett $15.5 million. Those deals suggest a one-year contract around $18 million before incentives could be a realistic starting point for Watson.
That would be a new expense for Cleveland.
The Browns still have roughly $86.2 million in cap charges left from Watson’s fully guaranteed $230 million contract, before any insurance credits.
The Browns’ decision to trade for Deshaun Watson divided the fan base amid multiple allegations of sexual misconduct stemming from his time in Houston.
If Cleveland considers an extension, the team has to decide whether another season with Watson as a bridge quarterback is worth prolonging what many fans see as a dark chapter in franchise history.
#Browns HC Todd Monken on how Deshaun Watson has turned things around from the Bills preseason game where he called out fans who booed him: "When we met after that, it really wasn't about his physical traits; it was really where you are mentally and emotionally...'Did you get… pic.twitter.com/aAhPQt54Kh
Watson already knows Monken’s offense and could give a younger quarterback time to learn it before taking over. The arrangement would make sense only if Watson were comfortable mentoring that player and stepping aside when the Browns felt he was ready.
The Browns still have time to make a decision on Watson. With seven games left, Cleveland can see whether Watson stays healthy and sustains the play that has put him in the Comeback Player of the Year conversation.
Watson has given the Browns a reason to consider another year. How he finishes the season will help them decide what that year is worth.
Noah Olson is a Northeast Ohio native and lifelong Cleveland sports fan. He graduated from The College of Wooster with a major in Communications and has been sports writing since 2024. As a writer for BIGPLAY On SI, Noah brings a blend of local pride and an insider’s perspective, focusing on thoughtful analysis and storytelling rooted in Cleveland sports culture.

title: This Underrated Defensive Back Is Making A Major Case For All-Pro Consideration
full_text:
There seems to be a revolving door of talented cornerbacks in the NFL each season.
However, none seem to stick around and provide lockdown coverage week in and week out like the Cleveland Browns' Denzel Ward. No matter which wideout he is expected to cover, he plays lights-out.
And although he may not always get the respect he deserves, it should be coming his way soon.
On Sunday, Nov. 15, the Browns took down the Houston Texans in a nail-biting finish, 27-24, to improve to 6-4 on the year. While starting quarterback Deshaun Watson stole the headlines with his sixth game-winning drive of the season, Ward was just as important to the Browns' ability to sneak out a victory.
Denzel Ward is the best CB in the league idc pic.twitter.com/UX24NDRGEV
"A lot of man-to-man, a lot of blitzes … they got their money’s worth out of this week," Ward said with a smile, speaking on the Browns' defense against Texans quarterback CJ Stroud.
He finished the game with three pass deflections and four total tackles, limiting Stroud from getting the team back in the game. According to Next Gen Stats, he allowed just four catches for a measly 16 yards on nine total targets.
Heading into the game, Texans wideout Nico Collins praised the lockdown cornerback and knew the day was going to be tough.
"Denzel, man, been one hell of a player for a long time in this league. Great Pro Bowler, man. Great with his feet, hands, technique," Collins said. "It's a great feeling to go against the best in this league, man."
Ward would go on to be awarded the Browns' game ball due to his efforts.
Most forced incompletions in Week 10 Denzel Ward             3 14 players tied         2 The Warden stays CLAMPING the offense 🔒 pic.twitter.com/aZOwmivuO1
"That is what it is all about," he said when asked about receiving the game ball. "That's why I play the game. Whatever happens on the field, you know, it doesn't matter; all that matters is coming home with the win."
On the season, the 29-year-old sits at just 3.8 yards allowed per target this season, which is the second-fewest among defensive backs entering the late window.
Browns cornerback Denzel Ward allowed 4 catches for just 16 yards on 9 targets against the Texans, recording 3 passes defensed. Ward has allowed 3.8 yards per target this season, second-fewest among CBs entering the late window (min. 30 targets). @HOUvsCLE | #DawgPound
He also has 38 combined tackles, one quarterback hit, 12 pass deflections, two forced fumbles and three interceptions . His total in interceptions is tied for the most in a single season in his entire career, flashing that, although he may be aging, he is still one of the game's most reliable cornerbacks.
As selfless as he is, and has always been, earlier this season, he credited his ability to keep playing at a high level to the image of success the Browns have embodied.
"Yeah, [Monken and Rutenberg mean] a lot. Just their leadership and the schemes that they brought in," he said. "I think the entire team has bought into it, and that's the biggest thing, once all guys are on the same page and bought into the system and believe in what they're coaching and what we're doing. After that, it's just about playing fast and letting your talents and abilities take over. I think that's the biggest thing for us.
"You can't do nothing but appreciate that you want somebody that's going to tell you what it is and be honest with you and like, okay, this is what you need to do to get better, or this is what you're not doing good at. That just gives you direction and can help you get to where the whole team wants to go."
No one else wants to say it.. fine I got yall. Denzel Ward needs to be in the running for DPOY. 🔒 https://t.co/THnMBjEZad
While he has five Pro Bowl selections across nine seasons in the NFL, somehow, someway, he has yet to earn All-Pro honors.
And if he keeps up the current pace he is on, there shouldn't be a shadow of a doubt that this year is finally the one where he gets the national recognition he deserves. After all, Pro Football Focus does have Ward honored as a mid-season All-Pro selection with a 90.6 overall grade , the best in the league.

title: Mike Pettine Influence Is Exactly What Cowboys' Defense Needs, Key Stats Show
full_text:
The Dallas Cowboys are entering Week 11 with a lame-duck defensive coordinator in Christian Parker , after he was demoted on Wednesday morning. Dallas stripped Parker of his play-calling duties , handing the reins over to veteran NFL coach Mike Pettine.
Pettine will call the plays moving forward while Parker is defensive coordinator in name only, but what does it mean for the team?
Some players have been vocal about their frustrations and have appeared upset about the move , but others are acknowledging that the move may be for the best.
Defensive tackle Kenny Clark is among those who praised Pettine's influence on the team, which is clear when you look at the numbers. Since Pettine's arrival, the Cowboys' defense has been moving in the right direction, and now that he's running the show, let's hope the unit can continue to improve.
Clark previously played under Pettine when he was the defensive coordinator for the Green Bay Packers from 2018 through 2020.
Take a look at the Cowboys' defensive rankings before Pettine and since Pettine arrived, via @SMICowbosyShow .
Yards/Play : 32nd EPA/Play :  32nd Succ Rate Allow : 32nd 3rd Down : 32nd
Yards/Play : 15th EPA/Play : 14th Succ Rate Allow: 8th 3rd Down : 24th
It gets even better. Through the first five weeks of the season, the Cowboys had just five sacks, which ranked No. 30 among NFL defenses. Since Pettine, the team ranks second in the league with 17 total sacks. You can't deny the numbers.
That influence appears to be coming directly from Pettine's influence, which includes changing up the defensive front in key situations. Clark highlighted Pettine's impact when speaking to the media.
“Just changing up fronts, especially in third down situations," Clark said on Wednesday afternoon.
"The pressure that we’ve been bringing, the different front structures that we’ve been having, in our rush packages and all that kind of stuff. He’s been doing a great job with that since he’s been here . It’s been helping us.”
Pettine and the Cowboys' defense will have a great opportunity to get rolling over the next two games, with the 1-8 Tennessee Titans and 2-7 Philadelphia Eagles coming to town for consecutive weeks. If the Cowboys' defense can't look competent in those games, there is no hope left.

title: Dallas Cowboys' 3 Keys To Victory In Week 11 vs Tennessee Titans
full_text:
Once again, the Dallas Cowboys find themselves looking to bounce back from a loss . This time, they're reeling from a 46-40 defeat at the hands of the San Francisco 49ers, which left the Cowboys with a record of 4-6.
Dallas is still somehow alive in the NFC East, which is why they made a drastic move this week. The Cowboys decided to take play-calling duties away from defensive coordinatr Christian Parker and announced that senior defensive assistant Mike Pettine will take over.
Pettine's first chance to prove himself comes against the struggling Tennessee Titans who are just 1-8. This is a great chance for Dallas to build some confidence, but they need to be able to execute to take advantage. That said, here are three key areas the Cowboys must focus on to ensure they leave Week 11 with a win.
Tennessee's offense as a whole is bad and they're just 23rd in the NFL in rushing. That doesn't mean they can't catch fire, and the Cowboys should know this very well.
The Titans' top rusher is Tony Pollard, who spent five seasons in Dallas. During his final two, Pollard topped 1,000 yards and did so again the past two years with Tennessee. Through nine games in 2026, Pollard has 628 yards and six touchdowns while averaging 4.4 yards per carry.
He proved how dangerous he can still be when he had 129 yards and three touchdowns in Week 8 against the Cleveland Browns, followed by 117 yards and two touchdowns in Week 9 against the Cincinnati Bengals. He was shut down by the Jacksonville Jaguars in Week 10 and the Cowboys should take notes from them. Allowing Pollard to get hot would be detrimental to the Dallas defense and could truly destroy their confidence.
Shutting down the run is just part of the equation. From there, the Cowboys' defense has to be able to stop Cam Ward. He's a young quarterback with plenty of talent, but can make mistakes when facing pressure. If Dallas allows him to sit comfortably in the pocket, Ward has the ability to move the chains. That's why they have to get after him and Pettine needs to do so by unleashing the blitz.
On the offensive side of the ball, the Cowboys have a huge advantage. The Titans are the worst defense in the league against the pass, surrendering 2,402 yards through their first nine games. Dallas, on the other hand, is the No. 3 passing offense with 2,655 yards.
Tennessee's secondary was already a problem, and it only got worse when they traded Amani Hooker to the Buffalo Bills. Dallas needs to exploit that advantage and dial up plays where Dak Prescott targets CeeDee Lamb and George Pickens down field often. Both Lamb and Pickens are playing excellent football. Lamb enters Week 11 with 976 yards and eight touchdowns on 77 receptions while Pickens has 678 yards and five touchdowns on 50 receptions.
This is a huge mismatch for Dallas and by asserting their dominance here, the Cowboys could go a long way toward picking up a much-needed win this Sunday.

title: Cowboys' Quinnen Williams Appears Furious Dallas Disrespected Christian Parker
full_text:
Week 11 off the NFL season is set to begin on Thursday night, with the Houston Texans hosting the Indianapolis Colts in primetime. But it's the Dallas Cowboys who are once again in the headlines after yesterday's adjustment to the coaching staff .
Dallas stripped defensive coordinator Christian Parker of play-calling duties, which led to a whirlwind of reactions on social media and online. Former NFL head coach and senior defensive assistant Mike Pettine, who gave Parker his first job in the league, is taking over those duties.
It's a move that undermines Parker and essentially makes him a lame-duck defensive coordinator for the remainder of the season. It seems like a lot of people in the building are not happy with the move, especially some players.
All-Pro defensive tackle Quinnen Williams is among the players who spoke to the media on Wednesday evening, and it was hard for him to hide his frustrations. When asked about his thoughts on the play-calling shift and the team's defense, Williams repeated the same non-answer 12 times: “I’m gonna keep that to myself.”
Quinnen Williams gave the same answer 12 times in a row talking to reporters. “I’m gonna keep that to myself.” pic.twitter.com/NSGW6H9gb8
When Williams did elaborate, it was about a question regarding Pettine taking over play-calling duties.  Regardless of who is calling the plays, Williams acknowledges it's up to the players to execute.
“Everything is on us. We’re on the field no matter what play gets called, no matter who calls it. We’ve got to execute the play," Williams said, via Tommy Yarrish of the team's official website. "That’s going to be around the NFL; that’s going to be youth football, college football, NFL; once the play gets called, no matter who called it, the players on the field got to execute it .
"And that’s what we haven’t been doing, we’ve got to do it going forward.”
After Dallas made the desperation move to strip Parker of play-calling in his first season, when he is the youngest defensive coordinator in franchise history, a first-time play-caller, and a first-time defensive coordinator, the unit better show some improvement.
It's clear Dallas wasn't ready for the growing pains that come with a coach like Parker, so the panic move needs to immediately pay off. Luckily, the Cowboys defense's next two outings are against the 1-8 Tennessee Titans and 2-7 Philadelphia Eagles.

title: 4X Super Bowl Champion Heaps Praise on Cowboys' Mike Pettine
full_text:
There was a big move made by the Dallas Cowboys this week when they decided to take play-calling duties away from defensive coordinator Christian Parker and handing the responsibility to senior defensive assistant Mike Pettine .
Pettine, who was hired to assist Parker following the Week 5 loss to the Tampa Bay Buccaneers, comes over with plenty of experience. He was especially dominant during his tenure with the New York Jets when he worked under Rex Ryan from 2009-2012.
During that time, the Jets were constantly chasing the New England Patriots, and Rob Gronkowski remembers how tough they were. Gronk, who entered the NFL in 2010, was a guest of Kay Adams on Up & Adams on Wednesday and said Pettine always made it difficult on opposing teams. He also said the Cowboys needed a change and that Pettine could provide a spark.
"They always made it confusing. Mike made it confusing as a defensive coordinator every time you went against him. He would load up the front. You didn't know who was blitzing. You didn't know who was going to drop back. Those types of schemes and disguises make it really hard for a quarterback to you know, to be able to do what he wants to do," Gronkowski said.
"It makes it harder for a quarterback as well because he has to make split decisions, you know, right away on every single play. And it makes it harder on players as well if you're hot, you know, because they're blitzing, so you've got to run a different route. Just all that type of stuff goes into play. But, yes, Mike with his defenses definitely stands out. I think this is a big spark. You know, for the Dallas Cowboys as well. They needed a change."
“Mike [Pettine] made it confusing as a defensive coordinator every time you went against him…You didn’t know who was blitzing” Gronk says Pettine is the “spark” the Cowboys defense needs to turn the season around ⚡️ @heykayadams | @RobGronkowski pic.twitter.com/gKMkZ5KcQx
Pettine also spent the past four seasons working with defensive coordinator Brian Flores, who is known for bringing the heat with the blitz as well. That should give Dallas fans even more confidence that their new play-caller could make a positive impact.
This week, Pettine will take on the Tennessee Titans , a team that is just 1-8 and has a young quarterback under center in Cam Ward. Gronkowski believes that could be an excellent matchup for Pettine, who should be able to get after Ward with the blitz.
"They're going versus the Tennessee Titans, who offense isn't particularly that great. You know, they still got a young quarterback who's still learning. So this is the game to, you know, go all out, you know, to put the blitzes on, you know, to get that spark that you were just talking about, to get boosted."
Gronk added that the 4-6 Cowboys are still in the playoff race , but that they must begin to win games. That's why they made the move now, since they can try and get right against a struggling opponent before the schedule gets tougher down the stretch.
