title: Rams Playoff Picture: What Will It Take to Make the Postseason?
full_text:
As the Los Angeles Rams enter their bye week at 6-4, they are right in the thick of the NFC playoff picture. While the Rams are on the outside looking in, they are in a three-way tie with the Seattle Seahawks and Green Bay Packers for the seventh seed in the NFC. That's who the Rams will be competing with in the playoff hunt.
There is still a lot of football to be played and a lot will change over the next seven games. However, the NFC remains extremely competitive. With the Minnesota Vikings trading for Kirk Cousins, a falloff doesn’t appear to be on the horizon. It’s possible that all four teams in the NFC North make the playoffs. Both teams from the NFC Championship Game last year could be left out.
According to ESPN’s model , the Rams have a 46 percent chance to make the playoffs. The Athletic’s model has the Rams at a 47 percent chance. That’s nearly a coin flip, and with matchups against the Packers and Seattle Seahawks over the next seven weeks, the Rams have an opportunity to control their own destiny.
It's not going to be easy for the Rams to make the playoffs . There's a chance that both the Seahawks and Packers go 10-7. With that said, because of the Rams' division record, the Rams likely wouldn't hold the tiebreaker. If the Rams want to safely make the playoffs, they almost need to go 11-6, which would mean a 5-2 record over the next seven games.
The Seahawks still have games against the 49ers, Panthers, and Rams on the road. They may not lose all three of those games, but those are potential losses. Home games against the Cowboys, Giants, and Rams could be challenging as well, but are winnable.
For the Rams to make the playoffs, the Packers losing as many games as possible is the best path. Jordan Love is playing at an MVP level, but they remain inconsistent on defense and have injuries on the offensive line. The Packers come out of their bye week to play the Rams on the road before facing the Bills and traveling to Chicago. They finish the season at home against the Texans and Lions. However, the Texans and Lions games are winnable and they also play the Saints and Dolphins.
However, the Rams' schedule isn't easy by any means. Going 5-2 won't be a walk in the park. It essentially means that the Rams can split their next two games, preferably beating the Packers, split their two games against the Seahawks, and win the rest of their games. The game against the Packers out of the bye week is almost a must-win and then the Rams likely have to win two out of three games between the 49ers and Seahawks. It's very possible that the Week 18 matchup between the Rams and Seahawks is for a playoff spot. They can't afford a bad game against the Cowboys or Buccaneers.
When all is said and done, it's possible we could be looking at a playoff picture like the one below. If the Rams sneak in as the seventh seed, it's going to make for a difficult path through the playoffs. The Rams may need to travel to Chicago or San Francisco in the first round, but that's the path they've built. It will take three straight road games to win, but with the current Rams' defense, it may be possible.
If there is any positive takeaway, it's that while the Rams haven't found any consistency, neither have the Seahawks or Packers. The Seahawks have a quality win over the Kansas City Chiefs, but the Packers' best wins have come against a Chicago Bears team that started Case Keenum and a very flawed New England Patriots team. It isn't much different from the Rams, who have close losses against two of the good teams they faced, while their best win came against a very flawed Philadelphia Eagles team.
As it stands, the Rams currently rank sixth in team DVOA via FTN Fantasy and the Seahawks are fifth. The Packers rank 14th. There is a clear and significant gap between the Rams and Seahawks on one side and the Packers on the other. The advanced metrics also place the Rams on the outside looking in or right with some of the best teams in the NFL.
The Rams have done a good job getting themselves back into the playoff conversation after starting 2-4. Entering the bye week, the Rams have given themselves a chance. The advanced metrics suggest this is a team capable of making noise in January. Whether or not they get that opportunity will come down to how they perform over the final seven games.

title: Rams Film Review: New Offensive Wrinkle Has Kliff Kingsbury's Fingerprints All Over It
full_text:
As the Los Angeles Rams beat the Arizona Cardinals 34-6 to improve to 6-4, Sean McVay proved why he remains one of the best offensive coaches in the NFL. Prior to Sunday, the Rams had not run a single play out of 20 personnel this season . In fact, they had used 20 personnel on just six plays during the McVay era, with all six coming on kneeldowns. On Sunday against the Cardinals, the Rams used 20 personnel on 17 snaps, and it became an important wrinkle in the offense.
It was a welcomed surprise when the Rams trotted out in "Pony Personnel" vs. the Cardinals. First play is an RPO that ends in a swing pass to Williams on the edge. pic.twitter.com/hRZPTB87zR
In order to get into the Rams’ adjustment to 20 personnel on Sunday , we have to go back to Week 7 of last season. When the Rams were without Puka Nacua last year against the Jacksonville Jaguars, the Rams implemented 13 personnel for the first time. Since 2021, the Rams had used 13 personnel on just six snaps on offense. On that Sunday in London, the Rams  ran 13 personnel on nearly 39 percent of their offensive snaps.
The Rams won that game 35-7 and they have since made 13 personnel a big part of their identity. It may be unlikely that the Rams go to that extreme with 20 personnel, but it also shows just how versatile the offense can be and how it can adjust on the fly. The fact that the Rams have introduced a new personnel grouping not once, but twice in two years, and executed it at a high level, is something that gets taken for granted.
A lot of what teams run during the season is installed in training camp. The Rams have now done this twice during the season while preparing for a game. It hasn’t even been during a bye week with more time to practice.
Out of 20 personnel, the Rams threw the ball on all 16 plays. Matthew Stafford went 12-for-16 for 202 yards and a touchdown with an EPA per dropback of 0.89. The Rams had a 56 percent success rate out of 20 personnel. The passing game has lacked some explosiveness, but on Sunday, all four Rams wide receivers recorded a reception of at least 20 yards.
The Rams' passing game has lacked some explosiveness this year. With Pony Personnel, the Rams got 20+ yard catches from all 4 of their WRs. pic.twitter.com/0hlFHPNXEe
It made sense that the Rams tried to get both Blake Corum and Kyren Williams on the field at the same time. Corum is good in the screen game and has improved in pass protection. Williams has developed a good route tree and has had moments as a receiver. Without Puka Nacua, those are arguably two of the best skill players on offense.
Many have wondered what Kliff Kingsbury’s role has been on the coaching staff since he joined as the Assistant Head Coach. However, Sunday’s game against the Cardinals had Kingsbury’s fingerprints all over it. Pony personnel is something that Kingsbury used as the offensive coordinator in Washington and more frequently as the head coach in Arizona.
Giddyup, cowboy. The Rams are a pony personnel team now. (This is probably not gonna be a thing like the 13 personnel revolution thing, but it's still cool) pic.twitter.com/EWyfqwx2Ao
Going into the game, many would have expected the Rams to utilize 21 or 22 personnel to limit the usage of the inexperienced wide receivers and lean into their tight ends. Instead, the Rams went to 20 personnel and had three wide receivers on the field.
Using no tight ends was a staple of Kingsbury's offense, given his Air Raid background. In 2019 with the Arizona Cardinals, Kingsbury leaned into 10 personnel. During the 2024 season, the Commanders used 21 personnel with Kingsbury at the 11th-highest rate in the NFL.
In fact, Xavier Smith’s touchdown was a play that Kingsbury had called for the Commanders back in 2024 to wide receiver Dyami Brown. The Commanders did it in 21 personnel, but it’s a similar wide receiver screen near the red zone.
The Kliff Kingsbury Commanders in 2024 running a screen to Dyami Brown near the red zone out of 21 personnel. ...play looks kinda similar to the Xavier Smith TD from Sunday. Rams in 20 personnel. pic.twitter.com/1t3xkHKbOF
It’s unlikely that the Pony Personnel becomes a main part of the Rams’ offensive identity like 13 personnel did. However, it’s still a fun twist and something that the Rams can build on going forward if they’d like.
Again, the Rams ran 17 plays in 20 and 21 personnel and all 17 were dropbacks. If the Rams can start to become less predictable and marry in the run game, they should be able to continue adding wrinkles, similar to what they did with 13 personnel.
It is exciting to think about what the future of Pony Personnel in the Rams offense could look like. If McVay and Kingsbury can marry in the run game, this could be how the Rams use 3 WRs going forward. pic.twitter.com/jZZjp2tniy
This may not become a staple in the Rams’ offense, but it’s something they can continue to build on. With Williams and Corum as good as they’ve been, it makes sense to use both on the field together. There is precedent in a Shanahan offense with the Atlanta Falcons doing this with Tevin Coleman and Devonta Freeman.
McVay has now shown twice in two seasons that he can make significant changes to his offense in a matter of days and have immediate success. As the Rams get healthier and continue building toward the postseason, having another personnel grouping that defenses need to prepare for only makes them more dangerous.

title: Rams Face Critical Offensive Line Decisions After Coleman Shelton Injury
full_text:
The Los Angeles Rams have been hit hard by the injury bug all season . While they have experienced injuries in the secondary, on the defensive line, at tight end, and wide receiver, they have mostly avoided injuries to the offensive line.
There is no doubt that the 2022 season was bad, but a lot of that was because of the constant game of musical chairs that the Rams played on the offensive line. The only position that the Rams stayed healthy was at right tackle with Rob Havenstein.
Once injuries hit the offensive line, things can begin to unravel and snowball. Through the first 10 games, the Rams have only had two games in which they didn't start their preferred five offensive linemen. The first game was Week 6 and that was because Alaric Jackson served a suspension. Last week, the Rams were without Steve Avila, who was managing a hamstring injury.
There are ways for an offense to scheme around injuries at the wide receiver or other positions. As seen last week, the Rams simply moved to 20 personnel and used both their running backs in the passing game. In combination with 13 personnel, the Rams were able to get by and come away with a 34-6 win.
It’s a lot more difficult to scheme around the offensive line. While the Rams are healthy at the tackle position, Coleman Shelton is set to miss 4-6 weeks. Avila also missed last week’s game with a hamstring injury and his status could be in jeopardy against the Green Bay Packers.
Shelton may not be an elite center in the NFL, but he’s extremely valuable to the offense because of his ability to set protections. Early in training camp, Kevin Dotson said that the offensive line sees Shelton as QB2.
"He's literally QB2 in our minds," offensive lineman Kevin Dotson said. "When it comes to play calling and stuff like that, whatever he says goes. I don't care if he tells me to do a backflip and go right, I'm gonna do a backflip and go right because he's put that work in. He's put in that dedication and watching the tape, being in there with the quarterbacks to know what the quarterbacks are thinking, what (Stafford) wants this week.”
The Rams won’t just be down to their backup center. After Shelton got hurt against the Cardinals, Dylan McMahon got hurt 10 plays later. McMahon was placed on injured reserve on Monday.
Due to the injuries along the offensive line, the Rams had to put Beaux Limmer at center, despite having played him solely at guard over the last two years. The Rams then put Bill Murray at left guard. With all the injuries and changes, the Rams were down to their third-string center and third-string left guard.
Limmer does have experience at center. Back in 2024, Limmer filled in at center for Jonah Jackson while he was hurt. Limmer filled in admirably, but ranked 29th out of 35 qualifying centers via PFF. His 97.7 pass-blocking efficiency ranked 26th. Additionally, in the NFC Divisional Round against the Philadelphia Eagles, Limmer had back-to-back mistakes in protection that led to the Rams losing on the final drive.
Just the absolute worst time to have protection botches with the season on the line. On both plays, Jalen Carter feigns like he's on a DL twist, so center Beaux Limmer's eyes look for a defender twisting towards him. But Carter works back (crazy agility from the big man). pic.twitter.com/kMTeeQdrUW
It was because of that experience that the Rams brought back Shelton that offseason. Again, Shelton has his limitations and deficiencies, but his football IQ makes him extremely valuable to the offense. That’s not easily replaced.
Avila’s injury is also significant. With the Rams moving to more of a gap/duo run game, they got bigger on the interior. The interior of the offensive line is very important to what the Rams want to do offensively in the run game. Additionally, given Stafford’s lack of mobility at 38 years old, it’s even more critical to keep the pocket clean, especially from the interior.
The New England Patriots have 12 different offensive line combinations to play at least 10 snaps. That’s the most in the NFL. It’s part of the reason they are 5-5. Everything starts up front in the NFL and messing with offensive line continuity is where things can begin to snowball.
That’s not to say that the Rams don’t have depth. They rushed for 200 yards last week against the Arizona Cardinals with Limmer playing most of the snaps at center and Murray at left guard.
With that said, it’s certainly not an ideal situation. The Rams are also in a precarious position with their depth. Prior to the season, the Rams placed Justin Dedich on injured reserve. Dedich was one of the more important depth pieces on the offensive line because of his ability to play all three spots along the interior.
However, the Rams can still bring Dedich back. Dedich was placed on injured reserve prior to roster cutdowns and given a return designation. The Rams could activate Dedich from injured reserve because they already designated him for return when placing him on IR before roster cutdowns.
If that were to be the case, the Rams could go with a starting offensive line consisting of Alaric Jackson, Justin Dedich, Beaux Limmer, Kevin Dotson, and Warren McClendon. There would certainly be some questions with Dedich having not played this year and Limmer moving to center, but it’s an option. The Rams could also put Dedich at center if they feel more comfortable with Limmer at guard.
Even if the Rams aren’t comfortable with Dedich playing fresh off of injured reserve, he at least provides good depth. The Rams could stick with Murray at guard and Limmer at center, which is what they did last week.
Another option, and it’s arguably the one with the most upside, is to have Keagen Trost at left guard and Limmer at center. There is some risk there with Trost’s inexperience. Still, he did practice at guard during training camp. With that said, Trost has been inactive on gamedays. It's also possible that the Rams see Trost as more of a right tackle and want to avoid messing with his development by forcing him to play a newer position along the interior.
For much of the season, the Rams have been managing injuries all over the roster. However, managing injuries on the offensive line presents a new challenge and will be much more difficult to navigate. As the Rams enter one of the more grueling sections of their schedule, injuries on the offensive line aren’t something they would have wanted to be dealing with.

title: Rams Week 10 Snap Counts Reveal Interesting Changes at Key Positions
full_text:
The Los Angeles Rams were forced to make several adjustments in Sunday's 34-6 win over the Arizona Cardinals. Injuries forced head coach Sean McVay to make some changes. With Puka Nacua and Davante Adams sidelined, the wide receiver rotation looked significantly different. Meanwhile, the running back rotation saw a surprising shift as well. Let's take a closer look at the snap counts from Week 10.
The Rams were without Puka Nacua and Davante Adams on Sunday against the Cardinals, relying on Konata Mumpfield, Tutu Atwell, CJ Daniels, and Xavier Smith. While most of those players were in the WR3 rotation prior to Nacua’s injury, someone was going to get the most snaps and targets.
That player ended up being Konata Mumpfield . Mumpfield led the Rams with four targets, but also saw 63 percent of the offensive snaps. That was three times as many as Tutu Atwell’s 21 percent and more than Xavier Smith’s nine percent.
However, it’s worth noting that rookie CJ Daniels was second in the rotation. Daniels only had one catch on two targets for 22 yards.Still, he played 61 percent of the offensive snaps and filled some of the Puka Nacua role because of his size.
The Rams may get Adams back for Week 12 against the Packers, but it will be interesting to see how the rotation continues as Nacua is out until Week 15 against the Dallas Cowboys.
For much of the season, Kyren Williams has gotten around 65 percent of the offensive snaps while Blake Corum has gotten 35 percent. That has generally been the split over the last four games as well.
Against the Cardinals, Corum and Williams each played 51 percent of the offensive snaps. Additionally, Corum led the Rams with 17 carries. It’s certainly a shift from what we’ve seen this season. Some of that had to do with the Rams running 20 personnel and both Corum and Williams being on the field together.
With that said, Corum was also the more effective back as he averaged 5.9 yards per carry and had his second career 100-yard game. Due to Ronnie Rivers closing out the final drive, he actually ended up with more carries than Williams as well. The running back rotation will be something to monitor, but the Rams still trust Williams.
Last week, Myles Garrett dominated with three sacks in his first game back. However, Garrett didn’t have much of an impact on Sunday against the Cardinals. He was only credited with one pressure via PFF. He also only played 43 percent of the defensive snaps, which was down from last week’s 59.7 percent.
Some of that was likely due to the score. Still,Garrett's ineffectiveness while on the field, combined with his admission last week that he's not 100 percent yet, leaves some room for concern.
This is likely going to be a week-to-week thing and the Rams having 10 days of rest should help. While Garrett is back on the field, his knee issue is something to monitor, especially with him showing up on the injury report last week.

title: Rams Position Grades: Running Game Shines in Blowout Win Over Cardinals
full_text:
The Los Angeles Rams beat the Arizona Cardinals 34-6 behind several dominant performances. Matthew Stafford played efficiently at quarterback while Blake Corum rushed for 100 yards. The Rams also got good production out of their wide receiver depth. Let’s jump into this week’s position grades.
This was arguably Matthew Stafford’s most efficient game of the season . While he still needs to clean up the turnovers, Stafford threw to nine different receivers, and his 0.63 EPA per pass was second only to Brock Purdy. The Rams don’t need Matthew Stafford to be special every week. If the Rams can get Stafford to be efficient while playing good defense, they will win games.
According to ESPN’s Sarah Barshop, The Rams have outrushed their opponents by 478 yards over the last four games. That’s their largest rushing yardage differential over a four-game span since 1984, which is also the year Eric Dickerson ran for 2,105 yards. Blake Corum, Kyren Williams, and Ronnie Rivers combined for 44 carries for 204 yards.It won’t look like that every week, but the Rams have a very strong rushing attack.
For the most part, the Rams’ wide receiver depth exceeded expectations . Konata Mumpfield led the group with three receptions for 81 yards as Xavier Smith scored a touchdown. All four players had at least one reception of more than 20 yards. This group will be challenged in the next two games, but they stepped up in a big way on Sunday.
While there has been a lot of conversation around the Rams and their usage of 20 personnel in this game, they still relied heavily on 13 personnel. The tight ends delivered as Tyler Higbee and Davis Allen found the end zone in the passing game.
The offensive line deserves a lot of praise for how it played on Sunday. They are a big reason why the Rams were able to run as successfully as they did. The Rams also did it with their third-string left guard and third-string center. They will hope to get healthy after the bye, but this group played well.
Wesley Bailey has been a star for the Rams as an undrafted free agent. Against the Cardinals, he became the NFL's first undrafted rookie to record an interception, multiple sacks and multiple forced fumbles in a season since at least 2000. Aaron Donald also recorded his first sack of the season .
It’s unlikely that the Rams would play Shaun Dolac over Nate Landman. It’s a limited sample size, but when he has been on the field, Dolac has played like one of the best linebackers in the NFL. Dolac also had a forced fumble that resulted in a turnover on downs while leading the defense in tackles.
This wasn’t as strong of a performance from Josh Wallace and Quentin Lake as we’ve seen from them this season. Lake got beat on the second drive of the game for a big gain in man coverage. However, McDuffie remains a lockdown cornerback when he’s healthy, and Kam Kinchens had a key interception at the end of the first half.
The Rams had two kickoffs land outside the landing zone or field of play. They need to get more consistency with the dirty kickoff because it is something that works. Special teams didn’t have too many mistakes outside of that, which makes it a positive week.

title: 10 Takeaways From Rams’ Dominant Win: Sean McVay's Masterclass, Blake Corum's Emergence, and More
full_text:
The Los Angeles Rams defeated the Arizona Cardinals, 34-6,  to win their fourth straight game. Despite managing injuries throughout the roster, it was arguably the Rams’ most complete win of the season as they now enter the bye week at 6-4. Let’s get into this week’s 10 takeaways.
For as much criticism as Sean McVay can get in losses, he deserves credit for these kinds of wins. The Rams were seen as the better team heading into Sunday, but there was a chance that it could be ugly without Puka Nacua and Davante Adams. McVay installed a new personnel grouping, utilizing two running backs on the field at the same time. That wasn’t something that he had done prior. When the Rams were down to their third center and third left guard, they used six offensive linemen on a handful of plays. What McVay did on Sunday against the Cardinals was a testament to his coaching and ability to adjust the offense to its personnel.
There were a lot of questions about how the Rams would replace Nacua and Adams. It’s fair to say that it was only the Cardinals. The next two games will test that depth further. With that said, Xavier Smith’s touchdown was a turning point. Konata Mumpfield led the Rams with three receptions for 81 yards. The Rams’ four wide receivers combined for seven catches for 174 yards and a touchdown.
Stafford threw an interception for the fourth straight game, and it seemed to be when attempting a no-look pass over the middle. However, he bounced back after that and had a QBR of 81.9. His 0.63 EPA per pass ranked second behind only Brock Purdy. Without Adams and Nacua, Stafford threw to nine different receivers and no player had more than three catches. That’s a drastic change to even a week ago when Nacua had 19 targets and no other receiver had more than five.
This isn’t to say that Kyren Williams doesn’t still have value in the Rams’ offense. However, Corum has outperformed Williams over the past month , and that was the case again on Sunday. Corum led the Rams with 17 carries for 100 yards. During the Rams' four-game win streak, Corum is fifth in the NFL in rushing yards, leads the NFL in rushing success rate and EPA per rush, and ranks ninth in yards after contact per attempt. Williams has a role, but it may not be a bad idea for the Rams to ride the hot hand.
The Rams were able to rush for over 200 yards and they did it without Steve Avila at left guard and Coleman Shelton at center. For much of the game, the Rams were down to their third left guard in Bill Murray and third center in Beaux Limmer. The Rams don’t rush for over 200 yards without the offensive line doing its job and creating rushing lanes.
Over the last two weeks, the Rams have allowed 16 points on the opening two drives of the game. After that, they’ve allowed three. In the first eight games of the season, the Rams allowed 21 points per game. They haven’t allowed more than 13 points in the last three weeks. Sunday was the fourth time this season that they haven’t allowed a single touchdown and it was the third time in the last five weeks. If the Rams can count on the defense to play like that, they’ll be tough to beat once the offense gets healthy.
It’s easy to see how Aaron Donald is enjoying himself now that he’s able to play alongside Myles Garrett. This isn’t to say that he wasn’t having a good time previously, but playing alongside Garrett was a big reason Donald returned in the first place. Donald got his first sack of the season on Sunday. With the monkey off his back, there will likely be many more to come over the rest of the season.
Sunday’s game against the Cardinals would have been a perfect time to give Simpson some live game reps. During Jordan Love’s first two seasons, the Green Bay Packers played him during blowouts. The Rams led the Cardinals 34-6 in the fourth quarter. Instead, Simpson remained inactive, and Stafford played until the final whistle in a 28-point win.
While the Rams had their usual slow start, this was arguably their most complete win from start to finish. The offense punted one time and had one interception. Outside of that, they scored four touchdowns while the defense held the Cardinals to six points and forced two turnovers. There have been a lot of games this season where the Rams disappear for long stretches. They were in control of this one from the jump.
Nobody would have been surprised if the Rams just got by the Cardinals with an ugly win . Instead, the Rams won 34-6 without their top two wide receivers and injuries along the interior of the offensive line. However, this is a Rams team that just keeps battling through every pitch thrown their way. We’re going to learn a lot about this team after the bye week, but at 6-4, they are right in the hunt.

title: Monday Morning Rambling: The Rams Have Become a Team That Refuses to Break
full_text:
Five weeks ago, the Los Angeles Rams were arguably at rock bottom when they lost at home to the Arizona Cardinals. They were 2-4, there were calls for head coach Sean McVay to give up play-calling, and given the injuries, there were predictions of how this was just going to be another 2022.
If this 2026 team had existed in 2022, it’s possible the coaching staff and players would have spiraled and things would have begun to snowball. However, that wasn't this Rams team, and it never was. After avenging their loss to the Cardinals , the Rams have now won four straight games and sit at 6-4 heading into their bye week.
This is a Rams team that, over the last four years, has become resilient. In 2023, they came back from 3-6 to make the playoffs. They recovered from 1-4 in 2024 to make the postseason as well. Heartbreak after heartbreak in 2025 and early on this season, the Rams continued to bounce back.
Resilience. That’s exactly what this Rams team is.
All season, they’ve managed heartbreak losses to the Denver Broncos and Buffalo Bills. They haven’t allowed injuries to define them. It wasn’t until last week that the Rams finally got Myles Garrett back in the lineup. They’ve missed key players such as Kobie Turner, Poona Ford, Jaylen Watson, Terrance Ferguson, and others.
Against the Cardinals, the Rams were without Puka Nacua and Davante Adams. Instead of waving the white flag, Konata Mumpfield led the Rams with 81 yards receiving. Xavier Smith, who was cut after Week 3, scored his first career touchdown at the end of the first half that completely changed the game.
Last season, when the Rams were without Nacua, McVay installed 13 personnel that week of practice before they beat the Jacksonville Jaguars 35-7. On Sunday against the Cardinals, the Rams ran 17 plays out of 20 personnel. They had only ever operated out of 20 personnel six times under McVay, and all six plays were in victory formation.
The Rams have gone through their share of hardships this season, but McVay has found a way to get them to the other side. There have been claims that McVay has lost his touch or should give up play-calling.
Sunday was another example of McVay’s mastery. To be able to install a new personnel grouping during the season isn’t easy. McVay has done it two years in a row when his team has been forced into that corner.
Without Nacua and Adams, there was a serious argument that Blake Corum and Kyren Williams were two of the best players on offense. When the Rams operated with three wide receivers against the Cardinals, instead of also using a tight end and lining up in their typical 11 personnel, they used another running back.
Beating the Jaguars in Week 7 was arguably the Rams’ most complete win up to that point. However, despite being without Nacua and Adams, an argument can be made that Sunday's performance against the Cardinals was even better.
Offensively, the Rams rushed for 200 yards and scored more than 30 points. The defense had two turnovers and didn’t allow a touchdown. It may have been a slow start, but the Rams effectively dominated from start to finish.
A win against the Cardinals is just that. Getting that first division win is nice, but beating the Cardinals 34-6 is what should happen. It’s important for the Rams not to put too much stock in that win, but after everything they’ve gone though, that is a win they can still feel good about going into their bye week. They've climbed out of rock bottom and are ready
The Rams using two-running-back sets on offense and pony personnel is something that I’ve been wanting them to do for years. They finally did it and had success. Now, it’ll be interesting to see if they use it more or if it was a one-week adjustment and the Rams go back to what they’ve done as they get healthy. Either way, it was cool to see the adjustment pay off.
This isn’t to say Kyren Williams doesn’t have value in the offense. The Rams have found a two-back system that works and should stick with that. However, Corum rushed for 100 yards, showing off his impressive jump cut and explosiveness through the hole. During the Rams’ four-game win streak, Corum ranks fifth in the NFL in rushing and leads the league in EPA per rush.
Following Week 3, the Rams cut Xavier Smith and that wasn’t necessarily the wrong decision at the time. However, the Rams brought Smith back this week with some of the injuries at wide receiver, and he scored his first career touchdown on a play that ended up changing the game. You could see how much it meant to Smith, and those moments are what sports are about. He shouldn’t see time as the team’s punt returner, but as a receiver, he’s shown some value.
It might be a cop-out to give Sean McVay the game ball as they don’t normally go to coaches. However, McVay deserves a lot of credit for that win and the changes made to the offense.For as much criticism as he gets when the Rams lose, he deserves credit when they win, especially after a coaching display like Sunday's.
That’s how many designed runs the Rams had on Sunday against the Cardinals. It’s worth noting that 15 of those runs came on the final drive. With that said, if the Rams are going to be successful without Adams and Nacua, they are going to have to run the ball and play good defense. Against the Cardinals, the Rams ran the ball 44 times and didn’t allow a single offensive touchdown for the fourth time this season.
We’ll get into playoff scenarios and things like that during the Rams’ bye week. However, as it stands, the Rams sit at 6-4. After the bye, things get much more difficult as the Rams have one of the toughest schedules in the NFL. In 10 days, they’ll play the Packers on Thanksgiving Eve at SoFi Stadium. If they want to make the playoffs, that one feels like a must-win.

title: How Ashton Jeanty's Production Highlights Raiders' Biggest Offensive Issue
full_text:
The Las Vegas Raiders are set to face the Denver Broncos on the road in Week 11. The Raiders' daunting schedule will not let up any time soon. Denver will present their own set of problems for Las Vegas on Sunday. However, one problem has persisted for the Raiders.
Las Vegas has struggled to run the ball for nearly four full seasons. They have legitimately tried to address several different aspects of their ground game, from coaching to the running back position itself. The Raiders' front office has invested in the position over the past two seasons.
Yet even after wholesale changes this past offseason, the Raiders have again struggled to run the ball. It has been one of the team's biggest downfalls over the past few seasons, and it has no end in sight.
After hiring Klint Kubiak, adding several new players to the offensive line, and changing their offensive line coach, the Raiders currently average the second-fewest rushing yards in the league. They have finished two of the past three seasons with the fewest rushing yards.
As the Raiders enter their Week 11 matchup against a formidable Broncos defense, Kubiak explained that he has seen improvement from the team's running backs in multiple areas.
“I’ve seen really a lot of improvements in our half backs and our identification of fronts. I was very pleased with how the first half went with some of the production that we got, and then you get 20 carries in the first half, and it’s only three-and-outs in the second half, and I think you had four carries. So, you’ve got to get first downs. You’ve got to get the first down to keep earning the right to run the ball,” Kubiak said on Wednesday.
The Raiders average the second-fewest rushing yards in the league despite drafting two running backs in two consecutive seasons, both undeniably talented. Ashton Jeanty broke the franchise rookie record for scrimmage yards. Mike Washington has flashed his skill set multiple times.
Jeanty leads all running backs this season in receiving yards, with 417 through 10 games. He had 346 yards in his entire rookie season. Of the 417 yards he has this season, 306 have come after the catch, meaning that most of his receptions were short passes on which he did most of the work.
For the Raiders to have the second-fewest rushing yards but also have Jeanty leading all running backs in receiving yards cannot be overlooked, nor overstated. Given all of the aforementioned changes Las Vegas made in the offseason, Jeanty's numbers are telling.
The additions of Kubiak, Jeanty, Washington, Rick Dennison, and Tyler Linderbaum are not in question. Kolton Miller and  DJ Glaze could use improvement, but have been dependable this season. Las Vegas addressed the quarterback position with rookie Fernando Mendoza.
Those were not just additions; they were adequate additions. There are only a few other positions on the offense where adequate additions have yet to be made . Jeanty's stats confirm those positions likely have plenty to do with the team's struggles to run the ball.
The fact that Jeanty leads all running backs in receiving yards, and most of those yards have come after the catch, confirms he has the physical ability and explosiveness to make it at this level. I personally do not think Jeanty is fully healthy, but in open space, he continues to excel.
However, when he has to run behind an offensive line with multiple positions that haven't been sufficiently addressed, he and Washington have struggled. This isn't by happenstance, and after all the offseason moves, the sources of the issues have narrowed.
For a Raiders' running back to lead all running backs in receiving yards while the team has the second-fewest rushing yards makes it fair to believe the issues lie more elsewhere than on the running backs.
Las Vegas will have to aggressively address several other positions on both sides of the ball this offseason. However, after four seasons as one of the league's worst rushing teams, the Raiders' front office must do all it can to fix the issue this offseason and beyond then.
Ezekiel is a former Sports Editor from the Western Herald and former Atlanta Falcons beat writer.

title: Inside the Mind of Mendoza: Rookie Reveals Secrets to His Progress
full_text:
HENDERSON, Nev.—The Las Vegas Raiders (4-6) head to Denver to face the Broncos (7-2) this weekend, and expectations couldn’t be higher in the Raider Nation.
Last year, NFL executives ranked Fernando the best QB prospect of the last four NFL Drafts, and the Raiders wisely selected him No. 1 overall.
The only thing Fernando Mendoza has done is make his head coach, Klint Kubiak, look smart. The young man has shone, even in difficult times, and has earned the respect of everyone closely associated with this organization.
One of the many things that has impressed me about Fernando Mendoza is his ability to process information without ego. He didn’t disappoint today as he assessed the learning curve after his first start.
“I’m very thankful to have such an intricate and detailed coaching staff, Coach [Klint] Kubiak, Coach [Mike] Sullivan, Coach [Andrew] Janocko, and there are a lot of great improvements that I’m going to make going into next week’s game that we detailed on film, and those adjustments. I’m looking forward to getting those right.”
One thing that tipped the Raiders off to Mendoza as a viable option was that he didn’t watch film; he devoured it. That matches Tom Brady, John Spytek, and his terrific first-year head coach, Klint Kubiak.
Mendoza peeled back the curtain and took us inside that first film session after Sunday’s loss to the Seahawks.
“I would say it’s different because with Kirk [Cousins], it’s been his 15th, 16th year of a rodeo of playing games in the NFL. So, I would say it was a little bit more leaving no stone unturned, making sure we cover all the coaching points, as there can be no assumptions made because this is my first time doing this.”
Kirk Cousins didn’t even spend one year with the Raiders, but his impact was immense, and he is still helping Mendoza, even as he resurrects the Minnesota Vikings.
"It’s great. He’s awesome. He’s been a great mentor of mine, and evidently he’s in a different building, and I still lean on him, and still lean on all the great mentors that I have in this building with the coaching staff and other players and leaders on our team.”
After Sunday’s game, Fernando Mendoza told me that it was a “Dark day.” So I asked him on Wednesday if, after reviewing the film numerous times, perhaps his perspective had improved.
“I believe that every opportunity that I get to go out there and fight alongside my teammates, it’s always a beautiful day. There are some days you might not like the result, but I’m blessed by God to be able to go out there, compete with my teammates, and have the opportunity to stay healthy and get better every week.”
Nothing helps a rookie QB more than having the best tight end in football on your team. With Brock Bowers day-to-day and his status uncertain for Sunday, Mendoza talked about building chemistry with his teammates.
“Brock [Bowers] is a fantastic player. He’s an all-world player, and along with Brock, I need to get chemistry with all the targets, and even operationally with the offensive line, whether it’s Tyler [Linderbaum] getting more snaps with him, whether it’s communicating to Connor [Heyward], or whether it’s communicating to the tight ends as well."
"So, there’s so many different aspects of the offense I need to gain more chemistry with. Evidently, Brock is a very important and integral piece of our offense. However, we have so many fantastic targets and pieces to our offense that I just need to get better chemistry with everybody.”
Being a rookie is hard, but in his first start, he faced the defending world champion defense of the Seattle Seahawks, and this week, another elite defense in the Denver Broncos. Does Mendoza feel like it’s a little bit of a baptism by fire?
“I believe getting thrown in the fire is the best way to learn, and the Seahawks and the Broncos both have considerably elite defenses. I really believe every NFL defense is elite because when you’re playing at this level, the margin for error is so small, and all the defensive coordinators are geniuses."
"So, I’m honored and blessed to go against a great defensive coordinator in Coach Robbie [Rob Leonard] every single day, especially in OTAs, fall camp, and training camp. So, I believe that’s helped prepare me, and now I’m excited to embark on this journey with my teammates.”
Aidan O’Connell is a terrific young QB in his own right, and it is no surprise to those of us who know him how his character has shone and how he has helped Mendoza. The rookie talked about their relationship.
“Aidan [O’Connell] is great. He has been such an integral piece to my development, and he’s essentially been a big brother to me. He’s so awesome, and I can’t thank him enough for everything. It’s been a growing relationship, and I’m looking forward to growing that relationship even more.”
So after so much film and coaching, can Mendoza pick one thing he is looking to fix after his first start?
“Yeah, there are a lot of different points of improvement and emphasis, and I believe it’s so great how Coach [Klint] Kubiak and the entire coaching staff make it simple in a way where we want to have a focused and detailed approach on what to attack at this moment. I’m going to leave that between us, but I really appreciate their approach.”
Mendoza is a realist and a champion. Of course, he wanted to win, but that didn’t happen, so how is he feeling after that start?
“I’m glad I was able to get out there and create a little bit of a callus and be able to compete with my teammates. All of those sacks were on me. I believe the offensive line played great, and I’m excited to get back out there this next Sunday.”
For years, I have reported that one of the biggest mistakes young QBs with Mendoza's physical skills and athleticism make is that they run too quickly rather than stay in the pocket. What did Mendoza think of that part of his game?
“There were a lot of moments in the game that we reviewed after in the film, whether it’s Coach [Klint] Kubiak, Coach [Andrew] Janocko or Coach [Mike] Sullivan, they made comments on whatever the situation was, whether it was some inefficiency or a play that in the future we want to change. So, I’m taking those day by day and trying to improve on them.”
Years ago, during Matthew Stafford’s rookie season with the Detroit Lions, he, Drew Stanton, and I were talking, and when I asked Stafford about adjusting to the NFL, he told me, “It’s like drinking out of a fire hose.” A quote that I have never forgotten, and I thought highly eloquent. I asked Mendoza if it is the same for him.
“With the great coaches we have, Coach [Klint] Kubiak, Coach [Andrew] Janocko, Coach [Mike] Sullivan, I believe they’ve been able to tailor it. So, instead of drinking out of a fire hose, I’m drinking out of maybe something a little bit more manageable, and I really appreciate them doing that. However, I have a tenacity and want to compete and learn at the highest rate possible to best serve my teammates.”
It has only been one week, but even on Wednesday, Mendoza looked more comfortable. Is that maturity, preparation, or something else?
“I would say there’s so many different aspects of the game that I feel more comfortable with, and even just playing. There’s so many different variables that go into playing and what makes someone feel comfortable, whether it’s their surroundings, the playbook, the operation, and so all those things I look forward to learning and growing by, so I can become more comfortable week after week.”
Mendoza is the most famous Indiana Hoosiers football player of all time, but one of his favorite targets is his tight end, Ian Thomas, a fellow Hoosier.
“Ian [Thomas] is also a Hoosier, so that was a great point of connection when I arrived here in Las Vegas, and so we’ve been able to hit it off. We’ve been to dinner a couple times. He’s a great guy. He has a great family, and I was actually able to hit him in the game this past Sunday, and I hit him in my first game against the Patriots. So, there’s…

title: Rob Gronkowski Shares Strong Take on NFL Prospect Fernando Mendoza
full_text:
HENDERSON, Nev.—The Las Vegas Raiders (4-6) take their prized rookie QB on the road to Denver to face the Broncos (7-2) this week, and ahead of it, a future Hall of Famer and one of the best friends of his owner, Tom Brady, is talking.
The game changed when superstar TE Brock Bowers missed the second half on Sunday. The Raiders' offense looked promising in the first half, but stalled in the second without him. The Raiders are holding out hope that he plays on Sunday, but Kubiak was emphatic that the situation is day by day.
While sources inside the building are optimistic that this is not a long-term injury, it could still keep him out this weekend, and the injury report was concerning. Could and do, however, are a long way apart, and the team has not decided as of yet.
For a young QB like Fernando Mendoza , there are so many elements that play into his development, but none are bigger than chemistry. He spoke a short time ago after practice today about developing that with his teammates.
“I believe it’s been going great because of all the great leaders we have on this team, and they’ve been able to give me great and nice constructive criticism, whether it’s the different aspects of operation or a specific ball thrown to them or timing. So, there’s a lot of those things.”
No teammate is more critical for him to develop that chemistry with than Bowers. It takes a superstar TE to know one.
Everyone who knows anything about Raiders' brass Tom Brady, football fan or not, knows that his all-time favorite target is Rob “Gronk” Gronkowski, and more importantly, Gronk is one of his best friends.
So when Gronk speaks, people listen, and he did just that on the “Up and Adams” podcast, specifically talking about Bowers and Mendoza.
“That Brock Bowers (Fernando) Mendoza relationship needs to be one of the best connections in the NFL. If they want to win a championship in the future.” Gronk wasn’t done. He made it very personal, and he would know.
“I’m talking like Brady Gronk type of relationship. I’m talking Travis Kelce, Patrick Mahomes type of relationship. That relationship needs to build to that level, if the Raiders want to be an offensive powerhouse. It has potential to be like that because Brock Bowers is that good of a player.”
So how does Mendoza develop that? Gronk had to do it with Brady, and it made it clear that it isn’t a simple or easy thing to do.
“I don’t think it’s easy; it's never easy in the NFL, you gotta work at it. You gotta build the chemistry, and that starts with practice. I think it's going to be easier for them to build that type of chemistry, because they’ve been building it over the last three months or so, since Fernando’s been drafted to the Raiders.”
He added, “That is why I really love this situation. I really love that he sat the first seven games, because he can go in and he knows what is expected of him. He can handle the situation; he can handle defenses, he’s been learning over the last seven weeks, and now I am sure he’s been building up that chemistry with Brock Bowers. If Fernando wants to have success, he has got to get that ball to Bowers on a continuous basis and let him do his thing.”
Sage advice, from one of the greatest football players of all time.

title: Raiders Hit With Tough News on First Injury Report Ahead of Broncos
full_text:
After notching his first career start against the defending Super Bowl champions and one of the best defenses in the league, Las Vegas Raiders rookie quarterback Fernando Mendoza will follow that up with yet another challenge in Week 11.
The Raiders are set to face the Denver Broncos on the road in a matchup that will take head coach Klint Kubiak back to a place he is very familiar with. Yet this time, the first-year head coach will be wearing much different colors.
Las Vegas has lost four of its last five games. They are in the middle of one of the league's toughest schedules, with no sign of it getting easier any time soon. The Broncos are next up on the list for the Raiders.
They hope they can beat a team with a winning record for the first time this season. If they do, they might be closer to a Wild Card berth than many realize. However, first things first, Las Vegas' Wednesday practice may point to an even more difficult matchup against Denver.
Las Vegas' injury report has been light over the past two weeks. However, the players who have been listed on those injury reports are players who make various levels of contributions on Sundays. That was again the case during the Raiders' first practice of this week.
Tight end Brock Bowers missed the second half of Week 10 with an ankle injury. He missed practice on Wednesday. Kubiak noted multiple times that Bowers is day-to-day. He remained mum on Bowers' chances of playing against the Broncos in Week 11.
Several other players were included on the injury report on Wednesday, including Thomas Booker, Folorunso Fatukasi, Matt Gay, Tonka Hemingway, and Ian Thomas. Booker and Thomas fully participated on Wednesday. Along with Bowers, Hemingway missed Wednesday's practice.
Fatukasi and Gay were limited participants.
As the Raiders enter Week 10 with Mendoza set to start his second game, figuring out how to be productive without Bowers on the field will be something Las Vegas' coaching staff will have to prepare the rookie quarterback for. Last week, the offense was nonexistent without him.
It goes without saying that Bowers' presence, or lack thereof, changes plenty for both the Raiders' offense and the opposing defense. Mendoza noted how much things changed in the second half of Week 10, as the Raiders struggled mightily without the league's best tight end on the field.
“In the second half, because of how the game was going, our defense did a fantastic job, but because of how we were playing offensively, at the forefront myself, we got behind there, and so it’s a little bit more of a passing situation. And then Coach [Mike] Macdonald dialed it up and did great,” Mendoza said after the game.
“There was a couple times that we tried to check someone else's protection, and he was playing chess, and he fooled me, and he got me a couple times. And I think it’s important to learn and grow from this, to throw my hot routes more often, to throw accurate balls when getting hit, and to practice that rather than everything just being sunshine and rainbows, then move forward and give our team a better chance each and every week.”
Bowers is a quarterback's best friend, regardless of the signal caller's experience. Yet he is even more of a safety net for a rookie quarterback in his first start on the road. Las Vegas' coaching staff must have a solid plan in place for Mendoza and the offense, should Bowers not play.
As challenging as the task may be, facing the Broncos on the road will be another valuable experience for Mendoza. After spending the first half of his rookie season on the bench, the Raiders' tough schedule should only expedite his development.
Mendoza must help compensate for some of the team's shortcomings roster-wise, especially along the offensive line.
Like in Week 10, Las Vegas' upcoming matchup against the Broncos is sure to highlight the many things Las Vegas still needs on both sides of the ball. However, with Mendoza leading the way, at least Sunday will be more interesting to watch. Sunday is another step in Las Vegas' rebuilding plan .
Ezekiel is a former Sports Editor from the Western Herald and former Atlanta Falcons beat writer.

title: Raiders Run Game Struggles Point to Clear Kubiak Flaw
full_text:
The Las Vegas Raiders entered the 2026 season with hopes of being a potent rushing attack, especially after they rushed for 130 yards against the Miami Dolphins in Week 1.
Since then, and in total, the Raiders have the second-worst rushing offense in the NFL, roughly seven yards worse than their league-worst unit last fall, despite a change in blocking schemes and coaching staffs. It is a problem that may not be resolved anytime soon .
While there are several factors as to why Las Vegas has struggled to run the ball, head coach Klint Kubiak seems to be one of them, and it dates back to his days as offensive coordinator for the Seattle Seahawks last season.
On his way to becoming a Super Bowl-winning offensive coordinator, Kubiak's unit was much more successful on the ground, with the 11th-most rushing yards per game (123.3) and two great running backs in Kenneth Walker III and Zach Charbonnet. Yet, the usage of both running backs and a sometimes inconsistent blocking unit on the ground led to peaks and valleys.
According to Next Gen Stats , the Seahawks were tied for the fourth-worst expected points added (EPA) per rush at -0.09, just behind the Jets, Saints, and Raiders. Their team stuff rate was 19.7 percent, the fifth-highest, and their overall rush EPA was -44.5, the fourth-worst.
It wasn't until the playoffs, when Walker had his phenomenal run that led to his Super Bowl MVP, that Kubiak leaned on his star running back. It feels like there is a similar trend in Las Vegas with Ashton Jeanty and Mike Washington Jr., though both are lesser talents at the moment, with an offensive line that might be the worst run-blocking unit in football.
At the same time, the aforementioned advanced statistics are much worse over 11 games this season, all of which are second-worst or last in football. At some point, the coach, who could do no wrong in a rebuild, must take some accountability and have self-awareness about why the run game isn't working.
There certainly needs to be some grace for this run game, as the Raiders will likely look to free agency and the NFL Draft to retool their offensive line. Yet, they have a running back situation that could be resolved if they went back to what had been working a couple of weeks ago in New York, when Washington handled the early downs and Jeanty was the third-down back.
It seems as if Kubiak is trying everything and seeing what sticks. No matter how hard he tries, there's a chance his brilliance as an offensive mind can make him too confident in what his units can do. It's clear Kubiak is a passing game savant who puts his pass-catchers and quarterback in positions to succeed, but the run game seems to be his catalyst; a flaw that needs fine-tuning in the worst way.
In the long run , Kubiak and this run game will get better, eventually. There will be a game where the Raiders have a productive day on the ground, and both Jeanty and Washington have their most efficient days of the season. Until then, the head coach and offensive play-caller deserve a key part of the blame for the run game's inconsistencies and underwhelming performances.
Jared Feinberg, a native of western North Carolina, has written about NFL football for nearly a decade. He has contributed to several national outlets and is now part of our On SI team as an NFL team reporter. Jared graduated from UNC Asheville with a bachelor's degree in mass communications and later pursued his master's degree at UNC Charlotte. You can follow Jared Feinberg on Twitter at @JRodNFLDraft

title: The Next Step for Raiders' Offense Has Come Into Focus
full_text:
The Las Vegas Raiders' Week 10 loss to the Seattle Seahawks was more productive than the game's results may show.
After leading the league in sacks allowed last season, Las Vegas' offensive line entered Week 10 allowing the third-fewest sacks in the league. The Raiders' line allowed only 11 sacks through the season's first nine games. However, this was partially because of Kirk Cousins.
The veteran's experience factored in on several plays where he got rid of the ball in time to prevent a sack. Mendoza's inexperience factored in as the opposite happened on Sunday. As Kubiak noted, some of those six sacks were on Mendoza. Some were on position groups other than the line.
“I think overall, as an offensive line, there’s a solid first half of run game production followed by a very poor half of protection, and that’s not all on them. That’s on getting open, that’s on getting rid of the ball, that’s on play calls. It’s a team thing. So, we win together and we lose together.”
With Mendoza now leading the way, the season's final seven games will be about setting up him and the Raiders' offense for the future. Those seven games will provide valuable experience as they continue working their way through one of the league's toughest schedules.
More importantly, the next seven games will solidify where on the offense the Raiders' front office must make wholesale changes this offseason. After 10 games, every position on Las Vegas' offensive line could use additional help or a complete overhaul this offseason.
Kolton Miller's performance does not match what the Raiders are set to pay him next season. Both of their offensive guard positions are underwhelming. After 11 games, Las Vegas still does not have answers at either guard position. Collectively, the position group is derailing the offense.
DJ Glaze has shown impressive durability, starting nearly every game at right tackle for the Raiders since being drafted a few seasons ago. He could use more development, but his durability and potential, performance-wise, make him a valuable asset to Las Vegas.
The Raiders will enter the upcoming offseason in desperate need of multiple offensive linemen. They could potentially be in need of several starting-caliber ones, which is far from ideal, but it is the reality of the situation. The six sacks allowed on Sunday weren't all on the Raiders' offensive line.
The sacks that could be attributed to Mendoza directly correlated with his inexperience, which he can only get by playing on Sundays. Such sacks and negative plays are a normal part of what comes with a rebuild being led by a rookie quarterback and first-time head coach.
There are certain things Mendoza will have to learn the hard way, to the tune of sacks, turnovers, and missed opportunities, but that is the only way for a player to learn. That is the NFL. That is life. The rookie shared some of his thoughts on playing in the NFL after his first career start .
“It’s a lot different. The NFL is a whole different level, and you need to understand your hot routes, which I need to do better, and we need to understand and essentially be a master at the protection scheme, because it’s one thing when we’re in the meeting room saying, ‘Okay, I would do this, this’ rather than in the heat of the battle," Mendoza said after the game.
"So those are things I need to improve on and will improve on and aspire to improve on to best help my team.”
Teams that select first overall in the draft usually do so because their roster was bad enough to lose enough games to earn the pick. That is how bad the roster Las Vegas had at the beginning of this offseason. The moves Las Vegas' front office made were enough for them to take a step forward.
However, the fact that all four of their wins have come against teams with losing records and all six of their losses have come against teams with winning records confirms the Raiders are somewhere in between those two opposing ends.
The next step they take will require them to add to both their offensive line and their group of wide receivers. Brock Bowers and Michael Mayer can only do so much. Sunday made it fair to believe that with a better supporting cast , Mendoza could lead this team to the playoffs as soon as next season.
Depending on how the cookie crumbles, he could potentially do so this season. It will depend more on the talent around him than him, though.
Ezekiel is a former Sports Editor from the Western Herald and former Atlanta Falcons beat writer.

title: Raiders Have Begun Process of Adding New Element to Offense
full_text:
Since the start of the 2023 season, the Las Vegas Raiders have gone through nearly 10 different quarterbacks. Until Week 10 against the Seattle Seahawks, the most mobile quarterback the Raiders started was Geno Smith, or possibly, Desmond Ridder. Think about that.
In a league where the best quarterbacks are a legitimate threat to run the ball, Smith and Ridder were the Raiders' most mobile signal callers in years. Sunday, the Raiders turned the page on years of failed quarterback acquisitions.
Las Vegas' second No. 1 overall pick in franchise history landed them Fernando Mendoza. Although he showed that he was a rookie quarterback in his first career start, he much more often showed a blend of skills that has largely been alluded to in seven quarterbacks the Raiders have started since 2023.
Sunday, Mendoza displayed many of the reasons why he was the top pick.
In Week 10, the Raiders rolled Mendoza out of the pocket on the first two plays of their opening drive. This continued through the first half and was effective. Mendoza's mobility kept Seattle's defense honest early in the game, as he extended plays that would have resulted in a sack in previous weeks.
Still, Raiders head coach Klint Kubiak wants Mendoza to prioritize throwing the ball first when escaping the pocket.
“Well, remain a passer. Number one, keep your eyes downfield. Remain a passer like he did to Jack Bech on that left sideline, like he did to Ian [Thomas] early in the game, getting through his progression. Remain a passer, and then obviously protect yourself when you start to run down the field," Kubiak said on Monday.
Entering Week 10, Las Vegas often struggled to sustain drives until they were down by double digits and multiple possessions in the second half. Mendoza's ability to move the pocket and run when necessary directly correlated with the Raiders extending drives in a way rarely seen this season.
Those extended drives for the Raiders' offense kept their defense off the field. This kept the Raiders' defense more rested than in recent weeks. In turn, the Raiders' defense played the best it has in weeks, and the team was the most competitive it had been for four quarters in months.
The coaching staff and players can fix more than a few things moving forward this season. Some of these things cannot be fixed until the offseason. However, Sunday's loss was arguably the best the Raiders have played on both sides of the ball in a full game this season.
The Raiders must not hesitate to let Mendoza use his legs, even if it is only for a couple of yards. The threat of Mendoza running can help open things up for Las Vegas' pass-catchers. Maybe more importantly, Mendoza's ability to extend plays and drives will help the Raiders' defense immensely.
As much as Mendoza's mobility adds to the Raiders' offense, there is a fine line for him to walk. Mobility is a nice quality to have, but it must be used wisely to be effective. Along with better blocking, live action on Sundays will help him figure out how to navigate.
“I need to stand in there more. I was a little sped up today. There were some times that if you can extend the play and it gives a good chance to get out clean, not take a sack, and extend the play because the defense did a really good job covering, then that’s acceptable,” Mendoza said after the game.
“But there are some times that I should have stayed in there, stepped up with one hitch, and then delivered a strike, rather than already looking to scramble. And it’s credit to Seattle’s defense. However, I need to be better, be more composed in the pocket.”
A quarterback starting his first career game against the defending Super Bowl champions and one of the best defenses in the league is a tall task. In his first full football game since January 19, as a collegiate athlete, it is fair to say Mendoza played a solid game.
Ezekiel is a former Sports Editor from the Western Herald and former Atlanta Falcons beat writer.

title: Hondo's Weekly Mailbag: Fans Know Exactly What They Don’t Want
full_text:
HENDERSON, Nev.—The Las Vegas Raiders (4-6) head to Denver this weekend to face the Broncos (7-2), in what is sure to be an old-school bitter AFC West rivalry game.
Things have changed dramatically this year, compared to the past 20-plus years, as the leadership of the Silver and Black has gone from getting kicked in the butt to receiving unexpected praise . It is a truly remarkable thing.
Gone is Kirk Cousins , and GM John Spytek wasted no time signing a notable name for the third QB in Henderson, and things are following the plan.
The Raiders rookie sensation Fernando Mendoza is coming off his first career start in the NFL, and he performed admirably, so things are looking up.
Before the team heads that way, I asked the Raider Nation via my social media X account to tell me, outside of the obvious win, what they are looking for the most, and you all responded in a big way.
So without any further ado, let’s get to your thoughts.
Ashton Jeanty and the running game to be successful. The offensive line is abysmal in the running game this season its embarrassing.
The Raiders invested a very high pick in Jeanty. Outside of the first game, he has struggled to get things going this year, and while the offensive line certainly bears some responsibility, he has to create as well. The battle between him and Mike Washington Jr. (MWJ) and it's been something to watch. Waiting for one of them to take it over.
To me, it seems like the job is ripe for the picking, despite all the obstacles, and I don’t think anyone cares who wins it; just somebody, please do. The entire Klint Kubiak system is predicated on running the football, and it would be nice to see.
Will they please give JPJ 1 more shot and sit Buford ? Can Tonka please stay on the field on all defensive plays ?
I find this fascinating. I don’t have a dog in this fight, but to me, Caleb Rogers is younger; I would think fans would want to see more of him or Bryce Cabeldue, whom you have seen. This isn’t an anti-JPJ message, but Spencer Burford, Jackson Powers-Johnson (JPJ), Caleb Rogers, and Cabeldue are all fighting for their future. I could see as many as two new guards here next year if one of them doesn’t do something quick.
I have told you for years that in the NFL, the best ability is availability, and JPH can’t stay healthy, is injury-prone, and has yet to prove he can play with any consistency at any high level.
Mendoza to get a consistent play call. They came out on fire. If they would have sustained that. We’d be talking about the upset we just witnessed and our high hopes against Denver. I saw a D give max effort an o-line that betrayed the franchise QB. A lack of Bowers didn’t help.
I think last week was the exception, not the rule, but I agree that from his first week to his second, the play calling needs to be better. I thought Klint’s play calling was terrific in the first half, and he struggled in the second. He acknowledges that, but he is elite; we all have bad days, and I think we will see something far different this week.
A better game from Fernando. 245 yards 2 passing tds. I would’ve said the running game performing, but I don’t think that’s possible or realistic
Is this a joke? A better game? It was his first start as a pro, against the world champions, no running game and suspect second-half play-calling, but you are looking for a better game from Fernando? WOW!

title: From Criticism to Applause: Raiders Brass Earns Unexpected Praise
full_text:
HENDERSON, Nev.—The Las Vegas Raiders are sitting at 4-6 on the year, but to those who are informed, they are in the midst of an extraordinary metamorphosis.
For over two decades, the storied Silver and Black franchise has languished in mediocrity. As soon as the fan base went ballistic, wholesale changes occurred that, whether they made sense or not, happened, abandoning the previous work and, while never publicly acknowledged, sending the Raiders back to the drawing board to fix the problem.
At no time was it clearer than when Mark Davis and his advisors hired Tom Telesco, who had just been fired by his fellow AFC West rival, the Los Angeles Chargers. He had spent the previous 11 seasons as the Chargers' general manager, from 2013 to 2023.
The firing of Telesco by the Bolts was shocking around the NFL, but not for the reasons those judging superficially would think. With the Chargers, Telesco's NFL Draft class success in hitting on blue-chip first-round talent like Justin Herbert, Joey Bosa, Derwin James, and Rashawn Slater was unquestioned. His low was an abysmal 84–95 overall record across three different head coaches, including his last, which was an epic failure.
I have a very close friend who worked in LA with Telesco, and vehemently defended him for several poor decisions, which my friend laid squarely at the feet of an ownership group that left “Less than desired football IQ.”
As a testament to his integrity, despite my private and public criticism (including in private, offering specifics that I was aware of through my friend), Telesco refused to blame ownership for anything. He could have defended ownership in public and in our private conversations, but he didn't. It happens all the time in this league. He never did.
That is why, to this day, I consider it an honor to call him a friend.
Telesco was hired as the Silver and Black general manager, a role that lasted only one season, from January 2024 until he was fired in January 2025. ​With the Raiders, his biggest high was nailing the 2024 draft class by landing All-Pro tight end Brock Bowers at 13th overall and starting right tackle Delmar “DJ” Glaze, The Mule, in the third round, LB Tommy “Freaking” Eichenberg in the fifth round, and burgeoning special teams star Dylan Laube in the sixth.
He inherited a first-year coach in Antonio Pierce, whom ownership hired before his selection, and a WR that I would best classify, in my opinion, as me-first diva, in Davante Adams.
Additionally, he signed free-agent splash Christian Wilkins, who suffered a season-ending foot injury, and oversaw a 4–13 season in which, other than the Wilkins injury, which he had no control over, virtually nothing he did failed, but several things he didn’t do.
It is ridiculous to me that, given the quality of so many NFL GMs, Telesco is not in one of the coveted 32 NFL chairs.
Additionally, the regime change that ousted him lasted only one year with Pete Carroll and a total collapse in 2025.
The Raiders have moved on, and despite Tom Brady remaining the dominant voice, things have changed since they trusted GM John Spytek with a louder voice last year.
The Raiders' rebuild is in full swing, and good things are happening as they finally show a true commitment to excellence, not just a mantra echoed to stir the faithful.
Speaking on AM 570 in Los Angeles, Telesco said of the trade of Kirk Cousins and the development of Fernando Mendoza, “I think they played this quarterback transition period perfectly. And they had a plan going in; they talked about the plan right after they drafted Fernando Mendoza, as far as how they were going to approach this season. And they stuck to the plan.”
Telesco then dropped a truth bomb on the organization’s past, but also offered high praise for what is happening now. He continued, “Believe me, from someone who has worked there, that hasn’t always been the case. So right now they had a plan, they totally stuck to it, and it's worked out perfectly.”
Telesco said out loud what multiple people have said quietly over the years, and I have reported it loudly.
Ownership deserves the blame for the past, but that doesn’t mean they don’t deserve praise for the present discipline and success.
Telesco has the right to be bitter; his integrity doesn’t allow that. But he's a voice of reason, and yet another NFL executive singing the praises of the unified front of Mark Davis, Brady, Spytek, and Kubiak.
Telesco's stamp of approval says a lot when you see it through the lens of what he endured here. It should encourage Raiders fans.
A few simple words should be Viagra to the soul of Raider Nation. A few words that haven’t been said around here in decades: “They stuck to the plan.” You may not have expected to hear that kind of praise from a fired employee, but the fact that you are should tell you a lot. After years of being kicked in the butt, the Raiders are finally earning pats on the back.
Davis, Brady, and Spytek all got a slap on the back. After years of this franchise getting kicked in the butt, it should tell the amazing fans, who see their fandom as a way of life, that good things are happening in year one of the Kubiak regime.
Hondo S. Carpenter Sr. is an award-winning sports journalist with decades of experience.
