title: 3 Key Raiders’ Narratives Emerging From Week 10 Defeat
full_text:
The Las Vegas Raiders fell to the Seattle Seahawks, 21-13, falling to 4-6 on the season.
Despite the loss, it wasn't all negative for the Silver and Black. Here are a few narratives surrounding the Raiders based on what transpired at Allegiant Stadium on Sunday.
Fernando Mendoza made his first career start on Sunday against one of the league's best defenses, and looked the part. The Indiana product showed why he was the unanimous top quarterback prospect in this past draft class. The Raiders went through it last season, leading to them inheriting the No. 1 overall pick, but fans will look back at 2025 and live with the result, as they have their future franchise quarterback .
The final stat line doesn't depict how impressive Mendoza was in his debut. The 6-foot-5, 225-pound signal caller completed his first six passes against Seattle. The Raiders' opening drive was flawless, as Klint Kubiak leaned on the run game to facilitate the offense. Mendoza capped off the drive with a 10-yard touchdown run. His mobility opens up an element of the offense that wasn't available with Kirk Cousins.
Mendoza was tricked several times by disguised blitzes, but that pre-snap diagnosis will improve with time. You can't be too harsh on the rookie quarterback for those lapses, as Mike Macdonald has made established quarterbacks look lost pre-snap. Overall, I was very impressed with Mendoza, and assuming Las Vegas' front office adds more talent on the offensive line and on the outside this upcoming offseason, Mendoza should have ample success starting in 2027.
As noted, Mendoza and the offense looked incredibly effective and sufficient in the first half, taking a 10-7 lead into halftime. That's when everyone was available. Bowers suffered an ankle injury early in the game, missing a handful of snaps in the first half.
The 23-year-old tight end would play sporadically in the opening two quarters and didn't appear to be completely hampered by the injury. However, Bowers was ruled out for the rest of the game after halftime. In the first half, the Raiders had 136 total yards, 10 first downs, and went 7-for-10 on third down.
Without Bowers in the second half, the Raiders' offense fell off a cliff, scoring three points, totaling 27 yards, and going 0-for-7 on third downs, producing only two first downs in the final 30 minutes of the game. Without his top pass-catching option, Mendoza completed 6-of-16 passes. When Bowers is off the field, Las Vegas' lack of a bona fide WR1 is glaringly apparent. That second half showed how far the Raiders are from competing in the AFC.
Again, I don't think it's fair to be overly critical of the Raiders in this game, considering Mendoza was making his starting debut against the reigning Super Bowl champions. Not to mention, nobody gave Las Vegas a shot at beating the Seahawks.
That said, results around the league allowed the Raiders to solidify their position in the race for the final wildcard spot. The New England Patriots fell to the Detroit Lions earlier in the day and potentially lost Drake Maye for the rest of the season. Their season looks over at this point. Meanwhile, the Houston Texans slipped to 3-6 with a loss to the Cleveland Browns.
Las Vegas is now two games out of the playoff picture, with an upcoming matchup against the Denver Broncos. With another loss next week, I think you could say the Raiders' playoff hopes might be over.
Logan Lazarczyk is a graduate of the University of Missouri-Kansas City, where he earned a Bachelor of Arts in Communication Studies with an emphasis in Journalism. Logan joined our team with extensive experience, having previously written and worked for media entities such as USA Today and Union Broadcasting.

title: Dolphins First Week 11 Injury Report: Brewer Status Quo, Punter Problem, and More
full_text:
Center Aaron Brewer missing another practice as he remains in the concussion protocol clearly was the biggest headline of the Miami Dolphins' first injury report for Week 11, but there are several other issues worth monitoring.
The most glaring ones would be at wide receiver, where injuries continue to happen, and at punter.
The situation with punter Bradley Pinion missing practice because a right groin injury maybe shouldn't have been easy to predict after the Dolphins signed punter Jack Browning to the practice squad earlier Wednesday.
As a general rule, NFL teams don't have two punters or two kickers on the team (active roster and practice squad) unless there's an injury, so the Browning move should have been a sign.
As we indicated earlier, Browning has appeared in five NFL games but none since the 2024 season and hasn't even punted in a preseason since then.
The issue at wide receiver is that rookie Caleb Douglas joined the list of injured players at that position as he was limited with a shoulder injury. There was good news there, though, with Chris Bell back at practice (albeit on a limited basis) after both he and Jared Wayne missed the game against the Indianapolis Colts on Sunday.
Wayne was among the five players who didn't practice, a group that included safety Dante Trader Jr. (shoulder/groin) and cornerback Jaylin Simpson (knee).
Trader has been battling injuries for a few weeks now and one wonders whether he'll need to be shut down at some point to allow him to get back to 100 percent.
While it's early in the week, the best projection if Trader can't play against Buffalo would be for Zayne Anderson to get the start alongside rookie Michael Taaffe even if Kyle Louis has been getting regular snaps on defense since coming off IR. Louis has been used as a type of nickel linebacker as opposed to a true safety.
Simpson is primarily a special teams contributor, and if Wayne can't play again, then it would mean another game for veteran Jalen Tolbert.
Along with the five players who didn't practice, the Dolphins had five others who were limited. Besides Bell and Douglas, there was LS Tucker Addington again (shoulder), CB JuJu Brents (neck) and C Andrew Meyer (neck).
In the event that both Brewer and Meyer wound up sidelined for the Buffalo game, then we'd be looking at Jarrett Kingston, who played center for two snaps against the Colts when Meyer briefly left the game.
The Bills also had five players sit out practice Wednesday, with guard O'Cyrus Torrence's absence related to a personal issue.
The focus for Buffalo should be in the secondary, which was missing Wednesday cornerbacks Dee Alford (concussion) and Christian Benford (groin).
Furthermore, three safeties were limited in practice, including recent acquisition Amani Hooker (knee) along with Damar Hamlin (toe) and Cole Bishop (shoulder).

He has lived in South Florida since the 1980s.

title: How the Dolphins (AKA Vice City Manatees) Have Embraced GTA VI
full_text:
It's officially the day before one of the most anticipated video games of all time releases on the PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X/S: Grand Theft Auto VI. Developed by Rockstar Games, the newest entry in the series will take players back to Leonida and Vice City for the first time since 2002.
The city of Miami has embraced the game's release in a way that hasn't been seen since Los Angeles hyped up GTA V all the way back in 2013. That includes the Miami Dolphins, who have partnered with Rockstar to ensure all of Miami-Dade County is ready when the game goes live.
Something you'll find in the game is a parody of the Dolphins that has appeared on real-life signs, billboards, and art. What we know about the in-game equivalent of the Dolphins is limited, but some clues could indicate they'll be a big presence in the latest story to come out of Vice City.
Just like the Miami Heat and Miami Marlins, the Dolphins have an in-game counterpart with a similar name, but not the same because of licensing and copyright issues. The Heat are known as the Narcos (yikes), the Marlins are the Flamingos, and the Dolphins are the Manatees.
The resemblance is undeniable, with the Manatees adopting an aqua and pink color scheme, and the logo featuring a manatee rocking a VC football helmet in front of a pink and black sunbeam. They compete in the American Football Federation (AFF). If you're one of the fans who miss the era of Dolphins logos that feature the dolphin wearing the M helmet, GTA VI has you covered.
Rockstar Games has prioritized advertising fictional in-game brands out in Miami, and the Manatees are no exception. Digital signage for the team has been spotted at Bayfront Park, Miami International Airport, and the Clevelander. Manatees merchandise, including jerseys and footballs, is being sold online.
Two people can be seen wearing Manatees jerseys in the game's trailers and box art. The first is Dre'Quan Priest, who appears to be friends with the game's playable protagonists, Jason Duval and Lucia Caminos. The second is the unnamed cover girl featured on the game's box art, wearing a cropped Manatees jersey over a bikini.
We don't know much about the Manatees, including whether or not they're also in a rebuild. We don't even know where they play, as Hard Rock Stadium might not be featured in the game, unlike the Kaseya Center (Sahara Arena) and loanDepot Park (Fleeca Field).
You would think the Flamingos would play at Flecca Field, but instead, it appears to be home to a second football team, the Mambas, according to banners hanging around the stadium. There's much less information about this team aside from a mention during a heist in GTA V, in which you steal a football signed by a former player, BJ Smith.
The Miami Dolphins have partnered with Rockstar Games, featuring GTA VI advertising at Hard Rock Stadium in the form of signage around the seats, video boards, and walkways leading into the stadium. It's equally hard to miss the Vice City-themed Goodyear Blimp flying over Hard Rock Stadium on game day.
From the Dolphins' perspective, the Vice City Manatees provide an opportunity for players around the world to want to become fans of the real-life team, just like the Narcos and Flamingos. Consdering GTA V sold 235 million copies worldwide and generated over $10 billion in revenue,  that's a lot of reasons to be all aboard the latest installment.
A popular trend on social media is seeing what people and teams looked like back in 2013, when GTA V was originally released on the Xbox 360 and PlayStation 3. That includes the Dolphins, who debuted their new-era logo and uniforms at Sun Life Stadium that year.
This was the second season for head coach Joe Philbin in what would be known as a mediocre era for the Dolphins, as he never got the team to the playoffs or even a winning record before being fired in 2015.
Miami ended up with an 8-8 record, with their most memorable win in 2013 coming on Halloween night over Cincinnati when Cameron Wake sacked Andy Dalton in the end zone in overtime for a game-winning safety.
Quarterback Ryan Tannehill led the Dolphins to three straight wins to begin the season with an offense that featured running back Lamar Miller and wide receivers Brian Hartline and Mike Wallace. On defense, Wake and Brent Grimes were the stars, allowing only one game in which the opposing offense scored 30+ points.
Turnovers killed the Dolphins, with Tannehill throwing 17 interceptions that season. They lost six of their next eight games before a late-season run, winning three straight (including a marquee win over New England) before dropping their final two games to Buffalo and the New York Jets.
They didn't do themselves any favors in the 2013 NFL draft, trading up to take defensive end Dion Jordan with the third overall pick. They passed on offensive tackle Lane Johnson, who was selected by Philadelphia right after. He would go on to play for the Eagles for 14 seasons, becoming a six-time Pro Bowl selection and winning two Super Bowls.

title: Breaking Down the Latest Dolphins Roster Moves, with Another Win for the 2026 Draft Class
full_text:
The Miami Dolphins have made their decision on rookie edge defender Max Llewellyn, and for the moment at least want to keep him around.
That's the takeaway from the latest Dolphins roster moves, as they signed Llewellyn from the practice squad to the active roster, clearing the way for him to be able to play against the Buffalo Bills at Highmark Stadium on Sunday.
In an accompanying move, the Dolphins signed punter Jack Browning to the practice squad to fill that slot. Browning has appeared in five NFL games, all with the Tampa Bay Buccaneers in 2024 when he averaged 42.5 yards on 10 punts, with a net of 34.6 yards.
Browning has been out of the NFL since December 2024 except for a one-week stint with the Arizona Cardinals in training camp this summer.
The Dolphins, of course, have veteran Bradley Pinion to handling the punting duties and there's nothing about Browning that suggests he could be a long-term answer, so perhaps Pinion is dealing with some sort of physical issue.
Llewellyn, the seventh-round pick out of Iowa, had been on the practice squad since he was waived the day after the cuts to the 53-player limit to accommodate the eight newcomers the team brought in from the outside.
Llewelly played the maximum three games allowed as a practice squad elevation when he suited up against the San Francisco 49ers in Week 2, the New York Jets in Week 7 and the New England Patriots in Week 8.
In those three games, he got only six total snaps on defense and eight more on special teams, but clearly the Dolphins liked his potential enough to want to see him in action again.
He becomes the sixth edge defender on the 53-man roster after Eric Watts also was signed from the practice squad Tuesday.
The Dolphins are very light at the defensive tackle position with only three players — Kenneth Grant, Keith Cooper Jr., Jordan Jefferson — after placing Zeek Biggers and Jordan Phillips on IR, but Watts (6-5, 277) might be able to slide inside for a certain number of snaps and veteran Matthew Butler figures to get elevated from the practice squad for the Buffalo game.
Llewellyn was the last of the Dolphins' league-high 13 draft picks this year and all of them are with the team — 11 on the active roster, linebacker Trey Moore on injured reserve, and guard DJ Campbell on the practice squad.
After all the moves of the past two days, here's the updated 16-man Dolphins practice squad (they do not have an international player exemption at the moment):

title: Why This Dolphins Season So Far Has Been a Success ... Even Beyond Getting a High 2027 Draft Pick
full_text:
The Miami Dolphins are tied for the worst record in the NFL after starting 1-8 in Jeff Hafley's first year as head coach, and it would surprise no one if they ended up at the very bottom of the league standings by the end of the season.
But the truth is they're still having a productive season, and not just because they'll end up with one of the very first picks in the 2027 NFL draft.
See, this season never was about wins and losses, something Hafley said time and time again to make sure his message didn't get lost or expectations would start surpassing reality.
The 2026 season, once the Dolphins overhauled their roster to clear up their cap situation for a fresh financial start, became about establishing a foundation, player development and player evaluation.
With regards to those objectives, the Dolphins are winning.
NFL writer Jourdan Rodrigue put it perfectly with a comment that accompanied placing the Dolphins in Tier 1 of teams in terms of problem-solving when it comes to roster management.
"If you don’t think the 1-8 Dolphins belong in this tier in this specific exercise , you simply don’t appreciate the elegance of the line they currently walk," Rodrigue wrote. "(I will add, it has to be really tough on the players and coaches.) From a team-building perspective, they have struck a perfect balance between showcasing young talent — rookie receiver Caleb Douglas is electric, second-year running back Ollie Gordon is a blossoming star and rookie linebacker Jacob Rodriguez will have a long career — while not sacrificing draft positioning. Even with recent injuries to starting quarterback Malik Willis and defensive lineman Zach Sieler, getting the present group valuable experience while keeping focus on a bright future is what is important here. They have also proven to be a scrappy out, including for the talented Detroit Lions."
Because we don't like the term, we're not going to use "culture" here even though many would, but regardless of the term the one identity the Dolphins have established in terms of play style is that they will play hard.
Just check out the weekly press conferences with opposing coaches and invariably they will mention how hard the Dolphins compete. Of course, maybe they'd be saying the same thing even if it weren't true because buttering up the opponent before a game is part of the game, but it's true in this case and it's actually pretty obvious to anyone who watches the Miami games.
While there's a lack of high-end veteran talent on the team, there's absolutely nothing lacking in terms of want-to.
This is a highly engaged group, and the postgame celebration after that one win against the New York Jets, while criticized in some circles for being over the top given the team's record, showed you a group of players who really want to win for their coach.
Now, contrast that to the shot of Justin Herbert in the L.A. Chargers locker room when they were celebrating their first win after an 0-8 start Monday night, and see if you can spot the difference.
That's a team in the middle of a storm with nothing but dark clouds ahead.
The Dolphins, on the flip side, also may be in the middle of a storm but there are clear skies on the horizon.
Beyond the early positive impression Hafley has made as head coach, including the fact he has an undermanned defense ranked 10th in the NFL in total yards allowed, are the contributions of the 2026 draft class.
One of the biggest goals for this season was having the largest draft class in the NFL produce a handful of players who would become key contributors on the road back to contention, and this looks like mission accomplished nine games into their rookie year.
It obviously starts at the top of the rookie class with Kadyn Proctor, Chris Johnson, Jacob Rodriguez and Caleb Douglas, with GM Jon-Eric Sullivan looking very much like he nailed his top four draft picks in his new job.
Beyond those four, safety Michael Taaffe is starting as a rookie fifth-round pick, leads the team with three interceptions, tight end Will Kacmarek should have a long NFL future as a blocking specialist, and Kyle Louis is getting more and more work as a nickel linebacker.
And that's not even mentioning Chris Bell and Trey Moore, who also could become contributors at some point.
Another goal for this season was getting a good sense of whether Malik Willis could become a long-term answer at quarterback, and that remains unsolved for a variety of factors, including how much he's limited by his supporting cast and durability concerns with him currently on IR.
Regardless, the Dolphins always were going to need to beef up the roster around the quarterback, Willis or somebody else, before they really can think about competing.
This season was about taking the first steps in the right direction, and it says here the Dolphins absolutely have done that.
It does stink that the Dolphins have such a poor record, but anybody thinking playoffs with all the personnel losses and dead cap space they were carrying was fooling himself.
The goals for 2026 simply were different. And in that respect, the Dolphins are having a perfectly fine season.

title: Poup's Perspective: Honest Assessment of Kyle McCord's Dolphins Debut
full_text:
Kyle McCord's NFL debut for the Miami Dolphins on Sunday was fine.
Nothing more, nothing less.
It was the kind of debut that told us we need to see more before forming any sort of big-picture evaluation in terms of McCord's ceiling and whether his ceiling is potential future starter, dependable backup or not even that much.
The final numbers were pedestrian, with McCord completing 17 of 32 passes for 209 yards with no touchdowns and no interceptions and a passer rating of 73.6.
More than anything, McCord showed the moment wasn't too big for him, which actually is a solid accomplishment because there have been previous quarterbacks — and we could name a couple of Dolphins examples — who clearly were overwhelmed by the moment.
Something else that was positive is the Dolphins had a chance to win the game and we could go as far as suggest they should have won the game but didn't because kicker Zane Gonzalez missed three kicks that cost the team seven points in a two-point loss.
The question, of course, is how much would McCord have had to do with the victory considering the Dolphins got a pick-six from rookie cornerback Chris Johnson and their first touchdown was a pass thrown by wide receiver Malik Washington.
To be sure, McCord was working at a disadvantage in a way because the offensive line was missing its best player, Aaron Brewer, and it might not be coincidence that the three passes batted down at the line of scrimmage came when his replacement Andrew Meyer gave ground to a defensive lineman.
That, of course, included the failed fourth-and-17 attempt for Kevin Coleman Jr. on the Dolphins' final drive.
The flip side, though, is that McCord had the benefit of going up against a bad Indianapolis defense.
This was a Colts defense a week removed from giving up 508 total yards against the Dallas Cowboys, that was missing two starting linebackers, that lost its two starting cornerbacks — and two best defensive players — to injury in the first half when Sauce Gardner and Charvarius Ward were injured.
So, Brewer or no Brewer, this was about as good an opportunity for a quarterback making his first start as there was.
And again, McCord was fine.
But, no, he wasn't better than Malik Willis.
The eye test should have been enough to see that, but for those who want numbers, we can try these:
-- McCord completed 53.1 percent of his passes; Willis topped that number in six of his eight starts and is at 58.2 on the season.
-- McCord's passer rating didn't match Willis' season number of 76.1, which includes figures of 130.7 and 92.1 against the Jets and Patriots before that number dropped to 50.1 against the Lions when he was visibly compromised by the groin injury that landed him on injured reserve.
-- In terms of yardage, McCord's number was higher than Willis' season average of 176.1, but Willis has four games between 208 and 220 yards.
In terms of certain analytics, there were some favoring McCord and some favoring Willis.
But one thing that was clear is the Dolphins designed a game plan to make things simpler for McCord, highlighted by a couple of screen passes that proved very effective.
In fact, McCord's first NFL completion was a short throw to fullback DJ Herman after he leaked out of the backfield that converted a third-and-7.
McCord had a couple of really nice throws, the sideline shot to Caleb Douglas, the deep middle crosser to Douglas, but he was victimized by a couple of drops and a couple of throws where his receiver simply didn't get open.
In other words, McCord was dealing with the same issues that have hampered Willis all season.
The one difference is that McCord was healthy, whereas Willis has barely spent a week without being on the injury report with one issue or another.
McCord will get at least three more shots at starting for the Dolphins before Willis is eligible to return from injured reserve, and it does look like he'll do his part and at the very least be able to manage the game.
That's the baseline that he seemed to establish with that start against the Colts, and there's no to dismiss the idea there could be more to his game because this, after all, was his first NFL appearance.
And for a first go, again, it was just fine.

title: More Bad News Amid Flurry of Dolphins Roster Moves
full_text:
The Miami Dolphins indeed went the familiar route when it came time to replenish the defensive tackle position, which took another hit Tuesday.
The team announced a series of roster moves that included Jordan Phillips joining Zeek Biggers in going on injured reserve.
The Dolphins also signed three players from their practice squad to the active roster — defensive tackle Jordan Jefferson, quarterback Brady Cook and edge Eric Watts.
Lastly, the Dolphins signed four players to the practice squad, including kicker Daniel Carlson. The others are WR Brady Boyd, DL Matthew Butler and DL Chris Smith.
The biggest shockwave of all the moves obviously involves the D-tackle position, where Phillips has joined Biggers in sustaining a season-ending injury, with ESPN's Marcel Louis-Jacques reporting Phillips will have surgery to repair a biceps tendon.
Phillips was spotted leaving Lucas Oil Stadium with his arm in a sling Sunday and was scheduled to undergo an MRI on Monday, so it always was fair to be concerned his injury also could be season-ending.
As we suggested in a story earlier Tuesday, the Dolphins replaced Phillips and Biggers with players with whom they're familiar because Butler was with the team in 2025, playing 12 games with one start, and was in training camp this summer before being released.
Because Jefferson is the only new defensive tackle on the 53-man roster, the Dolphins still have only three at that position with Kenneth Grant and Keith Cooper Jr. as the other two, so Butler seems like a logical candidate to get elevated for the game at Buffalo on Sunday considering his familiarity and experience.
Smith, the other new defensive tackle, hasn't played in an NFL game since 2024 when he made his five career appearances with the Detroit Lions after coming out of Notre Dame.
Grant now becomes the only defensive tackle of the Dolphins' projected group with Biggers and Phillips having joined Zach Sieler on injured reserve.
Thanks to those four, the Dolphins have moved up to 10th in the NFL in total defense and 10th in rushing yards allowed per carry, and those rankings figure to take a pretty big hit with the three players gone.
Watts' signing puts the Dolphins back at five edge defenders, as he joins Chop Robinson, Josh Uche, Malik Herring and Rodney McGraw.
Cook being signed to the 53 figures to be just a matter of time because he's going to be serving as the backup quarterback for at least four games while Malik Willis is on injured reserve.
Carlson, who tried out for the Dolphins a couple of weeks ago, seemed like the logical candidate after Zane Gonzalez was waived following his three misses in the 24-22 loss against the Indianapolis Colts.
The Dolphins didn't sign Gonzalez to the active roster until he exhaused his three practice squad elevations, so maybe they will use the same approach with Carlson — certainly hoping for better results.
As we indicated Tuesday, the Dolphins' field goal kicking has been a problem all season, with Miami next-to-last in the NFL in field goal percentage.

title: Examining Potential Dolphins DT Replacements
full_text:
The Miami Dolphins already were down two defensive tackles as of late Tuesday morning as we continued to await word on the status of yet another injured player at the position.
And regardless of what prognosis is delivered for Jordan Phillips, it's clear the Dolphins are going to need reinforcements at the position — and sooner rather than later.
In fact, we'd expect a flurry of roster moves by late Tuesday afternoon with the practice week kicking off Wednesday and we'd expect one and maybe two defensive linemen being added to the 53-man roster and/or practice squad.
The big question, of course, becomes who that one or two players will be.
One place to start would be on the Dolphins' own practice squad, where they simply could promote Jordan Jefferson to the 53-man roster. A 2024 fourth-round pick of the Jacksonville Jaguars with 10 career regular season appearances, Jefferson fits the mold of the players they've brought in this year as a 25-year-old unproven player looking to jump-start his career.
If they prefer a more veteran presence but someone they're also familiar with, then another logical choice would be Matthew Butler, who played 12 games with the team last season and performed well in training camp before he was released in favor of summer surprise Keith Cooper Jr., who was waived and then re-signed off the Carolina Panthers practice squad and now stands with 2025 first-round pick Kenneth Grant as the only healthy D-tackles on the 53.
And there's also Fatorma Mulbah, who showed flashes in training camp and has some NFL experience from his time with the New York Jets.
Yet another, even more familiar name is Christian Wilkins, who hasn't played a game since October 2024 and seems like a forgotten man in league circles. That idea doesn't appear to have any legs.
There are other defensive tackle without a team at the moment, and another place the Dolphins can look is on the practice squads around the NFL.
If the Dophins want to go the veteran route, options could include Phidarian Mathis with the Buffalo Bills, Isaiah Loudermilk with the New York Jets, Austin Johnson with the Jacksonville Jaguars and Byron Cowart of the Washington Commanders, a player who spent time in Miami a couple of years ago.
That, however, would go against the pattern the Dolphins have established, which is looking for those young players with upside who just haven't delivered yet.
Looking at the physical make-up of the three DTs the Dolphins have lost — Zach Sieler, Biggers and Phillips — we also should expect any addition to have some size, meaning undersized DTs need not apply.
Two names to watch here include Jordan Miller of the Denver Broncos because he was on the Dolphins practice squad at some point and the Seattle Seahawks' Cole Brevard, who the Dolphins tried out a few weeks back.
Former Dallas Cowboys first-round pick Mazi Smith is on the Packers practice squad, but the Dolphins already had him on their practice squad and moved on from him, so logic says Miami isn't going down that road, but who knows?
In any event, we'll find out soon enough.
In the meantime, here's a pretty comprehensive list of D-tackles around NFL practice squads who could interest the Dolphins: Amari McNeil (Jets), Eric Gregory (Patriots), David Olajiga (Ravens), Howard Cross III (Bengals), Zion Logue (Bengals), Junior Tafuna (Texans), Brandon Cleveland (Raiders), Zion Wilson (Eagles), Gabe Hall (Eagles), P.J. Mustipher (Giants), Jeffrey M'ba (Lions), Zacch Pickens (Falcons), Jalen Hunt (Rams).

title: Updated Dolphins Draft Picture With Critical Next Two Weeks Coming Up
full_text:
The Miami Dolphins are trying to win games this season while the main objective remains player development and evaluation, and it's also only natural to look ahead to the 2027 draft and how high a pick they could wind up having.
To that end, Week 10 of the 2026 season was a very good one for them, most notably their closs loss against the Indianapolis Colts and the Monday night game that saw the Los Angeles Chargers get their first victory of the season.
The Dolphins, Chargers and Tennessee Titans now are tied for the worst record in the league at 1-8, though the Dolphins' tougher strength of schedule currently has them with the third pick behind the Titans at number 1 and then the Chargers.
The rest of the current top five has the New York Jets (2-8) and the Philadelphia Eagles (2-7).
There are now eight weeks left in the regular season, so plenty of time for the exact order to change. And there could be some movement pretty soon actually because the Jets and Chargers face each other at SoFi Stadium on Sunday, and then the Jets come to Hard Rock Stadium to face the Dolphins in Week 12.
We could debate what's actually the worst team in the NFL right now among the Titans, Chargers, Dolphins and even Jets, but injuries likely will become a factor and Miami has gotten hit pretty hard over the past two games with Malik Willis, Zach Sieler, Zeek Biggers and potentially Jordan Phillips.
After the games of Week 10, the Dolphins are considered front-runners to land that top overall pick.
The Dolphins' current projected win total over/under betting line is at 2.5, according to DraftKings Sportsbook. That's the lowest in the league, with the Chargers and Titans at 3.5, the Jets and Eagles at 4.5, and the Colts at 5.5.
Of the Dolphins' remaining eight games, they have two that should be considered very winnable — the home games against the Jets and the Chargers in Week 16 — and the season finale against the New England Patriots at Gillette Stadium now looks different with the injury to quarterback Drake Maye, especially if the Pats are out of playoff contention by then.
Miami will be heavy underdogs in the other five games — at Buffalo, at Denver, home against Chicago, at Green Bay, and home against Buffalo.
Since the NFL went to a 17-game schedule in 2021, the worst record ever compiled was the 2-15 by the Carolina Panthers in 2023.
Finishing 3-14 has meant a top 3 pick every time except this year for the Titans, who picked fourth. And ending up 4-13 has meant a top 5 pick every time except for the Las Vegas Raiders having the sixth overall selection in 2025.
So based on their projected win total, the Dolphins are expected to have no worse that the fourth overall pick.
There will be plenty of time after the end of the season to really start diving and digging into the top prospects, but the early popular names include WR Jeremiah Smith, QB Drew Mestemaker, CB Leonard Moore, DE Colin Simmons and DE Dylan Stewart, and a case could be made for the Dolphins drafting any of them.
One thing to consider, too, is that the higher the pick the better chance of getting offers to move up from a team that's really zeroed in on a particular prospect, a move that could provide the Dolphins with more draft capital, which would help as they continue replenishing the roster.

title: Zeek Biggers News Is Another Big Setback for Dolphins D-Line, But It Could Get Worse
full_text:
The Miami Dolphins are going to be running out of bodies at the rate they're going — big bodies, that is.
In their first game with Zach Sieler on injured reserve, the Dolphins watched both Zeek Biggers and Jordan Phillips leave their 24-22 loss against the Indianapolis Colts with injuries, and the verdict has come on the severity of one of them — and it's not good news.
Biggers is done for the season after sustaining a meniscus injury in his right knee, according to NFL insider Ian Rapoport, citing sources.
#Dolphins DT Zeek Biggers, a former 7th round pick who has earned a starting role, will have knee surgery to repair his lateral meniscus, sources say, a procedure that ends his season. Biggers will make a full recovery in time for 2027. pic.twitter.com/nK6i2JzrPM
The question now is whether Phillips' injury wil be as severe after he left Lucas Oil Stadium with an arm in a sling and was scheduled for an MRI on Monday.
Head coach Jeff Hafley said Monday afternoon that both players needed more tests to determine the severity of the injury, but now the best the Dolphins will be able to do is salvage a second of the four defensive tackles from last year.
If Phillips is sidelined for a while, the Dolphins will be down to 2025 first-round pick Kenneth Grant and Keith Cooper Jr. on the 35-man roster, with Jordan Jefferson the lone defensive tckle on the practice squad.
The bad luck, of course, began when Sieler sustained a season-ending biceps injury in the Week 9 loss against the Detroit Lions.
Biggers' injury means the Dolphins will need to add at least one defensive tackle to the 53-man roster, and that number will go to two if Phillips also winds up having to go on injured reserve.
Two names to watch would be Fatorma Mulbah and Matthew Butler, who both were with the Dolphins in training camp before being among the final cuts to the 53-player limit.
Former Dolphins first-round pick Christian Wilkins certainly is an interesting name, but there's been no indication that any team has reached out to him this year and he hasn't played in a bit more than two years after sustaining a serious foot injury while with the Las Vegas Raiders in 2024.
Now that any time would be good for these kind of injuries, the timing really isn't good because the Dolphins are about to face one of the best rushing teams when they travel to Buffalo on Sunday.
Biggers was injured during Seth McGowan's touchdown run in the first quarter that gave the Colts a 7-0 lead.
He played in all nine games this season and made two starts, contributing at both defensive tackle and defensive end.
He was a seventh-round pick in 2025 after the Dolphins had selected Grant in the first round and Phillips in the fifth round.

title: How Jarrett Kingston Is Emerging as the Best Waiver Wire Pick-Up for the Dolphins As Another One Bites the Dust
full_text:
Hours after the much-publicized move to waive kicker Zane Gonzalez, the Miami Dolphins made another transaction Monday, that one involving edge defender Jamree Kromah.
And, like Gonzalez, Kromah was waived, ending his brief time in Miami that began after he was claimed off waivers from the Chicago Bears.
Kromah was let go after appearing in two games for Miami, including the 24-22 loss against the Indianapolis Colts on Sunday when his playing time occurred strictly on special teams.
The move left the Dolphins with three openings on their 53-man roster because they were at 52 players when they faced the Colts and haven't yet replaced either Gonzalez or Kromah.
More significantly, the move with Kromah provided more evidence that picking up players on waivers is a sound practice for rebuilding teams looking for hidden gems wherever they can find them, but it also rarely provides great answers.
This isn't to suggest the Dolphins should stop looking at the waiver wire in the hope of finding a good player on whom another team gave up too quickly, but at the same time understanding that the pieces to what the organization ultimately hopes is a contender likely will come through other methods, such as the draft or free agency.
Kromah was the 16th and most recent waiver wire acquisition by the Dolphins so far in 2026, a total that's just four shy of what they did in 2019 when they were undergoing another rebuilding project.
Of those 16 players picked up through waivers this year, exactly half already have come and gone. Of the other eight, only safety Julius Wood and guard Jarrett Kingston have started a game, and it's been one start each.
At this time, none of the waiver wire pick-ups has a significant role, though Wood is a core special teams player and Kingston just became the team's sixth offensive lineman for the game against Indianapolis on Sunday.
But the chances of any of the waiver wire pick-ups becoming key contributors on the team's road back to contention are pretty slim, and that's just the reality of making those moves.
And the Dolphins likely aren't done with moves like that because, who knows, maybe one of them could turn into Zach Sieler.
That's what happened in 2019 when the Dolphins claimed the defensive lineman from the Baltimore Ravens. Nearly seven years later, Sieler is well established as a core player for the Dolphins, a team captain and a major loss now that he's on IR.
To a much lesser degree, the Dolphins also hit in 2019 with Mack Hollins, but the success stories are extremely rare when it comes to waiver wire pick-ups.
It's why we always caution against expecting too much whenever a newcomer arrives, whether it's Kromah or even former Seattle Seahawks third-round pick Christian Haynes, who was claimed just a few days before Kromah.
The rationale is pretty simple: There's a reason the player's former team let them go.
Yes, there will be an exception to the rule at some point, which is why there's no harm in "turning over stones," as the saying goes. That's what the Dolphins did with Kromah.
And even though it didn't pan out, it still was worth the gamble.

title: Vikings Week 11 Mailbag: Kirk Cousins MVP Talk, Altitude Prep, Jennings Revenge Game & More
full_text:
While many Vikings fans are still riding the high of a Sunday beatdown against their rival Packers , the team is preparing for another high-stakes NFC battle against the 49ers in Mexico City. With an offense that finally looks competent and an already elite defense reaping the benefits, the sky may very well be the limit for this 2026 Vikings team.
I took to X to get your questions and takes before one of the biggest NFL matchups of the year.
To submit your questions, reach out to Jason Harmon on X .
If Kirk Cousins continues to play at this level , I’m not even sure that hearing his name in MVP conversations would be that surprising, especially if he does it while playing for two different teams. Cousins’ 2,547 passing yards rank fifth in the league, while his 22 passing touchdowns rank second. If he continues this success now that he’s back with the Vikings, it’ll be hard to find any other QB in NFL history who has put up that kind of performance with two different teams in one season.
I mean, what an absurd Kirk Cousins throw. Both to put the air underneath, and to keep it on the back shoulder. pic.twitter.com/RCwMnJLihQ
This has been a fascinating talking point around the Vikings’ upcoming matchup with the 49ers in Mexico City. The Vikings plan to hold a normal week of practice before heading south one day before the game on Saturday. Meanwhile, the 49ers are spending the week practicing in Colorado Springs to acclimate to the higher altitude before arriving in Mexico on the same day.
Different approaches to altitude preparation ahead of the 49ers vs. Vikings game in Mexico City: • 49ers: Arrived in Colorado Springs yesterday (6,621 ft). • Vikings: Staying in Minnesota (860 ft) until Saturday. • Mexico City game elevation: 7,280 ft.
While most football fans are used to seeing altitude affect games played in Denver, Mexico City’s altitude is about 2,100 feet higher. Oxygen intake will certainly be a factor. I’m no health expert, and medical professionals even seem to disagree on which approach may be best, but with San Francisco making their third trip across the border, they may have a leg up from experience alone.
If Kevin O’Connell’s statements this week are any indication, he’s expecting a big performance from Jauan Jennings on Sunday. With Jordan Addison recovering from thumb surgery, the Vikings will be reliant on Jennings to return from a calf injury that held him out against the Bills and Packers.
#Vikings HC Kevin O’Connell on Jauan Jennings’ revenge game vs the #49ers : “With us being down Jordan Addison, we’re gonna need him to make some plays in the pass game.” (Via @KFAN1003 ) pic.twitter.com/BOjGi3HeuY
It’s no secret Jennings has had a rough season so far, but more opportunities and better quarterback play may be exactly what he needs. Familiarity with his former team certainly doesn’t hurt either.  Sunday is just the start of what could be a highly productive month for Jennings, as Addison may not return until the Dec. 20 game against the Lions.  The back half of this season could be an entirely different story than his frustrating start.
Make no mistake, a win on Sunday against a great 49ers team could prove to be a season-defining moment for the 2026 Vikings. For all the offensive turmoil that plagued the team over their first eight games, Cousins’ return has brought optimism that this may be a truly special year after all.
Sunday night could easily be the biggest game of the 2026 NFL season. Shoutout to the fans in Mexico City who get to witness an all-timer. pic.twitter.com/37oFawfBs6
The Vikings defense is currently on pace for almost 70 sacks, a total not reached since the Eagles did it in 2022. They just so happened to make it to the Super Bowl that season. All Cousins and the offense need to do is hold on to the ball and score points on occasion. The stellar Minnesota defense and kicker Will Reichard will handle the rest.

title: Caleb Banks Could Make or Break His Season When Vikings Visit 49ers for Week 11 SNF
full_text:
It has been a quiet season for Minnesota Vikings rookie defensive lineman Caleb Banks. He was selected No. 18 overall in the 2026 NFL Draft and has played an average of 15.5 defensive snaps per game.
He got the most work in Week 2 against the Chicago Bears when he played 36 defensive snaps and finished with six tackles, including one for a loss. He had his best game on Sunday against the Packers, finishing with an 82.2 Pro Football Focus grade after having an initial grade of 90.6.
Banks seems to be developing well for head coach Kevin O'Connell and defensive coordinator Brian Flores, even though the team's patient approach has left many fans frustrated from not seeing results from the first-round pick.
The Vikings' defensive line is playing extremely well this season and has not needed Banks to play a lot of snaps so far. However, he is making an impact when he is on the field in a rotational/backup role when needed.
Here are the five other Minnesota defensive linemen and their PFF grades:
The 23-year-old defensive lineman can follow up his excellent performance against the Packers with a solid showing against the San Francisco 49ers. The high-profile international game will take place on Sunday Night Football in Mexico City, Mexico, giving NFL fans all around the world an opportunity to see the six-foot-six, 327-pound defender in action.
During that game, the Vikings will need to stop 49ers star running back Christian McCaffrey. He had a huge impact in San Francisco's 46-40 win over the Dallas Cowboys, finishing with 13 carries for 62 yards and a touchdown, plus four catches for 161 yards and two more touchdowns.
Minnesota will need to be at the top of its game to slow McCaffrey and have a solid chance to defeat the 8-1 49ers. It will all start in the trenches, where Banks can continue to showcase his disruption at the line of scrimmage and take away gaps in the run game and passing lanes.
Banks needs to prove that he can be a consistently good defender to silence his critics. Although the game against the Packers was a great start, he needs to keep the momentum going in the Vikings' prime-time matchup this week.

title: 3 Vikings Are Already Reaping the Rewards of Kirk Cousins’s Return to Minnesota
full_text:
It has only been one game since Kirk Cousins returned to the Minnesota Vikings, but the team already feels different. His arrival has brought hope that the Purple and Gold offense can help Brian Flores' defense and a strong special teams unit win games.
Cousins is a significant upgrade over Kyler Murray or Carson Wentz at quarterback, which will provide opportunities for players who were struggling in the Vikings' offense before the veteran quarterback's arrival.
Three players are already benefiting from having Cousins as Minnesota's starting quarterback, and it is making the future feel bright for a team that was among the worst in the league at passing the football.
Jefferson is a two-time first-team All-Pro and a four-time Pro Bowl wide receiver. Expectations are high for him to contribute every game, but in his seven games before Cousins' arrival, he averaged only 7.3 targets, 4.4 receptions, and 56.1 yards per game.
In his first game reunited with Cousins, Jefferson was targeted 13 times, catching nine passes for 74 yards. It was clear he would be the primary option in the Vikings' passing attack going forward, and that's a good thing for Minnesota.
Statistically, Minnesota is more likely to win when Jefferson is targeted 10 times or more in a game. Since being drafted by the Vikings, the team is 26-21when he gets at least 10 targets. If he continues to get plenty of looks, it will help the team win games.
When there isn't a valid threat of a passing game, defenses can focus on stopping the run. Despite that, Jones Sr. was able to average 4.1 yards per carry before Cousins' arrival, but only found the end zone twice in eight games while carrying the bulk of Minnesota's carries.
In the first game with Cousins at quarterback, Jones averaged 4.3 yards per carry and scored a touchdown. Cousins gives the offense balance and improves other phases of the game by being a competent passer, bringing even more value to having him back in Minnesota.
Furthermore, being able to run the ball keeps opposing teams guessing about what Minnesota's offense is attempting to execute and pinches defenders closer to the line of scrimmage, which opens up one of Cousins' biggest strengths: the play-action pass.
The Vikings' defense has been on the field a lot this season. They have played 563 snaps, which averages out to 63.5 per game. For a player like Josh Metellus or Eric Wilson, who play over 90 percent of the defensive snaps, that is exhausting.
The defensive snaps dropped to 55 against the Packers in Week 10. That is a significant difference from the 80 the team played against the Buffalo Bills the previous week. Having a defense that isn't exhausted and doesn't have to rotate players in and out is more efficient and productive, as fans saw at Lambeau Field last Sunday.

title: Hollywood Brown Continues to Scream Potential Vikings Target Amid Jordan Addison’s Injury
full_text:
UPDATE: Vikings head coach Kevin O'Connell told reporters on Wednesday that Jordan Addison will not be placed on short-term IR after having successful surgery on his thumb, per Alec Lewis of The Athletic .
Our original story as follow below:
The Minnesota Vikings were fortunate to have players like Myles Price, Gavin Bartholomew, and Tai Felton step up against the Green Bay Packers in Week 10, but can they be consistent contributors moving forward?
Earlier this week, the Vikings got some bad news. Minnesota's No. 2 receiver, Jordan Addison, is expected to miss multiple weeks while recovering from a thumb injury that will require surgery. He is expected to be placed on short-term injured reserve and be eligible to return after four weeks.
In the meantime, the Purple and Gold need someone to help take pressure off star wideout Justin Jefferson. Although Minnesota has Jauan Jennings returning soon and Odell Beckham Jr. on the practice squad, the team could still use additional help. Hollywood Brown could be an answer .
This season, Addison is averaging 54.29 offensive snaps played per game. That is a significant amount of time to account for while hoping to get contributions from Jennings, Price, Felton, or Beckham. Brown has proven himself as a field-stretching presence on offense, which could help take advantage of opposing defenses.
Minnesota likely wouldn't even need Brown to catch many passes. Having him on the field to run deep routes is enough to give him enough value to get him some offensive snaps that might have gone to a player who has disappointed since joining the Vikings, like Jennings or Beckham.
Brown has caught only five passes this season for 63 yards, but all five receptions have resulted in a first down. It's hard to deny that kind of efficiency, especially on a team that struggled to move the chains early in the season.
Now that the Vikings have Kirk Cousins starting at quarterback, every game feels winnable. With Minnesota's stout defense and strong special teams, even an average offense can make the Purple and Gold strong contenders this year.
Brown has cleared waivers since his release from the Philadelphia Eagles and is now free to sign wherever. If nothing else, the Vikings owe it to themselves to bring the 29-year-old receiver in for a visit to see if he'd be a good fit in Minnesota and if a reasonable contract can be negotiated.
At the same time, getting a deal done before Sunday night against the San Francisco 49ers could be big. The NFC West powerhouse is 8-1 this season and ranked second in the NFL in scoring, averaging 31.2 points per game. If that game turns into a shootout, the Vikings could use a deep-ball threat like Brown to make things hard for the 49ers' defense.

title: Vikings' Snap Count vs. Packers: Biggest Winners, Losers & Role Changes in Week 10
full_text:
The Minnesota Vikings surprised many fans watching the team's Week 10 game against the Green Bay Packers. The 30-10 victory was controlled from the start by the Purple and Gold, who finally put together a complete game.
The attack plan from head coach Kevin O'Connell and defensive coordinator Brian Flores worked extremely well at Lambeau Field, giving hope that the team can remain a contender for the remainder of the season.
How O'Connell and Flores managed their personnel was important too. Several contributors missed time due to injury . Knowing which players to use to fill particular roles paid off handsomely for the Vikings. Here are some winners and losers from Sunday's snap counts.
T.J. Hockenson was ruled out of this game with a wrist/chest injury, so the next man up to start was second-year tight end Gavin Bartholomew. He played the ninth-most snaps on offense for Minnesota against Green Bay, getting in on 53 offensive plays.
Bartholomew caught three of four passes thrown his way by quarterback Kirk Cousins, gaining 36 yards and scoring his first touchdown as a pro. On that 20-yard touchdown catch in the fourth quarter, he stiff-armed a Packers defender to give himself a path to the end zone.
James Pierre is having a great first season in Minnesota, earning a 72.7 Pro Football Focus grade this year, but he saw his workload on defense cut from 50 defensive snaps against the Bills to 27 against the Packers.
Pierre still ended the day with a pass breakup and a tackle, but the drastic decrease in usage on defense is alarming. He was still the third-most-used cornerback behind Byron Murphy Jr. and Isaiah Rodgers, so hopefully this isn't a sign that he's in the doghouse.
When Caleb Banks was a healthy scratch last week against the Bills, plenty of rumors were floating around about what was going on with the rookie defensive lineman. However, he played 17 defensive snaps against the Packers and looked great.
Earning a 90.6 PFF initial grade, Banks had two tackles (one solo) against Green Bay. This was an important statement game for the 23-year-old, and he put forth his best showing as a pro to date.
While Banks saw significant playing time against the Packers, fellow rookie defensive lineman Domonique Orange went from playing 22 defensive snaps in Week 9 to seven in Week 10 against the Packers.
Finishing the game with two tackles (one solo), the Vikings got amazing play out of Banks, Levi Drake Rodriguez, Jalen Redmond, and Elijah Williams, all of whom earned a PFF grade of over 70 in the big divisional matchup.
It was a big day for Minnesota's rookies last Sunday, and second-round pick Jake Golday participated in the action. With starting linebacker Blake Cashman out, Golday and Ivan Pace Jr. did their best to hold down the defense, and the results were mixed.
He struggled as a pass rusher, as evidenced by his 54.2 PFF grade (last on the team). He was much better as a tackler against the Packers, bringing down five ball carriers, including three solo efforts.

title: Under-the Radar Vikings WR Staring at a Golden Opportunity With Jordan Addison Hurt
full_text:
The Vikings may have dropped 30 points on the rival Packers in Kirk Cousins's return last weekend, but that doesn't mean the Purple and Gold's offensive issues have been solved. The wide receiver room still features more questions than answers, between Justin Jefferson's inconsistent usage, Jauan Jennings and Jordan Addison's injuries and the lack of production behind the top three WR options.
With a massive Sunday Night Football collision against the 49ers in the cards for Week 11, the Vikings will need all the help they can get from their wideouts. Although it's good to see Jennings trending in the right direction (h/t VikingzFanPage), he can't be fully trusted as the only reliable WR besides Jefferson. And can they really count on Myles Price to deliver back-to-back notable performances?
It's safe to say that Minnesota will need more bodies to step up against a San Francisco team averaging 31.2 points per game—second-best in the NFL. With that in mind, don't be surprised if the Vikings turn to a practice-squad option that's flying under the radar.
The trade deadline is behind us, meaning the practice squad and free agency are the Vikings' only paths for WR help . Head coach Kevin O'Connell might want to go with more familiar faces at this stage of the season, though, which could lead them to turn to undrafted rookie WR Dillon Bell.
Having just turned 23 earlier this month, Bell has been with Minnesota since April. He signed as a UDFA after the 2026 NFL Draft and eventually fought his way onto the 53-man roster. That only lasted a day, though, as he was cut before being re-signed to the taxi squad before Week 1 .
Bell has now had almost three months to develop and learn from the veterans and coaching staff around him. The Vikings clearly liked him enough to use a practice squad spot on him, and now it's time to see what he's made of—especially when the other options have proven to be futile.
Odell Beckham Jr.'s best days are clearly behind him, as he's recorded zero catches in four games played between the Giants and Vikings. Meanwhile, Jeshaun Jones only has a 32-yard catch in three appearances and has suited up just once since Week 5, as Minnesota has run out of elevations for him and would be forced to sign him to the 53-man roster.
Given that Beckham is slow and Jones isn't worth the 53-man roster spot, there's no reason not to roll the dice on Bell, who only saw three special teams snaps in his lone appearance (Week 2 vs. Bears). The preseason was a good indication of what he can do, catching seven of his 16 targets for 59 receiving yards (including 28 after the catch) and four first downs. Perhaps he could've been more productive if the Vikings had received better QB performances this summer (h/t Vikings on SI's Jason Harmon).
Poor Dillon Bell…. pic.twitter.com/KyNF9urLYv
Any UDFA signed to the practice squad is bound to be viewed as a project, but eventually it's time to see if the patience was worth it. That's the situation the Vikings currently find themselves in with Bell, who could see his first action since September because of Addison's absence. We already saw the positive impact that Cousins's presence had on Price, who tallied a career-high 49 receiving yards and his first-ever touchdown last weekend.
Could the Cousins effect lead to similar success for Bell? Maybe, maybe not; however, the only way to find out will be for the Vikings to throw the rookie wide receiver into the fire this weekend.

title: Kevin O’Connell Just Put More Heat on Jauan Jennings to End Rut Before Week 11 SNF vs. 49ers
full_text:
Your 7-2 Vikings have been through quite the November gauntlet, battling some of the league’s best teams. After going 1-2 against the Lions, Bills, and Packers, the Vikings will look to split a brutal four-game stretch by defeating the top-seeded 49ers in Mexico City this Sunday .
One Viking who’ll be especially motivated? Wide receiver Jauan Jennings, who signed with the team this past offseason after spending the first six years of his career in San Francisco.
After a slow start to his 2026 campaign, head coach Kevin O’Connell is expecting a big showing from Jennings against his former squad. With the team’s number-two receiver sidelined and a new quarterback throwing him passes, Jennings may be poised for a big game this weekend.
The Vikings announced Monday that wide receiver Jordan Addison would miss time after thumb surgery. Addison had been nursing the injury since camp, but a freak accident at Friday’s practice caused further complications. Now, it’s up to Jennings to step in during Addison’s absence, assuming he’s fully recovered from the calf injury that sidelined him for the last two weeks.
Kevin O’Connell joined local Twin Cities radio station KFAN 100.3 to discuss the upcoming matchup and what it means specifically for Jennings, emphasizing the need for him to step up .
#Vikings HC Kevin O’Connell on Jauan Jennings’ revenge game vs the #49ers : “With us being down Jordan Addison, we’re gonna need him to make some plays in the pass game.” (Via @KFAN1003 ) pic.twitter.com/BOjGi3HeuY
An international game against one of the league's best teams isn't exactly the ideal time to lose your WR2, but for Jennings in particular, Addison’s absence may offer the perfect chance to salvage a challenging season.
To say Jennings has had a rough start to his Vikings tenure would be a massive understatement. In six games, he’s brought in only six receptions for 54 yards and no touchdowns. Even though he was mainly signed for his run-blocking ability, no one involved could have expected his pass-catching production to be this frustrating.
Needless to say, the Vikings' quarterback woes haven't helped Jennings’s situation. Any all-22 viewing session repeatedly showcased Jennings getting open downfield, with Kyler Murray in particular simply not seeing him uncovered.
Kyler Murray's 35-yard run yesterday was great, and the #Vikings eventually scored a TD on the drive But... Before crossing the line of scrimmage, he missed a chance to throw to a WIDE OPEN Jauan Jennings for an easy TD pic.twitter.com/5a6CTK1Rdt
The 49ers and Vikings had even agreed to terms on a trade that would have sent Jennings back to San Francisco , but Jennings made it clear he wanted to stay in Minnesota despite the early struggles. Now, that decision may pay off, especially with Kirk Cousins taking over at QB and elevating the passing game to a level not seen in the past two seasons.
If Jennings wants to turn his 2026 fortunes around, Sunday’s primetime matchup against his former team is the best possible opportunity.

title: Vikings' Recent Late-Round Draft Success Generates Mixed Kwesi Adofo-Mensah Feelings
full_text:
The Vikings are 7-2 after one of the wildest ten-week spans imaginable to start an NFL season. The defense? Dominant. The offense? Dormant. The solution? Kirk Cousins. Needless to say, it’s been quite the ride.
The team has relied heavily on defensive stars like Andrew Van Ginkel and Blake Cashman, but one major reason for such an impressive start is the high-upside young players who are starting to step up. Interestingly enough, many of these late-round gems were drafted by a general manager the team fired 10 months ago .
With championship aspirations and a newly hired general manager in Nolan Teasley, there are fair questions to ask about the legacy that ex-GM Kwesi Adofo-Mensah left behind.
Were the Vikings too quick to part ways with their former GM? Were the accusations that he “couldn’t draft” fair? Does he deserve credit for the success of the 2026 Vikings? The answers are a bit murky, but it seems he certainly left some gifts on his way out.
The NFL Draft is an inexact science, but it’s typically safe to assume that players selected in later rounds will have a significantly harder path to contributing consistently at the professional level. Ironically, the Vikings are seeing almost the exact opposite scenario play out for many of their young contributors. 2024 17th overall pick, Dallas Turner, has been one of the most impressive defenders in the NFL this season, but he wasn't the only star Adofo-Mensah and his staff found in that class.
Defensive tackle Levi-Drake Rodriguez may be one of the best stories in the entire NFL. After playing football and baseball at Southwestern Assemblies of God University, Rodriguez transferred to Texas A&M University–Commerce in 2022. The big man was the definition of a draft day underdog. But Adofo-Mensah, former assistant GM Ryan Grigson, and defensive coordinator Brian Flores liked what they saw and ultimately took a swing at pick 232.
Two years later, Rodriguez is starting at defensive tackle and has already recorded three sacks this season.
Vikings DT Levi Drake Rodriguez was unbelievably good on Sunday. 93.3 PFF grade. 8 pressures, 2 sacks on 24 pass-rush snaps. The former 232nd overall pick out of Texas A&M-Commerce has become a key part of this defense. pic.twitter.com/zUuEeaDKXj
There’s also Will Reichard, who was selected with the 203rd pick in the same draft. Reichard has become one of the league’s top kickers and is currently second in the NFL with 23 successful kicks this season. It turns out Adofo-Mensah may have solved one of the most frustrating positions in Vikings franchise history.
The 2025 class also has a few names that are starting to make some noise. Former Maryland wide receiver Tai Felton was selected 102nd overall in 2025, and while he may not be a true “late-rounder,” he certainly had his work cut out for him in a stacked wide receiver room. Now, he’s starting to show signs of potential, especially with Jauan Jennings and Jordan Addison missing time . A strong camp and preseason are setting Felton up for a growing role.
Cousins to Tai Felton gets the Vikings near the goal line on another 3rd and long conversion MINvsGB on FOX/FOX One Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/T9zCEvmP3W
Defensive lineman Tyrion Ingram-Dawkins is another name Vikings fans are hearing more often. The former defensive tackle shifted outside this past offseason, slimming down along the way. He’s appeared in only three games this season and has battled through injury, but he’s proven disruptive in limited opportunities.
The Vikings’ final pick of the 2025 draft was tight end Gavin Bartholomew, who missed his entire rookie season with a lower back injury. One season later, the former Pitt Panther is starting to make waves. With T.J. Hockenson out against the Packers on Sunday, Bartholomew and Kirk Cousins quickly became friends as the second-year tight end caught three passes for 36 yards and his first NFL TD.
Kirk Cousins to Gavin Bartholomew for the TD pic.twitter.com/g1YUgVp8nr
For a team that has long battled through serious depth concerns, the emergence of young talent from later portions of the draft is a promising sign of what’s to come. But it doesn’t change many of the key reasons Adofo-Mensah was ultimately fired.
The Kwesi Adofo-Mensah era will ultimately be defined by much more than the success of his late-round draft selections. The fact that zero players remain on the roster from his 2022 draft class is a massive indictment. The 2023 class was not much better, as Jordan Addison and Jay Ward are the last remaining members of the six-player class. Then there’s the quarterback situation, which has been broken down ad nauseam.
Without an answer at the most important position in sports, and with little help from his first two draft classes, the resulting breakup seemed inevitable. At the same time, the Vikings’ former GM and his staff certainly didn’t leave Vikings fans empty-handed with some of his value selections.
For that, he deserves great credit.

title: Not Trading Ivan Pace Jr. at the Deadline Is Proving to Be a Genius Vikings Move
full_text:
This has been an interesting season for Vikings linebacker Ivan Pace Jr., to say the least.
Pace lost his starting job to Eric Wilson last season and appeared to be replaced when the team selected Jake Golday in the second round of the 2026 NFL Draft. While he looked to be expendable , the Vikings kept the 25-year-old defender through the final cuts to make the 53-man roster
Still, he looked like an even bigger afterthought after averaging just 8.4 defensive snaps in the first seven games of the 2026 season. No one would've blamed the Vikings if they traded Pace away, as it'd give the veteran a much-needed fresh start while opening more playing time for an up-and-coming defender.
Instead of a trade, Minnesota retained him at the deadline. It hasn't taken long for that move to look like a genius play by general manager Nolan Teasley and head coach Kevin O'Connell.
Pace is seeing more action on special teams than on defense this season, but having him available as depth while he fills a need on special teams has paid off in a big way for the Purple and Gold this season.
For the first time this season, Pace played more defensive snaps than special teams reps against the Packers in Week 10. He was in for a total of 57 plays against Green Bay, with 42 of those coming on defense.
As of Week 11, Pace has earned a 64.5 Pro Football Focus grade , as well as a 90.5 pass-rush grade, generating eight pressures and getting two sacks while blitzing. He has been a valuable defender to rotate in on defense or fill in when injuries keep a starter out of the lineup.
Ivan Pace Jr. brings the pressure 💥 📺 Watch live on @NFLonDAZN , @SkySports and @talkSPORT pic.twitter.com/O7XREgogYK
Starting linebacker Blake Cashman missed Week 10 with a concussion, and it is hard to know when a player will return from that kind of injury. Additionally, Andrew Van Ginkel is banged up with a quad injury after Sunday's victory. Having Pace ready to step in is a huge benefit in defensive coordinator Brian Flores's system.
Minnesota could have used Pace as a trade asset this season. Quite a few teams around the league could use an inside linebacker with his pass-rush skills, but the Vikings opted to keep him and are now benefiting from that decision. He is one of the 19 unrestricted free agents the Vikings will have to make decisions on in March, though, so it's hard to see how much longer he'll be around.
The Vikings are still using the fourth-year defender on special teams while having Pace fill in on defense when needed, so he is earning his roster spot. Minnesota's front office and coaching staff are showing foresight by keeping the team prepared for injuries, and Pace has risen to the occasion.
Now that the Vikings are being seen as serious contenders this season, having solid depth and youth at key positions could go a long way to ensure that Minnesota is prepared for any hardship that might come its way.
We'll see what kind of role Pace will play down the stretch, especially if LB-related injuries remain an obstacle.

title: Vikings Verdict Week 11: Judging Cousins's Return, Addison's Injury & More Overreactions Ahead of 49ers Clash
full_text:
And just like that, the Vikings are back on track.
A dominant win over Green Bay has Minnesota looking like a Super Bowl-caliber team . It's safe to say that there's nobody in the league who wants to see the Vikings on the schedule right now.
But has the addition of Kirk Cousins made this team unstoppable? Is Jordan Addison's injury really not that big of a deal?
Let's dive into those Vikings overreactions and more ahead of the Week 11 Sunday Night Football showdown against the 49ers.
Despite having only a few days to prepare, Cousins led the Vikings to a 30-10 dismantling of the Green Bay Packers on Sunday. His numbers—207 yards and two touchdowns to one interception—won't jump off the page, but the rhythm and consistency the offense experienced can't be overstated.
The defense got to Jordan Love eight times and forced four turnovers, but as incredible as their performance was, it's actually pretty easy to envision Carson Wentz losing this game. The Vikings' offense under Cousins held the ball for 35 minutes against the Packers. Compare that to the 41 minutes of possession combined over the last two losses before his arrival.
Gavin Bartholomew's first NFL TD makes it a three-score game! MINvsGB on FOX/FOX One Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/LlozbGAGyJ
It certainly doesn't feel out of line to say that the 38-year-old Cousins took this team to a level they wouldn't reach otherwise. This was still probably a 10- or 11-win team thanks to their suffocating defense, but the Vikings are real contenders now with a guy who can make the plays an average quarterback should make.
On Monday, head coach Kevin O'Connell announced (h/t MicNuggets) that Addison's thumb injury will require surgery, effectively knocking him out for at least a few weeks . Obviously, it's not ideal to lose the No. 2 receiver just as a new quarterback enters the fold, but at the same time, things may not be all doom and gloom either.
Jordan Addison is likely a short-term IR candidate after aggravating a thumb injury Kevin O'Connell: “Just on Jordan Addison, tried to see if we could get him all the way to game day and see if we could possibly have him yesterday. But he did sustain a thumb injury, actually a… pic.twitter.com/emDjOFc7dn
Cousins clearly showed that he and Justin Jefferson still have a special connection after the two linked up nine times against Green Bay, and both Jauan Jennings and T.J. Hockenson should return to the lineup next week.
Jennings certainly hasn't lived up to expectations , but Cousins has a strong bond with Hockenson, and the pair has connected for 113 receptions for 997 yards over their 18 games together.
Losing Addison certainly hurts, as there's no question the offense is better with him on the field despite his modest 18 catches this season. At the same time, let's not forget what Cousins was doing in Las Vegas with Brock Bowers and a collection of unheralded wide receivers.
The Vikings' defense is the NFL's boogeyman, and the dark, shadowy figure at the center of all the fear is defensive coordinator Brian Flores.
Any way you slice it, the Vikings' defense ranks in the top five for most major metrics, and there's yet to be an offense that has figured them out. With such dominance, Flores figures to be one of the hottest names in next year's coaching carousel, but is he a goner for sure?
On paper, there's no reason Flores wouldn't get another shot at being a head coach, but reality is also a thing we deal with here on Earth, and the Vikings' defensive coordinator sits in a complicated situation. His current lawsuit with the league and controversial coaching methods in Miami make things complex, and his best option seems to be off the table already.
Many fans have called for Flores to be promoted to O'Connell's position, but after the win at Green Bay that included ownership presenting the head coach with a game ball, there's almost a zero percent chance the Vikings are moving on. Minnesota should throw every last penny they can offer at Flores in the offseason to retain him as defensive coordinator, but another team could still opt to make him their next head coach.
Flores' standing with the Vikings for 2026 is very much up in the air, and it's likely why the Vikings have waited to extend stars like Blake Cashman or Andrew Van Ginkel before they know who will be running the show.
