title: Grading Patriots Offensive Position Groups 10 Weeks In
full_text:
With the New England Patriots on their bye week and sitting at 5-5, it's a good time to evaluate how New England's offense has performed through the first 10 weeks. Here's a look at each offensive position group's performance and a subjective grade.
It feels like an unfortunate time to grade the QB position, given the recent news about Drake Maye's injury. Nevertheless, a grade must be assigned. Maye has had a roller-coaster season, with exceptionally high highs and very low lows. Early in the season, his performances were a noticeable departure from the level of play that earned him MVP runner-up honors the year prior. His fortunes changed during New England's Week 4 trip to Buffalo, kicking off a six-game stretch in which he accounted for at least three touchdowns in every game. His efforts earned him AFC Offensive Player of the Month honors for October. After Maye went down with a reported fractured ankle, backup Tommy DeVito left much to be desired. Against the Lions, DeVito completed 12 of 24 passes for just 81 yards, with one touchdown and an interception. Given DeVito's limited opportunities, it's difficult to assign him a meaningful season-long grade. As a result, this evaluation primarily reflects Maye's performance.
Even with his early-season struggles, it's difficult to overstate how important he has been to New England's success. He's been the primary reason the Patriots have remained competitive, especially as injuries have depleted the talent around him. However, it's equally difficult to overlook his 11 interceptions, which lead the NFL and have cost the Patriots at several points this season. The supporting cast hasn't exactly made his job easier, but Maye still deserves his share of the responsibility. Maye's ability to elevate the offense has been impressive, but turnovers and early-season inconsistencies have kept him from earning a higher mark.
The Patriots made significant investments in their receiving corps this offseason, hoping to give  Maye a more dynamic group of weapons to work with. That started with acquiring A.J. Brown in exchange for a 2028 first-round pick and a 2027 fifth-rounder , followed by signing Romeo Doubs to a four-year, $70 million contract in free agency. Unfortunately, injuries derailed those plans almost immediately. Brown has appeared in just four games through 10 weeks after suffering a high ankle sprain in Week 1 and dealing with a prolonged degenerative knee condition. Doubs, meanwhile, recorded 14 catches for 261 yards and three touchdowns before landing on injured reserve with a shoulder injury. The result? Maye has played just 16 offensive snaps with both receivers on the field at the same time, leaving New England's anticipated upgrade at wide receiver largely unrealized.
Drake Maye played 16 total snaps this season with A.J. Brown and Romeo Doubs on the field at the same time.
Efton Chism III, Demario Douglas, Kyle Williams, and Mack Hollins have had their moments, but the unit as a whole has been underwhelming given the significant capital invested in the group.
As a unit, the Patriots rank 16th in the NFL in rushing yards per game. While there have been stretches of effective production, the group has also been shut down at times, struggling to find week-to-week consistency. Rhamondre Stevenson has continued to be a reliable presence in New England's backfield, contributing as a runner, pass catcher and pass blocker. He's been their do-it-all guy. Corey Kiner has also been a solid addition since the Patriots acquired him in exchange for a 2028 seventh-round pick , providing an effective downhill running presence (averaging 4.5 yards per carry on 60 attempts). Lan Larison has had limited opportunities to make an impact in meaningful playing time. He did record his first NFL touchdown against Detroit, hauling in a 10-yard reception, but the score came with the outcome of the game already largely decided. The Patriots were, however, blindsided by the unexpected absence of TreVeyon Henderson. He had been having a difficult start to the season before revealing that he was dealing with an unusual medical emergency that ultimately landed him on injured reserve.
🙏🏽 pic.twitter.com/l52XuixPOc
Some of the unit's issues can be attributed to the significant injuries New England has sustained along its offensive line, but the bottom line is that the running game has been relatively average to below average.
One position group that has delivered for New England this season has been the tight ends. Hunter Henry has been a model of consistency throughout his Patriots career, leading the team in receptions (34) while ranking second in receiving yards (383). While Henry has struggled as a run blocker, his role as Maye's safety blanket shouldn't be forgotten. Rookie Eli Raridon has also shown plenty of promise as a pass catcher. His 71.8 PFF receiving grade ranks third among rookie tight ends, and he's already found the end zone twice. New England also hasn't been able to utilize fullback Reggie Gilliam as much as they likely hoped. After suffering ankle and knee injuries following the Patriots' win over Buffalo, Gilliam landed on injured reserve, limiting him to just five games and 71 total snaps this season. Tanner Arkin and Cameron Latu have primarily served as blocking tight ends in his place. Their roles became increasingly important after Julian Hill, whom New England signed to a three-year, $15 million contract in free agency, suffered an injury during OTAs. Arkin and Latu have been serviceable replacements, helping maintain some stability in the blocking game.
The Patriots' offensive line has been dealt a difficult hand this season, particularly at guard, where injuries have forced considerable turnover. New England lost Mike Onwenu to an ankle injury in Week 2, Alijah Vera-Tucker to a hamstring injury after Week 6, and Ben Brown on two separate occasions due to knee injuries. Despite the constant shuffling, several players have performed well individually. Brown, Vera-Tucker, Matt Pryor and Jared Wilson have all posted pass-block win rates above 90%, according to ESPN Insights. At tackle, Will Campbell has been solid for most of his sophomore season, allowing just three sacks through 10 weeks. Morgan Moses has been slowed down by foot and knee injuries. He's only allowed one sack, but that doesn't tell the full story. Both tackles have accounted for six penalties this season, tied for most on the team. First-round rookie Caleb Lomu has shown plenty of promise filling in at both tackle spots, making two starts without allowing a sack across 103 pass-blocking snaps. However, the individual performances haven't translated into consistent success up front. The Patriots are allowing pressure on 43.8% of dropbacks, the third-highest rate in the NFL. They're also allowing the fifth-highest pressure rate when opponents don't blitz (39.8%). While New England leads the league in time to throw (3.3 seconds), that may speak more to Maye's ability to extend plays and evade pressure than the protection in front of him. Ultimately, injuries and constant lineup changes have taken their toll. There have been some encouraging individual performances, but the offensive line has struggled to provide consistent protection and establish itself as a reliable unit.

title: Patriots WR A.J. Brown Likely Missing More Time After Sustaining Third Lower Body Injury
full_text:
New England Patriots A.J. Brown could be heading back to the sidelines due to an injury, missing his seventh game of the season.
After sustaining a hamstring injury in the second half of the Patriots' Week 10 loss to the Detroit Lions in Germany, Brown was seen heading into the locker room. Brown, who had previously missed extended time with a high ankle sprain , made his return against the Lions after missing two weeks with a knee injury.
The veteran receiver, who the Patriots acquired from the Philadelphia Eagles in the offseason , rejoins a plethora of players who are unable to take the field for the Pats.
On Wednesday, ESPN's Jeremy Fowler reported the following :
"In the short term, where the offense turns next is fascinating. Brown has a hamstring injury, which most likely puts him out for a little while. Romeo Doubs is eligible to return from injured reserve after his shoulder injury. One of their most explosive players, TreVeyon Henderson, is on IR for at least three more games. Rhamondre Stevenson is banged up. The trade deadline has passed, so it's not like the team can identify instant improvements. So, scoring points must be a collective effort, starting with the running game."
Brown's most recent injury enters in the shadows of star quarterback Drake Maye's ankle fracture, which is reported to potentially keep the third-year quarterback out for the remainder of the season.
AJ Brown expected to miss more time with a hamstring injury. Per: @JFowlerESPN pic.twitter.com/FwZWFH93EU
New England's receiving core is at its most typical without Brown on the lineup . In Week 12, the Patriots will have Mack Hollins, DeMario Douglas, Kyle Williams, and Efton Chism III available at receiver.
Wide receiver Romeo Doubs will also be eligible to be activated off the injured reserve, if he's ready to play after sustaining a shoulder injury in Week 6.
Tommy DeVito is expected to start for the Patriots after they come off the bye in Week 12 against the Chargers. After DeVito's rough performance on Sunday , the fourth-year backup quarterback will need all the help he can get.
Although, Brown's production this season indicates he might not be of much help to the Patriots or their second-string QB. Three of the Pats five losses have come when Brown's on the field, and his 11 receptions rank second to worst among non-running backs, while his 128 receiving yards are the lowest of all pass catchers on the Patriots roster.
After paying a heavy price for the Super Bowl-winning receiver, the Patriots will have to wait even longer for his production to show.

title: Should We Give Up On the 2026 Patriots?
full_text:
What is there to look forward to for the rest of this season for New England Patriots fans? Truthfully, not much. But there are places where the Patriots can find success, and maybe even a playoff birth this season.
After what many are describing as a "Super Bowl hangover," the New England Patriots sit at 5-5 entering their bye week.
Losing half the amount of games in the first 10 weeks of play isn't what fans drew up for a team that lost just three regular season games and ran through the AFC playoffs. But there have been flashes of brightness, and despite a major setback, not all hope is lost for the Patriots.
Quarterback Drake Maye's injury during Week 10's game against the Lions is what has most people in New England ready to call it quits on the 2026 season.
Maye, whose ankle was fractured while being sacked on the final play of the drive , was ruled out indefinitely and reports say that he could miss extended time and potentially, the rest of the season.
Backup quarterback Tommy DeVito's performance on Sunday didn't give Patriots fans much to believe in either, as the fourth-year player completed 50% of his passes for 81 yards, as well as a touchdown and an interception.
While speculation remains about whether the Patriots stick with DeVito, switch to seventh-round pick Behren Morton, or look elsewhere for their starting quarterback , fans should pump the breaks at calling this team 'broken.'
There's no reason to have faith in DeVito as a backup quarterback yet. But if he can collect a few wins while Maye is recovering , then the Patriots stand a chance at earning a Wild Card spot.
Yes, you heard that correctly: while Maye is recovering. There is a very real chance that Maye plays football again this season. Though reports indicated Maye could be out for the rest of the season, the same insiders making these claims said that both Rhamondre Stevenson and TreVeyon Henderson would miss extended time with separate injuries that caused neither of the two to miss game action.
The skepticism behind the reports that Maye's injury is season-ending should be discussed more when evaluating the near future of this Patriots team.
Currently, the Patriots are sitting one game back from the seventh seed in the AFC playoffs. New England has seven games to play in the 2026 season, with a majority of those games against teams with a winning record.
The biggest competitors for the Patriots spot in the playoffs are the Clevleand Browns (6-4) and the Las Vegas Raiders (4-6).
Cleveland has proven to be a challenging team to get through, but each of their wins this season has come in a one-score game. This should indicate that their legitimacy to contend for a playoff spot is overvalued. They could drop more than half of their remaining schedule, which includes to games against the Bengals and a trip to New Jersey to face the Giants.
🏈AFC Playoff Picture through Week 10!🏈 Is your team gonna make the playoffs? pic.twitter.com/3thecJox41
The Raiders, aren't as much of a concern for the Patriots, after New England dominated Las Vegas in Week 5 . This head-to-head victory for the Pats helps break a tie if the two teams find themselves in one. Las Vegas and New England will both play one of the best divisions in football in the reamining weeks of the season, but Vegas has to face the AFC West one additional time, compared to the three matches slated for the Patriots.
Realistically, New England should hope to win four of the last seven games to squeak into the playoffs. Finishing with a 9-8 record would allow the Patriots to secure a Wild Card spot and their second straight trip to the postseason. This record is commonly seen with seven seeded teams in the AFC.
Houston will also pose a threat to the final Wild Card spot, despite winning just three games this season. Last year, the Texans went on a large win streak to secure a playoff spot after a poor start to the season.
The familiarity of rooting for a tank is all too recent in the memory of Patriots fans, who watched back-to-back seasons where New England earned top-four picks in the NFL Draft.
Unfortunately, five wins is most likely too many for a pick that high, but New England could still end up close to the top 10 if they continue playing like they have over the past two weeks.
In the trade for A.J. Brown, the Patriots gave up a 2028 first-round pick instead of their first-round pick from this upcoming draft.
Mike Vrabel isn't the type of coach to tank for a draft pick. He build his idenitity on believing in the players that show up to the Patriots facility on day one of training camp.
The vibes in the Patriots building are “not good” Per: @DanGrazianoESPN He describes it as a “total Meltdown”. - ESPN insider @JFowlerESPN notes “Mike Vrabel is known for culture-building and tough-minded defense, and cracks in the foundation are showing on both fronts.” pic.twitter.com/CkzMiJhUqV
For this reason, it's unlikely that the Patriots will intentionally lose games, or put themselves in position to lose games, in favor of a better draft position.
However, if the Patriots don't make the playoffs, they'll likely miss it by a small margin (unless they completely collapse for the remainder of the season), which would put them in a difficult position, drafting in the late teens (where the not good enough, but not bad enough teams end up).
After the buy-in the front-office exercised this offseason, it's playoffs or bust for the Pats, whether or not Maye is their quarterback.

title: Is Drake Maye Coming Back This Year? Patriots Teammate Doesn't Think So
full_text:
The outlook for Drake Maye doesn't look great, and a fellow New England Patriots captain certainly didn't help.
Kevin Byard, who was voted a captain alongside Maye in his first season with the Patriots, was speaking on WEEI's Rich & Ken Tuesday and was asked about players stepping up in the wake of several major injuries across the board.
He mentioned how that's the reality of the situation the Patriots are in, and also offered some information about Maye's potential timeline.
"Like at the end of the day, our quarterback's out. He's probably going to be out for the rest of the season. And the reality of the situation is, is that we're going to have to get behind Tommy Two Chains (Tommy DeVito) at the end of the day," Byard said. "And you know, we're all going to have to do more, myself included. Everybody has to play better around our quarterback.
"I mean, this is honestly before Drake was injured as well. But we got to play better around our quarterback. We got two choices: we can rally behind this guy or we can pack it up. I mean, that's just where we're at right now in the season."
The Patriots haven't offered any additional comments about Maye's ankle, which was injured in the first quarter of Sunday's 35-10 loss to the Detroit Lions. Maye was sacked by Aidan Hutchinson — who tore his ACL celebrating the play — and would head to the locker room after a short time on the sideline.
DeVito came in to replace Maye, who is feared to have fractured his ankle.
"I'm not going to make any comments about his status until he gets back here," Mike Vrabel said Monday. "He's en route back here. He stayed with a few of our people, and they're en route back here. So, once he gets back here, and our people are able to visit with him again and talk with him again, I think we'll have more to offer. But I wouldn't imagine him being available when we come out of the bye."
The Patriots are 5-5 and now on their bye week , so they'll have some time to figure out their plans under center if Maye can't go for the remainder of 2026. If he isn't able to return in any capacity, it's a major blow for a team that was looking to get back to the Super Bowl after a season of great forture injury-wise.
This year? Not so much. Maye has been the latest player to suffer an injury that's put the team behind the 8-ball. Whether it's DeVito, rookie Behren Morton or an external signing , there will likely be a new quarterback leading the way.

title: NFL Flexes Week 12 Schedule: Patriots Bumped Off Primetime vs. Chargers
full_text:
In the wake of the New England Patriots losing Drake Maye to an ankle injury and the Los Angeles Chargers' 1-8 record, the NFL is stepping in to make a change to their Week 12 schedule.
The league announced Tuesday that they're flexing the Patriots vs. Chargers game, scheduled for Sunday Night Football, to a 4:05 p.m. start on CBS. The primetime game will instead be replaced by the Cleveland Browns vs. Las Vegas Raiders game, originally scheduled for 1 p.m. that day.
The Tennessee Titans vs. Jacksonville Jaguars game moves from 4:05 p.m. to 1 p.m. as a result.
Tuesday was the deadline for the league to reschedule the Week 12 games, and because of Maye's injury, moving the Patriots out of a national audience became an easy choice.
Heading into the season, the Patriots going on the road to face the Chargers felt like a great matchup. Two teams that made the postseason season ago with young quarterbacks leading the way was a great pick for a pre-playoff push game. In the AFC Wild Card game last year, the Patriots beat the Chargers 16-3 in a defensive slugfest.
Instead, the seasons of both New England and Los Angeles have fallen apart.
Maye got sacked in the team's 35-10 loss to the Detroit Lions in Week 10 and subsequently fractured his ankle on the play. Now with the Patriots rolling with Tommy DeVito and Behren Morton under center, the Patriots don't seem like an exciting product as they sit at 5-5.
The Chargers came into the year with high expectations, hiring former Miami Dolphins head coach Mike MacDonald to be their new offensive coordinator. That decision backfired, as the Chargers are currently in possession of the NFL's worst record. They picked up their first win of the year last night on Monday Night Football against the Baltimore Ravens.
With the league scheduling games on Wednesday, Thursday, Friday and Monday of Week 12, finding a good replacement for Sunday Night Football was going to be tricky. The San Francisco 49ers and Seattle Seahawks would have been a good replacement, but it was unlikely that FOX would have given that matchup up.
This removes the Patriots out of what would have been at least three more primetime games this season. They're currently scheduled to host the Vikings on Thursday Night Football in Week 14 and travel to play the Kansas City Chiefs in Week 15 on Monday Night Football.
While the Patriots' game against the Chargers has fallen out of favor with a national audience, one big storyline elsewhere has made the new SNF game a bigger deal.
With the Raiders trading away Kirk Cousins at the deadline and having first overall pick Fernando Mendoza step up last week, it's an opportunity for the league to showcase a young star who scored his first-career touchdown in his first start last game.
On the other side are the Browns, who are currently in control of the AFC's seventh seed after beating the Houston Texans a week ago. Deshaun Watson has come back and played really good football and right now, the Browns are one spot ahead of the Patriots in the conference standings.
The Patriots aren't in action this week, but will look to try and beat the Chargers to get back over .500 — this time during the afternoon instead of the evening.

title: Former Patriots QB Tells Mike Vrabel to 'Hit Me Up' After Drake Maye's Injury
full_text:
Drake Maye goes down against the Detroit Lions on Sunday, and now the New England Patriots are looking for someone to step into the role at quarterback next week.
Tommy DeVito, the second string, came in and didn't look good . Third-string Behren Morton hasn't taken a snap yet. And while head coach Mike Vrabel didn't seem to indicate that the Patriots would be looking for an external quarterback just yet, one former teammate of Vrabel's has thrown his hat into the ring.
Matt Cassel, who played four seasons with the Patriots from 2005 to 2008 and was the primary starter during an 11-5 season in 2008, jokingly took to social media to see if the Patriots head coach would end up calling him. Cassel said he hadn't signed any retirement papers, but hasn't taken a snap in the NFL since 2018.
"Hit me up Vrabes!," Cassel wrote on a report from NFL insider Jordan Schultz about the Patriots potentially exploring the quarterback market Monday. "I never signed any retirement papers!"
Hit me up Vrabes! I never signed any retirement papers! https://t.co/lnpXnLU6Xw
Cassel was a seventh-round draft pick by New England in 2005 and was their top backup behind Tom Brady during his tenure. He's got some experience stepping in for an injured starter. After Brady tore his ACL in the opening week of 2008, Cassel took over the reigns and led the Patriots to a winning record.
Vrabel, once a linebacker for the Patriots, was a teammate of Cassel's for six seasons. After the 2008 season, the Patriots traded Cassel and Vrabel to the Kansas City Chiefs for a 2009 second-round pick (a draft pick that would turn into safety Patrick Chung).
He'd spend two years in Kansas City, going 6-12 as a starter. Cassel would later go on to play for the Minnesota Vikings, Buffalo Bills, Dallas Cowboys, Tennessee Titans and Detroit Lions.
Obviously the Patriots won't be dusting off Cassel's old No. 16 jersey out of the closest, but they're going to have to find a new quarterback somehow, someway. There are some players with Vrabel/Josh McDaniels connections around the league that could end up coming in, like Jimmy Garoppolo, Bailey Zappe, Will Levis and Dorian Thompson-Robinson.
"I don't see that being the case right now," Vrabel said Monday when he was asked about potentially adding some external help. "But we'll have conversations, and we'll discuss it, and we'll look and see."
The Patriots are currently on their bye week and won't have to suit up again until next Sunday against the Los Angeles Chargers. It's likely that they'lre going to have to start just their 11th quarterback since 2000 in the process.
And no, it certainly won't be Cassel under center.

"I don't think Drake's being in there or not would have really — I mean it may have. I would highly doubt it," Mike Vrabel said postgame about his concern level with that unit. "Until we start doing the little things better in all three phases, the fundamentals, being able to run the football, being able to get open and catch and protect our quarterback, tackle, get off the field on third down, create turnovers, obviously we have to start turning it over offensively and then special teams, got to be able to create a spark for us and create some momentum plays."

title: Why Patriots Should, Shouldn't Sign QB Jimmy Garoppolo
full_text:
Could the New England Patriots reunite with a Super Bowl champion quarterback in the wake of Drake Maye's ankle injury ? It's not impossible.
NFL insider Jordan Schultz mentioned that Jimmy Garoppolo , a 2014 draft pick by the Patriots who was part of two Super Bowl teams as a backup, could be an option for the Patriots under center as they start to re-evaluate their quarterback options. Currently, Tommy DeVito and Behren Morton are the two on the roster, and for now, no external decisions have been made.
"I don't see that being the case right now," Mike Vrabel said. "But we'll have conversations, and we'll discuss it, and we'll look and see."
But should the Patriots replace the current No. 10 with a former No. 10? Let's weigh the options.
When you think of a typical Josh McDaniels quarterback, Garoppolo is one of those guys who can operate it very well. Spending the first three-plus seasons with the Patriots offensive coordinator in New England, and then for a short time in Las Vegas in 2023, Garoppolo is well-versed in the Patriots' offensive terminology.
Sure, what you might get out of Garoppolo isn't the same you'd get out of the explosive 24-year-old Maye, but it's not like you're getting a quarterback who's in over his head in the playbook. Both DeVito and Morton know what the system is, but Garoppolo has proven to operate it well in the past.
Garoppolo is 35 and has already contemplated retirement. He hasn't started a game since 2024 and hasn't made more than one start in a season since the year prior. He isn't getting any younger and for a Patriots team that still has postseason expectations, throwing a dart at this dartboard might not be the ideal scenario.
In his final year as a full-time starter (2023 with the Raiders, before injuries and McDaniels' firing sent him to the bench), Garoppolo went 110-for-169 with 1,205 passing yards, seven touchdowns and nine interceptions in seven games. Since then, you have no real productive snaps out of him.
At first, it felt like Garoppolo would be the future behind Tom Brady. Then Brady kept winning and Garoppolo was sent off to San Francisco in 2017. How funny would it be for the Patriots to somehow reverse course and bring back their former quarterback-in-waiting nearly 10 years after trading him away?
Patriots fans have proven to enjoy Garoppolo's play, at least before injuries in 2016 soured how people viewed him. It would be pretty poetic for the Patriots, seemingly dead in the water , to be saved by the player fans once assumed would be the heir apparent.
The Patriots likely woudn't sign Garoppolo to a contract to stick him on the bench. If they make this move, that feels like it would mean he's the starter over both DeVito and Morton. The Patriots agreed to a two-year extension with DeVito in the offseason to make him the QB2, so it might not be worth bringing in a quarterback who'd want to start on a deal that might not make sense.
If the team is looking for more depth and/or experience, there's certainly a lot more names that could be added for much cheaper (Will Levis, a fomrer Vrabel draft pick in Tennessee, is currently on the New York Jets' practice squad).
At this point, the Patriots are 5-5 and currently possess a roster that is capable — on paper — to make a playoff run . Injuries have hurt them beyond belief, but the hopes and expectations are still there for this group to succeed in the stretch.
If Garoppolo, who's played in a Super Bowl as a starter before, is the best chance to get this Patriots team there, then why not pull the trigger. Based on how DeVito looked against the Detroit Lions post-Maye injury, it can't get much worse. The Patriots have a chance to become a surprising second-half team, and maybe all it takes is Jimmy G to make those surprises happen.

title: Patriots QB Drake Maye is Injured, So Now What Happens?
full_text:
The New England Patriots' fortunes have gone from bad to worse . According to ESPN's Adam Schefter, the Patriots are concerned that quarterback Drake Maye suffered a fractured ankle in their Week 10 loss to the Detroit Lions. Maye remained in Germany for further evaluation to determine the extent of the injury and whether surgery will be necessary. Regardless of the results, he is expected to miss an indefinite amount of time, with the possibility that his season is over. "Once he gets back here and our people are able to visit with him again and talk with him again, I think we'll have more to offer," head coach Mike Vrabel told reporters Monday. "I wouldn't imagine him being available when we come out of the bye." The prospect of losing Maye for any amount of time, let alone the remainder of the season, is a devastating blow to the Patriots and their hopes of making a playoff run. Regardless, New England has to pick up the pieces. Maye's potential absence will have a ripple effect across the roster, forcing the coaching staff to reevaluate their approach heading into the second half of the season. So, what's next?
Will the Patriots bring in a veteran quarterback to help weather the storm, or will they roll with backups Tommy DeVito and Behren Morton? For now, the former seems more likely. New England handed DeVito a two-year, $7.4 million extension during the offseason and selected Morton in April's draft. Despite a difficult outing in relief of Maye, DeVito appears to have the coaching staff's confidence moving forward. "I have a lot of confidence in Tommy," Vrabel said. "I know his toughness is going to be through the charts, and his competitiveness will be exactly what we need."
However, NFL insider Jordan Schultz reports that New England is expected to explore the quarterback free-agent market during the bye week. Vrabel pushed back on those reports when asked about the possibility of bringing in another quarterback. “I don't see that being the case right now," Vrabel said. "But we'll have conversations, and we'll discuss it, and we'll look and see." Still, several QB options remain available if New England wants to go down that route. Notably, former Patriot Jimmy Garoppolo, who was named in the aforementioned Schultz report.
New England and DeVito struggled to find much success through the air after Maye's departure, completing just 50% of his pass attempts for 81 yards, one touchdown, and an interception. That came against a Lions defense that entered Week 10 ranked dead last in the NFL in passing yards allowed per game (260.9) and was without their top pass rusher, Aidan Hutchinson, for most of the contest. While the Patriots have mainly moved the ball through the air with Maye under center, they'll need to establish a more consistent rushing attack moving forward to take pressure off DeVito. New England currently ranks 17th in the NFL in rushing yards per game, averaging 114 yards. That's a middle-of-the-pack unit that will likely need to shoulder a larger share of the offensive workload with Maye likely out of the picture. Guard Alijah Vera-Tucker will be eligible to return from injured reserve following the bye week, potentially giving the offensive line a significant boost ahead of its Week 12 matchup against the Los Angeles Chargers. Paired with the return of fullback Reggie Gilliam, New England could have some reinforcements to help get its ground game back on track.
Losing Maye is obviously a major blow to the on-field aspirations, but it also presents a significant challenge for Mike Vrabel and the coaching staff inside the locker room. New England is entering one of the toughest stretches of its schedule, with matchups against the 7-2 Minnesota Vikings, 8-1 Buffalo Bills, 7-2 Kansas City Chiefs, and 7-2 Denver Broncos looming. The Patriots have already dealt with considerable adversity this season. Now, they'll have to prove they can respond to another major setback without allowing it to derail the foundation they've spent the last year and a half building. "We'll have to look at all things that we possibly can and find ways to improve, find ways to be on the same page, find ways to believe that we're all in this together, which is the first thing I told them," Vrabel said. "That it starts with me, and we're all in this together, and that the coaches will be connected, and they'll find ways to help each other and be part of the solution." Ultimately, this stretch will test more than just New England's depth at quarterback. It'll test the culture, leadership and resilience Vrabel has been working to establish since arriving in New England.

title: Mike Vrabel Expresses Confidence in Both Patriots Backup QBs
full_text:
The New England Patriots, a few years removed from all the Mac Jones/Bailey Zappe hoopla, are back under the quarterback spotlight. Drake Maye's ankle injury is reportedly serious enough to potentially knock him out for the remainder of the season and now the job under center may fall on two of the team's backups.
Tommy DeVito, who earned a two-year extension in the offseason, came in to replace Maye after his first quarter injury and didn't look all that promising. Behind him is seventh-round rookie Behren Morton, who's been working as the Patriots' emergency third quarterback in each of the team's 10 games this year.
While Mike Vrabel won't comment on Maye's status any more than saying he likely won't be available in Week 12, it's clear that the Patriots will have to roll with someone not wearing No. 10 for a bit.
"He stayed with a few of our people and they're en route back here," the head coach said Monday. "Once he gets back here and our people are able to visit with him again, and talk with him again, I think we'll have more to offer."
Currently, the Patriots have just DeVito and Morton in the building — and Vrabel is confident in both of them.
DeVito, who has experience as a starter in the NFL , came in to Sunday's game against the Detroit Lions and really struggled. The Patriots offense could not move the ball and he completed just 50% of his passes and threw under 100 yards. It wasn't a promising outing.
"I mean, the assessment was pretty much like the team. I don't think it was good enough," Vrabel said of DeVito's play. "I think there was some things that he missed, but also not having a ton of live action since training camp. And really, I think he'll be ready to go coming out of the bye.
"I think that he'll be able to look at some things and understand — whether that's being able to transfer up into the pocket or, you know, get us int he right play or get the ball out quicker, or look at protections or tations, whatever that may be. I think that'll all improve."
DeVito has won games before as a starting quarterback, including one against these Patriots back in 2023. But with a tough slate of games and postseason expectations looming, this will be a tougher challenge for him.
"I have a lot of confidence in Tommy," Vrabel said. "I know his toughness is going to be through the charts and his competitiveness will be exactly what we need."
Right behind DeVito on the depth chart is Morton, who the Patriots drafted with the 234th overall pick this year out of Texas Tec h . He's yet to step onto the field this year in a regular season game, but did have some positive plays in the preseason — including a game-winning touchdown pass to Nick DeGennaro in the closing seconds of their second game.
It's expected that the Patriots will have Morton jump into the QB2 spot, but maybe an external addition enters the picture as well. For now, Vrabel feels like his rookie is getting better.
"Tommy and Behren have been in our system, have been working," Vrabel said. "Behren's been improving. He's been working each week and I know that if he has to play for us, that he'll be ready to go. And I'm excited for his challenge and I hope that everybody else is because that's really what we're at. We're 5 and 5 in the middle of the season, just past the middle of the season."
NFL insider Jordan Schultz reported that the Patriots could potentially explore the market for a new quarterback , but Vrabel pushed back on that notion.
"I don't see that being the case right now," Vrabel said, just mere moments before Schultz's report came out. "We'll, you know, I mean, we'll have conversations and we'll discuss it and we'll look and see."

title: The Good, Bad and Ugly: Can the Saints Do Anything Right?
full_text:
The New Orleans Saints had an opportunity to take control of the NFC South on Sunday, but instead delivered another frustrating performance that raised more questions about the direction of the franchise.
New Orleans (3-6) suffered a heartbreaking 20-17 loss to the Carolina Panthers at the Caesars Superdome, surrendering a game-winning 54-yard field goal by Ryan Fitzgerald as time expired.
Despite Carolina committing 17 penalties for 152 yards, the Saints couldn't capitalize, finishing with just 49 rushing yards, two turnovers and another disappointing offensive performance under head coach Kellen Moore .
The loss dropped New Orleans to 1-4 at home and 0-2 against NFC South opponents, leaving the Saints searching for answers as their season continues to unravel.
Here is the good, bad and ugly from Sunday's loss.
Rookie wide receiver Jordyn Tyson led the Saints with 11 receptions, the most since Pierre Thomas caught 12 passes against the Chicago Bears in December 2007.
After missing the first seven games of the season, the rookie wideout has wasted little time demonstrating why New Orleans selected him eighth overall in April's NFL Draft.
His separation, contested catches, and reliability complement Chris Olave and should make this passing attack even deadlier.
However, the offense has become too predictable.
After a strong performance last week, the Saints' rushing attack went back to its old ways, gaining just 49 yards on 23 carries (2.1 yards per carry) against Carolina.
Quarterback Shough led New Orleans with 25 rushing yards, while Travis Etienne Jr. (14 yards), Audric Estime (6 yards), and Alvin Kamara (4 yards, 3-yard touchdown) combined for minimal output.
Although the absence of right tackle Taliese Fuaga and center Erik McCoy provides important context, the struggles within the ground attack were already present prior to their injuries.
Moore was hired because of his success as the offensive coordinator of the Philadelphia Eagles , one that had the NFL’s top rushing offense in 2024 and propelled them to a Super Bowl victory. He must fix the run game for New Orleans to sustain drives and score consistently.
Through nine games this season, the answer has been a firm no.
Carolina repeatedly handed the Saints chances by committing 17 penalties and struggling offensively, but New Orleans failed to capitalize.
The Saints were shut out in the first half, committed two turnovers, and generated insufficient offense against a sub-.500 Panthers squad. Even after Charlie Smyth tied the game with a 55-yard field goal with 41 seconds remaining, a pass interference penalty on Kool-Aid McKinstry set up Fitzgerald's game-winning kick.
More concerning is the lack of progress under head coach Kellen Moore.
Over nine games, the Saints have struggled with offensive inconsistency, poor execution and an inability to close games. Their 3-6 record inspires little confidence, and individual flashes from Tyson, Shough, and the defense cannot mask overall failure. To make matters worse, the Saints have trailed in all but one of the 26 games that Moore has coached in as the head coach of the Saints.
With upcoming road trips to Chicago and Cincinnati followed by a home game against the Green Bay Packers , the schedule provides no relief. Instead of making a statement in the NFC South, New Orleans showed just how far it remains from contention.

title: Saints Find Another Way to Lose as Panthers Steal NFC South Victory
full_text:
The New Orleans Saints had chance after chance to build momentum and secure their first consecutive wins of the season. Instead, it was another game that left a sour taste in everyone’s mouths like tomatoes in gumbo.
Kicker Ryan Fitzgerald connected on a game-winning 54-yard field goal as time expired, lifting the Carolina Panthers to a 20-17 victory over the Saints on Sunday afternoon at the Caesars Superdome.
The loss dropped New Orleans to 3-6 under second-year head coach Kellen Moore , while Carolina improved to 4-5 and strengthened its position in the NFC South standings.
Despite overcoming a sluggish first half and taking a fourth-quarter lead, the Saints couldn't finish the job, and Carolina escaped with a crucial divisional win.
Tyler Shough went 25-for-36 for 187 yards, with a touchdown and an interception, while rookie wide receiver Jordyn Tyson had a breakout game, leading New Orleans with 11 receptions for 80 yards.
Running back Alvin Kamara provided the Saints' biggest offensive spark, scoring twice in the second half on a 3-yard touchdown run in the third quarter and a 4-yard touchdown catch in the fourth.
However, New Orleans struggled offensively throughout the opening two quarters, committing two turnovers and failing to score before halftime.
Shough's first interception came on the Saints' opening possession when cornerback Marco Wilson deflected his fourth-down pass intended for Chris Olave , and linebacker Devin Lloyd intercepted it.
The Saints' defense kept Carolina from capitalizing, with Carl Granderson sacking Bryce Young on fourth down near the goal line.
Another costly mistake came in the second quarter when Shough and Audric Estime mishandled a handoff, allowing Panthers linebacker Jaelan Phillips to recover the fumble.
Carolina capitalized on the turnover with a 2-yard touchdown run by Chuba Hubbard , taking a 7-0 lead into halftime.
New Orleans finally found some traction in the third quarter.
Kamara capped a nine-play, 64-yard drive with a 3-yard touchdown run, tying the game at 7-7 with 6:33 remaining in the period.
However, Fitzgerald answered with a 55-yard field goal to restore Carolina's three-point advantage entering the fourth quarter.
The Saints responded with their best offensive sequence of the afternoon.
Shough connected with Kamara on a 4-yard touchdown pass, giving New Orleans its first lead at 14-10.
That advantage proved short-lived.
Hubbard scored his second touchdown on a 1-yard run, putting Carolina back ahead 17-14 late in the fourth quarter.
New Orleans refused to go away, with kicker Charlie Smyth drilling a clutch 55-yard field goal to tie the game at 17-17.
But Young and the Panthers orchestrated one final scoring opportunity, setting up Fitzgerald's game-winning kick as time expired.
Young finished with 200 passing yards, while Hubbard rushed for 92 yards and two touchdowns on 27 carries.
For the Saints, the defeat represents another frustrating setback in a season defined by inconsistency, offensive mistakes and an inability to capitalize on opportunities.
The Saints will now prepare for a road trip to the Buckeye State to take on the Cincinnati Bengals .

title: Saints vs. Panthers Inactives: Who's Out for Sunday's NFC South Showdown?

title: Saints vs. Panthers Predictions: Will New Orleans Win Its Second Straight Game?
full_text:
Sign up for the daily Saints Newsletter by clicking here .
The New Orleans Saints (3-5) return to the Caesars Superdome on Sunday looking to build momentum following last week's victory over Cleveland as they host the Carolina Panthers (3-5) in a crucial NFC South showdown.
With both teams looking to turn their seasons around, the Saints will need another strong performance from quarterback Tyler Shough and their defense to secure consecutive victories for the first time this season.
Here are our Saints ON SI staff predictions for Sunday's matchup between New Orleans and Carolina.
I think this will be a relatively close game for the Saints.
While the defense is flawed in some areas, New Orleans arguably has the best pass rush duo in Chase Young and Carl Granderson , who are both in the top five in sacks. However, I’m still worried about its inability to stop the run, especially when the opposing team has a solid running back. Unfortunately for the Saints, Carolina has a pretty dadgum good running back in Chuba Hubbard , who has rushed for 619 yards and reached paydirt five times this season.
On top of that, the Saints’ defense will go up against a better quarterback in Bryce Young , who has thrown for 2,197 yards with 18 touchdowns and six interceptions and is the face of the fourth-best passing attack in the NFL and one that features wide receiver Tetairoa McMillan (46 receptions, 625 yards, 3 touchdowns).
The good thing for the Saints is that the Panthers aren’t the greatest defense when it comes to stopping the run as they are 28th in the league in rushing yards allowed. The Saints were able to run the ball effectively last week against the Cleveland Browns , who also had a similar issue, but execution will be key.
Can the Saints pull off the win and remain in first place? It’s definitely a possibility.
However, I cannot trust Kellen Moore’s ability to manage and put together a game plan for four quarters because Tyler Shough and the Saints have won three games despite the offensive staff’s ineptitude.
Also, add on the fact that the Saints are missing two of their starting offensive linemen on an already porous offensive line in center Erik McCoy and right tackle Taliese Fuaga , the Saints’ chances of winning decrease.
Prediction: Panthers 21, Saints 14
I'm not quite sure what to think of this "new" Saints team. It's almost like there's a new set of faces each week in different places.
On Sunday, the Saints and Panthers play for first place in the NFC South in the Superdome. Admittedly, both teams have three wins in their eight games, but first place is on the line, nonetheless. It's hard to believe, but it was just 2021 that Tampa Bay , a team tied for the bottom of this division, won it all.
Point being, things change rapidly in this professional sport Americans love so much.
Neither of these teams is impressive in its own right, but here we stand with the mid-season top-of-the-totem position on the line.
Are the Saints finally starting to find an offensive rhythm? I mean, they did score in the first quarter against Cleveland, the first time this season they've put any points in the first period column.
Is the defense poised to stop the run better? They held Cleveland to under 100 yards rushing as a team, only the second time this year, the other being against the New York Giants .
Is the defense poised to stop the run better? They held Cleveland to under 100 yards rushing as a team, only the second time this year, the other being against the Giants .
Is the field goal crap shoot fixed with Charlie Smyth ? The Irishman made three of four field goals last week, missing from almost 50 yards from that pesky left hash mark.
There is hope, and I am going with it.

title: Saints Activate Travis Etienne Jr. From Injured Reserve Ahead of Panthers Game
full_text:
Running back Travis Etienne Jr. will be activated from injured reserve for the New Orleans Saints ' Sunday game against the Carolina Panthers , according to Tom Pelissero of The Ringer.
The 3-5 teams face off for sole possession of first place in the NFC South. Etienne has not played since Week 3 against the Las Vegas Raiders on Sept. 27, when he suffered a hamstring injury.
Upon returning to practice this week, Etienne fully participated by Friday and was listed as questionable.
In New Orleans, Etienne is expected to share backfield responsibilities with Audric Estime and Alvin Kamara . Estime posted a team season-high 72 rushing yards last week against the Cleveland Browns , while Kamara has recorded 157 yards with a 3.3-yard average through seven games.
The Saints rank 26th in the NFL in rushing, averaging 95.3 yards per game and 3.8 yards per attempt under head coach Kellen Moore . They will test a Panthers run defense that ranks 28th, allowing 133.4 yards per game and 4.6 yards per rush. In his three games this season before the injury, Etienne rushed for 128 yards (4.3 per carry), including 57 yards against Las Vegas, and added 11 receptions for 51 yards.
The 27-year-old running back joined New Orleans during free agency on a three-year contract after four seasons with the Jacksonville Jaguars , who selected him in the first round of the 2021 NFL Draft. Etienne topped 1,000 rushing yards in three of his four years with Jacksonville. A Louisiana native out of Jennings High School, he played at Clemson, earning All-America honors three times and twice winning ACC Offensive Player of the Year.
In additional roster adjustments, New Orleans placed defensive lineman Christen Miller on Injured Reserve. The team also promoted tackle Easton Kilty from the practice squad to the active roster and elevated kicker Charlie Smyth for Sunday's matchup with the Carolina Panthers.
Smyth stepped into the starting role following the release of Daniel Carlson and capitalized on the opportunity. The Irish kicker provided all nine of the Saints' points through three quarters in a low-scoring battle against Cleveland, going 3-for-4 on field goals with conversions from 30, 27, and 48 yards.

title: Saints Injury Report: Tyler Shough Loses Two Key Protectors Against Panthers
full_text:
The New Orleans Saints will be short-handed in Sunday’s rivalry game with the Carolina Panthers , with the heaviest hits being on the offensive line.
Head coach Kellen Moore ruled out multiple players with injuries, including two starting offensive linemen: center Erik McCoy (bicep) and right tackle Taliese Fuaga (knee). The team will also miss rookie running back CJ Donaldson (shoulder) and second-round defensive lineman Christen Miller (knee).
The Saints got a little more than three quarters of football out of their starting five offensive linemen last week before McCoy exited with an injury. Then Fuaga suffered a knee sprain in practice. Moore said Fuaga isn’t expected to miss enough time to land on injured reserve, but McCoy’s outlook is less certain.
A few other players are questionable for Sunday’s game with the Carolina Panthers. Running back Travis Etienne Jr. (hamstring) is the big name, but cornerback Martin Emerson Jr. is one to watch, too. We’ll find out for sure when the inactives list is published on Sunday.
The Saints got more than three quarters of action from their starting offensive line in last week's win over the Cleveland Browns before McCoy exited with a biceps injury.
The situation worsened when Fuaga suffered a knee sprain during practice, leaving New Orleans without two important pieces of its offensive front.
Moore indicated Fuaga's injury is not expected to require a stint on injured reserve, although McCoy's recovery timeline remains uncertain.
McCoy's absence could prove particularly challenging as he plays a critical role in identifying defensive fronts, communicating protection adjustments and helping maintain continuity across the offensive line as the center.
Without him, New Orleans must rely on Cesar Ruiz to handle those responsibilities while adjusting to a reshuffled interior with Jeremiah Wright taking Ruiz’s spot at right guard.
Fuaga's injury creates another significant concern at right tackle, where Asim Richards could be called upon to step into the starting lineup.
The Saints also dealt with injuries involving left tackle Kelvin Banks Jr. (ankle) and guard David Edwards (knee) throughout the week. While both returned to full participation Friday, it’s another sign that this unit is not even close to 100%.
Even with Banks and Edwards, losing two starters makes it hard for an offensive line that has struggled with pass protection and consistency in the running game.

title: Why John Harbaugh Isn’t Worried About Abdul Carter’s Low Sack Total
full_text:
An old saying, attributed to author Aaron Levenstein , goes, “Statistics are like bikinis; what they reveal is suggestive, but what they conceal is vital.”
No one knows that better than New York Giants head coach John Harbaugh and outside linebacker Abdul Carter.
At first glance, Carter, in his second NFL season, is having an “off year” in terms of his pass-rushing game. The 23-year-old outside linebacker has recorded just 2.0 sacks in nine games, half of what he finished with last season in 17 games (nine starts).
His tackle total is also down, with Carter having just 22 tackles versus the 43 he had as a rookie.
Other metrics suggest Carter is just as productive as ever, including ESPN’s pass-rush win rate, where he ranks second (29%) behind Miami Dolphins linebacker Chop Robinson, and his 17 quick pass pressures (under 2.5 seconds), ninth-best in the league.
But to Harbaugh, the rush of numbers that, depending on one’s perspective, either confirms that Carter is making an impact or contradicts the notion means nothing.
“I don’t really look at the metrics personally every week. I don’t go through all those stats and try to dig out every little metric on every guy. We get a general accounting of it,” Harbaugh said.
“I definitely look at the team stats. But I’m looking at the tape. I’m grading every single guy. Plus, every coach is grading their position all the time. And he’s grading out really well on my sheet; I can tell you that, and the coaches’ sheet.”
Carter’s lack of numbers could be largely due to the absence of fellow outside linebacker Brian Burns, who was lost for the season due to an ACL injury back in Week 3. Since then, Carter has undoubtedly drawn more attention in the form of chips and double teams by opponents looking to slow him down.
As a result of the extra attention he receives, Carter is in fact opening up other opportunities for his teammates to swoop in and make plays.
As for the sacks, which Harbaugh didn’t dispute are important, they’ll come when they come.
“He’s a disruptive guy. I promise you they’re accounting for him,” Harbaugh said. “You’ve got to go play football. I mean, you can have a bunch of sacks and still not be playing that well. We’ve seen that before too.
“So he’s that kind of player. He’s a disruptive player. He’s a game changer, game wrecker, and I think there’s going to be a lot of game wrecks in his future.”

title: Giants’ D.J. Reader, Chris Manhertz Talk Teamwork With NYC Teens at Public Library Event
full_text:
The New York Giants know that any path to victory starts with teamwork.
That’s the message defensive lineman D.J. Reader and tight end Chris Manhertz, a Bronx native, helped deliver Monday night to dozens of teenage students in the New York Public Library’s “ Teen Reading Ambassadors ” program.
“We are delighted to have welcomed the New York Giants to the Library alongside Citizens for a mentorship event with our wonderful Teen Reading Ambassadors,” said Brian Bannon, the Merryl and James Tisch Director of Branch Libraries and Education and Chief Librarian.
“The Giants and our teens talked about the importance of teamwork, whether on the football field or working with younger children at their library branch, offering homework help and more.”
Manhertz and Reader are certainly no strangers when it comes to the importance of teamwork. As part of 11-man unit with a common, united goal on every play aimed at pushing Big Blue across the finish line, each man knows his role on any given play, which Manhertz said is key.
“Everybody has a piece of the whole pie, and your whole team is relying on you to be accountable to whatever role you have," he said. "We need different perspectives for each team. It helps carry the entire team a long way.”
Reader added, “You may be in a position where maybe you’re not the captain or something, but you still give a lot of value in leadership. So you also still want to bring those young guys along.
“Maybe you can help them with plays, things like this and that while also not stepping on anybody else’s toes. So those are important. You’ve got to listen to your leader and be able to have some of your lieutenants help you out.”
The New York Public Library’s Teen Reading Ambassadors program offers internships to teens to develop job readiness and leadership skills by mentoring younger children. Ambassadors also help promote the Library’s mission to inspire a lifelong love of reading and learning.
They are also involved in writing, designing, and editing Portal , the library’s magazine for children ages 6-12. The title was chosen because it means “doorway or entrance into something new.”
As part of the event, the Giants also donated $15,000 to the program.

title: NY Giants Will Need a "Special Game" to Upset the Jaguars
full_text:
New York Giants head coach John Harbaugh always made it clear from day one that he would play at a high level on special teams. That was the case during his 18 years with the Baltimore Ravens, and it was a product of his NFL beginnings as a special teams coach under Andy Reid in Philadelphia.
It made perfect sense as Harbaugh sought to bring the team back into playoff contention quickly. More often than not, the hidden yardage and points scored on special teams can lift a team to another level.
The Giants lived up to his expectations during the first month of the season, but the unit has struggled since its terrific start.
All-Pro punter Jordan Stout has been sensational, sans one shanked 12-yard punt that cost the Giants significant field position in the fourth quarter of last week's loss to the Washington Commanders.
He's tied for second in the NFL in gross punting average (50.8), tied for fourth in net punting average (43.7), and has posted a league-leading 3.4 net yards over average.
Rookie kicker Dominic Zvada (out of Michigan), meanwhile, is trying to break out of a month-long slump that started with three missed field goals during the Week 5 tie at Washington.
He has missed six of his last 10 attempts, with each miss coming from the right hashmark. Five of those misses have been from at least 44 yards, including three from 50 or more.
Zvada's downward turn was a big surprise since he opened his pro career with nine straight conversions, including three from at least 50 yards. Leg strength is his calling card, as shown by his 6-of-9 from 50+ this season. So far, the Giants have shown patience with him.
Despite finding a way to navigate earlier injuries, the return game has hit some recent rough spots. Returner Charlie Jones fumbled in Weeks 6 (New Orleans) and 9 (Philadelphia), and those led to him being waived this week.

title: Giants Notebook: Cam Skattebo to Cut Back on Backflips,  Practice Squad Tweaks, More
full_text:
New York Giants running back Cam Skattebo, known for his penchant for celebratory backflips, is apparently ready to shelve the action after suffering a season-ending knee injury during a post-sack celebration by Detroit Lions pass rusher Aidan Hutchinson last week.
Skattebo, per the New York Post , told reporters that it was hard to see Hutchinson get injured the way he did. “I’m saying yeah (no more backflips). Mentally, I’m like, ‘I’m not doing that.’ That ain’t going to happen to me.”
Skattebo’s backflips have been a source of consternation for both general manager Joe Schoen and head coach John Harbaugh.
In May, while still recovering from a broken ankle suffered in his rookie campaign, he did a backflip at the Brian Burns Celebrity Softball Game.
Then in early July at a FanFest event in New York City, Skattebo did another backflip on a bouncy stage, only this time failing to stick the landing. That action prompted Schoen to openly admit he'd told the running back to rethink doing the backflips.
More recently, Skattebo, who, in a team-produced documentary chronicling his rehab and return to the field from his season-ending ankle injury, said he’s been doing backflips since he was a young child, did a backflip after scoring on a touchdown in the team’s Week 10 loss to the Washington Commanders on Thursday Night Football .
That said, Skattebo said neither Schoen nor Harbaugh had talked with him about the celebratory move after the Hutchinson injury. Still, he isn't ruling out bringing back the backflips for a special occasion like the playoffs.
A day after the New York Giants cut cornerback Nikko Reed and receiver Charlie Jones from the 53-man roster to make room for cornerback Tavierre Thomas and receiver Xavier Gipson from the Minnesota Vikings and Eagles practice squads, respectively, both Giants were added back to the team’s practice squad.
Reed has appeared in three games for the Giants’ special teams unit after having signed with the team from the Los Angeles Chargers practice squad. He recorded one tackle in his appearances.
Jones had been the return specialist for the Giants following the season-ending foot injury suffered by Braxton Berrios earlier in the year. He had recently struggled with ball security and production in that role.
The Giants waived running back Eric Gray and offensive lineman Geno VanDerMark from the practice squad to create spots for Reed and Jones.

title: Giants’ Week 11 Injury Report Brings Good News on Key Starters
full_text:
Ahead of their Week 11 game against the Jacksonville Jaguars, the New York Giants have a relatively light injury report, with several pleasant surprises.
Cornerback/special teamer Nic Jones (knee) was the only player who did not practice on Wednesday. Jones, who wasn’t spotted during the media portion of practice, is someone to watch as a candidate for injured reserve this week.
The Giants, remember, poached cornerback Tavierre Thomas off the Vikings’ practice squad, and Thomas can fill the punt gunner role, where Jones had been contributing.
Otherwise, the only other notable injuries listed by the Giants were safety Jason Pinnock (hip) and outside linebacker Malik Harrison (groin).
Not listed on the Week 11 injury report were starting tackles Andrew Thomas (groin) and Jermaine Eluemunor (calf), quarterback J.J. McCarthy (hip) and receiver Malik Nabers (knee), all of whom were on the Week 10 injury report.
The Jaguars will reportedly be without starting center Robert Hainsey this week after the six-year veteran suffered a knee injury in the team’s win over the Tennessee Titans last week, leaving him week-to-week with a knee sprain.
Jonah Monheim is believed to be the next man up according to the Jaguars’ unofficial depth chart . Monheim relieved Hainsey last week, went on to play 33 snaps, and pitched a shutout in that showing.
The second-year center, a seventh-round draft pick out of USC last year, has allowed eight pressures in 140 pass-blocking snaps . But he is also on the injury report, listed with an ankle ailment that kept him limited in the team's Wednesday practice.

title: Giants vs. Jaguars: Where Trevor Lawrence Is Most Vulnerable
full_text:
The New York Giants begin the challenging part of their 2026 schedule this week against the Jacksonville Jaguars, who are fresh off a 40-23 win over the Tennessee Titans. It will be the second career game for Jaguars quarterback Trevor Lawrence against Big Blue, the first coming on Oct. 23, 2022, in a Giants win.
Lawrence will enter his next game against the Giants bearing the ninth-best completion rate (66%) in the league. He’ll face a Giants pass defense that has been very solid this season and currently ranks third in passing yards allowed (184.1/game) and second in average pass yards per play (6.2/attempt).
Meanwhile, on the defensive side of the ball, the Jaguars boast the ninth-best overall defense (319.2 yards/game) and the sixth-best run defense (91.0 yards/game), making for a formidable challenge for a Giants team that not only aspires to get to the postseason, but also to hang around.
The Jaguars have the fifth-easiest remaining strength of schedule , according to Tankathon. In their last three games, all wins, they have pounded their opponents (the Colts, Ravens and Titans) into submission, winning all three by two or more scores.
The key for the Giants? Stopping Jaguars quarterback Trevor Lawrence.
Lawrence and company are averaging 29.9 points per game (fourth). But there is a stat the Giants can potentially play to their advantage that doesn’t get talked about much: batted balls.
Lawrence has posted eight batted passes this year , tied for the fifth most in the NFL among quarterbacks, and one of those batted balls turned into an interception for the defense.
This week, he’ll face a Giants defensive front led by defensive tackle Shelby Harris, who has two batted passes this year (tied for 15th) and 18 batted balls since 2020, tying him for eighth most in the NFL.
This is a surprising stat considering Lawrence stands 6-foot-6, but on film, he is more prone to having passes knocked down at the line of scrimmage when he’s under pressure, and he compromises his arm angle.
Therein lies one challenge for the Giants defense. The Jaguars, per PFF, have allowed the fewest quarterback pressures this season (86), so getting to Lawrence is not going to be easy, even with the Jags having a banged-up offensive line, the latest addition to which is center Robert Hainsey, who is expected to miss this weekend’s game with a knee sprain.
It goes without saying that this week in practice, the Giants defensive coaches will place a strong emphasis on getting their hands up in the passing lanes, particularly if they end up getting stonewalled at the point of attack.
Interesting fact: Lawrence has a 55.1% completion rate when facing man coverage and a 72.4% completion rate against zone coverage. The Giants have played man coverage on 25.6% of their snaps (sixth most) and zone on 69.1% of their snaps (seventh lowest).
Although the numbers suggest man coverage is the way to go against Lawrence, there is a hidden danger that should give New York pause: Lawrence’s legs.
When facing man coverage, Lawrence has taken advantage of defenders having their backs to him, rushing six times for 32 yards (5.3 average) and converting four first downs.
When facing zone coverage, Lawrence has run 14 times for 76 yards (5.4 yards/carry) and has just five first downs.
No defense ever plays 100% man or zone, and that’s unlikely to start this week.
But it wouldn’t be surprising if the mix of man and zone coverage tilts more toward the latter, and if the Giants emphasize aggressive man coverage against receiver Parker Washington, who leads the Jaguars with 645 yards on 36 receptions and six touchdowns this season.
The Giants host the Jaguars on Sunday, with kickoff set for 4:35 p.m.

title: Giants Fall in MMQB Power Rankings After Commanders Loss
full_text:
Just four days after riding the immense high of beating the Philadelphia Eagles on the road for the first time since 2013, the New York Giants were quickly brought back down to earth by a gut-wrenching 24-21 primetime loss to the Washington Commanders last Thursday.
What stood out as the bigger disappointment for John Harbaugh and company was their blown chance to deal the knockout punch to a second divisional foe’s season in that span while adding another game’s distance between themselves and the Dallas Cowboys, who are currently trailing them in second place.
As a result, SI’s senior writer Conor Orr put a lid on their three-week ascension, dropping Harbaugh’s group four spots to No. 15 in his latest MMQB NFL power rankings ahead of Week 11.
Even with their recent setback in the standings, Orr still views the Giants as the NFC East frontrunners.
“Coming out of the miniature bye, the Giants still control the destiny of the NFC East,” Orr said.
“Even with Jacksonville, Seattle, Detroit and San Francisco on the remaining schedule, taking care of business against a lackluster field featuring Indianapolis, Cleveland, Dallas and Philadelphia will land Big Blue in the postseason,” Orr added.
Despite losing a game to the Commanders that some could argue the Giants gave away multiple times, they did manage to earn some help from San Francisco, which kept the Cowboys at bay by dropping them to 4-6 with a thrilling 46-40 victory in Arlington.
At 5-3-1, the Giants are certainly not safe atop their perch as they prepare to welcome the red-hot Jaguars, tied for the league’s second-best record, to MetLife Stadium on Sunday at the start of a difficult four-game window.
Typically, it takes until the last couple of weeks of the regular season before any semblance of “scoreboard watching” would draw the attention of teams vying for postseason positioning, but in a tight NFC East where three teams are still mathematically in the running for the division crown, the Giants could find themselves falling into the trap beginning this weekend.
As tempting as that might be, Harbaugh has to make sure his men stay focused on what they can control. Relying on outside factors is never a bold strategy in the modern NFL; instead, the Giants will likely have to prove they can take down at least one of the goliaths standing in their way.
The cards might be stacked against them with the Jaguars, who have been dominating opponents on the scoreboard and have made major improvements across their defense, which excels at stopping the run and forcing turnovers. The only saving grace is that the Giants will have had extra rest from their mini bye after Thursday night's game.
If they don’t get an upset over Jacksonville, some outsiders might say the team has a shot against Seattle, whose quarterback situation has been in flux due to injuries, or Detroit, whose defense took a major blow with the loss of All-Pro edge rusher Aidan Hutchinson, who tore his ACL in Week 10.
Regardless of how they get to the eight or nine wins that could be enough to get them over the hump and win the division, the best approach the Giants can take is the one they’ve already pressed onto black T-shirts that have been seen at practice during media viewing periods.
That is, to strive to go 1-0 in each of their remaining eight contests, which surely include a few they could feasibly conquer. The rest of the chips can only fall where they may, especially considering the Cowboys and Commanders also have to play most of the same opponents down the stretch.
Of course, the Giants could have made this a little easier if they’d handled their business against Washington and put their chase to bed, but that hasn’t been the story of Harbaugh’s first season in New York.
Not one of his team’s victories has come easily, and that will most likely remain the case as the Giants’ pursuit of one of the coveted postseason spots is still theirs to lose.

title: Giants-Jaguars Week 11: Xavier Gipson, Zvada and Nabers Among Key Storylines
full_text:
It’s gut-check time for the New York Giants , who, after a mini bye, dive right into preparing for the most challenging part of their 2026 schedule, starting this week with a home date against the Jacksonville Jaguars (7-2).
This nationally televised game is going to tell us a lot about the state of the Giants, starting with their resiliency, a characteristic that head coach John Harbaugh and his players have taken pride in showing through thick and thin.
It can probably be agreed that in the Thursday night loss to Washington, the Giants, from players down to coaches, did not have their best game and probably wanted a few things back.
But Harbaugh is not one to dwell on the past. The Giants head coach said he has the utmost confidence in his team, backed by their resilience in pulling off close wins.
“You’ve watched us play. People have watched us play. You know where we are. We’re going to do everything we can to win the game. Our guys are going to fight like crazy,” he said.
“They’re going to compete, and we’re capable of making plays. We can make plays on both sides of the ball. We’re chasing consistency, just like every single team in this league is.
“The so-called heavyweights, I’ve seen them play bad games too,” he continued. “This is a tough league. It’s pretty even. We’re in it just like everybody else. We’ll be fighting in there just like everybody else. And I know our guys; nobody’s going to outfight us. That’s for sure. Nobody is going to outcompete us without question.”
We’ll find out if he’s right starting Sunday, when the Giants host a heavyweight.
When we last left the Giants, the only player to miss the Week 10 contest against the Commanders was linebacker Malik Harrison (groin). Before the team took its mini bye, Harbaugh told reporters he expected to have Harrison back.
That doesn’t mean the Giants will have a completely clean injury report on Wednesday, as there are bound to be players with lingering issues, running back Cam Skattebo comes to mind, whose workloads might be managed.
Still, with the NFL season heading into the homestretch, the Giants are as healthy as can be unless something is lurking that isn’t yet known.
The Giants shook up their special teams return game, dropping receiver Charlie Jones and adding receiver Xavier Gipson from the Eagles’ practice squad. Gipson, who was with the Giants in training camp, will presumably take over kickoff and punt return duties, and the Giants hope he’ll be an upgrade.
His career numbers suggest that could be the case, as he has averaged 9.1 yards per punt return and 25.9 yards per kickoff return. However, he has also had some ball-security issues, recording six career fumbles on punt returns.
Harbaugh has already shown little tolerance for ball-security issues, so if Gipson wants his third stint with the Giants to last a while, ball security must be paramount.
The Giants haven’t had many players in for workouts in the last few weeks, and of those they have, none have been kickers.
That’s because Harbaugh still has confidence in undrafted rookie Dominic Zvada, who missed his lone field goal attempt (33 yards) last week and has six misses (all from the right hash) since Week 5.
Harbaugh has pointed to a problem with Zvada’s plant leg for his struggles. The question is whether the Giants can help him fix it, or whether the yips Zvada appears to be struggling with have become so embedded that things are beyond repair.
If the latter is the case, it’s fair to wonder how much longer the Giants will stick with the rookie.
After a stellar October in which he posted four straight games with 100-plus receiving yards, Malik Nabers has cooled off. In his last two games, he has caught 10 of 15 targets for 87 yards and no touchdowns. In fact, his last touchdown came in Week 5.
Nabers also has three drops this season and two fumbles, one of which he lost. Even more concerning, after averaging 3.83 first downs per game through his first six games, he is down to 2.3 over his last three.
Part of that obviously has to do with opponents erasing him from the game, but when opportunities do arise, Nabers has to be more consistent in making them.
He’ll have a challenge this week, as he’s likely to face Travis Hunter, who has been playing some solid ball. It will be interesting to see how the Giants plan to scheme Nabers open.

title: Wan’Dale Robinson’s Injury Could Cost Giants a 2027 4th Round Compensatory Pick
full_text:
Nov. 18 Update: Jim Wyatt of Titans.com, reported that Wan'Dale Robinson is out for the season .
The New York Giants ' path toward landing a fourth-round comp draft pick in 2027 has hit a snag, according to projections from Nick Korte of Over the Cap.
Korte projected that the Giants might be in line for an extra fourth-round pick as compensation for losing receiver Wan’Dale Robinson in free agency to the Tennessee Titans.
However, with news of Robinson landing on IR after suffering an ankle injury in the team’s Week 10 loss to the Jacksonville Jaguars, that move, which will require Robinson to miss a minimum of four games, could be problematic for the Giants.
Wan'Dale Robinson going on IR could be problematic for the round of the Giants' expected 2027 compensatory pick. He's been barely hovering above the 4th/5th round bubble, and missing 4 games could make it difficult for him to stay above that cutoff. https://t.co/kszjlueNQn pic.twitter.com/KzBSNvruhL
Korte explained that Robinson has “barely been hovering above the fourth/fifth round bubble” as it stood before landing on IR. Now that he’s looking at missing at least four games, the question is whether Robinson will finish within range for the Giants to get a fourth-round comp pick for him.
The Giants currently have five draft picks locked in for 2027: their own first, second, third, and sixth-round picks, and a sixth-round pick owed by the Jacksonville Jaguars in the Daniel Falaale trade.
The Cleveland Browns own the Giants' fourth-round pick, which they received as part of the package New York gave up to move in the third round of the 2026 draft to select wide receiver Malachi Fields.
The Minnesota Vikings also own the Giants’ fifth-round pick, which the Giants gave up to acquire quarterback J.J. McCarthy in September.
Korte added that the Giants should still be in line to receive a fifth-round comp pick so long as Austin Schlottmann remains the Titans starting center.
