title: Giants' 3 Toughest Remaining Opponents—and One Sneaky Trap Game
full_text:
The New York Giants (5-3-1) will only get red in the face if they dwell on their Week 10 home loss to the Washington Commanders. A surefire opportunity to take firm control of the NFC East instead became an unpleasant reminder that progress is not always linear.
Big Blue will have had 10 days to regroup by the time it plays its next game, and it must use that mini-break to sharpen its on-field execution and play-calling. The schedule is about to ramp up , so John Harbaugh had better have his team ready.
Three matchups stand out as ominous, and one could make fans combust if the Giants do not emerge victorious. The list kicks off with a huge challenge this Sunday.
The Jacksonville Jaguars (7-2) are, on paper, ahead of the Giants, and if their recent history with inferior squads is any indication, the home crowd at MetLife Stadium had better brace itself.
The Jags boast a +125 point differential, which is far and away the best mark in the NFL. Only two of their wins were by one possession. They scored 30 or more points in the other five, and their two losses were by a combined 10 points.
A 34-31 loss to the Houston Texans in London in Week 6 should give Giants fans some optimism, especially since New York beat that same team the following Sunday, but this is a daunting matchup .
Quarterback Trevor Lawrence operates an offense that ranks in the top five at 29.9 points per game, and the reloaded defense allows an AFC-best 16.0 points per game. The Jaguars are balanced, well-coached, and quite formidable on the road. And, oh yeah, kicker Cam Little has possibly the biggest leg in the league.
Harbaugh and his staff will really have to shine if they want to keep pace with this AFC title contender.
Two weeks after battling dangerous Jacksonville, the Giants will host the Super Bowl favorites. The San Francisco 49ers will push defensive coordinator Dennard Wilson to be more creative than ever.
Head coach Kyle Shanahan wields a wand over a dynamic offense that features MVP candidate Brock Purdy, former Offensive Player of the Year Christian McCaffrey, five-time All-Pro tight end George Kittle, and accomplished wide receivers Mike Evans (questionable) and Keenan Allen.
Outside linebacker Abdul Carter and the Giants’ defensive line must bring the pressure, otherwise Shanahan will work his magic at will. Fans may learn just how much this squad has progressed under Harbaugh when this one concludes.
The Detroit Lions may have the better record and the better offense, but for a young quarterback like J.J. McCarthy, who has already absorbed some big hits this season, a Dec. 13 meeting with the defensively ferocious Seattle Seahawks seems more intimidating.
The defending Super Bowl champions give up a mere 236.1 yards per game, nearly 37 yards fewer than the second-best mark. They are physical and savvy, allowing offenses little time and few opportunities to make something happen.
How Big Blue’s offensive line performs will likely dictate the outcome. J.J. McCarthy has shown what he can do when afforded the chance to scan the field. This may wind up being his toughest test of the year, especially with the unrelenting crowd at Lumen Field.
Defensively, New York will be challenged to stop Jaxon Smith-Njigba. But if its fairly stingy secondary can minimize the damage, the Giants could leave the Emerald City with a “W,” as playoff implications should loom large for both squads.
The Indianapolis Colts took a hammer to their foundation before the trade deadline and just snapped a five-game losing streak by beating a fellow rebuilding team in Miami. They face organizational uncertainty and have holes all over their roster.
So why should fans be worried? Simply put, the Giants have struggled to earn straightforward victories against weak competition. They needed game-sealing interceptions to hold off the last-place Tennessee Titans and Arizona Cardinals, and they also lost at home to the New Orleans Saints.
There is also the Daniel Jones element . It would be the most Giants thing ever if the former No. 6 overall pick, who has now underachieved on two big contracts, were to torch his ex-squad.
The Colts still have star running back and former New York trade target Jonathan Taylor. Harbaugh and general manager Joe Schoen withdrew an offer for the former rushing champ before the deadline, so they might take some joy in embarrassing Indy on its home field.
The Giants cannot come into this game overconfident, however. They still face the Jaguars, 49ers, Seahawks, Cleveland Browns, and Detroit Lions before the end of 2026. In other words, this team does not have another bad loss to spare.

title: 3 Jets Coaches Whose Jobs Should Be in Jeopardy to Begin Week 11
full_text:
Coming off their latest humiliating divisional loss after last Sunday's 31-12 defeat to the Bills, the Jets head into a two-game road trip that begins with a Week 11 meeting against the Chargers with their focus on ending a five-game losing streak.
With a 2-8 record through 10 games, there are clearly some glaring issues that continue to persist and there are only so many roster moves a front office can make throughout the season. Aside from trading former safety Andre Cisco to the Lions ahead of the trade deadline, this is still the same roster that began the season.
With two favorable matchups against the Chargers and Dolphins coming up before the Week 13 bye, it would not be unexpected to see some shifting responsibilities on the coaching staff or even some firings. After all, head coach Aaron Glenn just gave up his play-calling duties to defensive coordinator Brian Duker, although it remains to be seen who has the role going forward.
As they prepare for a trip out west to face the 1-8 Chargers, here's a look at three Jets coaches whose jobs should be in jeopardy going into Week 11.
With a 5-22 record as the HC of the Jets and an 0-9 mark against divisional competition, Glenn is simply on borrowed time at this point and could easily be the first coach out the door if Gang Green's struggles carry over into a pair of games they should have a shot to win.
While the Jets have been competitive and should have a much better record than they currently do with some better decision-making, that is ultimately not the case due to Glenn's repeated inability to make second-half adjustments and his conservative approach in goal-to-go and short-yardage situations.
Not only did Glenn hand his defensive play-calling over to Duker in the Week 10 loss to the Bills, which was a bad look by itself considering he has referred to play-calling as his "superpower," but his decision to settle for field goals when the Bills were punching it in for touchdowns remains a concern going forward.
"It's hard to win games when you operate that way," Glenn said, per Jets on SI's Nick Faria . "I think one thing we do a good job of is actually moving the ball, but once we get there that's what we've got to get better at and those are things we've got to continue to work on."
Sure, it was another injury-riddled loss to the Bills as the depth of this Jets roster continues to get tested. That said, the results have just not been there on the field, healthy or not, during Glenn's Jets tenure so far. Unless he can make the appropriate adjustments and win the next two games like he should be expected to, it will just be a matter of whether the front office gives him the ax immediately or waits for the season to end.
While some may argue that Reich could move into the role of interim HC if the Jets elect to fire Glenn during the season, especially due to his previous coaching experience with the Panthers and Colts, he is in just as much hot water as Glenn due to his failure to consistently get the ball to his best players.
To his credit, WR1 Garrett Wilson led the team in receptions (seven), targets (14) and receiving yards (106) in the loss to the Bills, but that has not always been the case throughout the season. On top of that, Reich's play-calling in short-yardage situations, third down and in the red zone has been questionable to say the least.
Those struggles and repeated decisions to settle for field goals eventually caught up to the Jets when Bills quarterback Josh Allen found wide receiver DJ Moore for a 45-yard TD (h/t NFL) to extend Buffalo's lead to 12 and take control late in the third quarter.
ALLEN TO DJ MOORE FOR 6 BUFvsNYJ on CBS/Paramount+ Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/hfrUwKQlws
Reich has some opportunities in front of him to make his seat a little cooler, but if he cannot consistently find a way to get his best players the ball and end Gang Green's current nine-quarter drought without a TD, he could be in trouble.
Although Duker did not have any prior experience calling plays when Glenn handed the duties over to him in Week 10, he is no stranger to the Jets HC, most recently serving as defensive assistant, safeties coach and defensive backs coach while Glenn was the DC with the Lions.
Still, it was an ugly debut for Duker as the Jets were outscored, 21-6, in the second half and allowed the Bills rushing attack to combine for 201 yards. The Jets have now allowed their last three opponents to eclipse 30 points and have the third-worst rushing defense (135.3 YPG), so it is not like this was a favorable spot for Duker to be put in.
Despite that, the Jets currently have three first-round draft picks and the pressure continues to mount regarding who is going to be part of this staff for the next phase of the rebuild. It was just one game for Duker, but Glenn's hesitancy to commit to him as the defensive play-caller shows there are still some concerns there, especially if no gains are made against two of the league's three worst scoring offenses.

title: 3 Pending Jets Free Agents That Deserve New Contracts Despite Disastrous Season
full_text:
Why would a 2-8 team in the NFL be willing to retain starters on their struggling lineup?
What if I told you there were players on the New York Jets deserving of new contracts, even if they haven't fixed much of what has plagued the roster this year?
New York has several pending free agents going into the 2027 offseason. Many have performed poorly this year due to a number of different factors . However, there are those who have played well enough to get more time in Florham Park.
Today, we'll go through the three most important players New York needs to re-sign here.
If New York let all their pending defensive free agents walk, most fans would understand. The one player who deserves a new contract, though, is safety Dane Belton.
The former New York Giant has become an everydown player for New York, with the third-best run defense grade of any safety in the league and an average mark in coverage. Those numbers alone are good enough to keep him on the team over the next few years.
In-the-box safeties rarely get massive payouts, but the Jets need a starter opposite Minkah Fitzpatrick next season, and Belton is the obvious choice to fill that role.
It's become almost a foregone conclusion that the Jets will take a quarterback in the 2027 draft. How they surround that rookie quarterback will remain a big question mark, though.
The most consistent and efficient way to allow a young signal-caller to develop is by putting him behind a veteran leader and an offensive minded coaching staff that will keep one system in place. Whether the Jets draft CJ Carr, Drew Mestemaker, or Darian Mensah, the team should follow that system to build around them.
That means keeping Geno Smith at all costs.
Smith has thrown 12 touchdowns to just three interceptions this season. He hasn't been a world-beater, but he's been competent at a time when so few things are working for New York.
New York should extend Smith into 2027 on a starting salary to allow them the chance to grow an incoming rookie behind a proven veteran. The process has worked for many teams before. It's time for the Jets to join in that plan.
Depth is incredibly important in the NFL, especially on the offensive line. New York hasn't gotten the best from Jordan Meredith this season, but if the team were smart, they should sign him to a limited extension thanks to his versatility and starting experience.
New York has a lot of issues to fix this offseason. One group that doesn't need to be overhauled, though, is the offensive line. With Parham returning, the team really only needs an upgrade at center to round out the group.
And with Meredith having experience at both guard and center, the team should be in a good position to bring him back and not worry too much about the group's depth going forward.

title: 5 Biggest Mistakes Made by Aaron Glenn Since Becoming Jets Head Coach
full_text:
By the time the Aaron Glenn era ends by the end of the season (as many expect), the New York Jets will have gone through a two-year run of futility rarely seen across NFL season.
Going into Week 11, the Jets are 5-22 under Glenn as head coach and 0-9 in the AFC East . The numbers are second-worst in team history, behind only Rich Kotite in the 1990s. There are a number of reasons why the team has struggled during this stretch.
But five mistakes matter most when we look back at the Glenn era.
There will be people tired of the idea the Jets should have kept Rodgers instead of moving on as they did following a five-win season in 2024.
But it's hard to ignore what could have been had Glenn and the Jets been more willing to keep the future Hall-of-Famer around, especially in an offense like the one they currently have.
Rodgers led the Pittsburgh Steelers to the AFC North title in 2025. They are well on their way to another playoff appearance this season as well. Part of that is due to their defense and run game, but Rodgers deserves credit as well.
Had Glenn looked to establish himself more, and given more of a buffer for his coaching abilities, keeping Rodgers would have made things easier from a winning perspective. Maybe the team would have still lost a lot of games, but fans would have targeted Rodgers more than Glenn after his first season.
Instead, Glenn's decisions were put in the spotlight from the very beginning. Moving on from Rodgers made the team worse last season. And it hasn't helped their chances in 2026 either.
At some point, the Jets and their fans are going to realize: introductory press conferences are the most meaningless things for head coaches. Guys who struggle and get made fun of for poor quotes at the beginning can turn into excellent coaches. People who give stellar answers may not know what to do once the headsets come on.
From the very beginning of his hiring, Glenn has focused heavily on keeping his passion and swagger on point. That has included answers and a showmanship bravado that can endear itself to fans...when a team is winning.
The problems come becuase Glenn's passionate quotes have rarely been met with on-field success. Whether it was commenting on a player's lack of breakout status due to "coaching" or that the team wanted to build something "fans could be proud of" or any other passionate stance Glenn has held.
There are several quotes Glenn has made over the last two years that have backfired spectacularly. With each whiff, his mistakes at the podium just compound his biggest issues.
Every coach wants their teams to look and play a certain way. But there's a difference between wanting a team to be tough and physical, and forcing a roster to play a specific strategic gameplan regardless of their opponent.
New York wants their corners to be excellent in man coverage. They want their defense to play a base 3-4 scheme. Nevermind the fact they don't have the players for each scheme, they simply want to play that way regardless of outcome.
Offensively, it's even worse. New York has all the talent in the world to be a pass first unit and force defenses to react to their talent and scheme. But the Jets are more focused on reacting to what the defense is doing, instead of dictating play. They push to be a run-first team, even when the roster is best used as a spread-out run-and-gun unit.
Good coaches alter their stragetic plans for the team they have. Not the team they want.
Glenn's big mistake is his inability to adjust to anything the NFL is putting out, instead expecting his style to win football games.
This was one that many people thought wouldn't be an issue going into Glenn's second season. With his decision to call plays defensively, he needed an experienced offensive mind to run the offense without needing his help.
But was Frank Reich the right choice? Hindsight is always 20/20, but not retaining young offensive coordinator Tanner Engstrand was clearly a mistake. Reich's offense this season has been stagnant despite better quarterback play, and better weapons across the board.
Engstrand's unit, while poor at times, had a scheme that used players all over the field, attacked matchups, and ultimately, was more effective despite the clear limitations brought to him at quarterback.
A big question should be what Engstrand could have done with Geno Smith as a starter this season, and with a full collection of weapons that the Jets have.
Instead, New York is seriously devoid of creativity this season and Reich is at the forefront of that issue. Because he wanted to replace Engstrand without realizing the benefits to keeping him, this mistake makes the list.
This is easily the most egregious of Glenn's mistakes. It's one to thing to whiff on a coaching hire, or at quarterback. These things can happen to an elite coach, let alone a bad one.
But Glenn's inability to understand analytics, and the importance of being aggressive at all times is his biggest weakness. It's a big reason why the team is 2-8 this season, and well on their way to another bottom-five finish around the NFL.
Glenn doesn't understand when to be aggressive. He'll be happy kicking field goals over going for it on fourth down to score touchdowns. He'll put in short yardage situations when the offense is moving. He sees a defense in the Jets that isn't the catalyst for the team, but wants to be the reason they win games.
Glenn's selective aggressiveness holds the Jets back. Sure, the roster may not be ready to beat the likes of Buffalo or Kansas City, but it's obvious around the league that teams know the coach won't make the right calls in order to help his team win in New York.
At this rate, with two years of tape, and two years of chances to fix it, Glenn's choice to be passive at all key moments will eventually be his undoing.

title: 3 WR Targets the Jets Need to Have on Their Radar After Omar Cooper Jr.‘s Injury
full_text:
With Garrett Wilson returning from the concussion protocol, the Jets entered their Week 10 matchup against the Bills with their original offensive starters for the first time since Week 1. However, the unit lasted just one play together, as rookie receiver Omar Cooper Jr. sustained an ankle injury.
This is the third time Cooper has had his right ankle rolled up this season, as Kenyon Sadiq was tackled into the back of his leg. The first incident happened in Week 1, which resulted in him landing on the injured reserve list, and the second occurred in Week 9.
Cooper underwent imaging on his ankle, and although the injury’s severity remains unclear, head coach Aaron Glenn told reporters Wednesday that he wouldn’t practice, per ESPN's Rich Cimini . While it’s still too early to rule him out for Sunday’s matchup against the Chargers, New York must have a backup plan ready in case he’s a no-go, especially with Isaiah Williams sidelined for Wednesday’s practice with a rib injury.
Other Jets injuries: Omar Cooper Jr (ankle) and Isaiah Williams (ribs) won't practice today. Joseph Ossai, Dylan Parham and Trevin Wallace will be limited. #Jets are opening the practice window for DT David Onyemata, who has been on IR for eight weeks.
With Glenn needing wins to have any chance of saving his job , the Jets must target veteran receivers in free agency or from other teams’ practice squads who can help contribute right away. With that in mind, here are three receivers New York must have on its radar.
Of the three receivers, Tyler Johnson is the only one who has ties to the Jets. He spent last season on New York’s practice squad, finishing the year with 12 receptions for 197 yards and a touchdown across 11 games.
Johnson briefly returned to the practice squad this fall after Cooper was placed on injured reserve, but he was released without appearing in a game. Given his experience and familiarity with the offense, the Jets could bring Johnson back and have him suit up for the team’s game against the Chargers.
While he isn’t as impactful as Cooper, Johnson is someone New York can trust immediately. He knows the system and has experience playing in the slot, lining up there for 41.4% of his career snaps, per Pro Football Focus.
Although he’s not an explosive downfield receiver, the Jets could use him in the short-to-intermediate areas on slants and crossers to pick up some yards.
K.J. Osborn doesn’t have the experience or familiarity with the Jets like Johnson; however, he’s arguably the better choice. The former 2020 fifth-round selection was a solid complementary option during his three years with the Vikings, registering 160 receptions for 1,865 yards and three touchdowns.
Regarded for his versatility, Osborn was effective both inside in the slot and on the outside. Although he doesn’t have elite top-end speed, he excelled as a vertical threat in Minnesota. The Vikings prioritized pushing the ball downfield.
In a limited role, Osborn can provide a similar spark. Despite not being as aggressive this season, Geno Smith likes to take shots downfield, and the Jets already have several vertical weapons.
Osborn's downside, however, is that he hasn’t had success outside Minnesota. He’s spent the past three seasons with four different teams and hasn’t appeared in a single offensive snap since the 2024 season.
But if Cooper is sidelined, Osborn should be on New York’s radar.
Samuel is the most productive player of the three and, at his peak, is the best. The former Ohio State Buckeye is a complete offensive weapon and has been used as such over his nine-year career, lining up in the slot and at running back.
While the Jets don’t need him in the backfield, they could use his explosiveness on the inside if Cooper misses time. Samuel has proven to be a quality playmaker in his career, with 1,509 of his 3,799 receiving yards coming after the catch.
Even though injuries and regression have slowed him down, he’s still a reliable pass-catcher who can gain extra yardage with his speed. New York can rely on him in a limited role and use him as a gadget player to ease pressure on Wilson and Adonai Mitchell to consistently create separation.

title: Latest Jets Tryouts Could Spell Bad News for Malachi Moore’s Future in Gotham
full_text:
The New York Jets may be looking for new blood at safety. Gang Green worked out safeties Sanoussi Kane and Mark Perry, as well as corner Reddy Steward, on Tuesday of Week 11, per ESPN's Richi Cimini. If New York signs one of the DBs they looked at, Malachi Moore may be on the way out.
The 25-year-old has underperformed this season. After the Jets traded Andre Cisco, Moore was thrust into a bigger role and hasn't settled in. He looks like the odd one out among the Jets' contracted players if they were to sign another DB. Either way, the safety needs to step up his performance if he wants to remain in his role with the team.
Moore didn't see much of the field before the Jets traded Cisco , and his Week 10 performance shows why. The safety played 28 snaps in the 31-12 loss against the Buffalo Bills. In those 28 snaps, Moore posted a 28.6 PFF grade . He also allowed a 45-yard touchdown reception late in the third quarter that put Buffalo up by 12.
Moore was a liability for New York, grading last on the defense in the loss . He had a chance to prove himself when New York moved on from Cisco, but it hasn't gone well. With the Jets working out two safeties on Tuesday, the writing may be on the wall if Moore doesn't start to show he can play. As it stands, his performance hasn't been one New York can put on the field if they want to improve a 2-8 record.
If New York signs a new safety, Moore is the easiest to let go. The Jets have Minkah Fitzpatrick and Dane Belton playing ahead of him. Those two guys are not going anywhere this season. The only other safety on the roster is rookie VJ Payne , whom the team patiently waited to activate after a bone bruise landed him on the IR. It seems the team believes in Payne enough to wait for him, leaving Moore on the outs.
Moore has experience in front of him and youth behind him; a bad combo if the team is looking to bring in safety help. The safety is also on a fourth-round rookie contract, which makes him easy to move on from. The dead cap hit would be less than $1 million over two seasons if the Jets were to release Moore. New blood on a short, cheap contract may be enticing over two more years of Malachi.
The Jets need more safety help, and it is clear it hasn't been coming from inside the building. With New York working out players at the position, it may spell the end of Malachi Moore's time with the team. Unless he turns it around soon, his performance combined with his contract could leave him searching for a new team.

title: It's Time for the Jets to Make a Demario Davis Decision They Can't Put Off Any Longer
full_text:
The New York Jets franchise did not learn from their prior CJ Mosley mistake.
After three dominant seasons with the franchise, Mosley's age began to creep up on him. New York, loyal to its veterans and locker room leaders, tried to find ways to get him on the field until he couldn't play anymore.
By the time Mosley played his last game with the franchise, the linebacker was 31 years old.
That makes it even more surprising that the Jets seemingly made the same mistake again - this time with veteran linebacker Demario Davis. The veteran linebacker signed a two-year deal with New York at 38 years old in the offseason. New York wasn't worried at all that his advanced age far exceeded Mosley, or that Father Time could hit him harder than they thought. They just needed quality leadership at the position.
But now, New York is suffering, and Davis is a key reason why . It leaves open further questions about what the team should do at linebacker beyond 2027 and for the rest of the season.
New York is running out of options for Davis. In last Sunday's 31-12 loss to the Buffalo Bills, the aging linebacker was one of the worst players on the field, recording a 34.6 grade from Pro Football Focus. It was the lowest grade of any Jets full-time starter in the Week 10 defeat.
"We didn’t do a good enough job; that’s the area we certainly got to be better," Davis said. "Too many explosive plays got in the red zone and didn't get off the field."
It's not like last Sunday's performance can be chalked up to one bad game, either. Davis has been one of the worst linebackers this year in the NFL. PFF has graded his 2026 season at a 40.5 grade - 82nd out of 82 linebackers.
As a leader, Davis remains an important part of New York's defense. He is in charge of getting everyone set and communicating as long as possible. But actually executing plays on defense matters more than leadership - especially for a 2-8 team.
And the tape shows Davis is a step slower than he once was.
It's only going to get worse as well, moving forward. Players don't suddenly get better when they lose a step.
It's why New York must find a way to start thinking about replacing Davis on the field in some way. They may not have answers in their backup linebacker room, but for a team needing wins to save their coach's job, Davis might have to be the first player moved.

title: Regrading Jets’ Free-Agent Signings 10 Games Into the 2026 Season
full_text:
The Jets were active in the 2026 offseason, making 17 free-agent signings, 10 of which came from other teams. These signings were meant to bolster the roster, but the Jets are 2-8 after 10 weeks in 2026, leaving more questions than answers for general manager Darren Mougey.
It is clear what type of team the Jets are 10 weeks into the season. The question is, how did they get there?
With the season more than halfway over, it is a good time to look back at some of the Jets' offseason signings and give them a new grade now that we have a sample size.
Dane Belton was signed to a one-year, $4 million contract and has been worth the money. The safety hasn't been perfect, but has performed well. Belton has struggled at times in coverage, but he leads his position with a 91.0 Pro Football Focus run-defense grade . He also ranks first at the position for solo tackles, amassing 60 so far in 2026.
The 25-year-old has been one of New York's most consistent players on the field. The defense has struggled overall, but Belton has been a bright spot on that side of the ball. He's been a stalwart in the box, even if his coverage skills could use some work.
That said, Belton has been one of the best 2026 signings for New York.
Dylan Parham has been one of the best guards in the league after signing a two-year, $16 million contract with New York. The guard has put up an 82.3 overall grade according to PFF , sixth at the position. So, why is this signing only a B? He has not been able to stay on the field.
Parham missed four weeks after a knee injury knocked him out against Detroit. He injured that same knee in Week 10 against Buffalo and now looks like he'll miss more time. The former Raider has been great when he's on the field, but staying healthy has proven an issue for Parham this season. While he has easily been the best free-agent performer on the field, he just hasn't been on the field enough.
The Jets brought Demario Davis home for the twilight of his career to the tune of two years and $22 million on his contract. The issue is that Davis clearly looks to be nearing the end of his career in the league. The 37-year-old looks his age, ranking dead last at the linebacker position with a 40.0 PFF grade.
One of the main reasons Davis was brought back was to provide veteran leadership on defense. The issue is that he has been a liability on the field . He's clearly lost a step in coverage, and his 14 missed tackles this season aren't doing New York any favors. Davis will always be a fan favorite in New York, but it is evident his time in the league is coming to an end.
If an F- grade existed, that is what this free-agent signing would get.
The Jets signed corner Nahshon Wright to a one-year, $3.5 million contract in the offseason. Wright led his position in interceptions in 2025; in 2026, he has played two snaps. The Jets basically threw money away with this deal, as Wright hasn't played.
The corner was supposed to be a ball hawk who brought an interception threat to a team that has only amassed two in the past two seasons. Instead, he is a $3.5 million check sitting on the bench. New York didn't get value for Wright at the deadline , and it would take a miracle for him to re-sign come this offseason.
Whether he is just not good enough to get on the field or not, wasting money on Wright was the wrong move by the Jets.
The Jets' largest investment in free agency was Joseph Ossai. The edge rusher was signed to a three-year, $36 million contract in the offseason and has not lived up to those expectations. Ossai has played only four games this season and has yet to record a QB pressure, much less a sack.
The defensive end has 11 total tackles in 123 snaps, so there is some promise there. Ossai's biggest issue is that he hasn't been able to stay on the field, and when he does play, he is still lacking. New York will hope Ossai improves, as he is on the books for two more years after 2026.
The Jets didn't swing big in the 2026 offseason, but they did swing a lot. New York made plenty of signings, but few have panned out. It's clear to see the Jets missed on quite a few signings as the team looks to be headed toward another season at the bottom of the NFL.
There are some bright spots, but the overall group of free agents has been a disappointment for New York this year.

title: Frank Reich Is Officially on the Clock to Save His Jets Job With Bye Week Looming
full_text:
Stop me if you've heard this before: it was another humiliating loss for the Jets on Sunday, a 31-12 defeat to the Bills that dropped Gang Green's record to 2-8 on the season.
It was not as if they completely laid an egg in the game, either, after heading into the break down four and cutting the deficit to one on their opening drive of the second half. However, the lack of adjustments and conservative approach caught up with them and led to a much too familiar outcome for Jets fans.
To be fair, injuries have taken a toll on this team all season, and that continued in the injury-riddled loss to the Bills as quarterback Geno Smith (concussion, ankle), wide receiver Omar Cooper Jr. (right ankle) and guard Dylan Parham (knee) dealt with setbacks of their own.
That said, it still does not account for the poor job this coaching staff has done all season in terms of failing to consistently get their best players involved on a weekly basis. Sure, head coach Aaron Glenn will continue to face a lot of the blame, but offensive coordinator Frank Reich is just as guilty and at fault amid the five-game losing streak.
Yes, he deserves credit for getting WR1 Garrett Wilson more involved with team highs in receptions (seven), targets (14) and receiving yards (106) on Sunday, but there is still no denying that he is on the clock to save his job with two favorable matchups against the Chargers (1-8) and Dolphins (1-8) coming up before a Week 13 bye.
Although seven of New York's 10 games have been decided by one score, the inability to keep pace for the duration of a game has proved costly for multiple reasons. That was no different on Sunday, when the Jets were 3-of-13 on third down, 0-of-2 in the red zone and settled for field goals in goal-to-go territory instead of getting aggressive and going for six.
The Jets were at the nine-yard line facing a fourth-and-4 with 12 seconds remaining in the first half, but rather than taking a shot in a seven-point game against a team they were not expected to beat anyway, they took the easy route on the 27-yarder. Sure, Smith was hurt on the third-down play and that may have played a factor in the decision-making, but that was still a missed opportunity.
Then, after a 10-play, 61-yard drive that took almost five minutes off the clock to begin the second half, Gang Green kicked the 22-yard field goal on a 4th-and-goal at the four-yard line.
Although another field goal on the next drive answered a Bills touchdown and kept it a one-score game, Buffalo responded two plays later with another TD— a 45-yard pass from QB Josh Allen to WR DJ Moore (h/t NFL)—to make it a 24-12 game and take control.
ALLEN TO DJ MOORE FOR 6 BUFvsNYJ on CBS/Paramount+ Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/hfrUwKQlws
From there, the Jets threw an interception, punted twice, fumbled and turned it over on downs in what turned out to be a blowout loss to the Bills . That lack of aggressiveness and failure to adapt to what is happening on the field is as much on Glenn as it is on the HC, but that still does not make up for the fact that Reich's offense has struggled to execute (particularly in the red zone) and get its best players involved .
While it is not always as common for teams to fire their HC during a bye week, coordinators tend to be dismissed when the product on the field is less than ideal. After all, the extra week off gives the front office additional time to look at some film and dive into the glaring issues without the immediate turnaround of another game the next week.
That is the position the Jets could find themselves in after a two-game road trip that begins with the Chargers on Sunday. Considering the Chargers (16 ppg) and Dolphins (16.4 ppg) are two of the three worst-scoring offenses in the league and have a combined 2-16 record, the next two weeks will be crucial for Reich to at least show that he is deserving of staying around through the end of the season.
The problems run just as deep for Glenn , but Reich should be feeling just as much urgency. You could argue that making a change midseason would not entirely fix the execution flaws that have plagued this roster through the first 10 weeks, but it would also minimize disruptions and give the new coordinator an extra week to get acclimated to a different responsibility.
There is also the Cade Klubnik conundrum as Smith faces some injury concerns , especially considering the former was late on some throws in his NFL debut and seemed hesitant with some of his decision-making in his first regular-season game.
At the same time, it is Reich's job to get this offense ready to play and to feed his best players the ball for the Jets to have any chance of getting back in the win column. With two winnable games before the Week 13 bye, Reich has two more opportunities to prove himself and keep his job in Gotham before some doubts about his future reach a boiling point.

title: Firing Aaron Glenn Should Happen ASAP as Jets’ Reasons for Change Keep Piling Up
full_text:
The Jets are heading down the barrow of another loss season .
At 2-8 with seven games remaining, the  Jets face the possibility of another losing season. More importantly, the organization must confront the possibility of making another head coaching change , as its current coaching regime isn't a long-term answer.
Jets head coach Aaron Glenn's seat is beginning to heat up as the team continues to struggle during his tenure. Despite arriving with expectations of turning the franchise around, Glenn has struggled to establish a winning culture in New York.
The Jets, who are fresh off a loss to the rival Bills, have struggled on both sides of the ball this season. The defense, which Glenn has identified as his superpower, has often failed to deliver. Meanwhile, the offense has continued to search for consistency.
To make matters worse, the team may be without Geno Smith , who is currently sidelined with an ankle injury. Smith has put together one of his better seasons so far through 10 games; he's thrown for 2,226 passing yards, 12 touchdowns, and three interceptions on a 67.1% completion rate.
Jets QB Geno Smith (ankle) hopes to play Sunday vs. Chargers, per sources. This week’s progress will determine his status but he was ‘doing good’ as of Monday and will try to push through it. pic.twitter.com/R4aN79uyOA
Based on the Jets' performance this season, Glenn is on borrowed time. Rather than waiting until the offseason, the Jets should cut bait with Glenn before the season concludes.
New York isn't officially eliminated from postseason contention, but at this point, it would take a miracle for the Jets to have a chance to represent the AFC in the 2026 NFL playoffs.
Cutting ties with Glenn would give the Jets a new voice in the locker room through the end of the season and an opportunity to salvage what has been another disappointing campaign.
The Jets' current coaching staff has several potential candidates who could take over, and the organization may already have an interim option on its roster.
Jets offensive coordinator Frank Reich has extensive head coaching experience, including stops with the Panthers and Colts. Elsewhere on offense, current quarterbacks coach Bill Musgrave gives the Jets another experienced offensive mind who could be considered for the interim position.
The Jets' defensive coordinator, Brian Duker, spent time with the Lions alongside Glenn during his tenure as their defensive coordinator from 2021-24. His familiarity with Glenn's defensive philosophy could make him another potential candidate to take over the team—especially now that Duker is calling Gang Green's defensive plays.
Aaron Glenn’s “superpower” for the #Jets lasted 10 weeks. Brian Duker calling plays for the team on Sunday is further a bad look for this current defensive staff.
At times this season, the Jets have looked like a team that has given up. Bringing in a new voice could help reinvigorate the locker room and give the team an opportunity to close out the 2026 NFL season on a stronger note.

title: Jets Face a Cade Klubnik Conundrum as Geno Smith Injury Creates QB Uncertainty
full_text:
From the moment the Jets completed the trade in March, they have stood by starting quarterback Geno Smith. The veteran signal-caller struggled in Las Vegas, but was seen as a perfect bridge quarterback for the 2026 team.
In many ways, he has been. Smith has completed 67% of his passes for 2,226 yards, along with 12 touchdowns and just three interceptions. He has not been New York's biggest problem throughout their 2-8 start.
For most of the year, Smith was on a trajectory to have one of the five greatest passing seasons by a Jets quarterback. That could be in jeopardy with his new injury.
And it opens up more questions about the team's quarterback room moving forward, especially when it comes to rookie QB Cade Klubnik.
Late in the second quarter of New York's 31-12 loss to the Bills , Smith received a big hit at the goal line and was quickly shuffled into concussion protocol. Later in the third quarter, the signal-caller suffered an ankle injury and did not return.
On Monday morning, Jets head coach Aaron Glenn provided a baseline answer for where they were in understanding his injury.
"(Geno) will get imaging today just to see exactly where we're at. So again, I will have more information on that later in the week," Glenn said. Less than 24 hours later, ESPN's Jeremy Fowler reported that the veteran QB "hopes to play" and will attempt "to push through it" in Week 11.
New York is usually quiet when it comes to injuries and the availability of players, which creates a competitive advantage over its opponents. But the team is also worse without Smith on the field. In his place, the Jets could turn to Klubnik, as they did on Sunday.
Cade Klubnik's first NFL pass is a completion to Garrett Wilson! BUFvsNYJ on CBS/Paramount+ Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/Cyxg8tuqzq
In relief, Klubnik completed 11-of-20 passes for 137 yards on Sunday while also throwing an interception. He added 26 rushing yards on scrambles, but was clearly late on throws and seemed too timid at times to pull the trigger.
In short, he looked like mid-round rookie quarterback who was getting on an NFL field for the first time in his career.
As the Jets move forward, though, their current standing opens the door for more of Klubnik beyond just being a backup. Even if the team doesn't want to think that way.
Speaking to reporters on Monday, Glenn made it clear: so long as Smith is healthy, he will be the quarterback for the team.
"Geno's our starter. That hasn't changed."
But the outlook of the organization clearly is better off having Klubnik play. New York isn't going anywhere this year. The Jets' record and draft standing have them on the outside looking in for a potential top pick in the 2027 draft and a chance at a top quarterback prospect.
The Jets even admitted that if Smith wasn't healthy enough, then they would be confident in their chances to win with Klubnik starting games.
"Very confident," Glenn said. "That's why he is on the team. If Geno can't go this week, Cade will be our starter, and we'll go from there."
But there are two reasons the team will continue to start Smith.
First, they are trying to give Glenn as much benefit of the doubt as they can. Any win that can prove he was the right head coaching hire is one they will gladly take. Smith gives the team the best chance to win.
Second, with a young group of players, New York needs a quarterback who can confidently move the ball downfield through the air. Klubnik's timing and anticipation are off as a rookie (which is still natural for a player of his standing) and will need time.
Jets throw an INT but get it back on a fumble on the return BUFvsNYJ on CBS/Paramount+ Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/f5vRx8b3m1
If the Jets were to start Klubnik, that would affect the development and film study of many of their young receivers .
So while it is best for the Jets to lose the remainder of their games for a top overall pick, the team's current standing and their belief in Glenn are why the team won't turn to Klubnik full time unless they have to.
New York still has plenty of decisions to make moving forward. As the team waits to see whether they can play Smith going into their road contest against the Chargers on Sunday, the Jets must soon decide on practice squad quarterback Will Levis.
The rival Patriots just lost Drake Maye to a reported broken ankle . Other teams around the league are also in need of quality quarterbacks moving forward.
If the Jets don't promote Levis to the active roster, another team like the Patriots may poach him away. That means they would lose out on a quality backup option should Klubnik get hurt at any point.
The Jets need to be proactive as a front office regarding their quarterback room, or else their outlook might get even worse.

title: Eagles Sticking With Sean Mannion Looks Even Bolder After Cowboys' Christian Parker Decision
full_text:
PHILADELPHIA—The struggling Dallas Cowboys stripped Christian Parker of defensive play-calling duties after 10 games. The Eagles, staring at arguably an even worse offensive situation, are sticking with Sean Mannion despite a 2-7 start and seven consecutive losses.
Both are first-time coordinators and play-callers. Dallas’s defense is last in the NFL in yards allowed (393.8 per game) and rushing yards allowed (154.1), and 30th in points allowed (28.2).
After surrendering a franchise home-record 584 yards and three long touchdowns in a 46-40 loss to the San Francisco 49ers, Cowboys head coach Brian Schottenheimer handed the headset to senior defensive assistant Mike Pettine while keeping the 34-year-old Parker, the former Eagles secondary coach and defensive pass game coordinator, as the DC.
Parker will still run meetings and lead walkthroughs. He just no longer will call the games. Schottenheimer framed it as a win-now decision with Pettine’s experience, not a full demotion, and reiterated that Parker has a bright future.
Parker's former boss in Philadelphia, Vic Fangio, agreed with that sentiment after watching the young coach aid in the development of Quinyon Mitchell and Cooper DeJean en route to a Super Bowl LIX championship with the Eagles.
“Patience is not in overabundance in today’s society, especially in the sports world, but Christian will recover from that,” Fangio insisted. “It happened to [Broncos Head Coach] Sean Payton many years ago in New York and I think he’s recovered nicely. Joe Brady, who’s the head coach at Buffalo, he got fired during the season, didn’t even get kept on. I think he’s recovered nicely, as has [Cardinals Head Coach] Mike LaFleur in Arizona. The Jets fired him during the season a couple years ago. He’s recovered nicely. Christian will do the same thing. He’ll be fine.”
The Eagles are in their own mess on the offensive side of the ball, of course. They are  last in total yards and near the bottom in scoring under Mannion .
Jalen Hurts is out for the season with blood clots, the offensive line and skill-position groups have been thinned by attrition, and the offense has struggled to generate consistent drives or an identity.
After a bye-week evaluation, however, Nick Sirianni confirmed Mannion remains the play-caller.
“Yeah,” Sirianni said when asked if Mannion is still calling the plays. “I think we had a really good bye-week process, got to evaluate a lot of things within that. You go through that — I think I put into pretty good detail how we go through things and the things that present themselves as you go through it.
“I think we have a good plan of action moving forward of the things that we want to do to move forward and to get better. Obviously, we haven’t been good enough on offense, but I like our plan of attack and our process that we went through last week.”
Pressed on what he sees beyond work ethic, Sirianni pointed to Mannion’s process: “I think he’s really smart. I think he has a great football mind. He thinks through everything. I think one thing I always value about him is [that] anybody can come and give a play and say, ‘Hey, I want to do this, or I want to do that.’ I think he just has a really good monotonous approach to figuring out everything that could potentially happen in that situation, what the downfalls are, what the upside is and whether we move forward with some of those things. I think that just speaks to the detail that he has.”
Sirianni admitted “it hasn’t gone well enough for any of us this year offensively.”
“That’s coaches, that’s players,” the Eagles coach said. “We all have things that we need to do better, but I do love that approach that he has with that. As we looked at some of our schemes that he’s brought in, some of those have been really, really good. It has to be better as a whole without getting too much into the specifics of what those are. We just need to build on that.”
The contrast here is stark.
Dallas treated 10 games of historically poor defensive performance as enough to strip a first-time play-caller of the job’s most visible duty. The Eagles are showing that patience Fangio noted is in short supply and giving Mannion more runway after an even longer stretch of bottom-of-the-league offensive production.
The dichotomy between two organizations reveals different risk tolerances – patience vs. pragmatism.
The Cowboys are prioritizing experienced in-game management while the division race still theoretically exists. Philadelphia is betting on the process, the detail, and the schemes, even as the demonstrated performance to date remains among the worst in the league.

title: Joe Milton’s New Nickname Comes With the Same Eagles Challenge
full_text:
PHILADELPHIA – "Bazooka Joe" might be a good name for bubble gum, but not for Eagles quarterback Joe Milton. Some might be trying to force that nickname on him, given an arm that can throw the ball out of a stadium. Don’t bother, though. He doesn’t like it.
“Bazookas only travel so far,” he said as to why he doesn't like it.
He prefers another nickname–"Mr. Rocket".
Whatever nickname he goes by won’t get him very far in his quest to finish the job as the Eagles’ starting quarterback. What matters is finding a way to win a game and snap a losing streak that has reached seven games. To break it, Milton will have to deal with a Dr. Jekyll and Mr. Hyde defense that is third against the run but 30th against the pass. Pittsburgh is a dangerous pass-rush team with J.J. Watt and has 27 sacks, which is tied for the fifth-most in the league.
Milton had an extra week to prepare and iron out the verbiage and pass protection calls. Perhaps that will help him get sacked fewer than the seven times he was sacked by the New York Giants in his first career start two weeks ago.
He said he returned from the bye week with more confidence, thanks to some help from his teammates, passing game coordinator Parks Frazier and offensive coordinator Sean Mannion.
“I'm great at asking questions, and I ask Parks [Frazier] and Sean a lot of questions,” he said. “I don't think I can ask no lesser questions than I already do. I think I do a great job at that, so yeah, just my confidence for sure.
“Just what do I need to do on this play? What is the quarterback's job specifically on this play? That goes for every play. Like, what do you exactly want me to do on this play? And if there's anything different, just tell me now. I ask questions every day. It can be the same question. I just wanna make sure I heard correctly and I took down the right note.”
On the other side of the ball will be his quarterback counterpart, Steelers veteran Aaron Rodgers. It’s a matchup that has Milton excited, even though they won’t be going head-to-head.
“To be honest with you, to be real honest with you, I [thought about it] last night,” he said. “I was watching film last night in my living room, and I was like, ‘Damn, I'm 26 going against A-Rod.’
“Like, that's A-Rod we're talking about. It feels different. It's also a blessing just because, I mean, he’s been in the league for however long he’s been in the league. And obviously this is, what, year three for me, and being able to play against him and starting against him is re- It's a blessing for sure.”
Milton should be helped by the likely return of DeVonta Smith and Tay Wicks. Smith and Wicks have each missed the previous three games due to injury. Both were listed as limited practice participants on Wednesday, which is a step in the right direction after being listed as ‘did not practice’ for the last three weeks.
Running back Saquon Barkley, who has dealt with several injuries so far this season, was a full participant.

title: 3 First-Round EDGE Prospects Eagles Must Already Have on Their 2027 NFL Draft Board
full_text:
It's never too early to start looking ahead. The Eagles sport a disappointing 2-7 record entering Week 11, making their playoff chances incredibly slim. General manager Howie Roseman's greatest opportunity to retool the roster in hopes of competing next year comes through the 2027 NFL Draft .
Nailing a first-round pick can do wonders for an organization. In Philly's case, building in the trenches is a top priority. The Eagles have averaged the fifth-fewest rushing yards per game (88.6) and logged the fourth-fewest sacks (16) in the NFL this season. What used to be a strength is now a weakness.
Let's stick to defense. Here are three first-round EDGE prospects that the Eagles must already have on their 2027 NFL Draft board.
Texas' Colin Simmons has been a game-wrecker ever since arriving as a top-25 recruit in the 2024 high school class. He won the Shaun Alexander Award as the National Freshman of the Year (48 tackles and nine sacks) before earning first-team All-SEC honors in 2025 (43 tackles and 12 sacks).
Simmons' performance this season has been even more impressive. The Texas native leads the SEC with 16 tackles for loss and 10.5 sacks across eight games. He has lived in the backfield by utilizing his sensational burst to get around the edge and quick twists to discombobulate offensive linemen.
Colin. Simmons.🔥 pic.twitter.com/CmlI0RndCH
Frustrating quarterbacks isn't Simmon's only strength. He's forced eight fumbles in college and shown the speed needed to reliably drop into coverage. Snagging Simmons with a top-five pick would create a nasty foursome alongside Jonathan Greenard, Nolan Smith, and Jalyx Hunt in Philly.
Dylan Stewart is Simmons' main competition to be the first edge rusher off the board. The South Carolina standout's traits are undeniable. Stewart uses an explosive first step to get past offensive linemen on pass-rush snaps and maintains a steady frame (6'5", 250 lbs) to close lanes in run defense.
Stewart has tallied 73 tackles, 27.5 tackles for loss, and 13.0 sacks in 31 college contests. The 21-year-old attacks quarterbacks with ferocity, ranking 18th among 869 qualified edge defenders in PFF 's pass-rush grade (90.4) this season. Stewart has also posted nine forced fumbles in his career.
Welcome back, Dylan Stewart😤 (Via: SEC Network) pic.twitter.com/U5z2P2nXql
Character concerns are holding Stewart back from being a no-doubt top-five selection. Multiple on-field infractions, ejections, and suspensions have put him in the headlines for the wrong reasons. The Eagles have made it work with challenging prospects before, though, with the most recent being Jalen Carter.
Notre Dame's Boubacar Traore is a name to keep an eye on if the Eagles grab an edge rusher with the first-round pick they acquired from the Jaguars. Traore's ceiling was considered a quality rotational pass-rusher in the NFL entering the 2026 campaign. That has since risen to an every-down disruptor .
Traore's versatility sticks out. He's recorded 33 tackles, eight tackles for loss, five sacks, three forced fumbles, and an interception in 10 games. Traore possesses the skills of an elite pass rusher and the athleticism to slide over to defensive tackle or read a quarterback's eyes in coverage.
Watch these guys work 🔥 #GoIrish ☘️ | @24era24 | @sneed_jaylen 📺: NBC pic.twitter.com/6CXVg5YGTW
Traore's non-stop motor and drive to win would fit in well along a Philly defensive line hungry to return to its former dominance. He's never shy to jump on a loose ball or track down a ball-carrier at the second level. Roseman has yet to draft a player from Notre Dame since taking over as GM in 2010.

title: Joe Milton Headlines Eagles Takeaways From Sirianni's Post-Bye Presser
full_text:
PHILADELPHIA – Joe Milton will get another start as the Eagles’ quarterback when the Pittsburgh Steelers visit Lincoln Financial Field in a Week 11 matchup in a battle of two Pennsylvania teams .
The Eagles returned from their bye week on Wednesday, and Nick Sirianni kicked things off with his first press conference since a Zoom call on Nov. 9, a day after losing 19-11 to the New York Giants. It was their seventh straight defeat and is now the longest losing streak in the NFL after the Los Angeles ended its 11-game slide with a win on Monday night.
Asked if he will start, Sirianni said that Milton will make his second straight start.
“Yeah, he'll be in there,” said the coach. “He works extremely hard with everything; I really love his approach, like his personality.”
Milton completed 53 percent of his passes and didn’t commit a turnover or throw a touchdown, and he was sacked seven times against New York.
Sirianni said that all his coaches are returning after the bye week, including embattled offensive coordinator Sean Mannion .
“I think he's really smart,” the coach said about his OC. “I think he has a great football mind. He thinks through everything. He, you know, I think one thing I always value about him is that he thinks through things.
"Anybody can come and give a play and say, ‘Hey, I want to do this,’ or, ‘I want to do that.’ But I think he just has a really good, monotonous approach to figuring out everything that could potentially happen in that situation, and what the downfalls are and what is the upside I think that just speaks to the detail of what he has.”
While there were no subtractions from the coaching staff, the Eagles added T.J. Paganetti as a consultant. Paganetti is on his third stint with the team. His first game was as an analyst for Chip Kelly in 2013. Later, he was Jeff Stoutland’s assistant on the offensive line in 2024 and a run-game specialist.
He left when Kellen Moore became the Saints’ head coach, but Moore fired him after a year-and-half as his run-game coordinator.
“He has been huge to the success of our football team in the past,” said Sirianni. “Really bright coach.”
The coach said he has done things like this in the past and reference Marcus Brady in 2022 and Jim Bob Cooter in 2021.
“It's just another pair of eyes that can look at it from a different lens,” he said.
Asked about defending Aaron Rodgers, Sirianni said that people have come up to him thinking he is the Steelers’ quarterback. There is a three-year age difference between the two (Sirianni is 45, and Rodgers is 42).
“People tell me I look like him and we look alike,” he said. “Someone asked me at a restaurant one time and said, ‘That, man, that's Aaron Rogers.’ But I got a lot of respect for him. He's so fun to watch throw the football, and how it comes off his hands and how he is able to get himself outta trouble, how he's able to direct the offense up there.”

title: 3 Reasons Why Eagles Have a Realistic Shot at Upsetting the Steelers in Week 11
full_text:
The Eagles will attempt to snap a seven-game losing streak when they host the Steelers at Lincoln Financial Field in Week 11. The two Pennsylvania squads haven't met head-to-head in the regular season since 2024, when Philadelphia triumphed 27-13 en route to winning Super Bowl LIX.
Pittsburgh boasts a 6-3 record and enters as a 4.5-point road favorite on FanDuel Sportsbook . Of course, that projection matters little once the players step on the field on Sunday afternoon .
Here are three reasons why the Eagles have a realistic shot at upsetting the visiting Steelers.
Running the football and protecting quarterback Aaron Rodgers has been the foundation of the Steelers' success this year. It's how they control the clock and avoid turnovers. Pittsburgh's offensive line has successfully carried out that strategy at home, but has faltered away from Acrisure Stadium.
Rodgers has been sacked just six times across four home victories. The veteran gunslinger has been sacked 20 times across five away games (2-3 record). Pittsburgh is also the only team in the NFL that has yet to score a rushing touchdown on the road. That's a big enough sample size to cause concern.
Boye Mafe gets the third sack of the game for the Bengals 🗣️ PITvsCIN on NBC/Peacock Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/pHk4cKIkEs
It's worth noting that Pittsburgh left guard Mason McCormick suffered an ankle injury in Week 10 that is expected to sideline him beyond Week 11. This is a matchup that Philly's Moro Ojomo, Nolan Smith and Jonathan Greenard can exploit. A few timely sacks could be the difference in a low-scoring duel.
Injuries have played a crucial role in Philadelphia's struggles in the passing game this season. Pro Bowl wide receiver DeVonta Smith has only appeared in four of the Eagles' nine games as he deals with a hamstring injury. Dontayvion Wicks has missed the last three weeks with an ankle injury.
Both players are trending in the right direction ahead of Week 11, though. Their returns would provide a huge boost for quarterback Joe Milton. Smith is a crisp route-runner and has the body control to haul in contested catches. Wicks provides versatility and excels at tracking deep balls through the air.
My understanding is that the #Eagles expect DeVonta Smith and Tay Wicks to return after the bye or shortly thereafter and are now in a position where they want to provide younger players more opportunities… https://t.co/epaEgIwSbj
The Steelers have surrendered at least 89 yards to an opposing receiver in each of their three losses. That includes when Cincinnati's Ja'Marr Chase tallied 231 yards on 11 receptions in Week 10. Relying on Milton's rocket of an arm to feed Smith and Wicks the ball could be the recipe for an upset victory.
The Steelers have lost 11 straight games in Philadelphia. It's a streak that dates all the way back to 1965. The past three clashes at Lincoln Financial Field haven't been close, either. The Eagles smoked the Steelers 27-13 in 2024, crushed them 35-13 in 2022, and destroyed them 34-6 in 2016.
It's clear that Philly's passionate fan base makes its presence felt whenever the Steelers come to town. Don't expect that to change on Sunday, despite the team's losing record. The Eagles have drawn in 349,395 fans through five home games (per ESPN ). That's the 10th-highest total in the NFL.
There's one more trend to point out. Pittsburgh head coach Mike McCarthy is well known in Philly from his time leading the Packers and Cowboys. He sports a lackluster 4-5 head-coaching record at Lincoln Financial Field. The Eagles will take any edge they can get in hopes of ending their skid.

title: Sean Mannion Is Officially in the Hot Seat as Eagles Return to Action in Week 11
full_text:
PHILADELPHIA, P.A. — The Eagles’ bye week is over. The self-scout is done. The excuses have a shelf life, and that shelf life expires for Sean Mannion on Sunday against the Pittsburgh Steelers.
Mannion’s first season as Eagles offensive coordinator has been a disaster. The numbers are ugly. The process has looked messy. The results have been even worse.
Head coach Nick Sirianni—and by extension, GM Howie Roseman and owner Jeffrey Lurie—has stuck by the unconventional hire through a seven-game losing streak and a 2-7 record overall. That said, any patience that was granted in September and October due to the attrition now has to be earned in the final eight games if Mannion wants any hope of a sequel.
Getting back starting receivers DeVonta Smith and Dontayvion Wicks , and potentially running back Will Shipley, does not require a 180-degree transformation. It does require proof that Mannion can elevate players through adversity instead of simply managing their absences.
Smith and Wicks have been the clearest examples of Mannion's rocky start. When both receivers have been healthy, the offense has at least looked like it has a pulse. When they have not, the drop-off has been steep, and the supporting cast has not been maximized.
That is the difference between a coordinator who is scheme-centric and one who gets the most out of what is available on a given Sunday.
Smith remains elite when healthy and is the most reliable separator on the roster; Wicks has shown he can win with his route running. Reintegrating both should make the passing game less one-dimensional, even with the inexperienced Joe Milton at the controls.
If the same late-to-the-line, overloaded-at-the-snap issues that have plagued the unit persist even with those two back, you can rest assured the problem is not solely personnel.
Shipley’s potential return also adds another layer. He is not Saquon Barkley, but he is a legitimate complementary back who can handle a share of the load and contribute to the passing game.
We have signed TE Zach Ertz and T John Ojukwu to the active roster and opened the practice window for RB Will Shipley. We also signed RB Jaydon Blue, LB Chance Campbell, and TE Hayden Rucci to the practice squad and released DB Shaun Wade from the unit. pic.twitter.com/CXy6mv1qm9
The Eagles have been thin at running back for large stretches of this season. Adding a functional piece behind Barkley should help. It also gives Mannion another chance to show he can build a more balanced attack rather than leaning on whatever is least injured against Pittsburgh.
The bye week gave the staff time to self-scout without the immediate pressure of a game plan. The Eagles also added old friend T.J. Paganetti , a run-game specialist, as a consultant on Monday. Those levers have to prove to be useful.
Any film sessions and schematic adjustments only matter if they show up in how the offense performs against the Steelers, an AFC playoff contender that hasn’t won in Philadelphia since 1965.
The Eagles don’t need Mannion to suddenly become the next Sean McVay. They do need him to demonstrate that his system can still function when key pieces are available, that the communication issues can be cleaned up, and that available players can be put in positions to succeed rather than simply asked to survive.
It’s esoteric and somewhat intangible, but that’s the bar for continued patience. Not a complete overhaul. Not a sudden jump into the top half of the league in scoring. Just clear evidence that the coordinator can raise the level of the players he has when they are actually on the field.
If that evidence does not appear soon, the conversation around the rest of the season will shift from “give Mannion time” to speculation about the next OC.
The bye was the intermission after a disastrous first act. Sunday is Mannion's first opportunity to prove that lessons were learned during the adversity.

title: Eagles Must Break the Chains Off These 3 Underused Players Coming out of Bye
full_text:
With a sixth consecutive playoff berth now just a distant dream, the back half of the 2026 NFL season should be all about development for the Eagles. If they're wise, they'll use their eight remaining games to give added on-field opportunity to some younger players to help them gain experience and confidence for the 2027 season and beyond.
With that in mind, here's a look at three underused Eagles who need to be unleashed from their shackles now that the bye week has passed.
Even though they held onto veteran tight end Dallas Goedert through the 2026 NFL trade deadline, the Eagles still need to unleash rookie Eli Stowers over the back half of the season to see exactly what they have in the young player after using a second-round pick to acquire him last April.
The fact that they drafted him in the second round demonstrates that the Eagles view Stowers very highly, but we haven't gotten to see much of him so far this season. He was sidelined for the first six weeks due to injury issues, and he's played sparingly since his return over the past three weeks. In total, he's tallied three receptions for 53 yards this season.
Coming out of the bye, the Birds need to break the chains off him.
By the time most people had turned the game off, Eli Stowers caught and ran this completely meaningless 34 yard pass to end the game. That ONE catch was enough to move him into 2nd place in receiving yards among Eagles TEs this season. He passed Mundt, who has played every… https://t.co/TCRQkY0u6w pic.twitter.com/bf5IwY4zFm
With Dallas Goedert heading to free agency, the Eagles will have to figure out how to properly address the tight end position over the offseason, and they won't be able to do that unless they have a better idea of what Stowers can bring to the field at this level. Getting him ample reps in relatively low-stakes games should be a priority for Philadelphia moving forward this season.
Edge rusher is a consistent area of need for Philadelphia, so they should see what they have in rookie Keyshawn James-Newby, whom they drafted in the seventh round in the draft in April.
The Eagles were prepared to trade linebacker Arnold Ebiketie at the deadline until the Bengals backed out of the deal . This shows that Ebiketie isn't in Philadelphia's plans beyond the current campaign, so some of his snaps should be reallocated to James-Newby, who has appeared in just two games so far this season. He flashed some potential during his limited time, though, including recording two pressures against the Panthers in Week 6.
The final eight games of the season will provide a perfect opportunity for the Eagles to increase his workload and see what kind of contributor he could be.
As the team's top pick from the 2026 draft, Makai Lemon has been receiving playing time all season. However, his role has expanded dramatically in recent weeks because the team's top two receivers, DeVonta Smith and Dontavious Wicks, have been sidelined due to injury issues.
Even if those guys are back in the fold in the coming weeks , the Eagles should still continue to give Lemon a larger load.
Lemon has shown some real potential in recent weeks. During that time, he has shown an impressive ability to create separation and get open, and he's also displayed some good hands, despite a couple of drops. He's tallied at least six receptions and 55-plus yards in three straight games for Philadelphia, despite inconsistent quarterback play.
Makai Lemon has shown flashes On pace for 70 Rec 589 yds 2 TD For an offense that’s mightily struggled future is bright for the kid! #FlyEaglesFly pic.twitter.com/PElS4TiabE
Allowing Lemon to continue gaining experience and confidence should be the Eagles' goal over the back half of the season. Offensive coordinator Sean Mannion should aim to feature him prominently moving forward.
Otherwise, he isn't doing his job right.

title: Breaking Down Eagles' Injury Report Coming Out of Their Bye (Who's Hurt & Who Could Return in Week 11)
full_text:
Injuries can quickly derail an NFL campaign. The Eagles have fallen victim to that notion in 2026, losing several starters during a disappointing seven-game losing streak . Returning to full health will be crucial to snapping the skid and being competitive in the second half of the season.
The Eagles' Week 10 bye provided extra rest for sidelined players ahead of a matchup against the Pittsburgh Steelers in Week 11. The team's first injury report of the week will be released following Wednesday's practice.
For now, let's take a peek at those on the mend in the City of Brotherly Love.
The Eagles have been without wide receiver DeVonta Smith for five of their nine games, as he deals with a hamstring injury. Philadelphia has been careful in this situation for a reason. Hamstring issues can be especially tricky for pass-catchers who rely on acceleration and change of direction in routes.
The news surrounding Smith is trending in the right direction ahead of Week 11. The Eagles released wide receiver Hollywood Brown, suggesting the team is banking on Smith being back on the field soon. The 28-year-old has tallied 310 yards and two touchdowns on 26 receptions (41 targets).
Smith isn't the only wide receiver Eagles fans are anxiously awaiting to recover. Dontayvion Wicks sustained an ankle injury in the fourth quarter of Philadelphia's Week 6 loss to the Panthers. The hope is that four weeks of rest are enough to get the exciting offseason acquisition back in the lineup.
Pay attention to Smith and Wicks's status on Wednesday's injury report. Even limited participation would be a big step toward playing on Sunday afternoon. Their returns would be a notable boost for quarterback Joe Milton. He completed 18 of 34 passes for 169 yards in his Eagles debut in Week 9.
Linebacker Jihaad Campbell played 37 snaps against the Cowboys in Week 7 before he needed to be replaced due to hamstring and quad injuries. The Alabama product was then sidelined in Week 8 and Week 9. A return to practice, in any fashion, will be the first step to getting Campbell back on the field.
Campbell's absence has opened the door for Jeremiah Trotter Jr. to play an every-down role at linebacker. He led the Eagles with 11 tackles (three tackles for loss) in Week 9's loss to the Giants. Keep an eye on how defensive coordinator Vic Fangio splits linebacker snaps once Campbell recovers.
Defensive back Michael Carter II suffered an abdominal strain in Week 5. The veteran returned to play in Week 8 but aggravated the injury in one snap. There hasn't been a concrete update on his status, other than the fact that he did not practice prior to being ruled out in Week 9. Expect clarity this week.
Carter allowed a 56.3 passer rating when targeted and just 5.5 yards per reception before going down (per PFF ). His return would be welcomed in a secondary that has been subpar as of late. Safety Andrew Mukuba is missing tackles, while cornerback Kenny Moore II is struggling in coverage .
Return specialist Britain Covey sustained a knee injury on Week 7's opening kickoff. He did not return to the game or practice before Philly's bye. Covey was not placed on injured reserve, though, so his activation should be near. Makai Lemon and Cooper DeJean will field kicks/punts in the meantime.
Quarterback Jalen Hurts was placed on injured reserve on Oct. 17 and isn't expected to return this season. The three-time Pro Bowler suffered a calf injury in Week 4, which caused severe blood clots to form. Those clots moved to his lungs. Hurts is under contract with the Eagles through 2028.
Philadelphia has opened the 21-day practice window for running back Will Shipley. The third-year pro had logged 88 total yards and one touchdown on 25 touches before going down with a foot injury. Fellow running back Tank Bigsby does not yet have a timetable to heal from a core muscle issue.
Other members of the Eagles' IR list include WR Johnny Wilson (knee), S Andre' Sam (foot) and S Tucker Large (knee).

title: Kracz: 5 Things Eagles Fans Should Know as the Bye Week Ends
full_text:
The Week 10 action is officially over, so now is the perfect time to catch up with the Eagles as they come out of their bye week . Here are five things that every Philadelphia fan must know heading into Week 11 of the 2026 NFL season.
When we last saw quarterback Joe Milton, he was sacked seven times while completing just 53 percent of his 34 passes in a 19-11 home loss to the Giants. Not great, but he wasn’t ready after being here for just three weeks. He made plays with his legs, though, and led the team in rushing with 64 yards on nine carries.
Milton will likely get the start on Sunday against the Steelers. Still, Sirianni could always change his mind on Wednesday, as he did when he infamously said, "Tanner's our guy," then benched McKee for Milton just days before the Eagles hosted the Giants.
This is what Sirianni said about Milton after losing to New York:
Still, Milton's fate is tied to the whims of his head coach.
The QB was asked how he would spend the bye week. He said he would probably take two days off, then get back to learning the Eagles’ system.
“I just want to be better,” he said. “We want to be better as a team.”
The Eagles went three-and-out and punted three times to start the second half, allowing the Giants to take control.
It’s not the first time the offense has been so inept for long stretches in games this year. In fact, offensive coordinator Sean Mannion’s unit has gone three-and-out on 43% of its offensive possessions, which is the highest rate of any team in the last three seasons and the highest rate for any Eagles team in the 21st century.
The Eagles filled two of the four openings on their 53-man roster, adding offensive lineman John Ojukwu and tight end Zach Ertz on Monday. Expect Ertz to make his march to the franchise record for most catches in an Eagles career. He needs eight more to break the mark of 589 set by Harold Carmichael from 1971-1983. In a lost season, at least it’s something.
We have signed TE Zach Ertz and T John Ojukwu to the active roster and opened the practice window for RB Will Shipley. We also signed RB Jaydon Blue, LB Chance Campbell, and TE Hayden Rucci to the practice squad and released DB Shaun Wade from the unit. pic.twitter.com/CXy6mv1qm9
The flip side is what happens with developmental second-round pick Eli Stowers. The rookie tight end got just seven snaps against the Giants.
The hole in the NFC East didn’t get much deeper for them during their week off, with the first-place Giants losing and the Cowboys stumbling again in Week 10. Still, the hole was already plenty deep enough to entertain any thoughts about making a late push to the top.
At 2-7 and incapable of winning a game since Sept. 20, Philadelphia is four games behind New York (5-3-1) in the loss column and entrenched in last place in the division.
It was a stunning move to see general manager Howie Roseman move on from Jordan Davis , a defensive tackle that he just opened the vault for in the offseason, but the return of a first-round pick next year and a second in 2028 was too great to pass up.
As for Arnold Ebiketie, the Eagles thought they had a deal done with the Bengals to get a sixth-round pick next year, but Cincinnati messed up and had to back out . So, it might be a tad awkward for the outside linebacker when he shows up in the locker room.
