title: T.J. Paganetti Reunion Could Shed Light on Eagles' Mindset as They Return From Bye
full_text:
PHILADELPHIA, P.A. — As they return from their bye week , the Eagles are bringing back T.J. Paganetti in a consulting role, a league source confirmed to Sports Illustrated .
The move mirrors previous outside voices the organization has brought in during the Nick Sirianni era, including Jim Bob Cooter in 2021 and Marcus Brady in 2022, not to mention Vic Fangio during the run-up to Super Bowl LVII.
Paganetti’s expertise is in offensive concepts—particularly the run game. Sirianni will speak on Wednesday and could offer more clarity on the role Paganetti will provide for the struggling 2-7 Eagles.
Although Paganetti’s institutional knowledge makes him a logical addition at a moment of clear offensive regression, the organization has used consultants in varying, sometimes unconventional ways.
For instance, Brady, a former offensive coordinator in Indianapolis and the current passing game coordinator in Baltimore, helped advise the defense in 2022 while Fangio offered up his defensive expertise to the offense before the Super Bowl that same season.
Paganetti held a variety of roles across his first stint with the Eagles from 2017 to 2024. He began as offensive quality control and assistant offensive line coach (2017-18) under Jeff Stoutland, then moved to assistant running backs coach (2019-20).
Under Sirianni, he first returned to quality control (2021-22) before being promoted to run game specialist/assistant tight ends coach in 2023 and run game specialist/assistant offensive line coach in 2024, where he again aided Stoutland. He was part of both Super Bowl championship staffs (LII and LIX) and left after the Super Bowl LIX win to become Kellen Moore’s run game coordinator with the New Orleans Saints.
Paganetti was later fired by the Saints earlier this month amid their own ground-game struggles earlier this season.
The timing is hard to ignore. The Eagles entered their bye week with all eyes on the offensive coaching staff and whether there would be any changes.
The organization went into the season intent on better marrying the running and passing games under new offensive coordinator Sean Mannion. That meant moving on from  Stoutland in favor of Chris Kuper (offensive line) and Ryan Mahaffey (run game coordinator/tight ends).
The shift has not produced the desired results . Philadelphia is currently mired in a seven-game skid, with the offense ranked near the bottom of the league and the line and run game a far cry from the record-setting 2024 unit that featured Paganetti in a specialized run-game role.
What’s somewhat strange—and perhaps telling—is the philosophical contrast between the two different ground game approaches.
Stoutland’s philosophy emphasized physical, vertical displacement, power-based downhill schemes, and a culture of technique, fundamentals and player development that turned the Eagles’ line into a sustained strength from the famed and marketed “Stoutland University.”
Mannion’s system, drawing more from zone-heavy influences, prioritizes lateral movement, wide-zone concepts, and better integration with the passing game. The personnel and teaching styles have not aligned cleanly this season, and the on-field product has reflected that disconnect.
Bringing back a Stoutland loyalist—even in a consultancy capacity—could be viewed as raising the white flag on the full transition.
At minimum, it reads as a concession that some of the old running-game principles that powered the Eagles’ previous sustained success need to be reintroduced.
Whether Paganetti can meaningfully influence scheme, technique, or messaging from a consultancy role is unlikely, but it remains to be seen. That said, the organization has at least signaled that the current run-game direction is not working as constructed.
With the season already largely lost and Jalen Hurts sidelined , the Eagles' focus seems to have shifted toward stabilization and identifying what elements of the one-time successful run-game identity are worth preserving.

title: Former Steelers Player Wants DK Metcalf Benched
full_text:
PITTSBURGH -- The Pittsburgh Steelers have not gotten enough out of wide receiver DK Metcalf. The team's "star" wide receiver has struggled for most of the season, and since Pittsburgh lost Roman Wilson and Michael Pittman Jr. to injuries, he has not stepped up in ways the team needs him to.
Against the Cincinnati Bengals, Metcalf has zero receptions for zero yards before the fourth quarter. That mark seems to be a trend for Metcalf, who has collected a good chunk of his stats in the final few minutes of games, while doing very little before the fourth quarter.
Fans aren't happy with Metcalf. And with his $150 million contract that the Steelers doubled down on in the offseason by restructuring it, it's becoming a question of whether or not Metcalf's play or his paycheck is what's keeping him on the field.
Former offensive lineman Trai Essex says that shouldn't matter. And he wants to see Metcalf moved down the depth chart.
"Find out a way to motivate DK to get the hell better," Essex said on his podcast 'The Snap Count.' “There’s no excuses at this point. We can’t coddle him and be like, ‘We’re not doing enough for you. We’re not running enough slants for you. We’re not running enough hitches for you.’ At some point, if you’re making $30-plus million, you need to figure it out or sit down until you do. … I think the most clear thing you can do and send a message to the team in that you are holding each and every position accountable is to bench DK and bring somebody else in."
That motivation may help. Metcalf has not played well, but the Steelers' solution has continued to be force feeding him the ball through screen passes and fades. Neither of which have worked.
Instead, maybe they should try a different approach.
Pittsburgh now has weapons at the wideout position. Michael Pittman Jr. and Roman Wilson returned to practice and could play as early as Week 11 against the Philadelphia Eagles. Rookie Germie Bernard and veteran Brandon Smith are still around, and Ben Skowronek is available if needed.
So, if the Steelers wanted to look at others to step up when Metcalf cannot, they can finally do so without having to put players with little experience on the field.
Will they? Probably not. Quarterback Aaron Rodgers and head coach Mike McCarthy have continued to praise Metcalf and stand behind him. Rodgers seems determined to force him the football more than any other weapon on the field.
So, don't expect them to listen to Essex. But maybe they should.

title: GTA VI Release Date: Where Steelers Were When GTA V Dropped
full_text:
The Pittsburgh Steelers and the entire world of football will have to battle for attention with Grand Theft Auto 6 this weekend.
GTA 6, which is made by Rockstar Games and will release on November 19, is among the most anticipated video games in recent memory, if not all-time. According to Sensor Tower , it has already sold just under 16 million copies and generated over $1.5 billion in revenue.
A major reason why there's so much hype surrounding GTA 6 is the fact that it's been 13 years since its predecessor, GTA 5, was put out in the fall of 2013.
Considering just how much of a phenomenon GTA 6 is, we thought it was worth looking back on the release of GTA 5 and where the Steelers stood at that moment in history.
While some might think the 2026 Steelers have it bad as GTA 6 comes out after losing 38-18 to the Cincinnati Bengals on Sunday Night Football in Week 10, this year's team doesn't hold a candle to the 2013 squad in that regard.
When GTA 5 was released on September 17 of that year, Pittsburgh was in the midst of its worst start to a season during the 21st century.
After collapsing down the stretch of the 2012 campaign, opening 6-3 before finishing 8-8 and missing the postseason for just the second time since 2007, the Steelers lost each of their first four games in 2013 and began the year at 0-4.
The Steelers did bounce back from there, going 8-4 to close out the season and finish 8-8, but it wasn't enough to make it into the playoff field in the AFC.
Antonio Brown was named an All-Pro for the first time in his career, earning second-team honors while finishing with 1,499 yards and eight touchdowns.
2013 was also the last time Troy Polamalu was named a Pro Bowler before later retiring following the 2014 campaign.
Furthermore, Cam Heyward is the only player left on Pittsburgh's current roster from the 2013 team. He started 13 of 16 games that year and recorded 59 tackles with 5.0 sacks.
Outside of Heyward, the only other member of the 2026 Steelers who was playing in the NFL during the 2013 campaign was Aaron Rodgers .
Rodgers was in the middle of his ninth season with the Green Bay Packers at the time and his eighth with Mike McCarthy as his head coach.
The future Hall of Famer only played in nine games, however, after breaking his left collarbone that November. Over that span, he threw for 2,536 yards, 17 touchdowns and six interceptions.
Only a few current Steelers were even playing collegiately when GTA V came out, as Chris Boswell was in his final season at Rice in 2013 while Jalen Ramsey (Florida State) and T.J. Watt (Wisconsin) were true freshmen while Robert Tonyan was a redshirt freshman quarterback at Indiana State.
Jack is a New Jersey native who graduated from the University of Pittsburgh as a Media & Professional Communications major in 2024 who is now covering the Pittsburgh Steelers and New York Yankees for On SI.

title: Steelers WR Help Coming: Roman Wilson, Michael Pittman Jr. Return to Practice
full_text:
The Pittsburgh Steelers are on the verge of several key pieces on the offensive side of the ball returning.
Ahead of practice on November 18, Steelers head coach Mike McCarthy told reporters that the 21-day practice windows for wide receivers Roman Wilson (finger) and Michael Pittman Jr. are set to open while the duo remains on the reserve/injured list for the time being.
The same goes for rookie offensive guard Gennings Dunker (knee), who now becomes all the more important for Pittsburgh as Mason McCormick recovers from a dislocated ankle that he suffered in Week 10's loss to the Cincinnati Bengals, and wide receiver Max Hurleman (undisclosed) as he moves from the practice squad/injured list to the active practice squad.
McCarthy noted that the team will evaluate all four throughout the course of the week in order to determine whether or not they'll be activated in time for the Steelers' Week 11 matchup with the Philadelphia Eagles.
Pittman Jr. hasn't played since Week 4 and Wilson hasn't seen the field since the first half of Week 5.
Hurleman, on the other hand, has yet to make his regular-season debut and is currently on the practice squad, though he is someone to watch out for as a potential solution at receiver moving forward now that he's back to practicing.
Since Pittman Jr. and Wilson were placed on IR in back-to-back weeks while Ben Skowronek just returned from a calf injury in Week 10 following a three-game absence, Pittsburgh has had to work through an extreme shortage of options at wide receiver.
The fact that DK Metcalf has struggled so mightily, particularly in terms of drops with six on the year (second-most among wide receivers according to Pro Football Focus ) while also not separating consistently, has only made matters worse for the Steelers. He is also on pace for a career-low 816 yards this season.
Second-round rookie Germie Bernard has shown some flashes, particularly in back-to-back outings of 80 yards or more in Weeks 6 and 7, but he's recorded a combined 57 yards over Pittsburgh's last three games.
With Pittman Jr. and Wilson on the precipice of a return, however, Aaron Rodgers and the entire offense is as flush with weapons at the skill positions as they have been all season long.
The level to which Pittman Jr. and Wilson can make an immediate impact whenever they are activated, whether that be later this week or down the line, remains to be seen. Regardless, having a full wide receiver room in the near future will open up more possibilities for the Steelers.
Jack is a New Jersey native who graduated from the University of Pittsburgh as a Media & Professional Communications major in 2024 who is now covering the Pittsburgh Steelers and New York Yankees for On SI.

title: Steelers Rookie Gennings Dunker Opens Return Window After McCormick Injury
full_text:
PITTSBURGH — The Pittsburgh Steelers received a devastating blow with the loss of starting left guard Mason McCormick, but there may be some good news on the horizon.
Not only did the Steelers received a slightly positive update regarding McCormick , they also shared a huge update on one of their injured rookies. McCormick might not be lost for the season, as was initially speculated, and could be back for the postseason.
In the meantime, the Steelers might welcome rookie offensive lineman Gennings Dunker back to the lineup. The recent third-round pick has been on Injured Reserve due to a knee injury, but head coach Mike McCarthy shared that the team opened his 21-day practice window.
In addition, the team also opened the 21-day practice windows for wide receivers Michael Pittman Jr., Roman Wilson and Max Hurleman, meaning all four players will be working their way back to full practice participation and eventually into the active lineup.
G Gennings Dunker, WR Roman Wilson and WR Michael Pittman Jr. returned to practice but remain on the Reserve/Injured List. 📝: https://t.co/35EEvgUGEG pic.twitter.com/UMNMbxFkwh
The timing on this update is perfect for both Dunker and the Steelers. The rookie lineman impressed during the preseason, but an injury sustained in practice took away several weeks from his first year in the NFL.
Despite the setback, the opportunity for legitimate snaps on offense might be there for Dunker upon his return to the field. The Steelers lost McCormick for at least the rest of the regular season schedule. That leaves eight more contests. Spencer Anderson is the starter in McCormick’s place, but he’s already been benched once this season. If Anderson struggles in his second chance along the first-team offensive line, the Steelers will need a “Plan B” to turn to.
Dunker is that “Plan B.” Although he played mostly at tackle during his collegiate career, the Steelers view him as an interior offensive lineman at the next level. He exclusively played at right guard during his preseason snaps, and while he has a ways to go in terms of his development, he has the skillset and mindset to be a starter in the NFL.
The Steelers have received plenty of contributions from their rookie class this season. On the offensive side of the ball, right tackle Max Iheanachor has been one of their best, while wide receiver Germie Bernard is arguably the top pass-catching option in Pittsburgh right now.
On the defensive side of the ball, the secondary has received significant snaps from Daylen Everette and Robert Spears-Jennings.
That doesn’t even mention how players like Kevin Jobity Jr. and Gabe Rubio have impressed in flashes, while Riley Nowakowski is quietly carving out a role on special teams.
It all sets up Dunker to be the next first-year player to make a positive impact on the Steelers. It might be a larger role earlier than expected, but that’s what the NFL requires some times.
And now, his practice window is open, meaning Dunker’s NFL debut is officially nearing.
Jacob is a featured writer covering the Pittsburgh Steelers for Steelers On SI and the NHL for Breakaway On SI. He also co-hosts the All Steelers Talk podcast. Previous work covering the NHL for Inside the Penguins and The Hockey News.

title: Eagles' Joe Milton Perfect Bounce-Back Candidate For Steelers
full_text:
After getting embarrassed by the Cincinnati Bengals in Week 10, the Pittsburgh Steelers will roll right into the perfect bounce-back opportunity against the Philadelphia Eagles.
Ahead of the Week 11 matchup between the two Keystone State foes, Eagles head coach Nick Sirianni stated that Joe Milton III will start at quarterback vs. the Steelers.
It will mark Milton's second straight start for a Philadelphia team in the midst of a seven-game losing streak as it returns from its bye week.
Pittsburgh certainly has to be cognizant of Milton's strengths, which include his athleticism and otherworldly arm strength. Regardless, he is a strong matchup for the Black and Gold's defense and could help the unit get back on track in a hurry.
Milton was a sixth-round pick by the New England Patriots in 2024 and was traded to the Dallas Cowboys in April 2025.
He was later let go by Dallas at the roster cutdown deadline back in August of this year and re-signed to the team's practice squad.
After Eagles starter Jalen Hurts was placed on the reserve/injured list due to blood clots in his lungs in mid-October, which ended his season, Philadelphia signed Milton to their 53-man roster off the Cowboys' practice squad.
The 26-year-old later made his first career start against the New York Giants in Week 9, and it didn't exactly go well. Milton completed just 18 of his 34 passes for 169 yards while also losing a fumble as the Eagles fell by a score of 19-11.
He did rush for 64 yards in that contest, though his issues with accuracy, varying the speed at which he threw and reading the defense at times ultimately came back to haunt him.
For a veteran defense like the Steelers , which had been a top five-to-seven unit in the NFL before allowing 38 points and 484 yards to the Bengals this past week, facing an inexperienced signal caller like Milton could be just what the doctor ordered.
Unlike what would've been the case had Hurts started against Pittsburgh, defensive coordinator Patrick Graham should be able to throw some coverage and pressure looks at Milton that he's unfamiliar with, which could throw him off his game.
Again, the Steelers have to be weary of Milton's legs and his ability to stretch the field, though his lack of refinement should work pretty heavily in their favor.
For a Pittsburgh defense that has largely thrived at getting after the quarterback and racking up sacks this season, that wasn't the case vs. Cincinnati.
Not only did the Steelers sack Joe Burrow just once all game, but they also logged just nine pressures (per Pro Football Focus ) and gave the Bengals' star quarterback plenty of room to step up in the pocket while dicing apart their secondary.
That hasn't been the norm for Pittsburgh this year, which is why there should be some optimism that its Week 10 performance was more of a one-off against an elite offense rather than its new norm.
In order for the Steelers to turn the tide, though, they have to get into the backfield and pressure Milton consistently.
The Giants laid the blueprint for the optimal game plan against Milton by blitzing him 31.25 percent of the time (per SumerSports ) and posting seven sacks as a result.
Pittsburgh blitzes 26.9 percent of the time according to SumerSports , which ranks No. 20 in the league, but raising that rate against Milton and the Eagles might just be the key to a dominant defensive outing at Lincoln Financial Field.
Jack is a New Jersey native who graduated from the University of Pittsburgh as a Media & Professional Communications major in 2024 who is now covering the Pittsburgh Steelers and New York Yankees for On SI.

title: Steelers' Cam Heyward Predicts Lamar Jackson's Future
full_text:
PITTSBURGH -- The Pittsburgh Steelers still have not met their fiercest rival, the Baltimore Ravens, this season. The two foes will meet twice over the final four weeks of the regular season schedule.
No matter where the Steelers and Ravens are in the standings or where they sit in the playoff picture, their matchups are always a battle to the final second. That's what bitter rivalries create in the NFL. That rivalry will continue as long as the NFL and the two franchises exist. It survives and endures through the multitude of superstars involved. The latest is Ravens quarterback Lamar Jackson, whom the Steelers have had the displeasure of game-planning against for nearly a decade.
But according to Steelers defensive tackle and team leader Cam Heyward, the years of Pittsburgh dealing with Jackson might be coming to an end. On a recent episode of his Not Just Football podcast, Heyward made a bold claim about Jackson's future in the NFL.
"Let. me get a little petty and stir the pot," he teased. "I don't think he is [the Ravens' quarterback in 2027]. I think he wants to go to South Beach. Or, this is the dark horse one, he goes to Atlanta to play with Bijan. And then you got wide receivers around you."
Heyward is indeed stirring the pot with these comments. For starters, it's noteworthy that he named the Miami Dolphins and Atlanta Falcons as two organizations to watch. He's speculating, of course, but it feels bit more accurate coming from a player who goes up against him multiple times per season.
Secondly, it highlights the uncertainty in Baltimore. With a new head coach and staff, plus Jackson's contract running through 2027 with no extension in place, there is a very real chance that the Ravens and their star QB are heading for a divorce, something the Steelers would love to see.
Jackson has played the Steelers 10 times in the regular season and once in the postseason over his nine seasons in the NFL. In the regular season, the matchup has overwhelmingly favored the Steelers.
Pittsburgh holds a 7-3 record over Lamar in their head-to-head matchups. In those games, Jackson has performed like an average quarterback rather than the MVP player he normally is. The Steelers have limited him to 139 completions on 241 attempts for. 1,741 passing yards, 12 touchdowns and 11 interceptions.
But the Steelers would likely celebrate Jackson's departure from the AFC North because that means they might not have to meet him in the postseason. Unlike the regular-season battles, the Ravens hold the edge in the playoffs.
The Ravens defeated the Steelers during the 2024 Wild Card Weekend, the only time these two teams have met in the postseason since Jackson's arrival. Jackson completed 16 of 21 passing attempts for 175 yards and two touchdowns, plus 81 rushing yards on 15 carries.
Jacob is a featured writer covering the Pittsburgh Steelers for Steelers On SI and the NHL for Breakaway On SI. He also co-hosts the All Steelers Talk podcast. Previous work covering the NHL for Inside the Penguins and The Hockey News.

title: What Happened to Steelers' Alex Highsmith?
full_text:
PITTSBURGH -- The Pittsburgh Steelers were handed an unexpected dose of reality during their 38-18 drubbing by the Cincinnati Bengals.
After storming out to a 6-2 record, the Steelers emerged from their bye week thoroughly outplayed by their AFC North rivals. Much of the loss can be written off to Cincinnati quarterback and MVP frontrunner Joe Burrow, who is at the top of his game right now. He dismantled the Steelers' defense, completing 35 of 44 passing attempts for four touchdowns and 409 yards.
The Steelers only sacked him once and forced zero turnovers. It was a disappointing outing for the defense, but it was especially so for the pass rush. While T.J. Watt battled against premier tackle Amarius Mims all night, Alex Highsmith faced significantly weaker resistance and was still unproductive.
For the seventh consecutive week, Highsmith was held to less than 1.0 sack in the contest. The output the Steelers are getting from their veteran leader is simply not enough, and in order to get back on track, Highsmith has to rediscover his game.
Through nine games, it's been an underachieving year for Highsmith. He's posted a total of 19 tackles, but only eight have been recorded individually, with the other 11 counted as assisted.
But tackles are only a piece of what Highsmith is judged on. The biggest piece is his ability to disrupt the quarterback, and he's well behind his usual pace. In nine games, he has just 3.5 sacks and five tackles for loss. His five tackles for loss rank 38th in the NFL amongst edge rushers with at least one snap, according to data from SumerSports. That figure is tied with Patrick Queen for second on the team, but that's exactly the problem.
Highsmith isn't getting home enough. The fact that he has the same number of sacks as the team's starting inside linebacker is concerning, but it's been disguised by the team's total sack numbers being at the top of the NFL.
One of the big reasons for Highsmith's decline in production this season is his average time to pressure. This refers to the amount of time it takes a defender, on average, to create a quarterback pressure. In years past, Highsmith has been one of the best. According to data from SumerSports, he averaged 2.40 seconds or less during the 2022, 2023 and 2024 seasons.
Last year, that number rose slightly, as he averaged 2.56 seconds.
This season, he's taking even longer. Through the first nine games, it's taking him 2.62 seconds on average to create pressure on the quarterback.
Why that's a problem is that most quarterbacks are releasing the ball in about 2.5 to 2.6 seconds. Take Bengals quarterback Joe Burrow. This season, he's averaging 2.59 seconds before he throws the ball.  Jacksonville Jaguars QB Trevor Lawrence is averaging 2.61 seconds. Kansas City Chiefs superstar Patrick Mahomes takes an average of 2.56 seconds. Green Bay Packers QB Jordan Love is averaging 2.45 seconds to throw in 2026.
What this demonstrates is the quickness and efficiency of some of the top offenses in the NFL. That's specifically a problem for Highsmith and the Steelers, who are counting on a four-man rush to get home and disrupt the quarterback.
Simple arithmetic is not on Highsmith's side right now.
Ever since the Steelers signed Nick Herbig to a new extension, the writing has been on the wall for Highsmith. One way or another, his time in Pittsburgh is closer to the end than the beginning.
The option most likely to happen is a trade. That's certainly a possibility in the offseason, as the Steelers will need to address their salary cap situation by moving on from at least one or two veteran players. Highsmith might not be having the most productive year of his career, but he's still 29 years old and one of the most complete EDGE rushers in football.
The more likely option, in my opinion, is that the Steelers let his contract play out and he walks away from the franchise following the 2027 campaign. According to contract data on Spotrac, Highsmith is entitled to a base salary of $15.5 million, plus a signing bonus, for next year. That adds up to a salary cap hit of $21.1 million, giving the Steelers three outside linebackers making over $20 million against the cap.
It's an expensive investment, but it remains the team's best position. And that's why I believe the Steelers will let this play out. Instead of taking a risk and moving on, the Steelers feel more likely to hold on to him and let him walk for nothing after 2027.
There's a lot of time until then, however. And the Steelers are trying to get back on track after being dominated by the Bengals. To get back on track, the Steelers need Highsmith to return to form and help snap the defense out of whatever funk Week 10 put them into.
Jacob is a featured writer covering the Pittsburgh Steelers for Steelers On SI and the NHL for Breakaway On SI. He also co-hosts the All Steelers Talk podcast. Previous work covering the NHL for Inside the Penguins and The Hockey News.

title: Steelers Could Get Mason McCormick Back for Playoffs
full_text:
PITTSBURGH -- The Pittsburgh Steelers avoided the worst-case scenario with offensive guard Mason McCormick, who left Week 10's game against the Cincinnati Bengals with an air cast on his right ankle.
McCormick suffered a pretty gruesome-looking ankle injury after running into quarterback Aaron Rodgers and left tackle Troy Fautanu on a play in the second half of the loss. He was carted off the field, with most of the staff and roster coming up to greet him as he was taken into the locker room.
Afterward, the belief was that whatever exactly happened wasn't good, and that McCormick was looking at a significant injury. Head coach Mike McCarthy said he hoped more news would be positive as the training staff continued to gather information, and according to NFL Network's Ian Rapoport, the team avoided the worst-case scenario.
Rapoport reports that McCormick suffered a dislocated ankle on the play, and while it's going to keep him out for some time, there's a chance that he can return for the playoffs.
McCormick will also avoid surgery with the injury.
#Steelers G Mason McCormick, who was carted off in an air cast on Sunday, suffered a dislocated ankle that unbelievably did not feature a fracture, sources say. No surgery needed, as the ankle was popped back in place on the field. There is a chance he’s back for the playoffs. pic.twitter.com/OElot8md3v
That's great news for the Steelers, who will hope to get their star left guard back on the field for a postseason run. McCormick is the heart and soul of the offensive line, and everyone, including defensive players, made that known after the game.
"Seeing Mason go down was pretty tough," defensive tackle Cam Heyward said after the game. "He has been kicking a lot of tail all year long, and on an offensive line, he's going to stand out. So it's going to be up to the guys to step up."
"The amount of work and just the presence that he brings to his offense and to this O-line room, it's a big loss, man," Fautanu said. "He's not going anywhere, but obviously being out there on the field, I know his presence is still going to be felt."
The Steelers will lean on Spencer Anderson to be their starter moving forward. The versatile offensive lineman started the season at right guard but was replaced by Brock Hoffman. At the time, it was revealed that Anderson was dealing with a fracture in his leg but was not going to undergo surgery during the season.
Behind him, Ryan McCollum will now become the primary backup at both guard and center. Rookie Gennings Dunker is on Injured Reserve with an MCL sprain but could make his way back to the active roster soon to add needed depth along the interior.

title: Steelers May Be Worried About DeShon Elliott Injury
full_text:
PITTSBURGH -- The Pittsburgh Steelers lost DeShon Elliott against the Cincinnati Bengals due to a pregame knee injury that ended his Week 10 before it got started.
Now, the team is doing their homework on defensive back help, signing A.J. Finley to their practice squad and working out Nazeeh Johnson and former Pitt star Jordan Whitehead two days after their Week 10 loss to the Bengals. While not adding someone to their active roster is a positive sign, spending so much time at the safety position might be an indicator that they're worried about Elliott's status moving forward.
And there are reasons to feel that way. Elliott suffered a season-ending knee injury in 2025 and after returning in training camp, the team made the decision that he was not ready to play come Week 1 of the regular season. He was placed on Injured Reserve and did not return to the lineup until Week 7 in Paris, France, against the New Orleans Saints.
He's played just two games this season, against the Saints and Cleveland Browns, and was limited to just 43 defensive snaps in those two weeks.
While the team has not yet revealed what happened to Elliott or what the injury is, there's reason for skepticism. With his knee having been injured in the past, if it's the same knee, the cause for concern is high. And while it doesn't mean Elliott is injury-prone, it may indicate that he needs more time than hoped for to fully heal and be able to play at a high level again.
Head coach Mike McCarthy has never been one to share too much about injuries. After the game, he offered very little about the situation, and did not expand on it during his Monday press conference.
"During his warmup, he had something that showed up, so we made him inactive," he said postgame.
If the Steelers are going to lose Elliott for an extended period of time, they'll likely make that announcement in the near future. For now, everyone can hope for the best. But Pittsburgh bringing in a handful of safeties to test out doesn't inspire the most confidence in the situation.
In the meantime, expect Robert Spears-Jennings and Jaquan Brisker to remain the starters for the Steelers. The seventh-round pick has become a very reliable piece of the defense and Brisker remains a player defensive coordinator Patrick Graham relies on in multiple situations.
As for Elliott, they'll hope he's good to go. And if not, they'll hope he can return again this season.

title: Steelers Add DB to Practice Squad After DeShon Elliott Injury
full_text:
The Pittsburgh Steelers are adding a safety to their practice squad following their 38-18 loss to the Cincinnati Bengals in Week 10.
Ahead of their Week 11 matchup with the Philadelphia Eagles, the Steelers announced that they've signed AJ Finley.
Pittsburgh hadn't previously made any additions to its practice squad, nor subtracted from it, since signing Marquez Valdes-Scantling on October 20.
Now, Finley joins the fray as the organization brings in additional depth in its secondary following a blowout defeat at the hands of its AFC North foes while DeShon Elliott deals with a knee injury that kept him out vs. Cincinnati.
A four-year player at Ole Miss from 2019 to 2022, during which he posted 243 tackles with eight interceptions and four fumble recoveries, Finley was not selected in the 2023 NFL Draft.
He proceeded to sign with the Los Angeles Chargers as an undrafted free agent and made their initial 53-man roster as a rookie.
Finley appeared in a total of 22 games for the Chargers through the 2024 campaign, posting 13 tackles and a forced fumble over that span.
He was later waived on November 25, 2024 and claimed by the Seattle Seahawks. Finley suited up for four contests with them to close out that season, logging a tackle along the way.
The 25-year-old did not play for Seattle in 2025 as it went on to win Super Bowl LX after suffering a knee injury that August.
Finley re-signed with the Seahawks this past offseason and later joined their practice squad after being let go at final roster cuts.
He did spend some time on Seattle's 53-man roster this year and played in three games while making a start, though he was waived on November 12 before finding his way to Pittsburgh.
Elliott's absence against the Bengals was evident, as Pittsburgh gave up 484 yards (406 of which were through the air) in that contest.
Cincinnati was able to do whatever it wanted against the Steelers' defense in the passing game as Joe Burrow and company were met with little resistance.
Now, with Elliott working through his injury after residing on the reserve/injured list until Week 7 this season while recovering from a season-ending knee/hamstring injury he sustained in Week 8 of the 2025 campaign, Finley becomes a potential option at safety for the team moving forward.
Pittsburgh also hosted former Kansas City Chiefs defensive back Nazeeh Johnson, who played in 29 contests for them from 2022 to 2025.
Johnson signed with the Tennessee Titans during the offseason but was suspended for the first six games of the year after breaking the NFL's performance-enhancing drug policy. Additionally, the 28-year-old underwent ankle surgery back in August and was released with an injury settlement.
The Steelers opted not to trade for a defensive back at the trade deadline this season, and that decision could end up haunting them. Now, they're doing whatever they can to help out their secondary on the fly.

title: Seahawks GTA Rewind: Seattle's Record for Every Game Release
full_text:
The Seattle Seahawks , the rest of the league and its fans are awaiting the long-overdue release of Grand Theft Auto VI.
It's been 13 years since the franchise released a game, so we figured that we would take a trip down memory lane to see how the Seahawks performed every year a game came out.
The Seahawks were still an AFC West team when Grand Theft Auto was first released in 1997. Hall of Famer Warren Moon was 41 years old and started 14 games for the team. It was the last of his nine Pro Bowl appearances. The team went 8-8 but missed the playoffs.
When the second iteration of the game was released, the Seahawks started 8-2 but lost 5 of their last 6 games, limping into the playoffs. They still won the division, but lost to Dan Marino and the Miami Dolphins in the Wild Card round. This was the last win of Marino's career.
The Seahawks had an identical record, but how they got there was a little different. Instead of starting 8-2, the 2001 Seahawks were 3-4 before winning six of their last nine games. Unfortunately for the Seahawks, it was not enough for them to move on to the playoffs in their final season in the AFC. The Baltimore Ravens and New York Jets advanced as wild cards with 10-6 records that year.
In Seattle's first season in the NFC, another installment of GTA was released. The Seahawks took a step back in their first NFC campaign, going 7-9 and missing the playoffs once again.
The Seahawks made it back to the playoffs for the second year in a row after snapping their drought in 2003. They won the NFC West in 2004, but fell to the St. Louis Rams 24-20 in the first round of the playoffs.
The Seahawks were in the midst of their rebuild by the time GTA IV came out. The following year, they hired Pete Carroll and went on the most successful run in franchise history.
The last time GTA released a game, the Seahawks went on to win the Super Bowl. The Legion of Boom was taking over and the Seahawks were establishing themselves as one of the top teams in the league.
Seahawks Record: 6-4 (so far)
The Seahawks finished as Super Bowl champs the last time Grand Theft Auto was released. That is a positive sign of what could happen this year, at least for Seahawks fans. The players themselves can take this weekend off , download the game, and relax as they get ready for the final seven weeks of the season.

title: Predicting the Final 7 Games on the Seahawks Schedule
full_text:
The Seattle Seahawks have seven games to go after their bye week and they have some work to do if they want to return to the postseason.
The Seahawks find themselves at 6-4 through 10 games , which is not good enough to be the first team on the outside looking in at the playoff picture. Here's a look at every game the team has left and a prediction for each contest.
Sun, Nov 29, 2026 | at San Francisco 49ers | Levi's Stadium | 1:25 PM PT | FOX
It's really hard to beat a division rival twice in one season, but that's what the Niners will look to do against the Seahawks after beating them in Week 5 at Lumen Field. The Seahawks were able to win last season in Week 18 at Levi Stadium to clinch the NFC West and the number one overall seed in the NFC, so this game will likely hold a lot of weight.
When it's all said and done, I believe the bye week will allow the team to have several players return from injury, which will help Seattle push through with a win to improve to 7-4.
Mon, Dec 7, 2026 | vs. Dallas Cowboys | Lumen Field | 5:15 PM PT | ESPN
The Seahawks return home for a Monday Night Football contest against the Dallas Cowboys, who are struggling so far this season with a 4-6 record. This game could turn into a shootout, as Dallas boasts one of the best offenses while also employing one of the worst defenses in the league.
The shootout type of game favors the Cowboys, but they have yet to face the number one defense in the league this season. A home matchup against them will challenge Dallas, but that is a unit that could make a dent against Seattle's defense.
Ultimately, the Seahawks defense will find a way to shut down the Cowboys and come out on top.
Sun, Dec 13, 2026 | vs. New York Giants | Lumen Field | 1:25 PM PT | FOX
The Giants may be on top of the NFC East, but they will likely enter this game as a big underdog against the Seahawks. Seattle will be on a short week after playing on Monday Night Football, but that shouldn't deter them against the Giants, who have been inconsistent on offense this season.
The Seahawks should be able to continue their winning streak against the Giants, which will likely push them into the playoff picture with three games to go.
Sat, Dec 19, 2026 | at Philadelphia Eagles | Lincoln Financial Field | 2:00 PM PT | FOX
The Seahawks are playing on Saturday of Week 15 because they are preparing for a Christmas Day matchup that will likely be an extension of the playoffs. The Seahawks are going on the road, but they will face an Eagles team that has had more misfortune than any team in the league this year.
This game on the schedule at the beginning of the season was looking a lot tougher than it does now, and Seattle should take advantage.
Fri, Dec 25, 2026 | vs. Los Angeles Rams | Lumen Field | 5:15 PM PT | FOX
This is where the games really start. The Seahawks and Rams are battling for likely one playoff spot, while the NFC North is playing extremely dominant football. All four teams have at least six wins and are in the playoff picture, but there's a good chance one of them falls by the wayside between now and the end of the year.
This game is easily the most crucial of Seattle's season, but playing at home should give them a boost that will continue their win streak.
Sun, Jan 3, 2027 | at Carolina Panthers | Bank of America Stadium | 10:00 AM PT | FOX
Regardless of the result against the Seahawks, this game against the Panthers on the road will also have major ramifications. The Panthers are in the hunt for a playoff spot, and this game could be a huge decision for them that dictates whether or not they make the playoffs. Given how hot Seattle could be down the stretch, I like their chances to win this game as well.
Sun, Jan 10, 2027 | at Los Angeles Rams | SoFi Stadium
This game could be a must-win for the Rams, and it could determine which team makes the playoffs and which team is on the outside looking in, especially if Seattle loses a couple more games that I expect them to. The final week of the season brings a lot of uncertainty about how important the game is for the Seahawks, but this should be considered a toss-up at this point.
Playing the Rams twice in the last three weeks of the season could very well determine whether the Seahawks advance to the playoffs. If they can win the games leading up to them, they won't have to cut it close.
They might even be able to have a shot at the division, depending on how the Niners do between now and the end of the year. Given that San Francisco is 2.5 games ahead of Seattle and Los Angeles, the division is theirs to lose and the Seahawks shouldn't rely on that as a path to the postseason.
A 12-win season will put the Seahawks in the playoffs, but that would require them to go 6-1 down the stretch. It won't be easy, but every game is winnable with the "Dark Side" defense, which should only grow in strength as the year progresses.

title: Seahawks Week 10 Snap Counts: Macdonald Leans on Depth Amid Injuries
full_text:
The Seattle Seahawks were beat up in Week 10, missing multiple key players and losing another in their win over the Las Vegas Raiders on Sunday. That varied their snap count totals from previous weeks, but it was enough to get a victory.
Offensively, the Seahawks had to make do with a backup quarterback and a patchwork offensive line that was missing three starters by the end of the game. On defense, the absence of Leonard Williams made head coach Mike Macdonald dig deep into Seattle’s depth.
Here’s a look at the Seahawks’ offensive and defensive snap counts from their 21-13 victory over the Raiders.
RG Anthony Bradford (57; 100%), LG Grey Zabel (57; 100%), C Jalen Sundell (57; 100%), LT Josh Jones (57; 100%), QB Drew Lock (57; 100%), TE AJ Barner (48; 84%), RT Bobby Hart (44; 77%), WR Jaxon Smith-Njigba (43; 75%), RB Zach Charbonnet (41; 72%), WR Cooper Kupp (35; 61%), TE Eric Saubert (26; 46%), TE Nick Kallerup (26; 46%), WR Rashid Shaheed (25; 44%), RB Jadarian Price (16; 28%), RT Abraham Lucas (13; 23%), FB Brady Russell (12; 21%), WR Tory Horton (10; 18%), WR Irvin Charles (3; 5%)
Lucas suffered an ankle injury during the game , thrusting Hart into action at right tackle. He played most of the game on an offensive line that was already missing left tackle Charles Cross and left guard Quenton Nelson.
It was a run-heavy day for the Seahawks (35:17 rush-to-pass ratio), so all three of their top tight ends played 46% or more of the total offensive snaps. Only Barner (three catches for 19 yards) was used in the passing game, while Saubert and Kallerup were extra blockers.
Charbonnet saw significantly more snaps than rookie Jadarian Price , and the former totaled 20 carries for 94 yards. Price finished with 10 total touches for 44 yards. That split will likely remain while both players are healthy.
LB Ernest Jones IV (59; 100%), S Julian Love (59; 100%), CB Devon Witherspoon (59; 100%), S Ty Okada (59; 100%), CB Josh Jobe (58; 98%), LB/DB Nick Emmanwori (57; 97%), DL Byron Murphy II (42; 71%), LB Drake Thomas (39; 66%), OLB DeMarcus Lawrence (36; 61%), OLB Derick Hall (31; 53%), OLB Uchenna Nwosu (27; 46%), DL Jarran Reed (26; 44%), DL Rylie Mills (24; 41%), OLB Dante Fowler Jr. (20; 34%), DL Mike Morris (14; 24%), CB Nehemiah Pritchett (12; 20%), DL Brandon Pili (12; 20%), CB Trevon Diggs (9; 15%), OLB Connor O’Toole (5; 8%), LB Patrick O’Connell (1; 2%)
Beyond the defensive line adjustments, there weren’t many changes against the Raiders. Jones, Love, Witherspoon, Okada, Jobe and Emmanwori all played the vast majority of snaps once again, with the typical rotations at linebacker, defensive line and edge rusher.
Morris and Mills continued to see an uptick in usage with Williams on the sideline. Once Williams returns, he will command most of that usage. Fowler also played more snaps than he has most of this season, and he had one of Seattle’s six sacks on the day.

title: Tory Horton’s 500 IQ Play Wins Special Teams Player of the Week
full_text:
Despite having a relatively minimal impact on the outcome of the game on Sunday, there was a lot made of Tory Horton’s play on a kickoff return late in the fourth quarter . Many people who have been watching NFL football for decades claim they’ve never seen a play like it before. The referees reacted as if they had never seen it before either. And now, it’s an award winner.
Just to refresh our memories, let’s talk about the play itself. The Las Vegas Raiders are kicking off to the Seattle Seahawks after making it a 21-13 ballgame with 2:04 remaining. With two timeouts left, their goal is to boot the ball out of the back of the endzone so no time elapses. If they do that, they can force a three-and-out that leaves plenty of time left to tie the game.
Matt Gay boots it through the endzone…except Tory Horton skies up and bats it back into the field of play before going out of bounds. He tells Rashid Shaheed to pick the ball up and return it. Shaheed does, getting out to the 19 yard line before getting tackled, using about seven seconds and forcing the two-minute warning to tick off before the possession starts.
The NFL has responded to this play by naming Horton the NFC Special Teams Player of the Week. Usually, that reward goes to a player who returns a kickoff or punt for a touchdown, or maybe a kicker who boots 5 or 6 field goals through the uprights. To win it for a play that isn’t even really quantified by statistics is very atypical, and also very cool.
It’s also a bit odd that they would give out an award for a player that they also threw a penalty flag on. According to Bill Vinovich’s crew, who deliberated on the issue for several minutes, the play constituted an illegal bat. Perhaps this is an acknowledgement that the flag was thrown in error, and the play actually is legal. After all, this was the only play that Horton had.
The thing that made the play stand out so much was how smart it was on Horton’s part. This was a very specific game scenario, and a very specific play that permitted it. For Tory to realize that it was the right thing to do, and then do it, in the few seconds he had to put the pieces together, is very impressive. How often do we see players fail in these moments?
A couple weeks ago, during the game between the Seattle Seahawks and Chicago Bears, we saw the exact opposite of this kind of thing on a first quarter punt. Michael Dickson looked like he had laid it up perfectly around the five-yard line, but Rodney Thomas II knocked it into the endzone for a touchback instead. Shoutout Tory for coming through here.

title: 3 Risers and Fallers Heading Into Seahawks' Week 11 Bye-Week
full_text:
The Seattle Seahawks (6-4) have some momentum coming out of the 21-13 Week 10 road win over the Las Vegas Raiders. Seattle has won two consecutive games for the first time since Week 1 and 2 of this season. The offense is finally playing with some consistency and the defense has addressed some of its biggest problems early. Now the team looks to develop more as a team during the bye week.
​At the halfway point of the season, there are changes happening to the Seahawks’ roster . Some players are seeing great changes while others are losing their role or status on the team. A player’s traction on the team can temporarily affect their status or, possibly, affect their future.
​Wide receiver Jaxon Smith-Njigba is already the best player on the Seahawks and the best receiver in the league. JSN, however, is proving that he should be easily the favorite for his second offensive player of the year award. He should also be considered for the league MVP award as he is on pace to break Calvin Johnson’s single-season receiving yards record . There hasn’t been a player more reliable than JSN this season and this season shows he is the standard of how to be a franchise wide receiver.
​For several weeks, there were Seahawks fans and media outlets were ready for the Seahawks to move one from veteran edge rusher Dante Fowler Jr. In the last two games, however, Fowler has been a more reliable defender off the edge. Fowler accounted for three total tackles, two tackles for loss, a sack and a quarterback hit. The Seahawks didn’t trade for an edge during the NFL Trade Deadline, but they have an emergence in Fowler.
​Veteran running back Zach Charbonnert was only six yards away from accounting for his third 100-yard rushing. He rushed for 94 yards on 20 carries for an average of 4.7 yards per carry. Originally, Price was projected to be the No. 1 running back, but the coaching staff seem to want Price to learn under Charbonnet. The coaching staff also values Charbonnet’s veteran leadership , which should be a big boost for his next contract.
​This season has been difficult for the Seahawks’ offensive line, which has regressed as a unit. The player who has arguably regressed the most is right tackle, Abraham Lucas . While he has been a solid run-blocker, he has been a below-average pass-protector. Lucas has allowed six sacks, four hits and 26 pressures this season. Lucas left the game versus the Raiders with an ankle sprain. Head coach Mike Macdonald doesn’t have a timeline set for Lucas to return .
​Just a few weeks ago, there were opportunities for second-year wide receiver Tory Horton to see an increased role and reps after the minor knee injury to Rashid Shaheed, who returned in the game versus Las Vegas. Horton didn’t take advantage of the opportunity to get more playing time. In the game against the Raiders, Horton only had 10 offensive snaps and three special team snaps against the Raiders while not seeing a target.
​Rookie defensive tackle Deven Eastern saw his opportunity by being added to the 53-man active roster after the injuries to veteran defensive tackles Leonard Williams and Brandon Pili . He was added to the roster mostly for depth and as an emergency defensive tackle. After being on the roster for two games, he was waived and signed back to the practice squad.

title: 2 Bye Week Goals for Seahawks
full_text:
The Seattle Seahawks are 6-4 as they approach their upcoming Week 11 bye.
The Seahawks are in the mix for a playoff run in the NFC , but to achieve their goals, they need to make the most of their bye week. Here's a look at the two main goals the team should have over the next couple of days.
The Seahawks are incredibly grateful to have Jaxon Smith-Njigba on offense. The reigning offensive player of the year is looking to rack up another trophy, as he is on pace to break the NFL record for most receiving yards in a single season.
With JSN on a record-breaking pace, no other receiver on the offense has more than 300 yards, including Rashid Shaheed, who signed a 3-year, $51 million contract over the offseason. The Seahawks need to find ways to get other players on the offense involved to give them more versatility and optionality.
The fact that the offense is so one-sided toward Smith-Njigba is not good for what the future holds for the team. A predictable offense is harder to win with later in the season, so the team needs to figure out how to make other players more dangerous to other teams. That opens things up for Smith-Njigba because teams will skew their game plans toward stopping him and do whatever it takes to make sure he is blanketed.
JSN has broken all of those tests this season, but eventually someone is going to figure it out. If the Seahawks can showcase a threat elsewhere, it will only make things easier for the unit.
The Seahawks have struggled to stay healthy this season, but even with those struggles, they have maintained a winning record. Getting players like Sam Darnold and Leonard Williams back to full health, along with trade acquisition Quenton Nelson, will likely determine how far the Seahawks go this season.
One of the strengths the Seahawks had last year, which helped them win the Super Bowl, was that a lot of their top players were healthy going into the final weeks of the season. As the team heads toward Thanksgiving, they need to figure out a way to heal so they can put their best 53-man roster on the field on Sundays.
Given how talented and top-heavy the NFC is, this could ultimately be the difference between who advances to the playoffs and who is sent home earlier than they should be.

title: Making the Case for Sam Darnold and Drew Lock as Seahawks Starter
full_text:
This 2026 NFL Season has been confusing for the Seattle Seahawks (6-4) and the 12. May signs show the Seahawks may have taken a few bad steps back from their Super Bowl-winning form. The offense may be finally establishing itself after the 21-13 road win at the Las Vegas Raiders on Sunday. There might still be some questions at quarterback that need to be answered.
On Monday, head coach Mike Macdonald already issued a statement that Darnold will be the starting quarterback moving forward, if he is healthy. The biggest factor is whether he is healthy, as he has missed the last two games with a quad and broken ribs injury. There are several reasons why Darnold should start the rest of the season, but there are key reasons why Lock should start.
​The Seahawks have already decided that Darnold is the best fit for the offense long-term. He needs a lot of things around him to be right or nearly perfect. He needs the offensive line healthy, an established running game, competent play calling and a reliable pass-catcher. Darnold has only had one of those all season with wide receiver Jaxon Smith-Ngiba . Once he has them, he can outperform expectations, as evident in the NFC Title game.
​With Price and Charbonnet back, offensive coordinator Brian Fleury getting more comfortable with the offense and the offensive line returning healthy, Darnold has what he needs to push the limits for an explosive offense. Darnold possesses the consistency and big-play vision to get the offense rolling. His downside is his turnovers , which have been an issue due to the limited offense and his injuries. Darnold has more upside due to his experience and familiarity with the team.​
Lock is an average starter on other teams that don’t possess the tools for a top-ten offense. When he does, with a team with great experience and the league’s best receiver in JSN, Lock can be inserted into a productive offense and up to the standards of a playoff-caliber quarterback, but only with the Seahawks.
​Through nearly four games for Seattle, filling in for the injured Darnold, Lock has completed 73.1% of his passes for 837 yards, seven touchdowns, no interceptions, a QBR of 85.8 and the league’s second-highest quarterback rating of 125.6. He has been one of the most productive quarterbacks in the games he has started. Lock, however, has started against some of the worst defenses in the league: the Arizona Cardinals (twice) and the Raiders.
​For Lock to be the starter for the rest of the season , he would be the much healthier option and he would need to show he can play against great defenses. The Seahawks will face the San Francisco 49ers (8-1) in Week 12 after their upcoming bye week. San Francisco possesses the fifth-ranked total defense and the 12th-ranked scoring defense in the league. This would be a good test for Lock with this Seahawks offense if Darnold can’t play due to injury.

title: 3 Reasons Why the Seahawks Are Sticking With Sam Darnold
full_text:
I’ve been fairly open in recent times about my preference for the Seattle Seahawks sticking with Drew Lock at quarterback. Yesterday, Mike Macdonald came out and stated in no uncertain terms that Sam Darnold will be getting his job back when health allows. Not my preference, but I can still seek to understand it. So here are three reasons why Sam is the guy.
This first one is nice and simple. The Seahawks won the super bowl about nine months ago, and they did it with Sam Darnold at quarterback. For most of the people in this organization right now, it’s the one and only super bowl they’ve won. I can certainly understand why the team would feel obligated to let Sam play while there’s any hint of ambiguity on who to play.
Lock has mostly played weak defenses this season, while Darnold’s struggles have largely come at the hands of stronger units. He’s also been without his top running backs for most of his games. That’s enough to open the door, and given what Sam did last season, maybe it’s just a matter of respect. He’s earned himself a few more rolls of the dice.
This is probably the ‘best’ reason I can come up with. Maybe the Seahawks believe that Drew Lock has a ceiling lower than winning a championship. Maybe there’s a higher floor with Drew, and maybe there’s more stability to be a playoff team, but when you’re playing a team like the 49ers, Bears, or Vikings, he’s just not going to be able to do enough to get the win.
Darnold, while he’s fully capable of playing some truly awful football, has accessed that ceiling quite a bit here. The ceiling that allowed him to be an MVP candidate in the first half of the season , or out-duel Matthew Stafford to win the NFC. Maybe the assumption concerning Lock is wrong, but if the goal is to win it all, then you play the player who can accomplish that.
This is the one that feels a little more cynical to me. But even still, on some level, I get it. The Seattle Seahawks are a few months away from making a massive decision on Sam Darnold’s future . The decision they make will have a giant effect on the team for the next several seasons. They have to get it right. And right now, they’re not working with a lot of data.
Darnold has missed several games this year, has played through injuries in some of the games he’s played, and has been without several key teammates. Maybe they feel like they have to give Darnold these last seven starts to make sure they know exactly what it is before they make a decision. Even if it costs them a chance to defend their title this year.

title: Jaxon Smith-Njigba Is Embroiled in the Greatest OPOTY Race of All-Time
full_text:
In a season full of battles and arguments between members of the fanbase of the Seattle Seahawks, one man is uniting all sides. Jaxon Smith-Njigba’s game is beyond any debate or discussion . But is that uniquely dominant season going to be enough to win Offensive Player of the Year? Normally, yes, but this year is far from normal.
Chances are you already know all about JSN’s incredible season to this point. He’s currently in possession of the NFL’s receiving triple crown, leading the league in receptions (79), yards (1,207), and touchdowns (10). He’s on pace to break the single-season receiving yards record by nearly 100 yards, and his 134 reception and 17 touchdown tracks would be top 10 all-time.
He’s also tops in receptions of 20 or more yards (19), yards after catch (422), and receiving first downs (57). His 82-yard touchdown in week 2 is currently the longest catch in the league for 2026. And he’s doing it in an offense lacking any other credible threats, a run game, high-level quarterback play , or capable offensive coordinator. He might be the best ever.
This is the primary competition right now. While JSN is tracking to have maybe the best WR season ever, Gibbs is making a play to have the greatest RB season ever. He’s the first one to crack 1,000 rushing yards on the year, and is also sitting on 41 catches for 384 yards. Throw in a league-leading 13 touchdowns, and you can see why this is going to be difficult.
His pace, since he’s only played nine games, is 452 touches (4th all-time), 2,613 scrimmage yards (1st by over 100 yards), and 23 touchdowns (8th). If Gibbs can hold these lines, on a great offense with other viable options (Amon-Ra St. Brown is on pace for over 1,400 yards, Jameson Williams for nearly 1,000), it might be better than JSN’s pace.
OPOTY has become the ‘non-QB MVP award’ in recent years, more or less, but it hasn’t always been. As recently as 2018, a quarterback (Patrick Mahomes) won MVP and OPOTY. Matt Ryan, Cam Newton, Peyton Manning, and Tom Brady have done it too. Adrian Peterson, not a quarterback, also managed to win both. So it can most certainly happen.
If it happens this time, it’s Burrow who can pull it off. Joe Shiesty leads the NFL in completion percentage (74.7%), yards per game (310.6), touchdowns (27), and QB rating (117.7) among QBs who have played the whole season. His paces are 5,279 yards (4th all-time) and 51 touchdowns (2nd) are MVP and OPOTY caliber. His QB rating would be 6th in NFL history.
Right now, the odds are in Gibbs’s favor, sitting at +100 compared to JSN’s +125. But that’s not at all definitive. Burrow is essentially off the board, +8000, perhaps indicative of the belief that he won’t win it if he wins MVP, where he’s -115 right now. I’m not sure I agree with that, but assuming the award really is earmarked for non-QBs now, it’s a two-man race. (Odds via DraftKings Sportsbook )

And it really might be the best two-man race of all-time. In two months, we really might be looking at the best wide receiver season ever against the best running back season ever. title: Tory Horton May Have Earned Larger Seahawks Role After Raiders Game
full_text:
The Seattle Seahawks dominated on defense and were outstanding on offense, especially in the third quarter against the Las Vegas Raiders in their Week 10 victory . Still, it was a special teams play that might have sealed the deal going into the bye week.
With just 2:04 left to go in the game , the Raiders kicked off to the Seahawks after knocking down a field goal to make it a one-score game. The Seahawks knew that a touchback would result in an additional time stoppage, so they wanted to avoid this at all costs. That prompted wide receiver Tory Horton to make arguably the biggest special teams play of the season.
The effort by the Seahawks special teams to prevent the touchback and keep the clock running 👏 SEAvsLV on CBS/Paramount+ Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/YF6eTRh4gs
"It kind of bounced off my hands and I kind of just like drifted out of bounds," Horton said via the team's website.
"So, kind of just pointed at Sheed (Rashid Shaheed) to pick the ball up and return it. Just wanted to just keep the ball in play. I wish I caught it with one hand, but that's a pretty hard catch to do with the ball and go inflight like that. So I was still happy that Shaheed recognized the ball was in play and picked it up after I told them and just happy that we got it under 2 minutes."
Going into the contest, Horton wasn't even supposed to be in that position to begin with. However, circumstances changed throughout the game, and that forced Horton into that situation.
"It was a tremendous play," head coach Mike Macdonald added after the game.
"Tory's actually trying to catch that ball, albeit with one hand. Just an incredible play. With George Holani going down, we had to take JD (Jadarian Price) off of kickoff returns, so those are guys that haven't necessarily practiced (kick return) a bunch in a while, especially with this game plan. So to be able to step in and be able to execute some of those critical situations is some great stuff by them, great job by our coaches, and it really helped us close the game out."
Knowing that Horton wasn't even supposed to be in that position but made a play on the fly in a crucial situation that normally doesn't pop up is exactly how the Seahawks want to identify themselves. They have a next-man-up mentality that places importance on all 70 players on the main roster and practice squad, giving them moments to shine like this.
This identity helped carry the Seahawks to the Super Bowl last season, and it is what has them on pace to go all the way once again. It's going to take more plays like this after the bye, but this is a sign that the Seahawks are getting ready to make a run.
The Seahawks will return after the bye week to take on the San Francisco 49ers on Nov. 29. Kickoff is scheduled for 1:25 p.m. PT inside Levi's Stadium in Santa Clara. Fans can watch the game on FOX or stream it on the FOX One app.

title: 49ers HC Kyle Shanahan Gushes Over Vikings DC Brian Flores
full_text:
Kyle Shanahan and the San Francisco 49ers will face their toughest test on offense this season when they take on the Minnesota Vikings in Mexico City.
The Vikings' defense is the best in the NFL, thanks to the brilliant scheme led by defensive coordinator Brian Flores . Shanahan has struggled against Flores since he joined the Vikings.
The chess match with Flores will demand Shanahan and the 49ers to be at their best. It's a matchup that is stressful to plan for, but it also invokes a ton of admiration from Shanahan for Flores. He can't help but gush over Flores' brilliance.
"He's more unique than all the other 31 guys," Shanahan said. "He's the one guy who commits to this and it's not just a fad for these nine games or whatever. He's been doing it his whole time in Minnesota. He did the same thing in Miami. He's as good as it gets at that stuff. Anybody who lives in that world as much as he does, it's usually a matter of time.
"They put so much pressure on the quarterback, the play caller, the O-Line, the receivers, on everybody. A lot of times when you go into an NFL game, the pressure's really on people on third down and stuff like that because those are things where everything can come and when you play against Brian it's 70-straight plays of that.”
Saying that a defensive coordinator is "more unique" than the rest is as good a compliment as you can get. Flores should be blushing over the heap of praise Shanahan bestowed upon him.
It makes sense why Shanahan feels that way. He's battled Flores' defense over the year. It's always tough to crack and get the upper hand.
Not even in 2023, when the 49ers went to the Super Bowl, were they successful against the Vikings' defense. Odds are, it's going to be more of the same in Mexico City.
The 49ers are doing everything in their power to make sure it's different this time. Unlike in 2023, this matchup has significant playoff seeding implications.
If there were ever a game for the 49ers and Shanahan to finally get the best of Flores and the Vikings' defense, it's this one. In any case, you can expect a tough and gritty matchup.
"You're going to try to be consistent and efficient in everything, but I promise you that's not going to happen for all the plays. Brian creates too much stuff.

title: Vikings Defense Has a Weakness the 49ers Can Exploit
full_text:
The San Francisco 49ers will need to be at their very best when they take on the Minnesota Vikings on Sunday in Mexico City, especially on offense.
Minnesota's defense is easily the best in the league.  Moving the ball and putting up points against them will be difficult. It will be night and day compared to playing the Dallas Cowboys.
Kyle Shanahan and Brock Purdy have always struggled against the Vikings' defense thanks to defensive coordinator Brian Flores . However, as vaunted as the Vikings' defense is, they have a weakness the 49ers can exploit.
It's their run defense. Minnesota's run defense ranks No. 17 in yards per game allowed at 111.9. They've also allowed the 13th-most runs of 10 yards or more.
This is where the 49ers will find success. In fact, it's the only way they will beat the Vikings. It's if they can successfully exploit this weakness.
For starters, it will wear down the Vikings' defense, especially with the game being played at high altitude in Mexico City. Of course, the 49ers can tire on offense as well, which is why rookie Kaelon Black will need a lot of carries.
Tiring games also tend to favor the offense. Just look at the 49ers' defense last week against the Dallas Cowboys. Shanahan said that their defense was gassed, especially the defensive line.
Another reason running the ball will help the 49ers is because of third down. This will help them stay in manageable third-down situations. That is crucial to defeating the flurry of blitzes from the Vikings.
It will place Purdy in an advantageous position to drop back for a quick pass to either Keenan Allen or Christian McCaffrey. There won't be enough time for the blitz to get to him since the yardage for a conversion will be short.
Shanahan must avoid dialing up a ton of passes for Purdy to get blasted on early downs. That will set them back well behind the chains and make converting first downs extremely difficult, if not impossible, against Minnesota's defense.
The run-blocking will need to be elite for the 49ers. Left guard Connor Colby will be their biggest worry, especially since he struggled against the Cowboys last week.
Everyone else should be fine to execute at a high level. Everything hinges on the 49ers running the ball against the Vikings.
If the 49ers can't find success on the ground , they won't win the game.

title: 49ers Have Clear Mike Evans Decision After Injury Update
full_text:
San Francisco 49ers star wide receiver Mike Evans missed practice once again with his Achilles injury. Evans has not practiced since Week 5 and has not played since Week 6. Head coach Kyle Shanahan said that the team is hopeful to get him back at practice on Thursday. However, whether he practices or not, the plan for Week 11 should be clear. There is no reason to play Mike Evans.
First off, Evans is 33 years old. He missed two games in 2024 and nine games in 2025. He is starting to be on a downward trend due to injuries and age in the NFL. Still, the team signed him with one idea in mind, and that is to win a Super Bowl.
If the 49ers can get three or four healthy games from Evans from January into February, the team will have gotten their money's worth. In the first six games, they saw just how good he can be when he is on the field.
They are sitting at 8-1, and they have a three-game lead in the NFC West. They also have wins over the two teams that matter in their division. A loss to the two-loss Vikings would hurt their chances at a home game in the NFC Championship. However, if you asked most 49ers whether they would rather be at home for that game or have Mike Evans fully healthy, most would take Evans.
So, the team should be cautious and only play him when he is 100% ready to go. Even if he is close, there is no reason to push it, and he should take the extra week.
It is not like the 49ers are certain to lose without him, either. They are currently lis ted as short favori tes. The team just got Deebo Samuel back healthy. They just traded for Keenan Allen. More than that, second-year wideout Jordan Watkins is starting to ascend in recent weeks.
When adding in Demarcus Robinson as a depth option, the team is not thin at receiver right now. Adding Allen and seeing Watkins emerge has allowed the team to take things slow with Evans and not see it impact them on the field.
So, there is no reason to push it. We will see if he practices later this week. His game status should be determined Friday.

title: 49ers Star Misses First Week 11 Practice vs. Vikings
full_text:
Kyle Shanahan was hopeful that San Francisco 49ers star wide receiver Mike Evans could practice this week in preparation for the Minnesota Vikings.
However, Evans missed the first Week 11 practice, making it more of the same. Shanahan did add that Evans will "hopefully" participate in the second practice on Thursday.
It's a tough call with Evans as he deals with Achilles tendinitis . The injury has kept him out of the last three games. He's been working hard to calm down the tendinitis since he first sustained it.
The 49ers have been doing fine without Evans, losing only to the Falcons in Week 7. But this week they are facing their greatest threat in the NFC.
The Vikings have the best defense in the NFL. This is a game where they desperately need Evans back help them win.
And while it's only Week 11, this matchup will have a significant impact on playoff seeding. Attaining the No. 1 seed is always crucial, but especially for the 49ers who have a bunch of older star players.
Still, as badly as the 49ers need Evans, they mustn't push him if he's not 100%. The last thing they want to do is have him ruin all the hard work he did to calm his tendinitis down.
They also mustn't let Evans make the call on whether he plays or not. That's the reason the 49ers and Evans are in this mess to begin with.
They allowed Evans to tell them he's playing in Week 6 despite missing an entire week of practice with Achilles soreness. It was such a foolish move by the 49ers to abide by Evans.
Teams have to protect players from themselves. And if they have to go one more week without Evans, with a critical matchup looming, so be it.
Speaking of protecting players, Dre Greenlaw was also out of Wednesday's practice with a neck injury. It's unclear when he suffered the injury.
Shanahan never shared that Greenlaw was hurt in the Week 10 postgame or on Monday while on a conference call with reporters. It's very strange that he suddenly got hurt.
In any case, they're hopeful Greenlaw will return to practice on Thursday, like Evans. Last but not least, Renardo Green was limited on Wednesday. He's been nursing a back injury he suffered in Week 9.
He toughed it out against the Cowboys before exiting the game in the second half. There was concern that he could be out of practice this week.
But he's managed to participate in a limited capacity, which is an encouraging sign. All eyes will be on Evans and Greenlaw for the rest of the week.

title: Brian Flores Reveals What Makes 49ers HC Kyle Shanahan Elite
full_text:
When the San Francisco 49ers take on the Minnesota Vikings in Week 11, it will be what most would declare the best defensive play caller in the NFL against the best offensive play caller in the NFL. When Vikings defensive coordinator Brian Flores had a chance to discuss how tough Shanahan is to face off against, the star coordinator did not hesitate to call Shanahan elite and one of the best minds in the NFL.
Flores noted that the most impressive trait Shanahan brings is his ability to branch plays off of each other.
“Where do I start? I mean, everything is high level; it's thought out,” started Flores. “There's a rhyme and reason behind it all. There's complementary plays.”
Flores used the way that he lines up players, for example. He noted that fullback Kyle Juszczyk does not have much production. However, Flores is impressed with how Shanahan uses him to trick coaches into thinking they found a tell.
“You know, (Kyle) Juszczyk, when he’s lined up there, they do this,” Flores referenced. “ No, they do that. They got a complement off of that. And so everything has that. He's done a great job for a long, long time.”
Flores added it is not just that, either. The team is so good at that because they are strong everywhere. Teams have to respect all aspects of their game.
“From a run game standpoint, it's elite,” stated Flores. “From a protection standpoint, it's elite. From a play design standpoint, it's elite. All of it's elite.”
So, the Vikings coordinator did not mince words when saying that it is clear Shanahan is one of the best in the NFL.
“When you talk about the best coordinators, play designers, I mean, he's always right there,” stated Flores. “There's no conversation without him in it. And so he's one of the best.”
This will be a great test for the Vikings, but also for the 49ers. While Flores is complementary to Shanahan, he is 5-0 against Shanahan when the teams have faced off.
Flores is 2-0 against the 49ers as the Vikings defensive coordinator. He beat Shanahan once when he was the Miami Dolphins head coach. Flores was with the New England Patriots when Shanahan lost to him as the Falcons play caller in the Super Bowl. Then, New England beat Shanahan and the Washington Commanders once.
