title: Exclusive: How 49ers TE George Kittle's Positive Mindset Helped Him Through Achilles Rehab
full_text:
San Francisco 49ers tight end George Kittle's biggest strength is his infectious energy and unwavering drive to strive for excellence in everything he does.
It's no surprise that this mindset has helped him become the franchise's all-time leader in touchdowns among tight ends.
However, the highs of Kittle's career were met with a significant setback during the offseason, as his life changed drastically after he suffered a torn Achilles in the NFC Wild Card game against the Philadelphia Eagles.
Yet despite the adversity of his biggest injury setback so far, Kittle recalled that his unwavering positive energy kept him going throughout the offseason, always keeping Week 1 in sight.
"Yes, my life definitely changed," admitted Kittle to 49ers on SI's Henry Cheal.
"My off-seasons have been pretty consistent for the last ten years. I had another surgery after the 2023 season, but that was fairly straightforward and the rehabilitation process didn't take too long.
"This time, my goal throughout the entire process was simply to get back out there for Week 1.
"When I spoke to my surgeon, even before the surgery, he told me, 'Hey, you have a chance.' And I said, 'That's all I need. Just tell me I have a chance.'
"You don't really have to do much to motivate me. I'm a pretty motivated person every single day when I wake up. I love life, I play football for a living, and I don't have a lot to complain about. I'm pretty excited to get up every single day.
"I think that mindset was one of the things that allowed me to get back because every day of rehabilitation was enjoyable for me. Yes, it was meticulous and incredibly boring at times, but overall, I thoroughly enjoyed it.
"I will say that my off-season didn't change as much as I thought it was going to. With an Achilles injury, you don't necessarily need someone working on you every single day.
"For example, if you have a knee injury, you might need people stretching your knee and working on your legs every day. With my injury, I was able to do a lot of the first eight weeks of rehabilitation by myself.
"That meant I could still go on holiday with my wife and enjoy myself, which I thought was important for my mental health. You don't want to spend every single day in the same building doing the same thing over and over again. I think that would have driven me mad!
"Overall, I think having a very, very positive mindset can take you a long way."
Kittle subsequently made his return to the field for the season opener in Melbourne in Week 1. Since then, he has recorded 557 receiving yards and five touchdowns, performing as though the Achilles injury had never happened .
Sometimes, motivation can be found in the lowest moments, and Kittle made sure to use that adversity as fuel.

title: 49ers FB Kyle Juszczyk Opens Up on How Much Longer He Wants to Play in the NFL
full_text:
The San Francisco 49ers face an intriguing decision this offseason regarding veteran fullback Kyle Juszczyk .
The 2026 season, like fellow teammate George Kittle, marks a decade with the 49ers after both joined in 2017.
Juszczyk is 35 right now, and after hitting free agency momentarily in March 2025, he signed a two-year contract, which means he will become an unrestricted free agent heading into 2027.
The noticeable achievement of playing for San Francisco can't be ignored. A decade with one team deserves all the praise. That said, considering that half of the regular-season games have been played, there's been no talk or speculation about an extension.
When asked by NBC Sports Bay Area about setting a goal on how much longer he wants to play in the NFL, Juszczyk shared: "I don't. It's so hard to put a number on it.
"I was having this conversation with Fred Warner the other day. It's easy to say you've got a few more years left. What's difficult is when you're looking at that final year.
"I've been saying I've got a few more years for a long time. That's what I told Fred because he said he couldn't imagine what it would be like playing for 15 years.
"I told him that he might say that now, but it's easy to say you've got a few more years when you're not looking at the final one. When you're thinking, 'This is my last year,' it's not easy to pull the trigger and say you're done.
"That's kind of where I feel like I am right now. I'm just going to keep saying I've got a few more years because I can't say this is my last season. I don't want to say next year will be my last year, either. It's easier to keep pushing that decision down the line a little bit."
Regardless of how long he's around for, whether Juszczyk stays or goes will be a major talking point in the offseason. What will his valuation be? What will the 49ers decide to do? He also recently said he's a "fullback when it comes to contract negotiations" while calling himself a tight end.
There are arguments to be made on both sides, but it remains a fascinating situation for the 49ers to think about. Juszczyk's experience, versatility and importance within the locker room will all factor into the decision, making his future one to watch closely as the offseason approaches.

title: Why Kyle Shanahan Sees Christian McCaffrey as a 'Perfect Mentor' for 49ers' Kaelon Black
full_text:
If one aspect of the San Francisco 49ers deserves praise this year, it's their running back coaching .
Christian McCaffrey's reduced workload has played a massive part in that. The 49ers kept their word throughout the offseason, and rookie Kaelon Black is already proving to be a valuable addition in easing the burden, albeit only some of the time .
The two running backs are producing at an identical rate, averaging 4.5 yards per carry. McCaffrey has naturally (and unsurprisingly) had more opportunities, accumulating 519 rushing yards from 115 carries, while Black has managed 356 yards on 79 attempts.
Black has now spent half a season learning from McCaffrey. There are few better running backs in the league to learn from. McCaffrey is not only an excellent runner but also a reliable receiver who offers plenty in the passing game. His 1,000-1,000 yard season says enough.
With injuries to offensive weapons becoming a frequent occurrence in 2025 and this season, McCaffrey's importance to the 49ers has only increased. He led the team in both rushing and receiving last season and currently ranks second in receiving behind George Kittle.
“I think Christian’s the perfect mentor just because even if he doesn’t say anything, just how Christian works every second. Christian’s the most detailed, focused, obsessive player I’ve ever been around," shared head coach Kyle Shanahan on Monday .
"Just watch how he blocks when Deebo’s [Samuel Sr.] running back and he’s playing receiver and just the technique and the effort he goes through on every single play.
"Just the way Christian plays football is the best example or mentor to anybody who’s on our team or anybody who wants to watch how a football player goes about his business. I also think Christian really respects Kaelon.
"I remember Christian telling me right when he got here how much of a pro that guy seemed like and seemed like he was made of the right stuff.
"It’s because K.B., similar to Christian, he works at everything. He’s very hard on himself. He’s very tough and approaches each day to get better. As talents and as people, I think they pair together very well.”
This could prove particularly valuable for San Francisco in the long run. McCaffrey won't be able to maintain his current level forever, but Black showing similar traits gives the 49ers another reason to be encouraged about their future at running back.
Black has made a notable impact in several games, but his performance against the Dallas Cowboys saw a big step in his development.

title: Why 49ers LT Trent Williams Could Play in the NFL in His 40s
full_text:
San Francisco 49ers left tackle Trent Williams has teased retirement at the end of 2027, but has now stated he could play for even longer.
Back in April, Williams signed a two-year contract extension, meaning he will be 39 upon expiration.
He's previously said he's open to playing until he's 40 , but he's also hinted that the contract he signed could be his last due to understandable family reasons. Nobody knows what he'll ultimately decide, of course, but his recent interview could suggest that he's considering playing well into his 40s.
“I’m a huge competitor. This game has changed my life in so many ways and I just can’t find a reason to let it go," Williams shared on Bay Area Radio Station KNBR .
"I know the accolades and everything is fine, me being 38 years old is fine, but I still have a passion to play this game. I think I’ve been supremely blessed to be able to have the ability and the mindset to take me deep into my career to where I still want more.
"It’s an obsession of mine. Football is one of the things I dream about. I wake up thinking about it. I go to sleep thinking about it.
"If I still have the ability to put what I think is good productive play on film, it’ll be hard for me to look at my teammates in the face and hang my cleats up. As long as I feel that god gives me the grace to get out there and be the player I know I can be, I’m gonna be lacing them up.”
Realistically, Williams has all the leverage if he continues to produce at a high level. He's still one of the best players in the league at his position.
Whether that means continuing with the 49ers or elsewhere, nobody truly knows. What's certain is that San Francisco needs him right now. He's ranked second among tackles in the league by PFF with a 90.1 overall grade, second in pass-blocking grade with an 87.8, and fifth in overall grade with an 84.9.
Stats like these, especially when considering Williams' age, show that at 38, he continues to prove he's a once-in-a-generation player whose impact cannot be overstated.
No matter what happens, his importance to San Francisco remains undeniable, and replacing a player of his caliber would be an enormous challenge for the organization when the time of his departure arrives.

title: Kyle Shanahan Explains 49ers Tough Nate Hobbs Decision
full_text:
The San Francisco 49ers did not activate cornerback Nate Hobbs from the IR despite returning to practice for a second week. Head coach Kyle Shanahan made it clear that the decision was purely roster-related. They thought that Renardo Green and Deommodore Lenoir were healthy enough to get through the game. On top of that, they liked Ephesians Prysock as their backup over Hobbs.
"Because we thought those two gave us the best chance to win," said Shanahan on why he did not decide to activate Hobbs.
When asked if the team would activate Hobbs this week, Shanahan made it clear that it would have nothing to do with his ability or health. It would be more of a decision about roster numbers.
"I'm not sure,” said Shanahan on Monday after the game. “It's Monday, so we've got to see how it goes. You've always got to cut someone to activate someone too, so we've got to see how everyone is. But he's looked good these last two weeks. I know he's chomping at the bit to get back out there and won't hesitate to do it if that makes sense for our 53."
The 49ers have until November 25th to activate Hobbs. So, they can let him sit for one more week, but they would have to quickly make a move before Week 12 to activate him and release a player from their roster.
San Francisco is thin on the defensive line and at cornerback. However, both Nate Hobbs and C.J. West are expected to return to the lineup soon. The team could release Khalil Kareem as one of the corresponding moves. However, the other move that they would make is tough .
If San Francisco likes Prysock over Hobbs, and Siran Neal is their best special teams asset, there is no defined role for Hobbs on the roster. They would add him to the roster and make him a healthy scratch in his first game back.
Still, they have to activate him. They are not the team to let a healthy player be lost for the season because of too much depth. Green and Lenoir are still working through injuries, and Prysock is still unknown. It helps that they trust Prysock right now and do not have to force Hobbs onto the roster.
However, the move is going to have to come soon. We will see who gets released.

title: Buccaneers Know They Must Stop This Lions Star
full_text:
Alex Anzalone knows a thing or two about the Detroit Lions.
Before joining the Tampa Bay Buccaneers in the 2026 off-season, Anzalone played with the Lions from 2021-25 and achieved a good amount of success there while also being a team captain for multiple seasons.
He is also not the only transplant from Detroit, as fellow Buccaneer Al-Quadin Muhammad also joined the Bucs this offseason and was with the Lions from 2024 to 2025.
Both of these players know what the Lions are capable of, especially on the offensive side of the ball as they faced the Lions' stars every day for multiple years. One major player they are going to have to keep an eye on in this upcoming game is Jahmyr Gibbs.
Gibbs has already had a fantastic season for the Lions, reaching 1,000 rushing yards through only nine games and also posting 11 rushing touchdowns, 384 receiving yards and two receiving touchdowns as well. He may very well be the best running back in the entire NFL and is a surefire candidate for Offensive Player of the Year
Anzalone has a simple answer when asked to describe Gibbs and players like him.
"In the league, when you play against players like this, I call them Aliens," Anzalone said. "They're from a different planet, and you have to play them differently... Gibbs is obviously one of them, and he's proven that."
Thankfully for the Bucs, the defense has been playing very well as of late in terms of getting turnovers and has been especially good at stopping the run this season.
Right now, the Bucs have the No. 1 rushing defense in the NFL in terms of yards allowed and are also first in the NFL in rushing touchdowns allowed. However, it is important to note that teams have not tried to run against the Bucs much this season, as they are second-to-last in rushing attempts against their defense.
The biggest concern that could be Gibbs' receiving ability. Both Anzalone and Trotter have struggled in moments with coverage this year, but have been doing much better in recent weeks.
If the Buccaneers are able to slow down Gibbs and really take control of the game as they were able to do in games against the Carolina Panthers and Atlanta Falcons with good defense, they could get their biggest win of the season to date.

title: Buccaneers Get Good News and Bad News After Bye Week
full_text:
Despite the fact that the Tampa Bay Buccaneers are a disappointing 3-6 on the season, in addition to being one full game outside of first place in the NFC South, there are still positives to be found regarding the team's outlook for the remainder of the regular season.
Most notable among those positives is the Buccaneers' remaining strength of schedule, which is widely considered to be the easiest in the NFL after what was a difficult first half of the year. The other is that, despite their struggles, the Bucs remain undefeated in division games (2-0) on the season with four NFC South games still remaining.
Despite the potential that somehow still exists for the Buccaneers to go on a run and make the postseason, a few things will need to go right. And right now, one of the main things is the injury front.
As it stands right now, the Buccaneers have several key players dealing with injuries, which could threaten their availability for this Sunday's matchup against the Lions in Detroit.
Despite exiting last week's game vs. the Bears due to a knee injury, OLB Yaya Diaby appears to be trending in the right direction to play on Sunday.
First practice back from the bye — Antoine Winfield Jr. and Baker Mayfield didn’t practice, but Yaya Diaby IS practicing.
After practice, Bowles confirmed that Diaby is "trending in the right direction", which is a big boost to a defense that has played like one of the best in the league over the past month or so. The Bucs will need all of the defensive reinforcements they can get in order to slow down the Lions' explosive offense.
Another piece of good news coming out of Tampa today is that All-Pro LT Tristan Wirfs was also at practice. Although Wirfs didn't necessarily sustain a significant injury, as far as we know, he was seen limping off the field after the team's tough loss in Chicago.
Not only was star safety Antoine Winfield Jr. not seen at practice on Wednesday, but Bowles cast some serious doubt on Winfield's availability for this game in Detroit when he spoke to the media after practice.
Todd Bowles says that Yaya Diaby is “trending in the right direction.” Antoine Winfield Jr. is “very sore right now” and Bowles didn’t seem as optimistic about his chances this Sunday
Winfield left the game vs. Chicago when he injured his ankle trying to make a tackle and he did not return. Although the Bucs' defense looked excellent as the game went on even without Winfield in the lineup, his presence is still essential for Bowles' defense to function at full capacity.
Trying to limit the impact of players like Amon-Ra St. Brown, Sam LaPorta, Jahmyr Gibbs and Jameson Williams will be that much more challenging without Winfield on the field than it would be if he were to suit up for this game.
When the Bucs promoted QB Easton Stick to the 53-man roster and signed Cooper Rush to the practice squad, it was an obvious sign that Baker Mayfield's status was in serious doubt for this contest. Mayfield took a number of big hits last Sunday night in Chicago, and he was hobbling around most of the night with a foot injury.
Although we haven't got much specific info about the nature of the injury, those moves did not inspire much confidence in the belief that Mayfield would be healthy enough to start this weekend.
That being said, Bowles was not ready to not rule Mayfield out for this game after Wednesday's practice.
"He's made a lot of progress," Bowles said. "We want to see him do some things later on today and tomorrow and kind of make that determination on Friday, but he's a lot better than he was a week ago. I don't know if that's ready or not, I want to see it myself, and we'll see what he can do tomorrow."
Any time a starting quarterback is hurt, it can't be good news for the team. That being said, the fact that a glimmer of hope still exists for Mayfield to play this weekend is worth taking note of.
Regardless of whether Mayfield suits up on Sunday in Detroit or not, the Buccaneers will need to have as many healthy players on the field as possible in order to upset a very talented Lions team.

title: What We Saw From Baker Mayfield at Buccaneers Practice and What it Means
full_text:
The Tampa Bay Buccaneers are 3-6 and still treading water as they look to make the playoffs. They're a game out of the division lead, but every game is crucial from here on out — and they have what may be their toughest game of the year on Sunday.
The Bucs are set to play the Detroit Lions on the road in Week 11. The Lions are 7-2 and boast one of the best offenses in football, and the Bucs will have to keep up on both sides of the ball to pull off the upset and get the win.
Their best shot at doing that would be with their starting quarterback, Baker Mayfield. But Mayfield is dealing with an ankle injury he picked up against the Chicago Bears, and his status for Week 11 heading into this week has been up in the air.
Here's the latest report on Mayfield's status, combined with what we saw from him at One Buccaneer Place on Wednesday:
ESPN insider Jeremy Fowler reported Wednesday morning that Mayfield is a "long shot" to play against the Lions, but that he's more likely than not to play against the Carolina Panthers in Week 12's divisional game.
"From my understanding, the Bucs know Mayfield is probably a long shot for this week but also know Mayfield will push to get ready and play, so they aren't ruling out the possibility," Fowler wrote . "There's more optimism about next week's matchup with Carolina, a crucial divisional game."
Wednesday's practice seemed to corroborate that. Mayfield did appear at toward the end of practice, but he was a non-participant. He did not appear to be in a walking boot, however, which is a good sign for the long-term status of his injury as the Bucs head into a crucial set of games.
First practice back from the bye — Antoine Winfield Jr. and Baker Mayfield didn’t practice, but Yaya Diaby IS practicing.
If it were to lean one way, it doesn't seem like Mayfield will play. The Buccaneers have already moved quarterback availability to Thursday as opposed to the usual Wednesday, and if Mayfield didn't practice at all on Wednesday, he's unlikely to rally and start against the Lions on Sunday.
Should Mayfield be unable to play, the Bucs would turn to Jalon Daniels, who has already started three games for the team. In his three starts, Daniels is 1-2 with three touchdowns and five interceptions. Mayfield himself is 2-4 as a starter in Tampa Bay this year, throwing three touchdowns and four interceptions.
The Bucs will face the Lions at Ford Field in Detroit at 1 p.m. It will be a tough task, but from here on out, every game is crucial for this Bucs squad.

title: The Craziest Buccaneers Stats Through the First Half of the Season
full_text:
The Tampa Bay Buccaneers have had a season of ups and downs (mostly downs). They're 3-6 and have the worst passing offense in football, but they're just a game out of the NFC South, have an elite defense and boast an impressive running game.
The Bucs are, in many ways, a statistical enigma — it's hard to tell whether they are much better than their record or right where they're supposed to be. We've collected a few stats that make the Bucs a bizarre football team throughout their first nine games of the season.
The Buccaneers have the best rushing offense in the NFL (163.9 rushing yards per game) and the very worst passing offense in the NFL (141.9 net passing yards per game). They also have more rushing yards than passing yards at this stage of the year — not great.
The Bucs have to find ways to throw the football if they want to win games. They can really lean on the run game (and have in all of their wins), but the passing game has failed them in more ways than one.
Bucs kicker Chase McLaughlin has yet to miss a kick in any capacity. He's a pristine 22-for-22 on field goal attempts and he's 18-for-18 on extra point attempts. He's also Tampa Bay's leading scorer, currently accounting for 84 points.
We don't mean to jinx him, but McLaughlin could be on his way to a historic season. Three NFL kickers in history — Gary Anderson, Jeff Wilkins and Mike Vanderjagt — have had a perfect kicking season during the regular season.
Only Vanderjagt has had a perfect season through the regular season and the playoffs. The Bucs would have to make it to the playoffs for McLaughlin to test out that record, too.
The Buccaneers are 3-6 and one of the worst teams in the NFL by record (and most of the others are also in the NFC South). Despite that record, though, the team has a positive point differential of +24 points. That's the 11th-best number in the NFL.
Every team ahead of Tampa Bay has won six or more games. The Bucs have lost every single one of their games by one score, and two of those losses were by three points.
Tampa Bay has had a blowout against the Panthers to help increase that number, and holding the Atlanta Falcons to zero points the week after helped their differential, too. But two things seem to be for certain — the Buccaneers find themselves in close games a lot, and they have a lot of trouble actually winning them.
The Bucs have been doing this for the past few years now, but they seem to play better on the road than they do at home.
The Bucs are 2-2 on the road this year, but they're just 1-4 when playing at Raymond James Stadium. Their average points scored across those splits is also fairly interesting — they average 16.8 points per game on the road and 29.5 on the road.
The team's win over the Panthers is a bit of an outlier, by either way, the Bucs seem more comfortable on the road. Thankfully, they'll be heading to Detroit to play the Lions next Sunday at 1 p.m.

title: Chris Godwin is Costing the Buccaneers $85,000 Per Yard Right Now
full_text:
The Tampa Bay Buccaneers passing attack has been their weakness this season.
The Bucs currently own the NFL's worst passing game in the league, having not even thrown for over 1,500 yards at the midway point of the season and not a single wide receiver eclipsing the 300-yard mark.
It hasn't been pretty, and for one wideout in particular, it's starting to look even worse thanks to how much money he is making.
Former Pro Bowl wide receiver Chris Godwin signed a contract extension with the Bucs before the start of the 2025 season for three years, worth $66 million. The $22 million per year was enough to keep him in Tampa Bay rather than seeing him walk to a team like the New England Patriots.
But now, just a year and a half into that deal, it's looking like a massive overpay.
Godwin has never looked quite right after dislocating his ankle in 2024, and his stats mirror that sentiment.
Last season, Godwin had the lowest receiving yardage total of his career with just 360 yards. He also only saw action in nine games as he dealt with rehab and injuries, and he only found the end zone twice.
Now, Godwin, who has already seen as much action as he did all of 2025, is set to have yet another down season. Godwin has only mustered 29 catches for 259 yards and no touchdowns.
That means that he is currently earning nearly $85,000 per yard in annual cash compensation. That is not a great return on your value or investment. If you account for his actual salary cap hit, that number gets higher at $130,050 per yard.
It's highly unlikely that a magic wand is waved and the Bucs' passing game improves enough for Godwin's contract to be worth it. That means the Bucs' front office should be looking at alternatives this offseason.
Godwin's team option, $20.7 million, is in 2027. However, the Bucs do have a potential out once the 2026 season concludes if they decide to cut bait with the aging wideout.
If Tampa Bay decides to cut Godwin outright before June 1, they would not only save the $22 million he is owed in salary, but they would also save approximately $13.7 million in cap space with his dead money coming way down.
There are always options on the table, however. Godwin and the Bucs could decide to meet for him to take a massive pay cut to stay with the team until his contract runs out — see Jamel Dean just last year — before he hits free agency.
They also could come together on a trade that could net them draft capital this offseason, but this scenario seems highly unlikely as they should have traded him beforehand if they were to go that route.

title: Why Wide Receiver is the Buccaneers' Biggest Need
full_text:
The Tampa Bay Buccaneers have plenty of areas to look at fixing this offseason when the regular season wraps up.
The Bucs are 3-6 at the moment, and if that gets worse, head coach may be an area the Bucs try to improve on after five years of Todd Bowles. The team could also serve to shore up its interior offensive line, and tight end will definitely be a point of consideration.
There's one area that may be the most crucial for Tampa Bay, though. And unfortunately for the Bucs, they've spent a lot of draft capital investing in that position very, very recently.
There are a lot of problems with Tampa Bay's offense. Bucs' offensive coordinator Zac Robinson is having some trouble scheming up the passing game, and quarterback Baker Mayfield is having some trouble executing that already-poor scheme.
Those are all parts of it. But the Bucs need wide receivers desperately because, right now, the lack of talent in that room is a big reason why the passing game has faltered the way it has.
Wideout Jalen McMillan is injured and has been since Week 2 of the NFL season. In his absence, the Bucs have rolled with three main wideouts — Emeka Egbuka, Chris Godwin and Tez Johnson. Neither of those receivers have over 300 yards at the moment, with Egbuka leading the pack at just 278.
Godwin is on a three-year, $22 million deal, and his age has shown itself over the past two seasons. Johnson has been good in spurts, but he doesn't have the skill set to be a main target in Tampa Bay, and he isn't big enough to be a viable threat between the hashes that the Bucs desperately need at the moment.
Finally, there are the two players the team drafted over the last two years. Egbuka was supposed to be a future WR1 for this team when he was drafted in the first round of the 2025 NFL Draft, but he hasn't looked the part at all from the back half of last season through this one. He lacks physicality at the catch point, struggles with getting separation and has been battling injury frequently this year.
The Bucs also drafted wideout Ted Hurst in the third round of this year's NFL Draft, and while it's very early, he hasn't made much of an impact this year. He's dropped two passes that could have been touchdowns, and his drop problem was bad enough against the Chicago Bears that he got benched early in the game.
The Bucs are 3-6 right now. It's unknown exactly where they are going to pick in the 2026 NFL Draft, but they should definitely be looking for help at wideout. They need a receiver who can open up the middle of the field for them and be able to get separation through either their speed or their route-running acumen — the Bucs have neither on the squad right now.
Tampa Bay plays the Detroit Lions at 1 p.m. on the road Sunday.

title: What the Buccaneers Signing Cooper Rush Really Means
full_text:
The Tampa Bay Buccaneers added to their quarterback room on Monday, signing quarterback Cooper Rush to their practice squad. The move would have been very strange just a few days ago, but new information puts the move into perspective.
Rush comes to the Buccaneers after a new report about starting quarterback Baker Mayfield. Mayfield is reportedly dealing with an injured leg and ankle, and his status against the Detroit Lions is uncertain.
Rush's signing might reveal more about that uncertainty, though, and it may not be good for the Bucs.
Rush signing with the Bucs at all makes it more unlikely than not that Mayfield plays against the Lions.
The Bucs would need an emergency third quarterback on the practice squad should Mayfield be out, and Rush would serve that role. He has no prior experience with any Bucs coaches, but he is a veteran who has started two games in the NFC South so far this season.
The Bucs would probably have turned to quarterback Brett Rypien for this, but Rypien signed with the Raiders' practice squad before they pursued Rush.
Additionally, Tampa Bay's previous practice squad quarterback, Easton Stick, was elevated to the 53-man roster on Monday after hitting the limit for three elevations, which he accrued while backup Jalon Daniels filled in for Mayfield when Mayfield dislocated his thumb in Week 3.
Rush's signing — and Stick's elevation — seem to mean that the Bucs are seriously worried Mayfield will not play in Week 11 against the Detroit Lions, if they aren't absolutely certain of it by now. Should that be the case, Daniels would serve as QB1, Stick would back him up as QB2 and Rush would only enter the game in an emergency as the team's emergency QB3, which all teams are allowed to have on game day.
The Bucs will face off against the Lions in Detroit at 1 p.m. on Sunday. Rush's arrival seems to indicate that Daniels, an undrafted free agent rookie, will take the helm of the offense once again.

title: One Buccaneers Rookie Is Making a Lot of People Look Wrong
full_text:
The Tampa Bay Buccaneers drafted linebacker Josiah Trotter early in the second round of the 2026 NFL Draft with the expectation that he would contribute to a unit that had declined drastically over the years.
Like any rookie entering the league, there were plenty of red flags around him. His coverage, particularly in space when matched up with running backs and tight ends, was horrendous, and his passion for the game would sometimes cause over-aggressiveness, which would then lead to missed tackles.
While he still has his moments, Trotter has quickly taken himself from a rotational linebacker in Todd Bowles' defensive scheme to a three-down starter, shutting up those who doubted him or thought he was drafted too early.
Trotter has played extremely well for a rookie alongside Alex Anzalone, and he has been a key piece in the defensive turnaround this season.
Trotter's biggest strength has been the ability to fill gaps in the running lanes, and he is tied for 17th overall in the NFL in total tackles with 76. He is fifth among all rookie linebackers in tackles, trailing Anthony Hill Jr. (82), Arvell Reese (81), Jacob Rodriguez (80), and Sonny Styles (80) — all of whom have a game or two in hand on Trotter.
Trotter also has three passes defended, three tackles for loss, one quarterback hit, one sack and an interception that he took back for a touchdown — the only rookie defender in the league with a pick-six this season.
His run defense grade of 72.9, per Pro Football Focus, nets him as the 19th best out of 80 qualifying linebackers, only trailing Jaishawn Barham and Rodriguez amongst rookie linebacker run-stop rates.
Trotter has also been excellent when rushing the passer, grading out 22nd among 80 qualifying at his position (70.5). Bowles has found something in Trotter's instincts for seeing the ball and getting the ball, which has also led to him generating multiple pressures.
While Trotter has silenced his critics with improvement in his run defense, pass rushing, and tackling efficiency — just a 6.2% missed tackle rate on the year — he still has tons of room for improvement when it comes to coverage.
Even though Trotter has improved this area of his game since his time in college with Missouri, there is plenty of room to get better. His 53.8 coverage grade places him 54th out of the 80 qualifying linebackers, allowing 18 completions on 27 targets for 146 yards (5.4 yards per target) and a 74 passer rating against him.
Trotter has an extremely bright future ahead of him, but if he wants to throw his name in the hat as one of the best pure linebackers in the game, he must brush up on his ability to cover in the passing game while continuing to be a ball hawk against the run and when rushing the QB.

title: Bucs Sign Veteran QB After Concerning Baker Mayfield Injury News
full_text:
The Tampa Bay Buccaneers entered the offseason this year with a quarterback room of Baker Mayfield, Jalon Daniels, Connor Bazelak and Jake Browning. Since then, things have changed significantly.
Both Bazelak and Browning were cut at the beginning of the season. That made way for Easton Stick to join the Buccaneers' practice squad, and when Mayfield dislocated his thumb and was out for three weeks, Brett Rypien also joined the team while Daniels started and Stick was elevated to the active roster, and he was then released on Oct. 27.
Now, though, Mayfield appears to have picked up another injury. Because of that, the Buccaneers are bringing on yet another quarterback to the practice squad, and he's already started football games in the NFC South this season.
ESPN's Adam Schefter reported on Monday that former Atlanta Falcons quarterback Cooper Rush was signing to the Tampa Bay Buccaneers' practice squad.
Rush has started two games this season for the Falcons. He threw for 229 yards, one touchdown and four interceptions with a total QBR of 4.3 across both of those games — naturally, with a statline like that, he was released by the Falcons on Oct. 19.
He comes to Tampa Bay after Rypien's departure and during a time where Mayfield is dealing with another injury. He picked up a leg injury against the Chicago Bears, and he's reportedly been in and out of a walking boot during the bye week.
This move would indicate that the team is genuinely preparing for Mayfield to be out. The Bucs have Stick and Rush at their disposal if Jalon Daniels were to start against the Detroit Lions on Sunday.
Stick has already been elevated from the practice squad three times since Mayfield was injured the first time. Were the Bucs to elevate him a fourth time, they would have to sign him to the active roster, so it would be interesting to see how they approach who backs up Daniels between Rush and Stick.
The Bucs play the Lions at 1 p.m. on Sunday in Detroit. Who will be their starting quarterback, and who will be that starting quarterback's backup, remains to be seen.

title: Buccaneers' Week 12 Game Just Became Even More Important
full_text:
The Tampa Bay Buccaneers got to rest and recuperate during their bye week, but now, they have to get back to work and try to win the NFC South.
The NFC South race is quite close. And while the Bucs won't play a division game right off the bye — they have to contend with the Detroit Lions first — they'll play a division game the week after in Week 12 that could now be the most important game of their entire season.
The Bucs started the bye week half a game back of the Carolina Panthers, and after this week's Sunday slate, the Panthers are still Tampa Bay's main roadblock.
The Carolina Panthers beat the New Orleans Saints 20-17 on Sunday, moving to 4-5. As a result, the Panthers and the Bucs have now played the same amount of games, so Tampa Bay is one game back of the Panthers for the division.
The Bucs beat the Panthers once already in Week 7 in dominant fashion, winning 43-13 in Charlotte. That could give them the upper hand in any tiebreaker scenarios to come, but Tampa Bay will want to win both games against Carolina to be absolutely sure — and they have the chance to do that in two weeks.
The Bucs play the Panthers in Week 12 on Monday Night Football, and that could very well be for the division lead. The Bucs have to play the Lions first, though, and the Panthers will play the Baltimore Ravens at home in Week 11.
If the Bucs win and the Panthers lose in Week 11, they'd have the same record heading into that matchup. If the Bucs win and the Panthers win in Week 11, the Bucs would be one game back with the chance of evening their records and securing a tiebreaker, and if the Bucs lose and the Panthers win in Week 11, the Bucs would be two games back and would desperately need to beat Carolina.
No matter how it's stacked up, this Week 12 game is crucial. But before that, the Bucs will head to Detroit to play the Lions at 1 p.m. next Sunday.

title: Why All Signs Point to Tony Pollard’s Revenge Game vs. Cowboys Leading to a Titans Win
full_text:
On Sept. 8, 2019, a 22-year-old rookie from Memphis, Tennessee made his NFL dreams come true, debuting in his first career game under the bright lights of the iconic AT&T Stadium. A Week 1 rivalry battle between the New York Giants and Dallas Cowboys finished with a dominant 35-17 home win, and the rookie recorded 13 carries for 24 yards.
Now, more than seven years later as a member of the Tennessee Titans, RB Tony Pollard returns to Arlington, where his NFL career began.
Prior to returning to his home state in 2023, Pollard played his first five NFL seasons as a Dallas Cowboy. In the navy and silver, he blossomed from RB Ezekiel Elliott's backup to taking over the starting position and earning a Pro Bowl nod in 2022.
In Pollard's half-decade tenure with the Cowboys, he had three 1,000-yard rushing seasons and led Dallas in rushing twice.
Dallas with Pollard made the playoffs three consecutive years from 2021 to 2023, including a monstrous 31-17 victory over the Tampa Bay Buccaneers on the road in the Wild Card, which was the final game of QB Tom Brady's unprecedented career. Since his departure, the Cowboys haven't won a playoff game again.
On Sunday, Pollard will face his former team, who are desperate for a win, for the first time as a Titan.
Over the previous few weeks, the former Cowboy has had an unbelievable resurgence for a running back in his age 29 season.
Since Week 7, Pollard leads all running backs with five rushing touchdowns and is tied for the most 20-plus yard rushes. Furthermore, he ranks in the top-10 for running backs in rushing and receiving yards and receiving touchdowns, according to Fantasy Pros .
It's important to note that Pollard didn't play Week 9 due to Tennessee's bye, and his stats are being compared to running backs who have played one more game than him in that stretch.
Across his last three games against Cleveland, Cincinnati and Jacksonville, Pollard is averaging 130 yards from scrimmage and two touchdowns per game. Pollard became the first Titan to record at least 390 yards from scrimmage and six touchdowns in a three-game stretch since future Hall of Famer RB Derrick Henry in December 2018 .
Pollard has been the backbone of an improving Tennessee offense . The Titans were averaging a league-low 11.6 points per game, which has improved to a ninth-best 25.5 since Week 6.
The Cowboys' defense has been heavily scrutinized, especially after a falling out with future Hall of Fame talent EDGE Micah Parsons that led to a franchise-altering trade with the Green Bay Packers. Dallas hoped to make a strong push for the playoffs after spending big in the offseason to improve their weak defense.
However, they're is in second place in the NFC East with a middling 4-6 record, trailing the New York Giants, who have a 5-3-1 record despite losing their starting quarterback for the season in Week 2. A loss to Tennessee would be devastating for their playoff hopes, especially if the Giants defeat Jacksonville on Sunday.
The Cowboys have scored the second-most points this season with 286 while allowing 282 points, which is the third-most in the NFL. Dallas has a near one-to-one scoring-to-points allowed ratio.
Pollard will be the focal point of the Titans' offensive attack on a Cowboys defense that allows 154.1 rushing yards per game and 5.2 yards per carry, which are both league worsts, according to Team Rankings.
Over the last three weeks, Pollard has averaged more than 4.8 yards per carry and 93 rushing per game. Tennessee has been giving the starting back a workhorse role all season, preparing him for a perfect matchup like this one against Dallas.
When facing a fellow bottom-10 run defense in yards per rush and yards per game, Pollard dominated with 117 yards on the ground and two rushing touchdowns on 5.6 yards per carry against the Bengals.
On Wednesday, news broke that the Cowboys defensive coordinator Christian Parker has been removed from play-calling duties in favor of senior defensive assistant Mike Pettine.
The Cowboys' defensive struggles this season could lead to a high-scoring dogfight with an improving Tennessee offense led by a charging Pollard. Tennessee has a legit chance of upsetting the Cowboys, who are 1-4 at home this year, and it all ties back to the latter's former RB.
Isaiah is an award-winning journalist and photojournalist. A graduate from the University of Kentucky, he has previously been published by BloodHorse, KY Insider, and the Kentucky Kernel for multimedia sports coverage. Isaiah is a Tennessee Volunteer at heart bringing his local expertise to Titans coverage.

title: Why the Titans Will Beat the Cowboys in Week 11, Why They Won't, and a Prediction
full_text:
The Titans just lost their eighth game in nine tries, but there's a lot to like about where Tennessee stands right now.
Between deadline trades that added strength to the franchise's rebuild and promising development from young players across the board, the Robert Saleh era is slowly building into something fans can get behind.
In Week 11, his Titans team has a chance to win their second game of the season on the road vs. the Dallas Cowboys. Here's one reason they'll get it done, one reason they'll fall short, and my own prediction for how things will ultimately pan out.
The Cowboys, after allowing 46 points to the San Francisco 49ers in a loss last week, just turned over defensive play-calling duties to senior assistant coach Mike Pettine. Dallas' defense is struggling, and if the Titans win, it'll be because Cam Ward and Tony Pollard take advantage of that.
Ward has been on a short tear as of late, doubling his touchdown total through seven games in the last two. The second-season QB has also eclipsed 200 yards in back-to-back games for the first time this year. With WR Carnell Tate likely to return, Ward is tracking for another leap.
On the ground, meanwhile, the Cowboys' rushing defense is last in the league in yards allowed per game (154.1) and yards per carry (5.2). This marks Pollard's first game against his former team; the numbers are supportive, and the stakes are there.
The Titans' offense has simply been on a team-wide heater as of late. It'll take another inspired performance from key playmakers to pull it off, but Tennessee has a clear angle to a road win.
However, Tennessee's defense has been trending in the opposite direction. As has been the case in the past two weeks, Saleh's bunch have mostly erased positive offensive momentum and cost the Titans' two chances at winnable games.
If Tennessee were to fall short in Week 11, I have to think it would be for the same reason.
As Saleh himself said after the team's latest loss, you aren't going to win allowing 40 points a game. The Titans' previous two opponents have crossed the 40 mark, and Dallas, in spite of their loss, score as much against a better 49ers defense this past week.
Dallas is a veteran-led group in the middle of a difficult year; their down season can't be compared to that of the Titans, and QB Dak Prescott is sure to run this defense through the ringer. On the road after arguably their worst showing of the year, Saleh's defense has their back against the wall.
With that said, I still think the Titans find a way to pull this one out. If the away team can strike a balance between their growing offensive attack and a defense that isn't allowing Dallas to do whatever they want, a close win is in the cards.
The Titans have yet to play a full, complete game this year. Even their Week 6 victory over the Indianapolis Colts saw Tennessee trailing 13-0 at halftime. I'm predicting that the Titans get this done, and do so by offering a solid showing through all four quarters.
That means a consistent Cam Ward, a defense that bends, but doesn't break, reliable play-calling on either side of the ball, and at least a little good luck on the injury front. A lot has to go right, but this game wouldn't have been seen as winnable only a few short weeks ago.
For that reason, I believe the Titans will win it.
Lane covers the Tennessee Titans, where he brings an evolving team's journey to fans on a daily basis. A longtime sports fanatic and recent baby blue jersey aficionado.

title: Cam Ward's Week 11 Outlook Just Skyrocketed Due to the Cowboys Making 1 Simple Change
full_text:
I think it's fair to say that Titans fans are feeling good about Cam Ward entering Week 11. The general outlook has changed from questioning Ward's status as the franchise QB to comfortably assuming he'll be there by the end of this year or beginning of next season.
The Dallas Cowboys provided Ward with a favorable matchup this week already, but the team deciding to make a serious personnel shift right before Tennessee travels to Arlington has taken the hype around Ward's growth to the next level.
Per Ian Rapoport, the Cowboys are handing over defensive play-calling duties to senior assistant Mike Pettine. DC Christian Parker will remain on the staff, but has been relieved of calling the plays due to a stretch of defense that head coach Brian Schottenheimer called "unacceptable."
#Cowboys senior assistant coach Mike Pettine will now take over as play-caller, so do for the first time since he was with the #Packers in 2021. Action from coach Brian Schottenheimer after a stretch of defense he called “unacceptable.” pic.twitter.com/RDXeOPMZ2G
Pettine produced some elite defenses in his early days with the New York Jets, but he hasn't called plays on that side of the ball for a reason. His last stint in such a position came with the Green Bay Packers from 2018-2021, where a defensive breakdown in the NFC title game led to the Packers choosing not to renew his deal.
Five years removed from that effort, Pettine is facing a flaming Titans offense. Dallas is looking for a refresh with the move, but now looks like the worst time.
The Cowboys just allowed 46 points to the San Francisco 49ers in a loss. FOX Sports has their defense ranked dead last in the league (just above the Titans) allowing nearly 400 total yards per game.
It makes sense why Dallas would want to try something new, and on paper, who better to do so against than the 1-8 Titans? The issue is, the Titans' record doesn't tell the full story of a team that has improved in large part due to consistent QB play.
Not only that, but Pettine isn't a hidden defensive mastermind or anything, even if his experience bodes well for Dallas. Think back to when Brian Callahan handed over offensive play-calling duties to Bo Hardegree last season for the Titans. He made the move just before Tennessee let him go.
This feels more akin to that - a desperate, deep-staff change - than something that's going to completely right the ship for the Cowboys. Entering Week 11, Titans fans should see this as a promising turn of events for Ward's climb rather than something that could put a stop to it.
Look out for a big game from Ward this coming Sunday against, hopefully, a Cowboys defense that hasn't figured out their league-worst problems in a matter of seven days.
Lane covers the Tennessee Titans, where he brings an evolving team's journey to fans on a daily basis. A longtime sports fanatic and recent baby blue jersey aficionado.

title: Titans' WR Room in for a Major Shakeup in Week 11... and That's a Good Thing
full_text:
The Tennessee Titans' injury report in Week 10 was a major factor in the team failing to mount a winning effort over the Jacksonville Jaguars; that, and the Jags were 6-2 with a runaway lead in the AFC South. Some teams are just further along.
It was already bad enough, but things got a little worse in that regard for Tennessee. The most notable news on the injury front came in the form of WR Wan'Dale Robinson being sent to IR with an ankle injury. He'll miss at least four weeks of football for Tennessee.
Robinson hasn't been great in his first year with the Titans, but he's a vet-leaning pillar in an otherwise young unit. Although, upon a closer look, that becomes the exciting part about Robinson missing time from Week 11 on.
The Titans are 1-8. They've got two first-round picks and a second-rounder ready to bolster this rebuild. Cam Ward has almost convinced Tennessee that he's the long-term guy for the job under center. What better time is there to see what your young guys have?
Not only will Elic Ayomanor and Chimere Dike get to continue in their recently-expanded roles, but rookie WR1 Carnell Tate is also tracking to return from his two-week absence.
Throw practice-squad regular and fan-favorite Xavier Restrepo into the mix, and you've got a pass-catching room comprised almost entirely of young and developing playmakers. Calvin Ridley is the lone exception, but his snap count in Week 10 doesn't inspire confidence in his involvement.
It also works out that multiple guys in that rotation are trying to prove something, to some extent, about their role in Nashville. Ayomanor came into this season behind Ridley, and has since been climbing in the rotation. Effectively the WR1 when Tate was gone, Ayomanor will look to keep pace even in his return.
Dike has seen a recent uptick in pass-catching snaps, breaking his Pro-Bowl mold as a returner. He's got seven receptions over the past two games, including a touchdown. Dike wasn't in the WR rotation really at all to begin this year, and now has a window to continue to cement himself within it.
Finally, Restrepo was just promoted to the active roster to fill in for Robinson. This is a guy who has come close so many times, including making the initial 53-man cut this season before being promptly released. The next four weeks should pose multiple opportunities for him to leave a lasting mark.
To top it all off, Ward and the Titans' offense have a favorable matchup with a middling Dallas Cowboys defense. Look for a lot of movement through the air, and potentially some movement in Tennessee's WR room too.
Lane covers the Tennessee Titans, where he brings an evolving team's journey to fans on a daily basis. A longtime sports fanatic and recent baby blue jersey aficionado.

title: Breaking Down Titans’ Injuries in Week 11: Xavier Restrepo In, Wan’Dale Robinson Out vs. Cowboys
full_text:
After falling to the Jacksonville Jaguars at home in Week 10, the Tennessee Titans will pack their bags and hit the road for AT&T Stadium to square off against the Dallas Cowboys in Week 11.
Tennessee enters Sunday's contest against Dallas with a 1-8 record, while the Cowboys are 4-6. Both teams have had disappointing seasons so far, and both will be looking to bounce back from losses. Dallas lost a close 46-40 shootout to the San Francisco 49ers this past weekend.
The Titans will return to the practice field on Wednesday to prepare for Dallas, but before then, the team made a few roster moves, including placing one of its prized free-agent additions from the spring on injured reserve.
On Tuesday, the Titans announced that wide receiver Wan'Dale Robinson is being placed on injured reserve . Robinson left Sunday's loss to the Jaguars in the third quarter with an ankle injury.
As a result, Tennessee promoted second-year receiver Xavier Restrepo to the active roster and added Jamari Thrash to the practice squad.
Robinson, who signed a lucrative four-year deal with the Titans in March, will now miss at least the next four games. However, the slot receiver's role in Brian Daboll's offense was already diminishing before he exited the game on Sunday .
Tennessee opted to give Chimere Dike more of the work at receiver than Robinson. Elic Ayomanor also out-snapped Robinson. Dike finished Week 10 with two catches for 16 yards, while Ayomanor posted five receptions for 79 yards.
Robinson has been incredibly underwhelming this year, tallying just 38 catches for 272 yards and three touchdowns. The 25-year-old hasn't been the consistent slot threat he was with the New York Giants, and we may not see him again until late December.
Restrepo played just 16 passing snaps against Jacksonville, but made the most of his opportunity by hauling in three passes for 31 yards. The Miami product is now on the active roster and should receive even more opportunities.
Depending on whether Carnell Tate returns from his shoulder injury this week, Restrepo could find himself in a starting role in Dallas this weekend. Even if he doesn't, the former undrafted free agent receiver should be an active part of the offense with Robinson out, and given his chemistry with quarterback Cam Ward, he should be able to make an impact.
These next few weeks will be critical for Restrepo and his future in Nashville. We'll see if he rises to the occasion.
Dharya Sharma is a sportswriter from Nebraska who has been covering the Tennessee Titans through his website, SharmSports, since 2023. He is also an NFL and NBA writer for The Sporting News and had a previous stop with Sportsnaut. Follow him on X @SharmSports

title: How Cam Ward, Titans' Offense are Making an Undeniable Case for Tennessee to Draft WR Jeremiah Smith
full_text:
The Tennessee Titans opened this season with demanding questions about the offense. Cam Ward looked unsteady, and Carnell Tate had a rough rookie preseason that threw his trajectory as the Titans' WR1 into doubt. Those worries lasted all the way up until Tennessee got a win in Week 6.
Then, things began to change. The Titans are 1-3 from Week 6 on, but the team's averages have changed drastically. In fact, it's Robert Saleh's defense taking the majority of the public heat, while Brian Daboll's offense has fallen somewhat into the background.
In Weeks 1-5, the Titans averaged an abysmal 11.6 points per contest. Since that turnaround against the Indianapolis Colts, in Weeks 6-10, the average has leapt to 25.5.
Tennessee's offense has been on the rise the last few weeks 📈 (via: @Ihartitz ) pic.twitter.com/oZS4mMfvaT
That's more than double, and the sample size is consistent. Ward has gotten better, and as a result, the body of the snake has too. It's a working system that, sooner rather than later, is likely to win the Titans a few games.
But if it doesn't? Well, the offense's rapid uptick is making the perfect argument for Tennessee to use their currently-held first overall pick on a generational WR talent. Jeremiah Smith is on the board, and the Titans look more ready than ever to make good on drafting him.
Ward's 4:1 touchdown-to-INT ratio in the last two contests, combined with two of his three 200+ yard games on the season, tell the story of a rising franchise QB in Nashville. Smith, a former teammate of Carnell Tate (who has turned out just fine, by the way) at Ohio State, is as promising a prospect as they come.
At 6'4", 222 lbs, Smith has the physicality you'd expect from a superstar playmaker. His 80 receptions (15 touchdowns) speak for themselves. He also holds the B1G record for receiving yards and touchdowns. Any team could make a case for drafting Smith.
No team could pair Smith with Tate, however, and with Ward developing at this rate, the signal caller also appears to be an ideal fit as someone who could grow alongside Smith. It's a blessing and a curse for Tennessee's offense to be clicking at this juncture in the season.
Robert Saleh is vying for more wins; a late-season playoff push is off the table, but the Titans can absolutely top their three-win total from the previous two seasons. Without a doubt, that would disallow drafting Smith.
We'll see what happens, but if the Titans' defense is the reason Tennessee ends up with the top pick, Smith ending up in the baby blue and white is starting to look all too convincing.
Lane covers the Tennessee Titans, where he brings an evolving team's journey to fans on a daily basis. A longtime sports fanatic and recent baby blue jersey aficionado.

title: Titans' Snap Count Analysis vs. Jaguars: 2 Playmakers Pulled Away, While 1 WR Keeps Slipping
full_text:
A battle between the top-seeded team of the AFC South and the bottom seed ended in a 40-23 blowout, with the Jacksonville Jaguars proving supreme. Unfortunately, Titans' fans haven't seen a home win in almost an entire year. Tennessee's lone victory this season came against the Indianapolis Colts on Week 6 at Lucas Oil Stadium.
The Titans' last home win came against the Patrick-Mahomes-less Chiefs on Dec. 21, 2025, last season. With three home games left on the schedule, the original Nissan Stadium is yet to see a win in its final season.
It's time we dive into the snap-count winners and losers for the Titans in Week 10.
After missing Week 1 with a concussion, many fans assumed LB Cedric Gray would return to action as one of the primary linebackers for the Titans this season. However, Gray has been regulated to around 30 snaps per game, behind the likes of LB Cody Barton and rookie standout LB Anthony Hill Jr.
However, against Jacksonville, Gray was one of the only bright spots on the Tennessee defense.
He capitalized on his season-high 68 snaps. A big uptick from Week 8 against Cincinnati, where he only recorded 33, according to PFF . On Sunday, Gray recorded his first career interception while leading the Titans with nine tackles, one tackle for loss, and two pass deflections. Making him the first Titan to accomplish those stats since former First-Team All-Pro S Kevin Byard in 2020 .
Last season, Gray racked up the fourth most tackles in the NFL with 164, which was the most of any Titan. The 24-year-old linebacker is still a difference maker on a young Titans defense.
On Sunday, WR Elic Ayomanor had his best game of the season. For the second consecutive week, blooming star and rookie WR Carnell Tate was out with a shoulder injury, which has placed a greater responsibility on the remaining wide receiver core.
Ayomanor was the answer for second-year pro QB Cam Ward, serving as his top target throughout the game. He recorded a career-high 79 receiving yards from five receptions, including a 50-yard from a perfectly run post route by Ayomanor, resulting in a career-high pass and catch for Ward and Ayomanor.
Against Jacksonville, the 6-foot-2 wideout recorded 54 snaps, which is up from 50 snaps previously played against the Bengals. Although the number difference appears insignificant, Ayomanor's role was the difference.
Ayomanor was targeted 10 times against the Jaguars, which is a season-high, and double the targets he received from the previous game in Cincinnati. His targets and snaps saw an uptick, and so did his production.
In Cincinnati, Ayomanor had three catches for only 34 yards. However, his performance against the Jaguars was a positive for the future of Tennessee's offense.
This offseason, WR Wan'Dale Robinson was the big ticket acquisition for the Titans. The former New York Giant signed a massive four-year contract worth up to $70 million, making him the highest-paid Tennessee signee this past offseason, according to Spotrac .
Against the Jaguars, Robinson's snap count was down to 20 with an early exit due to an ankle injury. It could be assumed that his low snap count was because of his injury. However, Robinson's injury wouldn't tell the whole story because it didn't occur until late in the third quarter.
Robinson's production has been far from elite this season. In Cincinnati, Robinson recorded 72 of 77 offensive snaps but was still out-gained by TE Gunnar Helm and WR Chimere Dike, who aren't considered to be focal point offensive players.
Part of Robinson's decline in snaps has to do with drops and a recent trend of being outplayed by other receivers like Tate, Ayomanor and Dike.
Against Jacksonville, he only recorded three catches for 10 yards. His fourth game with three or fewer receptions this season, which is an obvious concern for a receiver one year removed from a career year where he had 1,000-plus yards with the Giants.
Robinson hasn't been the player Tennessee expected, especially for how much they paid him. In times like these when Tate is out due to injury, Robinson should be stepping up and playing like a true top receiver.
Isaiah is an award-winning journalist and photojournalist. A graduate from the University of Kentucky, he has previously been published by BloodHorse, KY Insider, and the Kentucky Kernel for multimedia sports coverage. Isaiah is a Tennessee Volunteer at heart bringing his local expertise to Titans coverage.

title: Chargers' Win Just Delivered Titans the Top Pick in 2027 Draft — But How Long Will it Last?
full_text:
Last night under the bright lights of primetime, the Los Angeles Chargers toppled the Baltimore Ravens for their first win of the season. Justin Herbert and the squad are now 1-8, but they weren't the only ones celebrating the victory. The Titans scored big on Monday.
As a result of Los Angeles pulling even with Tennessee's record, the Titans now hold the first overall pick in the 2027 NFL Draft. If the event were to kick off today, Mike Borgonzi and Robert Saleh would have their pick at any player in one of the best classes in recent memory.
This is massive news for any rebuild, but the kicker is obvious; we've still got eight games of football ahead of us. The Titans' overhaul demands a refresh of young talent, with that need being exasperated by Jeffery Simmons and Amani Hooker both being traded.
But if the last two weeks of competition have taught us anything about this Titans team, it's that they're both getting better and getting closer to beating good teams. Tennessee almost took down the Cincinnati Bengals on the road in Week 8.
This past Sunday, the now 7-2 Jacksonville Jaguars were in a tight race with the Titans through three quarters. A failed fourth-down conversion turned the tide negatively in what has previously been a close contest.
Either way, this is a Titans team ticking up, led by Cam Ward's steady development. This puts the franchise between a rock and a top pick. With a player like Jeremiah Smith on the line, the difference between a few spots is no laughing matter.
The superstar Ohio State pass-catcher is the B1G's all-time leader in receiving yards (3,875) and receiving touchdowns (42). A former teammate of Titans' stud Carnell Tate, reuniting the two would give Ward perhaps the best young playmaking duo in the NFL.
That would only be one of two first-round selections for Tennessee, no less. The vision is there for a historic draft class led by Smith that could turn a near-solid Titans team into a winner overnight. But win a few games now, slip a few picks, and Smith is out of the picture.
You see the conundrum. As Tennessee enters what I believe is a favorable matchup with the Dallas Cowboys in Week 11, Titans fans shouldn't grow too attached to this projection. The Titans haven't finished with less than three wins since 2014, when they went 2-14.
1-8 won't last forever, and the sweepstakes for the first-overall pick have really just begun.
Lane covers the Tennessee Titans, where he brings an evolving team's journey to fans on a daily basis. A longtime sports fanatic and recent baby blue jersey aficionado.

title: Grading Every Titans Position Group After Week 10: Defensive Ups and Downs Define Defeat vs. Jaguars
full_text:
The Tennessee Titans put up a valiant effort despite being severely undermanned, losing to the Jacksonville Jaguars 40-23 in this past Sunday's matchup.
This game was far more competitive than the score would indicate. The Titans are improving on a week-to-week basis, but the much more talented team pulled away... as things currently stand in the AFC South.
Nevertheless, there were a handful of discussion-worthy spot on either side of the ball as we ease out of the bye week and back into weekly football. So, let’s not waste any more time and get right into this week’s positional grades breakdown.
QB Cam Ward produced another strong performance against the Jags on Sunday. The second-year signal caller completed over 71 percent of his passes, totaling 231 passing yards, 39 rushing yards, two touchdowns, and one interception.
These aren’t numbers to write home about by any means, but there’s no denying how much he’s improved from Week 1 to now. Ward undoubtedly still has plenty of room to grow, but he’s quietly strung together a couple of games that should have Titans fans feeling optimistic about his potential going forward.
Over his last two games, Ward has completed 68% of his passes for 535 yards through the air, 80 yards on the ground, along with four touchdowns to just one interception.
And what’s most impressive is the fact that he’s done this without his best receiver and top two guards. At this rate, you can’t help but wonder what he could look like a year from now once Tennessee has turned its picks into actual players who could help the team.
It’ll be interesting to see how Ward closes out the season, especially once rookie WR Carnell Tate returns. But if this is the type of production the Titans get moving forward, then they should feel confident that they have their guy under center for the foreseeable future.
The Titans’ ground game was unable to find any kind of rhythm throughout the contest. RBs Tony Pollard and Tyjae Spears combined for just 61 yards on 13 carries.
It’s hard for any running back to get going when you’re not even hitting 10 carries for the game. Unfortunately, the Jaguars’ high-powered offense essentially forced the Titans to throw more than they probably wanted. That unbalanced attack put the Titans in a position where they simply didn’t have the offensive firepower to match the team across from them.
The majority of Pollard’s production came in the passing game, catching a team-high eight catches for 66 yards and one touchdown. So, for that, I’ll give this group a slightly above-average grade. But make no mistake, for this offense to reach its full potential, they need the ground game to be more of a factor than it was on Sunday.
Given the context that this group was once again without their best player, it was a very solid performance overall. Sadly, it wasn’t nearly good enough to compete with an elite team like the Jaguars.
WR Elic Ayomanor led the way with 79 yards on five catches, while WR Xavier Restrepo sneakily added 31 yards of his own.
No other receiver on the team eclipsed the 20-yard mark, as WRs Wan’Dale Robinson and Calvin Ridley were once again non-factors throughout the contest. A looming divorce with both veterans feels inevitable at this point, so limiting their snaps as much as possible would be ideal going forward.
Look for Tate to have an even bigger role once he returns from his shoulder injury, especially if Ward continues the progress at the rate he is.
TE Gunnar Helm was unable to follow up his big game in Cincinnati with another strong performance. The Texas product reeled in just four balls for 23 yards, while TE Daniel Bellinger added a touchdown and six yards off his two grabs.
The two also played a part in the ground game’s shortcomings with their inconsistent blocking, so I believe a C- is more than fair for this mediocre-at-best performance.
According to PFF , the Titans’ offensive line allowed a total of 19 pressures and one sack on Sunday. RT JC Latham and LG Chandler Zavala led the way, each giving up three pressures on their 43 pass-blocking snaps.
Certainly not ideal, but a solid performance overall, considering they were down two starters along the interior.
Nonetheless, their lack of a run game starts with this group upfront, and with LG Peter Skoronski on injured reserve, this could be a budding issue that could become more of a problem as the season plays out.
The Titans’ defensive line combined for just six pressures and one sack between the entire unit. DL John Franklin-Myers led the way with three pressures, while DE Jacob Martin added two of his own along with the lone sack of the game.
But it’s clear that without DT Jeffery Simmons, this is a group that appears to be punching above its weight class more often than not.
Martin has had his moments, and to be fair, he’s surpassed everyone’s expectations to this point. But the reality is, he’d be much better suited playing opposite another dominant edge as opposed to trying to be the lead dog himself.
Not having a reliable pass rusher who can wreak havoc on a down-by-down basis is why QB Trevor Lawrence ultimately lit them up the way they did.
The Titans were down both starting linebackers in this one, subsequently forcing LB Cedric Gray into a full-time starting role for the first time this season, and he made the most of it, totaling nine tackles, five run stops, and one interception.
The  top tackler was among the best at his position in Week 10:
#Titans ' Cedric Gray posted a 90.5 overall defensive grade, per @PFF , highest of any LB with at least 10 snaps so far in Wk. 10.
Dorian Mausi also played the first defensive snaps of his career on Sunday, and he performed admirably, all things considered. Mausi finished with seven tackles and two run stops. Nothing truly notable at the end of the day, but they were hardly the defense’s biggest problem on a day where they got gashed for 459 yards of total offense.
Not every DB was bad on Sunday. S Tony Adams continues to be one of the most underrated players on the team, earning a team-high grade of 84.1 for his performance against the Jags.
But that’s pretty much where the positivity ends for this secondary. The Jaguars had their way with the Titans’ pass defense. WR Parker Washington, in particular, looked like prime Megatron out there with how unguardable he was throughout the contest.
Washington finished the game with seven catches, 152 yards, and one touchdown en route to a comfortable 17-point win. As for Lawrence, he completed over 71 percent of his passes for a whopping 352 yards, three touchdowns, and one interception.
The Titans’ trio of corners Cor’Dale Flott, Joshua Williams, and Alontae Taylor allowed a staggering 284 yards between the three of them, per PFF . As if those numbers aren’t jarring enough, the three of them were targeted a combined total of 20 times on Sunday, 17 of which were completed.
Those are unsustainable numbers by NFL standards. You can’t consistently win at this level when your starting corners are giving up nearly 300 yards on 85 percent of their targets, especially when facing elite quarterbacks.
The Titans don’t have the talent to overcome that type of offensive output, and until this gets cleaned up, the Titans will need to score a lot of points just to have a chance on Sunday’s.
This group as a whole had a solid outing, but K Joey Slye is what gets this grade to an A.
On top of nailing all three of his kicks from beyond-50, Slye went viral for a monstrous hit on Jaguars KR Josh Cameron that separated him from the ball. It was the type of hit we haven’t seen from many Titans defenders this year.
That type of effort, along with his perfect performance in the kicking game warrants the only A grade for the game. I don't make the rules (I do). Slye's all-time slam deserves a special nod on this 1-8 Titans team.
Shaun is a longtime Titans fan who has years of experience in the field. He missed being on the team beat, and is here to change that.…

title: 2 Major Reasons Why Titans' Performance in Loss to Jaguars Hints at a Breakout Coming in Week 11
full_text:
The Tennessee Titans have never made losing feel so tolerable as they have in the last two weeks. It's worth saying again that there are no moral victories; this football team is 1-8. That won't cut it in any circumstance.
Although, the Titans are improving. Slowly, steadily, but unavoidably. The Tennessee team from the past two weeks looks lightyears removed from the one that took the field in Week 1 vs. the New York Jets.
Robert Saleh has this group moving in the right direction, and their performance against the Jacksonville Jaguars yesterday suggests a breakout could finally be on the horizon. Here are three reasons to expect it when the Titans face the Dallas Cowboys on the road next Sunday.
Cam Ward, who we'll get to, started settling in right when his favorite target was sidelined with a shoulder injury. Leading rookie receiver Carnell Tate, along with starting LBs Anthony Hill Jr. and Cody Barton, were forced to miss in Week 10.
Today, Coach Saleh said the Titans are hoping to get all three back against the Dallas Cowboys next week. It was the defense that needed help yesterday, even with LB Cedric Gray making his case as a starter without his two teammates on the field.
If all three of Tate, Hill, and Barton return, it'd be at the perfect time on either side of the ball. Ward can only benefit from returning Tate, while the defense will get one of their top tacklers and foremost veterans back. That's a win-win, that could lead to an actual win.
Circling back to Ward, the Titans' QB is starting to look the part of a franchise guy. Ward has doubled his season-long touchdown count in the past two games compared to the previous six. He's settling into an up-tempo offense that, finally, looks crafted for him.
A showing from Ward akin to Weeks 8 and 10 against a non-playoff team, like the Cowboys, could finally yield the winning result Tennessee fans have been waiting on. Every game from here on out is about Ward's development, but at this pace, he appears capable of winning at least a few of them.
The sophomore passer has already cleaned up many of his consistent early-season mistakes. With two straight two-touchdown outings under his belt, it's about crossing the finish line for Ward from here. Week 11 is shaping up to be a promising opportunity to do so.
Lane covers the Tennessee Titans, where he brings an evolving team's journey to fans on a daily basis. A longtime sports fanatic and recent baby blue jersey aficionado.

title: Jayden Daniels Takes Step That Could Help Commanders Sign Brandon Aiyuk
full_text:
ESPN's Jeremy Fowler reported Wednesday that San Francisco 49ers wide receiver Brandon Aiyuk and Washington Commanders quarterback Jayden Daniels have repaired their relationship. Fowler's report says Aiyuk reached out about a month earlier, and Daniels was receptive, and the two resolved their differences. With the trade deadline passed, San Francisco is expected to release Aiyuk by the time its roster exemption expires Monday, November 23. Daniels and Aiyuk were teammates at Arizona State, and Aiyuk's offseason was filled with videos and posts showing his desire to play in the burgundy and gold. Their relationship deteriorated after Aiyuk’s summer social media comments targeting Daniels and his mother, Regina Jackson. While Fowler confirms the two mended fences, his latest column leaves the door wide open on what exactly that means. The report mentions nothing about any of the steps that would follow, including current interest levels, if any, of the Commanders. "Not sure what that means for Aiyuk’s chances — or his previously stated desire — to play in Washington, but he and the quarterback are good again," Fowler wrote.
The NFL reinstated Aiyuk from San Francisco’s reserve/left squad list on November 9. The league gave the 49ers a two-game roster exemption that expires on November 23 . While Aiyuk currently remains under contract, San Francisco must resolve his status by either adding him to its 53-man roster or releasing him. Since the trade deadline has passed, a release would subject his contract to waivers. He'll likely find no suitors at the price he was getting paid. Aiyuk last played on October 20, 2024, when he tore the ACL, MCL, and meniscus in his right knee. His agent, Drew Rosenhaus, told Dianna Russini on November 17: "He’s 100% healthy right now, in shape, and working out full force." With Terry McLaurin out for the season after tearing his patellar tendon against San Francisco, Stefon Diggs, Treylon Burks, and Antonio Williams have taken on the primary receiver responsibilities . It's not 100% clear what role Aiyuk would play or how he would fit the Commanders' attack, although his skill set isn't something you generally see lying at the top of the trash pile.
